I have never written a game review but this game has been so fun it deserves a write-up.  Let me state first, I am not an FPS person.  In most FPS's I don't have the skills to survive very long without my son helping me.  We play Halo 4 online and he follows me around avenging my death.  I am usually the person with the highest death count while my son ends up with the highest kill count.  Borderlands is the first FPS that I have really enjoyed.  The cartoonish graphics are well done and the style of the characters go well with the comedic story line.  For what ever reason, I have managed to avoid death far more in Borderlands 2 then any other FPS.  That has helped me want to continue playing for hours at a time which in turn has helped me increase my targeting and camera control.  I can now play other FPS games which I never would have attempted before.  I'm grateful that the developers designed the levels the way they did making mobs easy enough for me to kill but hard enough to make me have to work at it.  The increase in my FPS skills opened up many more games that I can play with my son now.  I really enjoy our gaming time so anything that increases it is great.
Anyone that has issues with their FPS skills shouldn't be afraid to try this game.  I think it's the type of game everyone will enjoy.

I’ gonna give you the god honest truth about this game, and this is from a man that almost has a total of 400 hours into it so listen up.
This is the type of game that if you are considering getting, you want to make sure you have people that are going to play with you, you absolutely do not want to play this alone, it is a huge bore if you do.
That being said, it’s not a bad game by any means. It’s interesting, challenging, fun, it has a lot of good content but it is not without it’s flaws and boy does it have flaws.
It’s great in the sense that all the characters feel completely different, they all have unique skills and playing styles so when you create one it feels as though you are playing a completely different game which is really good for replay value. Once you beat the story for the first time, another harder story mode called “True Vault Hunter Mode” will appear scaling the enemies to the level you were when you beat it for the first time which is cool it means you get to beat the game again with all your endgame gear and get nicer stronger things and have more of a challenge which is pretty cool for the first time. But then it happens again, with “Ultimate Vault Hunter Mode” in which the same thing happens but in truth this is when all the problems in Borderlands 2 begin to arise, and hard as hell.
The story quickly becomes dull, and the humor in the game is really only somewhat funny the first time and then quickly becomes annoying.
But my biggest gripe with Borderlands is the scaling system that comes with the guns and the enemies. OH YOU JUST FOUND A NEW SHOTGUN THAT DEALS 20% MORE DAMAGE THAN YOUR PREVIOUS ONE?
WE'LL JUST RAISE THE "LEVEL" OF THE ENEMY YOU'RE FIGHTING SO THEY ALSO GET 20 % MORE HP RENDERING THE QUESTION AS TO WHY WE EVEN BOTHERED TO DO THIS IN THE FIRST PLACE.
The enemy scaling is awful, they don’t become harder game play wise they just become bullet sponges and gain health regeneration.
And then there’s the awful drop rate of legendary weapons and gear. Guns in the first game could carry you for a pretty long time. In Borderlands 2 they become outdated and out damaged by the most common gun pretty quickly due to the bad level scaling, and this is especially true in UVHM forcing you to farm the same boss for hours, maybe days due to the 1/1000th chance it might or might not drop.
The DLC is just ‘okay’. It’s nowhere near as good as the first games but Tiny Tina’s assault on Dragon’s Keep is pretty good.
I know what you may be asking. “Hey if this game was that flawed why did you sink so much time on it?”
Because it’s very fun with friends, and I’m a huge sucker for having an adventure and it did deliver on that, and as awful as the enemy scaling was it did make it challenging so when we beat stuff as a team there was a big sense of accomplishment especially for raid bosses.

Short analysis:
I spent way to much time on this game to find out it's not the game for me.  If you are willing to dedicate 2-3 plus hours a day, or accept starting from scratch very frequently, or like the gut-wrenching feeling that happens every time you log on waiting to see if you've been killed and your fort raided, then this game might work for you.  Otherwise, i believe you can enjoy or spend your time more effectively elsewhere.
Longer Analysis:
After rage quitting (not the first time) I began to wonder if maybe I was approaching the game incorrectly.
I browsed reddit and steam forums to see why I was not enjoying Rust like I thought I should.  While the game is enjoyable, I found myself getting turned off the longer I played.  I have compiled my own thoughts as to why I cannot recommend this game:
-Rust is a survival formulated on getting out (advantages) what you put it.  The game linearly rewards those who put in more time.  If you cannot dedicated 2-3 + hours a day, reconsider.  For those with a full time job, like myself, reconsider.
-The game (at least currently) appears unbalanced as it ultimately is biased to the dedicated, invested gamer.  Those who wish to play casually or game lightly cannot recieve the same payout as those who spend 7 or 8 or 9 or more hours a day.  The more invested gamer will always have the advantage.  Righfully so.  However, in my experience, the disparity is difficult to overcome and often not worth the amount of required effort.
-What I understand, Rust is designed to foster social collaboration, to give you a sense of belonging as you "work together".  Most every server i tried, this was not the feeling i got.  Most of the time I found myself having to selectively choose a server that did not leave me frustrated or bitter.
-Every person on Rust has their own agenda.  These can very loosily be generalized into two categories: those that want to co-exist, and those that want the rush of raiding and killing and expanding.  Generally I interacted with the latter group more frequently.
-I found pleasure in the game was based too much on picking the right server rather than learning how to play the game.  While i understand you have the right to be picky with your server choices, success in the game should not be determined based mostly on the community you choose.
In summary:  Rust was an amazing game.  I really enjoyed the graphics, the crafting and building, and the environment.  Exploration and surviving both the elements and community was adrenaline pumping!  There is a reason it took me until 250 odd hours to decide I had enough. Ultimately, the community (players) does not support enjoyable game play, the game is imbalanced leading to a strong bias against the casual or less invested gamer, and that success is achieved solely off of either quantity of game time played or lengthy trial and error to find an acceptable server.  Cannot recommend.

I have never written a game review but this game has been so fun it deserves a write-up.  Let me state first, I am not an FPS person.  In most FPS's I don't have the skills to survive very long without my son helping me.  We play Halo 4 online and he follows me around avenging my death.  I am usually the person with the highest death count while my son ends up with the highest kill count.  Borderlands is the first FPS that I have really enjoyed.  The cartoonish graphics are well done and the style of the characters go well with the comedic story line.  For what ever reason, I have managed to avoid death far more in Borderlands 2 then any other FPS.  That has helped me want to continue playing for hours at a time which in turn has helped me increase my targeting and camera control.  I can now play other FPS games which I never would have attempted before.  I'm grateful that the developers designed the levels the way they did making mobs easy enough for me to kill but hard enough to make me have to work at it.  The increase in my FPS skills opened up many more games that I can play with my son now.  I really enjoy our gaming time so anything that increases it is great.
Anyone that has issues with their FPS skills shouldn't be afraid to try this game.  I think it's the type of game everyone will enjoy.

That's when I realized this game was self aware of my actions, even if I died it is shown by the reactions of the characters. When I fought bosses it didn't force me to go through their dialogue. This gave me an appreciation for the game mechanics as they knew we didn't want to go through the same thing twice. And the ending was so wild that my brain couldn't comprehend what was going on! It thrilled me!
But then I started playing on the pacifist route. I never realized how guilty I felt. All the pain I caused. I killed monsters, even the ones who showed me mercy. Somehow, every encounter would burst me with emotion I even cried when I went against toriel and cried again when I fought the king. at the end I get a summary of what happened via phone call. I was happy to see that I didn't hurt anyone. Not even SWktor made me cry and that system had the choice to choose the light or evil similar to undertale. But perhaps the diffirence was that I didn't fight anyone and that the game was self aware of my choices.
With all honesty, I rate this game a 9/10. For being able to touch my heart! You deserve a standing applause my friend!

Short analysis:
I spent way to much time on this game to find out it's not the game for me.  If you are willing to dedicate 2-3 plus hours a day, or accept starting from scratch very frequently, or like the gut-wrenching feeling that happens every time you log on waiting to see if you've been killed and your fort raided, then this game might work for you.  Otherwise, i believe you can enjoy or spend your time more effectively elsewhere.
Longer Analysis:
After rage quitting (not the first time) I began to wonder if maybe I was approaching the game incorrectly.
I browsed reddit and steam forums to see why I was not enjoying Rust like I thought I should.  While the game is enjoyable, I found myself getting turned off the longer I played.  I have compiled my own thoughts as to why I cannot recommend this game:
-Rust is a survival formulated on getting out (advantages) what you put it.  The game linearly rewards those who put in more time.  If you cannot dedicated 2-3 + hours a day, reconsider.  For those with a full time job, like myself, reconsider.
-The game (at least currently) appears unbalanced as it ultimately is biased to the dedicated, invested gamer.  Those who wish to play casually or game lightly cannot recieve the same payout as those who spend 7 or 8 or 9 or more hours a day.  The more invested gamer will always have the advantage.  Righfully so.  However, in my experience, the disparity is difficult to overcome and often not worth the amount of required effort.
-What I understand, Rust is designed to foster social collaboration, to give you a sense of belonging as you "work together".  Most every server i tried, this was not the feeling i got.  Most of the time I found myself having to selectively choose a server that did not leave me frustrated or bitter.
-Every person on Rust has their own agenda.  These can very loosily be generalized into two categories: those that want to co-exist, and those that want the rush of raiding and killing and expanding.  Generally I interacted with the latter group more frequently.
-I found pleasure in the game was based too much on picking the right server rather than learning how to play the game.  While i understand you have the right to be picky with your server choices, success in the game should not be determined based mostly on the community you choose.
In summary:  Rust was an amazing game.  I really enjoyed the graphics, the crafting and building, and the environment.  Exploration and surviving both the elements and community was adrenaline pumping!  There is a reason it took me until 250 odd hours to decide I had enough. Ultimately, the community (players) does not support enjoyable game play, the game is imbalanced leading to a strong bias against the casual or less invested gamer, and that success is achieved solely off of either quantity of game time played or lengthy trial and error to find an acceptable server.  Cannot recommend.

I’ gonna give you the god honest truth about this game, and this is from a man that almost has a total of 400 hours into it so listen up.
This is the type of game that if you are considering getting, you want to make sure you have people that are going to play with you, you absolutely do not want to play this alone, it is a huge bore if you do.
That being said, it’s not a bad game by any means. It’s interesting, challenging, fun, it has a lot of good content but it is not without it’s flaws and boy does it have flaws.
It’s great in the sense that all the characters feel completely different, they all have unique skills and playing styles so when you create one it feels as though you are playing a completely different game which is really good for replay value. Once you beat the story for the first time, another harder story mode called “True Vault Hunter Mode” will appear scaling the enemies to the level you were when you beat it for the first time which is cool it means you get to beat the game again with all your endgame gear and get nicer stronger things and have more of a challenge which is pretty cool for the first time. But then it happens again, with “Ultimate Vault Hunter Mode” in which the same thing happens but in truth this is when all the problems in Borderlands 2 begin to arise, and hard as hell.
The story quickly becomes dull, and the humor in the game is really only somewhat funny the first time and then quickly becomes annoying.
But my biggest gripe with Borderlands is the scaling system that comes with the guns and the enemies. OH YOU JUST FOUND A NEW SHOTGUN THAT DEALS 20% MORE DAMAGE THAN YOUR PREVIOUS ONE?
WE'LL JUST RAISE THE "LEVEL" OF THE ENEMY YOU'RE FIGHTING SO THEY ALSO GET 20 % MORE HP RENDERING THE QUESTION AS TO WHY WE EVEN BOTHERED TO DO THIS IN THE FIRST PLACE.
The enemy scaling is awful, they don’t become harder game play wise they just become bullet sponges and gain health regeneration.
And then there’s the awful drop rate of legendary weapons and gear. Guns in the first game could carry you for a pretty long time. In Borderlands 2 they become outdated and out damaged by the most common gun pretty quickly due to the bad level scaling, and this is especially true in UVHM forcing you to farm the same boss for hours, maybe days due to the 1/1000th chance it might or might not drop.
The DLC is just ‘okay’. It’s nowhere near as good as the first games but Tiny Tina’s assault on Dragon’s Keep is pretty good.
I know what you may be asking. “Hey if this game was that flawed why did you sink so much time on it?”
Because it’s very fun with friends, and I’m a huge sucker for having an adventure and it did deliver on that, and as awful as the enemy scaling was it did make it challenging so when we beat stuff as a team there was a big sense of accomplishment especially for raid bosses.

Borderlands 2, in my eyes, is a game that changed my gaming experience and I consider it a masterpeice crafted by the folks at Gearbox Software. As it always goes on sale, this game is something that you want to pick up. I only have 24 hours on this account, but on Xbox 360 I have over 200+. It will leave you playing until 5 in the morning and hooked for weeks. Borderlands 2 defined what gaming should be.
You don't need to play the first one to really grasp the story, it does help though as they make a lot of little connections throughout the game that I found really awesome. The story of Borderlands revolves around the world of Pandora, a land filled with bandits, goons, monsters, and flying Rakks. You pick your class, whichever fits your playing style, whether it be the Siren, a Commando, a Gunzerker, or an Assassin. There are also two DLC classes available, which are the Mechromancer and the Psycho. You battle and quest your way to vanquish Evil Jack, the storys antagonist or villain. You hop online to receive help from some buddys or just complete the game solo. When you reach the end and finish the campagin, you're given another option of playing through the campaign again, in which the gameplay really starts to shine.
The gameplay of Borderlands 2 is what really got me hooked. Borderlands 2 is a first-person shooter, similar to Call of Duty or Battlefield, but with a twist. The fun part is that is that it adds elements from RPG's like loot, quests, and leveling. For every enemy you kill in the world of Pandora, they drop loot -- whether that be a nice new shiny gun with some enchantments, a new grenade mod, a legendary shield, or even a new personilization item for your character. Every enemy killed, or quest completed, also gives you XP that helps you level up your character. With every level your character gains, you gain a skill point. Each class has a distinct skill tree that you can spec. This adds much replayability to the game as you can mix and match different builds to your playing style. This adds hours of fun to the game and what really makes Borderlands, well, Borderlands!
Overall, I reccomend this game to anybody out there. It mixes some of the most addicting aspects of gaming into one. The requirements to play the game aren't that demanding and the visual aspect is a lot of fun, giving you that cartoon feel. Anybody with a mid-end build could run it. This was one of the first games I bought when I went to PC. With Gearbox adding new DLC almost every month, it will keep you entertained. Borderlands 2 for me redefined gaming, and I think it will you redefine your gaming experience as well.

Here's why: It's not fun. Pure and simple.
The first problem you'll have is getting the game to even run at a playable framerate. People's experiences vary wildly, with some running it no problem on competent computers, and some getting 10 fps on a total gaming rig. Myself, I had to turn all the visuals down and do some ini tweaks to get 30 fps. I'm running about 16gb of vram with an nvidia gtx980M.
Once you're actually in the game, your only goal is survival. There is no endgame, no overarching structure to the gameworld. You can't even make your own, really, given how otherwise incomplete the game is. Every playthrough is essentially try to find a gun and kill people, because what else is there to do? And if that is all you want to do, why not play a proper fps that works? The goal is survival but there's no particular reason to. You're not surviving for anything. I'm not going to say that the combat scenarios aren't raw and exciting, because they are. They are, however, so few and far between (not to mention broken because desync up the♥♥♥♥♥ that it's not worth it. Don't buy this "game," buy an actual game. Although a challenging game starting off and an almost always cancerous community, This game is one of my favorites of all time. With developers who update their content monthly, Hilarious player interactions you'd expect from a Garry's game, and the feeling of reward when you win that rock fight. The only negative aspects which should be noted in this game is the people, yes there can be very nice players who help you when starting off but its a sort of hit or miss. Inside of small servers which new players usually join to get their bearings, large groups of players drive the solo and small group players away by constant raiding which they can't do much about. Even if the players in the large clan are garbage, with that many players respawning, picking eachother up, and shooting then the lower populations don't stand a chance. This isn't to say that all servers will be like this or that large groups are bad. Inside of larger servers those kinds of clans are too busy fighting each to really bully the smaller guys. If you're looking for a challenging fun game with high stakes rewards and even higher stake losses then I would recommend this game.

First game I've ever been really addicted to. I've caught myself playing Rust 14 hours in a day if left undisturbed. It's so much fun. There are quite a few negative reviews going around so for my review I just want to provide some instructions for how to have a great time in Rust, I think these will help you avoid most of the negative experiences people are describing.
1. Play with your friends. If you don't have any friends, try to make some in Rust, it's not hard. This is a post apocalyptic survival game and much like the real post apocalypse loners will have a really hard time. Dealing with the social problems of organizing people together is a HUGE part of this game. An additional point to this is: GET A MICROPHONE. Absolutely essential in rust, it's a game where you talk to people as much as shoot at them.
2. Play on community servers, choose your server wisely. From what I hear the official servers are filled with hackers and have terrible communities. A well moderated servers will have few incidents of hackers because they get banned. If you're a beginner try to play a less crowded server so you can learn how to survive in the wild before people are shooting at you and trying to raid your little shack. Hackers nowadays are using AIMbot and ESP to headshot you and see through walls. Story time - > My favorite was this one time I am fully geared but didn't have any guns. Just a fire axe. I proceed up this construction building to scavange when I reach the middle of the stairs I see two players prone facing the stairs. Both with clown masks and full of loot. They both don't look friendly and try to tell me to stop in my tracks. I knew it was a trap and I would be killed if I stayed! It didn't look good, since I was outnumbered and in an enclosed area. I then took off running and was in the junk yard now. Looking behind me they are both in pursuit and are telling me they want to take my shoes. One catches up to me and hits me with his axe and I start to bleed, I zig-zag and manage to lose him again. I keep running but I'm bleeding and I know I will eventually bleed out. So as a human being you have to options fight or flight. Flight would get me killed since I'm bleeding and losing 2 persistant players isn't gonna be an easy task. I turn around and start trying to kill the melee player and maneuver around in circles. His friend armed with a shotgun is trying to get a clear shot at me but is careful not to friendly fire since we are both moving quickly/ sporadically. He shoots and misses, he trys to reload and is clearly under stress. I take this advantage to attack him since he can only reload 2 shells at a time (double barrel shotgun) I hit him with an axe and he starts bleeding he retreats to bandage his wound. I then focus on his friend with the axe who I clearly in shock that I had reversed the entire situation.
The hunters have now become the hunted. With quick movement and focus I proceed to kill the axemen and chase after his friend with the shotgun. He is still bleeding and trys to bandage/reload but doesn't have enough time to. I swing my axe at him and he starts to die but decides to try and save his character by logging off.
Moments like these make Day Z so much fun and worth it. Random events like this make the game spontanous and intense. No other game makes you feel like a survivalist and stressed at the same time.
TL;DR : Got ambushed by two guys in clown masked. Asked me to stop and kept running. One has shotgun and tries to shot me while other trys to dismember me with an axe. Turns the tides by killing one and making the other log off like a wuss. Day Z is fun due to moments like these.

Borderlands 2, in my eyes, is a game that changed my gaming experience and I consider it a masterpeice crafted by the folks at Gearbox Software. As it always goes on sale, this game is something that you want to pick up. I only have 24 hours on this account, but on Xbox 360 I have over 200+. It will leave you playing until 5 in the morning and hooked for weeks. Borderlands 2 defined what gaming should be.
You don't need to play the first one to really grasp the story, it does help though as they make a lot of little connections throughout the game that I found really awesome. The story of Borderlands revolves around the world of Pandora, a land filled with bandits, goons, monsters, and flying Rakks. You pick your class, whichever fits your playing style, whether it be the Siren, a Commando, a Gunzerker, or an Assassin. There are also two DLC classes available, which are the Mechromancer and the Psycho. You battle and quest your way to vanquish Evil Jack, the storys antagonist or villain. You hop online to receive help from some buddys or just complete the game solo. When you reach the end and finish the campagin, you're given another option of playing through the campaign again, in which the gameplay really starts to shine.
The gameplay of Borderlands 2 is what really got me hooked. Borderlands 2 is a first-person shooter, similar to Call of Duty or Battlefield, but with a twist. The fun part is that is that it adds elements from RPG's like loot, quests, and leveling. For every enemy you kill in the world of Pandora, they drop loot -- whether that be a nice new shiny gun with some enchantments, a new grenade mod, a legendary shield, or even a new personilization item for your character. Every enemy killed, or quest completed, also gives you XP that helps you level up your character. With every level your character gains, you gain a skill point. Each class has a distinct skill tree that you can spec. This adds much replayability to the game as you can mix and match different builds to your playing style. This adds hours of fun to the game and what really makes Borderlands, well, Borderlands!
Overall, I reccomend this game to anybody out there. It mixes some of the most addicting aspects of gaming into one. The requirements to play the game aren't that demanding and the visual aspect is a lot of fun, giving you that cartoon feel. Anybody with a mid-end build could run it. This was one of the first games I bought when I went to PC. With Gearbox adding new DLC almost every month, it will keep you entertained. Borderlands 2 for me redefined gaming, and I think it will you redefine your gaming experience as well.
-H9

Borderlands 2 gets a lot right and simultaneously a lot wrong.
If you love to horde loot and you somehow don't already own this game, pick it up. Loot is its bread and butter. And, just like bread and butter in real life, it gets old fast when you have too much of it. So many of the guns look and feel identical, even if they aren't. This is because of the way that Gearbox generated the loot, where none of the non-mission guns really stand out as anything special. The gun system is a cool gimmick at first, but I'd rather see a selection of awesome, hand-crafted guns instead of a mish-mash of random parts.
Borderlands 2, like its predecessor, is designed to be played in co-op. There are no puzzles in the game that have any requirement for co-op, nor any bosses, but it's very clear that it was meant for more than one person. I've played through the story twice - once with a new character, once with the same character in the game's version of New Game +, Vault Hunter Mode. No matter how hard you train, the enemies seem to be always one or two levels higher than you, and a large portion of them have surprisingly large amounts of health. This makes the game a lot harder than you'd expect, and, if you're like me, playing mostly solo, you'll be spending a lot of time hiding behind cover, reloading whatever subpar gun you're currently using as the grunt level bad guys two shot you. In short, it's tedious.
The art style is fantastic. It really nails the comic book aesthetic while still staying original. The textures themselves are nothing special but the game runs well so no complaints. The PhysX effects, while sometimes taxing, definitely add to the atmosphere - shame they only work on Nvidia cards. The characters look interesting and fine... until they speak. Their heads become locked onto you and they almost bend at weird angles. I'm fairly sure I never saw a character change their facial expression for the entirety of the game, which looks terrifyingly unnatural. Also, none of the dialogue or cutscenes are skippable, which is frustrating when you're playing the game for the second time and don't care about hearing the story again. The enemies look cool for the most part and the effects are good too.
The story is fine, better than the first game but nothing special. Voice acting is very good but the jokes can be weak at times (especially when they reference memes, which is just downright irritating). The music was unmemorable but I remember thinking it was fine. Some characters can get really annoying, like Claptrap, but they have their moments so you look past it. There's an incredibly large amount of DLC, but most of it is just costumes which don't matter. Either way, try and pick up the GOTY version, which gives you access to all the main story DLC and the two new characters.
Last but not least, gameplay. Each character has special abilities and skill trees which are fine. Some of the skills are really fun, like when the Gunzerker goes to dual-wielding any of his guns. But the most important part is the gunplay itself, as that's what you will be focusing on for the majority of the game. Just about every gun feels different, which is super cool. What isn't cool are some of the minor things, like how every gun seems to have bullets that are slower than arthritic snails. It's a real pain sometimes, as enemies like to dodge a lot but your bullets don't move at real bullet speeds so they can't reach the enemies in time. Some people like this, but I really don't.
In conclusion, despite all the negative opinions I've brought to light, I'd still recommend this game. It's a lot of fun, even if it can get tedious at times. Do I personally want to play it again? No, but I feel that I've most definitely gotten my money's worth, which was about $20USD in a sale.

Ok. Read ALL of this before you buy it:
i have, to date, 1629 hours on this game. It is by far, the most addicting, intense survival game on the market with some really down to earth devs that listen to their clientbase on Reddit, and are always updating the game with new content.
Lets start with the community,
The community, are cancerous, toxic keyboard warriors that constantly spout♥♥♥♥♥♥and pretend that you're not even human. and i love it. If you are over sensitive, or cannot take an insult, or someone backstabbing you, then you need to steer clear. If you're slightly more resillient, keep reading.
Next Is the gameplay.
I can't believe its taken this long in the gaming generation for a game like this to be made. it's amazing, It's definitely a grind, you will be hitting lots of trees and rocks if you want to really achieve in this game, and with the mechanics the way they are, once you play it, you are 100% committed. you have work at 8AM and its getting on for 1AM, but you need to get your base secured with an airlock before you can even think of going to bed, but then you need to eat because you've literally starved yourself all day getting yourself set up on a server.
Depending on how lucky you are, you may get set up quite quickly, but if you come across a group of newmans, or a bear, or a wolf, unless you think fast, you are knackered, dead, and back to square 1.
Once you have a stone/metal base, with an airlock (1 hour for an experienced solo player) the game really starts to get interesting, you'll come across other people that will kill you out of desperation to be the best. you'll be farming rocks and trees, each hit loud enough to be heard within a 75m radius, the intensity of waiting for someone to come and shoot you in the back of the head with an arrow to take the stuff you spend 30 mins farming. you're always on your guard, your always focused on that one mission. to survive.
you come across one guy, think you can get the jump on him, he's wearing good gear and is carrying that AK47 that you so desperately want. you ping an arrow, it's a headshot, and he's panicking, one more arrow hits, and he's down, you've done it! he's down, and gear is there to be claimed! you head over, and as soon as you've taken 10 steps, 3 of his teammates that were nowhere to be seen have just appeared, you're suddenly on the backfoot, trying to escape the rounds being peppered towards you. Taking cover in the bushes, and the trees you try and gain some ground on them, hiding in bushes, is a cowardly thing to do. but placing landmines and bear traps in them is just freaking genius, Of course the moment is all too intense, and by the time you've calmed yourself to a state where you can even equip a landmine let alone place it, you are dead.
At the moment, this game is heavily favoured for groups/teams. It can be extremely hard for solo players to survive a wipe. if you log out with your base intact, don't even think that it will be safe in the morning, the people love an easy offline raid.
oooh yes, raiding!
Once you're established, you'll make, armour, guns, ammo, traps, turrets, and it gets really interesting. building a safe, unraidable base being the objective, you'll learn how to mislead offline raiders, build internal defensive points to defend against an online raid, this is the fun part. all that sulphur you collected when you wanted that stone and metal now comes into use.
turn it into gunpowder for C4 or Rockets and Rocket launcher. and go raiding someone elses base.
got a target? someone that flamed you before, some neighbours that are always trying to shoot you from their roofs? take your rocket launcher, and go level that friggin base! take them out!
In a nutshell.
This game is by far the most entertaining game ive played. battlefield 4, FIFA, Rocket league, are all great games, but most of my life this year has been dedicated to this marvelous game, while the others collect dust.
Get Rust, Live Rust, Breathe Rust, Die Rust.

Where do I even begin? It seems these days, pixel art-type games are better liked than most triple A games. I'm not surprised. The simplistic style of art and beautiful world design speak mountains about this game. It shows you just how amazing such simple-looking things can be.
The story, which is very important as this game is mostly story driven, is incredible. It's original, it brings to question philosophy and morals, and most importantly it gives you a sense of freedom that most other games fail to serve. Despite that, unlike most story driven games, it doesn't fail to deliver equally amazing gameplay.
The fighting style is unique, and tough. It gives the player a challenge to eliminate the sense of boredom one can get by playing other random encounter games. Each mob has its own story, its own feelings. No fight is ever the same. There are puzzles littered here and there, ones that could take a little while to figure out, but none that are impossible.
There are bits and pieces of Easter eggs scattered around, sometimes things that have nothing to do with the story. It gives a sense of reality. Other things go on in life, nothing completely surrounds the story. Life goes on. In Undertale, monster lives go on.
100% recommend, and also thanks Toby Fox for making this brilliant masterpiece.

Let me start by saying that this game is unfinished. Yes, I know it's in early accses, but it feels like it's not even that.
The world in Rust feels pretty much the same on all servers, despite being randomly generated(like in Minecraft). The radtowns feel meaningless, since you can't build there, all you do is shoot at others who had the same bright idea of farming blueprints. Other than that it's just player built bases, which would be ok if they didn't look all the same(stone on 1 lvl, metal on the others). The areas look pretty bland, the only obvious differences is that some have woods, and one has snow. Now I don't like everything being too obvious, I just want some of them to a bit more diverse not just woods and rocks. Some nuked towns, like in Falllout, would make a great addion. Now whenever I talk to my rust fanboy friend Ocean-Master he says quote :"It'll be added soon". I mean if that's Facepunch's exuse for everything. i'm glad there's no season pass for everything "to be added" at the very least.
The gameplay is oh so very boring. It's just you farm wood and stone with your rock, then with some tools, the you build a base and start raiding other's for greasy loot until someone raids yours. and then you start it all over again. The hitboxes are the one good thing about it as in if someone hits you in the back of the head, a mask won't protect you. There are very few guns, and they feel pretty cluncky, and i think have too much recoil.
Base building is pretty basic: you put a fundation, than walls and start expanding. I didn't really like it, it felt to basic, and I think it could really use some cosmetic features. Then again, those will be added soon.
But the reason I completely hate this game instead just disliking it is the ABSOLUTELY TOXIC comunity. Literaly all players I've come accross just shot me on sight. Well escept for one who me made a slave and one night just blew up our entire base. You cannot, I reapet, cannot interact with these human shaped animals. Whenever they see you, they shoot. So there's no room for building clans with people you dunno without fearing they will stab you in the back the second you go AFK to take a♥♥♥♥♥♥ or when you dissconect. In order not to get raided you need to stay logged in24/7, wich is something I, and many others, cannot do. Whenever I tried buildinga town and collecting fees and taxes from the the peaceful dwellers of Goodtown, someone would just come and shoot me with a shotgun. Just like that.
Those are the reasons I refuse to play Rust anymore. Maybe it'll change. Maybe, maybe , maybe...

Where do I even begin? It seems these days, pixel art-type games are better liked than most triple A games. I'm not surprised. The simplistic style of art and beautiful world design speak mountains about this game. It shows you just how amazing such simple-looking things can be.
The story, which is very important as this game is mostly story driven, is incredible. It's original, it brings to question philosophy and morals, and most importantly it gives you a sense of freedom that most other games fail to serve. Despite that, unlike most story driven games, it doesn't fail to deliver equally amazing gameplay.
The fighting style is unique, and tough. It gives the player a challenge to eliminate the sense of boredom one can get by playing other random encounter games. Each mob has its own story, its own feelings. No fight is ever the same. There are puzzles littered here and there, ones that could take a little while to figure out, but none that are impossible.
There are bits and pieces of Easter eggs scattered around, sometimes things that have nothing to do with the story. It gives a sense of reality. Other things go on in life, nothing completely surrounds the story. Life goes on. In Undertale, monster lives go on.
100% recommend, and also thanks Toby Fox for making this brilliant masterpiece.

The short story is the game looks good, the buildings are good.  But the game lacks a player base and the full release is so far away that the game will be dead .. and will not arise as a zombie.  There is simply too little "game" and too much fluff (they are working on player characters actually 'aging' rather than more vehicles, private servers or something to actually DO in the game)
Take a look at the reviews and click on the RECENT button.  They are almost all negative yet the game has a "mostly positive" overall review.   That tells us that the game is not meeting its expectations.   People expected the game to be nearly complete and working at this point .. its been released as "Early Alpha" for TWO YEARS and was in development for a year before that!   There were a million sales in about the first week of release,  thats $30 MILLION of income and yet they cant get spend a million or two on a few extra devs to get this completed?   The recent 'patch' actually REMOVED zombies from the zombie game!   Lead Producer Hicks in a forum post said they were "reduced", which is true .. reduced to zero (I played for 30 minutes or so, ran through 2 towns and saw ZERO zombies.    While this is a temporary issue its indicative of the entire game.   It was a year wait for vehicles ... I realize they are adding things all the time but they aren't adding anything to make many people actually want to play the game.
I hadnt played in over a year having lost interest in the wait for vehicles, weapons, and mostly private servers without which, every server is identical and you even spawn in the same spot with the same gear.
I loved the Dayz mod, played it for 3000 hours, ran a bunch of servers, am a
.. But I just cant say the DayZ Standalone is worthwhile purchasing AT THE MOMENT ...   Now maybe when they get it completed and allow private servers so each server can be UNIQUE, it will be a good game ..
But I fear that day will either never arrive or it will be way too late .. if its not already too late. There is a constant steady decline in players because everyone who bought it finds nothing entertaining so they move to some other game.
Yes, the game looks good. The buildings have furnished interiors .. but there is no GAME to go along with it ..
When I played, there were about 15 servers with more than 10 players, perhaps a hundred had 1 or more players.

I had really high hopes for this game. Played the mod a bunch and enjoyed it very much, then was one of the first to buy into the standalone to support the devs and help jump-start further development.
Sadly all that money that they got from me, and other fans like myself, was not put to good use. They have some interesting ideas but for the amount of money they got to make this game really good the speed of progress is completely unacceptable!
I will not go into all the ways this game is still a mess (bugs, net code, game balance, etc.), which were acceptable when it was a non-profit mod but are completely unacceptable now.
As a huge Fan of the genre in general and the DayZ mod in particular it pains me to see how they are wasting this oppertunity to make something really great. I have the sinking feeling that they simply took most of the money as "payment" for work they already did when they programmed the mod and left a skeleton crew to pacify fans with minor updates
Honestly if you look at the amount of money they made from the early access sale its clear by now that they are either scamming people or are at the very least terribly ineffective at actually making this an AAA title. Maybe programming a half♥♥♥♥♥♥♥mod was all they were ever destined for and things like actually fixing the engine is simply beyond them.
The early access devs in general have to understand that people are paying the (high!) price for these titles not because the game is worth it now, but because they want to help the devs to create the game they hope it will one day be. While not legally binding, you are selling a promise, NOT an unfinished product. If early access status is just an excuse to sell people unfinished products, then this wont have much of a future and we are back to AAA studios and everything we dislike about them. But at least then you pay for a finished product.
So do i recommend this game ? The current version is just not worth the price and i lost faith that this will change anytime soon. The only real reason to accept it is that every other game in the genre is hardly better if at all. But to me, at least, thats not enough and i am not willing to sponsor a race to the bottom.

Let me start by saying that this game is unfinished. Yes, I know it's in early accses, but it feels like it's not even that.
The world in Rust feels pretty much the same on all servers, despite being randomly generated(like in Minecraft). The radtowns feel meaningless, since you can't build there, all you do is shoot at others who had the same bright idea of farming blueprints. Other than that it's just player built bases, which would be ok if they didn't look all the same(stone on 1 lvl, metal on the others). The areas look pretty bland, the only obvious differences is that some have woods, and one has snow. Now I don't like everything being too obvious, I just want some of them to a bit more diverse not just woods and rocks. Some nuked towns, like in Falllout, would make a great addion. Now whenever I talk to my rust fanboy friend Ocean-Master he says quote :"It'll be added soon". I mean if that's Facepunch's exuse for everything. i'm glad there's no season pass for everything "to be added" at the very least.
The gameplay is oh so very boring. It's just you farm wood and stone with your rock, then with some tools, the you build a base and start raiding other's for greasy loot until someone raids yours. and then you start it all over again. The hitboxes are the one good thing about it as in if someone hits you in the back of the head, a mask won't protect you. There are very few guns, and they feel pretty cluncky, and i think have too much recoil.
Base building is pretty basic: you put a fundation, than walls and start expanding. I didn't really like it, it felt to basic, and I think it could really use some cosmetic features. Then again, those will be added soon.
But the reason I completely hate this game instead just disliking it is the ABSOLUTELY TOXIC comunity. Literaly all players I've come accross just shot me on sight. Well escept for one who me made a slave and one night just blew up our entire base. You cannot, I reapet, cannot interact with these human shaped animals. Whenever they see you, they shoot. So there's no room for building clans with people you dunno without fearing they will stab you in the back the second you go AFK to take a♥♥♥♥♥♥ or when you dissconect. In order not to get raided you need to stay logged in24/7, wich is something I, and many others, cannot do. Whenever I tried buildinga town and collecting fees and taxes from the the peaceful dwellers of Goodtown, someone would just come and shoot me with a shotgun. Just like that.
Those are the reasons I refuse to play Rust anymore. Maybe it'll change. Maybe, maybe , maybe...

I'm going to give my honest opinion on this game:
I really love Day Z- I really enjoyed the Day Z mod in Arma 2 and I really like Day Z standalone. The problem with this game still is stability. The movement, combat, and hit detection mechanics are very choppy and just outright frustrating to deal with. I have been in countless fights with people where we would run around for minutes like crazy trying to hit each other with our melee weapons. Same with the guns- I would be shooting at someone who is running at me with a hatchet and they run in these crazy serpentine movements moving unrealistically fast. I have a very powerful computer and I STILL get frame rate lag in large city areas. I'm tired of trying to keep going into the Day Z files to try an tweak the settings. Hopefully this will be fixed and tweaked very soon to help everyone's performance with the game.
Now for what I really do like about the game:
The entire map in Day Z is outstanding. There are so many places to explore and loot it's not even funny. The realistic feel to the game as well makes it really feel like a true survival game. The survival mechanics are very realistic as well and I think that it really gives the game some difficulty. The concept of the game is also great- it has lots of potential! There's other little things too that make the game enjoyable.
BE PREPARED FOR SOME GLITCHES. BE PREPARED TO WALK A LOT.

When I bought Undertale, I can honestly say that I did not expect this. I had a few extra dollars on my steam wallet and it was on sale, so I thought, "what the heck, Ive seen a few good reviews, might as well." I played it for a bit, the combat interested me, and the humor was mostly spot on for me. (I was dying when I attempted to eat the instant noodles) But I think that most people will agree with me, that the two places Undertale shines brightest is in its music, and in the consequenses of your choices. The first time I played I went with a primarily pacifist route (I killed toriel before I realized she could actually die, so I got nuetral) and everything seemed pretty ok. But then I started a genocide route. Im not yet through it, but after getting to know a lot of these characters, it does feel hard to kill them. After seeing their relationships, it genuinely feels like you are breaking something apart. I know that there are people who wont feel that way, because there are people who wont care for the game, or dont really get invested into games as easily as I do, but if you are a fan of turn based games, bullet hell, or replayability, then this game is 100% for you. If you are still on the fence about it, go listen to some of the soundtrack on youtube, but be very carful to avoid spoilers, as this game is truly the best when playing with an open, yet blank, mind. Dont play with expectaions, just dive in.

I love this game. So many things about this game are great.
Gameplay is a lot of fun. It can be tedious at times to get resources and materials, but overall, ocne you get set up, it's really not an issue anymore.
Making bases is pretty creative and you have to find all sorts of ways to keep your base from being easy to raid. Many bases end up with like every room in a 1x1 area has doors, just to make the raiders waste more resources to get to the good loot.
Raiding other bases is the really fun part though. You spend most of your time surviving and gathering resources so you can survive better, but when you really don't need to worry about survival anymore, you worry about keeping trust bonds and alliances with other groups in your area (Great way to meet new people). If those trust bonds, you feel aren't worthy enough to keep, or you feel like betraying them, you just blow their walls sky high, greet them with an Assault Rifle, and blow them to the ♥♥♥♥ing moon.
Devs are good with keeping the game updated and glitches and bugs are ironed pretty quickly. I've seen better in other games, but Facepunch isn't lacking when it comes to keeping the game good.
Performance isn't much of an issue if you have a mid-range gaming pc. I have a Radeon 270x and can run this game at 30fps on max graphics, so I'm not complaining about the performance.
BEAUTIFUL game btw.
Roadmaps are realistic and can be achieved. They might be behind sometimes, but they catch up very quickly.
All in all, game is amazing and I 100% recommend it.
GG Facepunch.

So I just finished playing this game. Took the true pacifist route.
Now don't be mistaken, I didn't need 17 hours for my first playthrough.
It took me 6-8 hours for a casual playthrough.
The rest of the time was me staring at the True Reset button, wondering if I should do a genocide run.
I'm still hesitant.
DO NOT GET THIS GAME (unless you are going to kill everyone.)

SPOILERS:
I believe that this is probably the most emotional game I have ever played in my life. This game is rivaled only by the moment in Gears of War 3 when Dom sacrificed himself for the team. That is the only moment I have ever cried in a video game, and it took me five years of attachments to those characters to bring me to that state. This game took me 13 hours. By the final moments of the pacifist run, you have been broken down into a mess of both sad and happy feelings for all of the characters you come across, and a love for all people in the games universe. You not only feel good by the end of the game, you feel accomplished, loving, joyful, and sad that your journey has come to an end. You feel like you need more to fill the hole in your heart you have from leaving those characters behind, but you dare not open up the game again. You know that if you do, you will reset all that you have done and wipe away your adventure for good. I feel that I have to do the genocide run, but if I do, I will be completely broken down, and no longer enjoy the game, so I never will. Buy this game now and play it to completion. Do not do the genocide run.

Rust is the best game ever IF the stars align and a few different variables are working together perfectly. Rust is the most frustrating, screen punching, rage quitting game if just a couple of these variables are out of line, so let me tell you what these things are.
- Good Server admins: people who won't cheat, who make sure to ban hackers and greifers, who keep the server up and running and stable. If you don't have this the server can crash, your base gets hack looted, your base gets trolled and you can lose, and i'm not exaggerating, easily over 50 hours of work. Thankfully it's not hard to find good admins and fairly stable servers, and there is an anti cheat system thata as far as I know works.
- Server population density: you want enough people to make the world feel alive and dangerous, but not so many you can't have your own little piece of saftey where you can farm resources unmolested, and monuments where you get vital materials aren't farmed out by big bully clans. This can be difficult and is subjective to whether you enjoy relative crowdedness or not, but ultimately it's a tricky one to get right as servers can die off, or bad admins can up server pop and make the 100 man server which was perfect density into a 150 man cluster ♥♥♥♥.
- You have a competant team: rust is not designed for solo play, period. A lot of raiding tactics, farming etc. is unarguabley better with more than 1 person, even 2 people makes a huge difference. A small clan of 3-5 people is perfect for most medium sized servers, but getting this is harder than it seems. Rust is a big time sink, gather resources takes a huge amount of time, raiding takes a lot of time, and more often than not there will be a few less active members of the clan who aren't pulling there weight and this just leads to tension and arguments. To get a small group of competant players who are fun to be around and pull their weight is extremely difficult to do, but it's core to having fun and not getting rekt in every gun fight.
-free time: you better be able to dedicate your whole existance to this game, because a larger % of the server than you'd think are doing this. Staying up for 2 days straight, cutting trees and raiding bases of those who actually sleep IRL is the essence of Rust. If you work anything more than a part-time job, or are in the middle of exams then you should just not play rust, you'll spend your time building a base and collecting resources only for a 7 man clan of no lifers to come and farm with UTTER EASE from your base. You'll lose everything and probably didn't even have that much fun doing it. In rust, unless your winning, it's not fun, mostly. Farming is a grind, building a base is a grind, but it all makes the victory so much sweeter as the risk/reward ratio is incredible.
now if these stars align! it's not impossible for them to do so, then you will have one of the most immersive, addictive and great experiences of your life. You'll meet great people and experience great memorable moments, if the stars don't align you'll want to kill yourself, throw your PC out the window and eat yourself into a diabetic death. Rust is war and like war it contain's ecstatic highs and heart wrenching lows.
find those 2 weeks of freedom, some friends, a good server, plan a base out and immerse yourself in this incredible game, but be warned, if the recipe isn't complete you'll want to rage quit and cut your own♥♥♥♥♥♥off in utter rage.

Undertale is the story of a man in his early 20's making a game in an engine regarded as a joke by many professionals, with a budget that wouldn't pay for the UI of a AAA game, and making all these "professionals" look like a bunch of amateurs.
Undertale is the best game I have ever played.
A bold statement, sure, but a sentiment that rocked me to the core as I watched the credits roll.
To address everyone's immediate gripe with the game. No, it’s not very long. However, my playthrough took about 12 hours. It really does depend on how you play the game. How many people you talk to. How many endings you wish to see. And so forth.
The gameplay is very fun. Battles are enjoyable, and figuring out the puzzle for sparing a character really never gets old. The overworld puzzles are fairly simple, but never boring.
The real meat of Undertale is the story. I don't think I have ever played game that was more hilarious, more heartbreaking, more heartwarming, or more intense. It not only successfully mimics the writing style of the Earthbound/Mother series (Silly but whith an extremely serious core) it surpases the games it was inspiered by.
Id rate undertale 11/10, but no one would take that seriously, so, 10/10. Undertale is a rare example of a perfect game.

Rust is the best game ever IF the stars align and a few different variables are working together perfectly. Rust is the most frustrating, screen punching, rage quitting game if just a couple of these variables are out of line, so let me tell you what these things are.
- Good Server admins: people who won't cheat, who make sure to ban hackers and greifers, who keep the server up and running and stable. If you don't have this the server can crash, your base gets hack looted, your base gets trolled and you can lose, and i'm not exaggerating, easily over 50 hours of work. Thankfully it's not hard to find good admins and fairly stable servers, and there is an anti cheat system thata as far as I know works.
- Server population density: you want enough people to make the world feel alive and dangerous, but not so many you can't have your own little piece of saftey where you can farm resources unmolested, and monuments where you get vital materials aren't farmed out by big bully clans. This can be difficult and is subjective to whether you enjoy relative crowdedness or not, but ultimately it's a tricky one to get right as servers can die off, or bad admins can up server pop and make the 100 man server which was perfect density into a 150 man cluster ♥♥♥♥.
- You have a competant team: rust is not designed for solo play, period. A lot of raiding tactics, farming etc. is unarguabley better with more than 1 person, even 2 people makes a huge difference. A small clan of 3-5 people is perfect for most medium sized servers, but getting this is harder than it seems. Rust is a big time sink, gather resources takes a huge amount of time, raiding takes a lot of time, and more often than not there will be a few less active members of the clan who aren't pulling there weight and this just leads to tension and arguments. To get a small group of competant players who are fun to be around and pull their weight is extremely difficult to do, but it's core to having fun and not getting rekt in every gun fight.
-free time: you better be able to dedicate your whole existance to this game, because a larger % of the server than you'd think are doing this. Staying up for 2 days straight, cutting trees and raiding bases of those who actually sleep IRL is the essence of Rust. If you work anything more than a part-time job, or are in the middle of exams then you should just not play rust, you'll spend your time building a base and collecting resources only for a 7 man clan of no lifers to come and farm with UTTER EASE from your base. You'll lose everything and probably didn't even have that much fun doing it. In rust, unless your winning, it's not fun, mostly. Farming is a grind, building a base is a grind, but it all makes the victory so much sweeter as the risk/reward ratio is incredible.
now if these stars align! it's not impossible for them to do so, then you will have one of the most immersive, addictive and great experiences of your life. You'll meet great people and experience great memorable moments, if the stars don't align you'll want to kill yourself, throw your PC out the window and eat yourself into a diabetic death. Rust is war and like war it contain's ecstatic highs and heart wrenching lows.
find those 2 weeks of freedom, some friends, a good server, plan a base out and immerse yourself in this incredible game, but be warned, if the recipe isn't complete you'll want to rage quit and cut your own♥♥♥♥♥♥off in utter rage.

Rust, what is it exactly?
Whether it is you surviving through the night, with hope of daylight saving you. Or is it perhaps finding the next victim to kill. One thing is the same, we all want to win. And that's what makes Rust so unique. Everyone who you meet is differnet, whether it is where they are from, how they speak, or even their personality. So you may have one partner who is a chill American, while the next is a stressed out Asain. The thing is, it's always fun no matter what. So just remember to have an open mind when you join that first server, and remember this one thing. Rust never stays.

To be honest, Rust is at the same time both a generic game and a unique one.
Generic because it fits in one of the most popular (as popular in the last 2-3 years, imho) genre of games: both survival, and sandbox.
Unique, because no other game can give you the emotions you get playing Rust.
You know that feeling when you are outside of your house, probably far away, with just a crossbow or even a bow and you see a geared guy coming towards you, while holding his AK like no one can touch him. And you touch him. With an arrow. Straight to his head. You go loot the body and BAM! Jackpot.
That's one of the feelings I get in Rust, probably almost everytime I play it. Because no other game gives you the adrenaline rush Rust gives you.
One moment you have everything. The next moment you may be naked on a beach, with just your dong giving you company, instead of the guns you had before.
I recommend Rust to people that are willing to:
- s/ Drop their social life for a game, and play it non-stop everyday for the rest of your life (even if you will be thinking otherwise, you'll end up being a 24h/24h Rust player. Trust me). /s
- Have a unique experience, that no game can give you.
- Rage a lot because some 12 years old kid will be screaming "get rekt, git gud" while they're raiding your base.
- Have fun in a game that doesn't want you to have fun.
I DON'T recommend Rust to people that don't want to:
- play everyday or every 2 days, for at least some hours a day.
- expect that this game has a toxic community, consisting about 90% of KOSers.
- have a unique experience, that no game can give you (yes. I repeated myself. So what?).
Overall I recommend Rust.

You have to reeeeeeeeeeeeeally love Borderlands to get the most out of this one. Otherwise you just get sick of it relatively quickly like I did. Even still, you may think you love Borderlands a lot after playing the first one, and think you'll really love this one too, and then realize that maybe you don't like it as much as you thought.
Objectively speaking, everything about BL2 is better than the first. It's incredibly polished, loaded with content, easier to play with friends (or strangers), highly replayable (that is, if you reeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeally love Borderlands). So much improvement, but just not as addicting. Exploring is pointless because there's nothing to find, and the only good weapons come from grinding bosses. I just couldn't get hooked like I did on the first one.
Mostly fun while it lasted, but I'm so bored of it all, and it's feeling like a chore just forcing myself to finish the last (and apparently best) DLC. The humor is enjoyable too, I suppose, but it quickly becomes predictable.
All in all, I'm in a strange place with this recommendation. If I could go back in time and tell myself not to get it and that I wouldn't enjoy it as much, past-me wouldn't believe future-me and would still buy this game and it's DLC anyway. I can't say I regret the 107 hours spent playing this game, but I can't say it was time well spent either.
Curiosity satisfied, Borderlands hunger satiated, that's it for me. Thanks Gearbox and 2K, but I won't be getting BL3.

As survival games go, Rust is pretty standard. Open-world exploration, base building, PvP and PvE, with other worldly dangers to worry about. There are some pretty neat features in Rust, however, that make the game stand out from some other entries in the genre.
, I'm going to discuss how difficult Rust can be. Often, and especially on official servers, other people will be geared up, and most people practice a kill-on-sight attitude, regardless of your danger to them. In a game like this, where you spawn with absolutely nothing, getting shot at like that can be painful.
, I'm going to talk about the performance. It's difficult for me to run the game (Core2 Quad, GTX660) on low settings, but my friends (with a 970 and another with 970 SLI) have no trouble and hit 60+ FPS in all areas. It helps to turn down render distances, and turning down settings dependent on location (outdoors, indoors, etc.) can help, as there are multiple levels of quality for different areas of video settings.
will be some gameplay. I think, where Rust differs from other survival games, is a) the interesting character generation, b) the recipe discovery, and c) the atmosphere.
Overall, Rust is a somewhat different experience from other survival games, expecially open-world ones. It's not particularly expensive, and it has a great developer working on it. There are updates almost every week, including updates inspired by community wants and needs. The game's unique atmosphere, endless playability, and this great community-developer connection make it a great buy.

First, let me start by stating: I know more than you do about DayZ.  This is going to be a long review, but I feel that it is warranted for people to have a more complete picture of what DayZ aspires to be, and what it is as of the time of this review, circa November 2015. Way back in the day, when DayZ was just a fledgling Arma II mod, the game was the first of its kind: a huge real world zombie simulator. There were ultimately hacker problems that lead to the idea of a standalone game. That game is what we know today as DayZ standalone. Although initially promising, and through a huge word of mouth campaign, DayZ became hugely popular among casual gamers and serious survival mod experts alike. At the height of DayZ's success (probably in mid 2014) it was not uncommon to see well over 30,000+ players online at once, exploring and hacking their way through the huge zombie wasteland. Although the developers were very clear that this is "just an alpha" and that we - the paying players - were in no way entitled to give critical feedback, most people could deal with and accept the problems. This is where this review takes a turn. Somewhere in late 2014 into early 2015, the dev team started focusing on hipster items such as NEW HATS and SHOES, and neglected the fundamental gameplay problems, such as Zombies which walk through fences and walls as if the barriers were invisible. There were so many weapons that RAMBO would have no chance to kill a player, even a n00b or bamby could arm up to the teeth with m4’s and unlimited ammo in less than 1 hour. To add insult to injury, it was clear that the community cared deeply about the fate of DayZ, and were voicing their displeasure with the direction and focus of development. It was clear that the players wanted one thing - functioning game mechanics such as Zombies that were bound by the same rules as the players (ie: no walking through walls), and some way to control the hackers... Yes the hackers were back, even though the whole point of the standalone was to circumvent the hackers ability to own the entire map at one time (this, later became known as the BUBBLE - DayZ only rendered a small area for each player, making it seemingly unhackable on a large scale - hackers wouldn't know where you were if you were far enough away from them). Fast forward to the end of 2015, DayZ is a largely broken game. There are NO ZOMBIES - yes you read that correctly. Read it again – NO ZOMBIES. The Developers took the zombies out, why? Nobody knows, (well that’s not entirely true but it is beyond the scope of this review) because if you voice your opinion of DayZ and are in ANY WAY CRITICAL of their mod, I mean, standalone game - that you paid for - they BAN you from the community. This in a nutshell is the problem with DayZ, and why it will suffer the same fate as Duke NuKem FOREVER. The community of DayZ has become cannibalistic - they are in a death spiral of criticism and expectations – both of which they cannot satisfy. DayZ was nice for a while. There are more details to be had – I challenge you to read the community forums for yourself. The updates are increasingly fewer and farer in between. The update news is more of the same broken promises. DayZ mod for Arma III is where you should be focusing your attention. The DayZ standalone will never be a success. It is the very definition of people who do no learn from the past (DUKE NUKEM FOREVER) and I feel bad for those that spend hundreds of hours of their time, like me, wasting away in a fundamentally flawed engine, and mod, I mean, standalone game  that is constantly hacked. The vehicles turn and handle like AIRCRAFT CARRIERS, the zombies, if you can find any, are painfully stupid and predictable, the players are so fed up with the server wipes and destruction of their game that they WILL KILL YOU ON SIGHT only to make you suffer more for purchasing this game. You fool. You were warned.

I originally didn't like the game when I got it over Christmas. However, as the months went by, I found myself interested in the game again, and so decided to give it another go. I've completely changed my opinion since.
Undertale is a smart game that isn't afraid to take a jackhammer to the fourth wall, and the sharp, witty writing and plot twists just kept coming. One of the best RPG stories I've played to date.
Mechanically, Undertale presents a unique option in RPGs where you can choose to talk to enemies, persuading them to not fight you. Some of these options result in hilarious outcomes that are so well crafted.
Special mention to the amazing soundtrack, with tons of memorable tracks that to this day, I still find myself absent-mindedly humming occasionally.
To say what makes Undertale truly special would spoil the plot, and that's doing it a disservice. Highly recommended.

You have to reeeeeeeeeeeeeally love Borderlands to get the most out of this one. Otherwise you just get sick of it relatively quickly like I did. Even still, you may think you love Borderlands a lot after playing the first one, and think you'll really love this one too, and then realize that maybe you don't like it as much as you thought.
Objectively speaking, everything about BL2 is better than the first. It's incredibly polished, loaded with content, easier to play with friends (or strangers), highly replayable (that is, if you reeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeally love Borderlands). So much improvement, but just not as addicting. Exploring is pointless because there's nothing to find, and the only good weapons come from grinding bosses. I just couldn't get hooked like I did on the first one.
Mostly fun while it lasted, but I'm so bored of it all, and it's feeling like a chore just forcing myself to finish the last (and apparently best) DLC. The humor is enjoyable too, I suppose, but it quickly becomes predictable.
All in all, I'm in a strange place with this recommendation. If I could go back in time and tell myself not to get it and that I wouldn't enjoy it as much, past-me wouldn't believe future-me and would still buy this game and it's DLC anyway. I can't say I regret the 107 hours spent playing this game, but I can't say it was time well spent either.
Curiosity satisfied, Borderlands hunger satiated, that's it for me. Thanks Gearbox and 2K, but I won't be getting BL3.

Rust
Set in a post nuclear apocalpyse, where the world is brutal and the people that inhabit it are even more so. You forage, mine, chop and kill to survive. Build bases to keep your booty safe and hope someone doesn't come along to take it and your pants.
What Rust lacks in story, it makes up for with the interactions of its other inhabitants. One minute you could be taking a nice stroll along the road, next minute a naked person will try to smack you in the head with a rock. What do you do? Kill them? Make peace? Run away? That choice is up to you. Your adventures would also entail building a base, that is, if you want to keep all the stuff you find. Which may end up stolen in the future, if you aren't vigilant.
I find Rust to be a great game, no matter how much people say that the community is bad. In my experiences so far, I've met people who will help you and those that will destroy you. The game is all about your interactions with players, without them, it's just not as enjoyable.
My personal rating for Rust is a 10/10, because it can be so damn great, no matter how much you rage.

I bought this Game in Oct. 2015 and I was shocked to find that the .58 servers were completly unplayable... There was barley any loot, you could barley survive unless you found an apple tree/water pump and even then after eating/drinking for what seemed to be forever I coninued to recieve messages that said "you are hungry/thirsty" etc... Luckily because of the lack of loot most players were friendly due to the fact that they wouldn't have a weapon/ammo to kill you... But the thing that shocked me the most was that there were NO ZOMBIES!!! After learning this I was heavily contenplating contacting steam because the fact that DayZ had no Zeds made no sense and made me feel as though the Dev team was false advertising a "Zombie survival game"... I chose to wait it out and luckily in late October 2015 the servers began to spawn much more loot and fixed the hunger/thirst system... as of now the 0.58 stable branches are playable aside from some major glitches... and the 0.59 experimental servers have been released that brought back ZOMBIES!!!(and new cars) In November there have been a few updates to the experimental/stable servers including one that was just released today as I write this (50MB)... Aside from all the major progress made within the last couple months, there have been a few major glitches that seriously need to be adressed like the lack of cars/trucks that work(Every car/truck Ive found would not work even with all the parts needed) and the major issues with the inventory screen where items when combined/attatched to other objects will semi-permanatly stay in your inventory until you log off and log back in, and many times when I drop Items on the groud the object will teleport to somewhere nearby or dissapear completly, not to mention the sub-par fps you will get in big cities especially with zombies... So in conclusion DayZ is a serious work in progress and depending on how patient you are and how interested you are in the developmental process will determine whether or not this game is for you.... Personally Ive been involved with this game ever since the first mod came out on Arma 2 and Im amazed how many people have copied this game structure... Unfortunatly for them a rehash is just not as good as the original and there truly will only be one DayZ...

Set in a post nuclear apocalpyse, where the world is brutal and the people that inhabit it are even more so. You forage, mine, chop and kill to survive. Build bases to keep your booty safe and hope someone doesn't come along to take it and your pants.
What Rust lacks in story, it makes up for with the interactions of its other inhabitants. One minute you could be taking a nice stroll along the road, next minute a naked person will try to smack you in the head with a rock. What do you do? Kill them? Make peace? Run away? That choice is up to you. Your adventures would also entail building a base, that is, if you want to keep all the stuff you find. Which may end up stolen in the future, if you aren't vigilant.
I find Rust to be a great game, no matter how much people say that the community is bad. In my experiences so far, I've met people who will help you and those that will destroy you. The game is all about your interactions with players, without them, it's just not as enjoyable.
My personal rating for Rust is a 10/10, because it can be so damn great, no matter how much you rage.

Although Undertale is a game that warrants a detailed explanation, saying too much about it would ruin the whole point of the game, so I won't be going into much detail about the game's contents.
When Undertale first released, the internet was quickly hooked. Everyone was talking about it, and I made the mistake of dismissing it as just another pretentious indie game that had more attention than it deserved. I recently decided to give it a go, and my feelings towards it progressed in three stages. First, I was intrigued by the retro feel the game had, and how strange it was. Then, as I progressed through the game I found myself really enjoying the humour and the excellent music. Finally, by the 'end' of my playthrough I was utterly obsessed and emotionally invested. Undertale for me has been an experience that no other video game has come close to giving me.
Undertale's soundtrack has been rightly praised by many, and is certainly the best soundtrack of 2015 in my opinion; and probably the among the best ever. Whether it is the theme to an area you are exploring, or a character you have encountered, you will probably have it stuck in your head for days.
Toby Fox - the mastermind behind Undertale - has managed to create a fascinating world, full of wonderful characters and a story that slowly creeps up on you. The way in which you interact with this world (and indeed the way it interacts with you) is extremely clever too.
I would advise you to put any preconceptions you might have about this game aside and try it, as I really believe that Undertale is an experience that every gamer should have.
