Undertale both ruined, and invigorated my life. Let me ♥♥♥♥♥♥ tell you why,
I Have played over 40+ hours of this game, trying to find every hidden easter egg and alternative ending. There's the True Pacifist ending, MULTIPLE nuetral endings, and a Genocide Run. Let me explain to you why its nearly imPOSSIBLE to succesfully complete a genocided run; killing everything in your path.
Undertale has one of the most jam packed, richest story lines i've ever seen in a game, in my enire life. I'm getting my BA in fiction writing, and I'm honestly mad at myself that I didn't write this beautiful game. The characters are gorgeous, and each and every single one of them has likes and fears, hopes and hair triggers. You will fall in love with them, as well as many other aspects.
The soundtrack is one of the most beautiful ones i've ever heard; songs like Quiet Water, Memory (In Game Version) Home, and just Undertale itself make beautiful songs to meditate to, or fall asleep to. Megalovania and Bonetrousal are two absolutely wonderful songs that fit their characters so flawlessly. I could go on for days about just the soundtrack alone, but I will continue.
The multiple endings never seem to cease; you have options to MERCY, ACT, or ATTACK and every time you do, the outcome of the entire game will change.
Basically, all in all, you need to play this game. I have NEVER come across a video game, book, movie, short story, song, or anything that i founf no flaws in,
This is it though, this is a flawless game.

I'll be perfectly honest... I don't get this game. I really like shooters, RPG's, and games with great stories and interesting NPCs, but I don't like this game! Borderlands 2 managed to capture my attention for quite awhile until I realized at one point that I wasn't having fun anymore. Why? THE WEAPON GRIND! I am a child of the SNES era playing Japanese-made RPGs that require hours of grinding before you can enter the next town/dungeon, but this game had a kind of grinding that is much more annoying. You spend literally half of this game checking weapon stats! Every enemy you kill drops a shield/gun/item and the game wants you to pick it up an check it against all of the items you currently have. one time, after I had finished playing for about two hours, I realized that I had spent 1:15 just checking weapon stats, collecting weapons/items after a fight, and selling weapons! After that, I decided no more checking weapon stats or collecting weapons unless I was specifically grinding for weapons. Guess what? I started to die a lot more! The game is designed so every stupid weapon you collect is 1-2 points better AND worse than the weapon you have in SOME way (there are like 6 stats to consider per weapon). So after replacing your weapons like 25 times, you have a weapon that is much more powerful than the first one, but in finding those 25 weapons you have spent a cumulative of 4 hours of playtime just looking at a stat screen. No Thank You!

TL;DR
Pros:
- Great soundtrack
- Unique game mechanics
- Nostalgic
- Non-linear experience
- Unique characters
Cons:
- Outdated graphics
- Limited character itemization
- Shallow storyline
- Replayability
Like most people, if you ever came across this page for the first time, you would never think to try out this game because of graphical limitations. However, if you are look past the graphics, most people who played this game will tell you that this game is a unique experience.
Unlike most RPGs, Undertale does not focus on grinding from level 1 to 25 to eventually beat a dungeon boss. The creators of Undertale wants the player to feel immersed around the environment and characters in the game. Every character you meet in the game is likable in their own way, even the bad guys. Additionally, each character has their own theme song, and makes you feel "OH SHI-", or in wrestling terms "mark out" to a degree. Even with all the positives with the characters in Undertale, these characters do not add much depth to the story. However, these do not retract to what makes Undertale special.
For each enemy interaction in Undertale, you have the choice to either kill or not kill each enemy. Although, killing does not penalize you, it makes a difference in where the story ends. Not killing every enemy is rewarding at the end.
If you are turned off in how Undertale looks, do not let that deter you from playing this one of a kind game.

The other DLC, Pirates and Torque are also very good. Mister Torque is one of my favorite new characters (after Tiny Tina of course). EXPLOSIONS!!!
All in all, I recommend this game hands down one of my all time favorite games. Hopefully, you will find it enjoyable as well.

I'll sum this game up in one ironic quote. Ready? 100% ready? Ok:
"870 gazillion weapons... 27 inventory slots."
The Borderlands franchise. The one series of games that Gearbox did correctly.
if you've played the original Borderlands, then you would know that it is all about the guns. Nothing else matters. Borderlands 2 picks up on this train of thought perfectly as it is the only thing that really shines in this game. Collecting guns of all sorts is amazing in this game! However. The game does not come without its faults. As stated before, its all about guns. Nothing else matters. That statement is very true indeed. There is nothing more the game has to offer. Sure, the game has some nice lore (Especially the backround of Zer0, and why Handsome Jack is the way that he is under his mask. I wont spoil anymore.). But for the most part its just lackluster story, toilet humor and some just-above-OK DLC packs.
Final Verdict. If you enjoy the looting elements of RPGs mixed with an FPS gameplay style, and you can tolerate toilet humor and a pretty bad story (With some nice lore), then pick up the Game of the Year version of Borderlands 2, as some of the DLC is good and some of it is bad (But all in all its good to have a bit of end game content to play around with ;D!)

TL;DR
Pros:
- Great soundtrack
- Unique game mechanics
- Nostalgic
- Non-linear experience
- Unique characters
Cons:
- Outdated graphics
- Limited character itemization
- Shallow storyline
- Replayability
Like most people, if you ever came across this page for the first time, you would never think to try out this game because of graphical limitations. However, if you are look past the graphics, most people who played this game will tell you that this game is a unique experience.
Unlike most RPGs, Undertale does not focus on grinding from level 1 to 25 to eventually beat a dungeon boss. The creators of Undertale wants the player to feel immersed around the environment and characters in the game. Every character you meet in the game is likable in their own way, even the bad guys. Additionally, each character has their own theme song, and makes you feel "OH SHI-", or in wrestling terms "mark out" to a degree. Even with all the positives with the characters in Undertale, these characters do not add much depth to the story. However, these do not retract to what makes Undertale special.
For each enemy interaction in Undertale, you have the choice to either kill or not kill each enemy. Although, killing does not penalize you, it makes a difference in where the story ends. Not killing every enemy is rewarding at the end.
If you are turned off in how Undertale looks, do not let that deter you from playing this one of a kind game.

After that, I decided no more checking weapon stats or collecting weapons unless I was specifically grinding for weapons. Guess what? I started to die a lot more! After 530+ hours of playing this survival game, I cannot help but recommend it to CERTAIN PLAYERS.
Now first off, let us talk about what players I am speaking to. Rust is a very demanding game. What I mean by this, is that you will spend ungodly amounts of time in the game. Only certain players who have a good amount of time to spend (Hence why there are a lot of younger players) can truly flourish. This does not mean people with less time to spend will fail, it just may be more difficult for them to truly enjoy the game.
Secondly, you cannot get mad at people who steal your items. Most of the time people play on official servers, which are loaded with 200+ people. Community servers have a much lower amount of people, ranging from 10-70 usually. By playing on these smaller servers, you essentially make the game more "fun". You can relax a bit, knowing you won't get shot every 5 minutes. This ties into to the stealing items: people kill you because they don't want to work to get the items, and you would most likely kill a player to get items in Rust as well, don't try to deny it. Hell, it happens in society today. Think of a bank robbery.
Lastly, you must make friends in a server and survive together. Rust is more of a social survival game but this is a tricky must, because not everyone is honest. I recommend playing with IRL friends when you build a base together, but try to make allies by trading with people, talking with them, or even giving small gifts to them. Just don't be annoying. I've made over 40+ friends on my list from rust, and still talk with a good 15+ with them.
Overall, it is an amazing game. I truly recommend it. But please, prepare yourself when you play it. You will get killed. You will lose items. You will find toxic people.
Such is life in Rust.

DayZ is a good game. It's one of those dream games that people come up with in their salad days of development and wanna keep putting more and more into. It's exactly like that, because those games always end up unfinished. That said...
-The entire game has been ported to a new engine, the Enfusion engine, and is leaps and bounds more optimized than when it first came out
-They updated APIs from DirectX 9 to DirectX 11. That's the difference between Windows XP era API and Windows 7 era API. This, along with the enfusion engine, has made the game playable on any reasonable gaming computer at high settings. Anyone can get a playable framerate in DayZ.
-The sound technology has been updated to that of ArmA 3's Eden, making supersonic bullet cracks attenuate and directionalize properly, bouncing off hills and sounding appropriately different at distance. Compare with games like Squad.
-Dynamic lighting and weather have been on the table for a long time, and are finally working properly. Ask anyone with 100+ hours and they will be hard pressed to find a more beautifully wild game than DayZ. It looks incredible. Check out the screenshot gallery if you don't believe me.
The game is going into beta soon, with an entirely new player movement animation system. By the end of 2017 this patch will release; it is already developed. You can see for yourself on youtube. If nothing else, I would have to recommend that all those previously disappointed, or all those seeing the massive wall of circlejerked hate that has surrounded this game since Dean 'Peace Out B!tches' Hall bailed on its development, wait until the Beta patch releases to buy it.

I'll sum this game up in one ironic quote. Ready? 100% ready? Ok:
"870 gazillion weapons... 27 inventory slots."
The Borderlands franchise. The one series of games that Gearbox did correctly.
if you've played the original Borderlands, then you would know that it is all about the guns. Nothing else matters. Borderlands 2 picks up on this train of thought perfectly as it is the only thing that really shines in this game. Collecting guns of all sorts is amazing in this game! Its by far the best part of the game! Trust me on that, ive got 120+ hours invested into BL2!
However. The game does not come without its faults. As stated before, its all about guns. Nothing else matters. That statement is very true indeed. There is nothing more the game has to offer. Sure, the game has some nice lore (Especially the backround of Zer0, and why Handsome Jack is the way that he is under his mask. I wont spoil anymore.). But for the most part its just lackluster story, toilet humor and some just-above-OK DLC packs.
Final Verdict. If you enjoy the looting elements of RPGs mixed with an FPS gameplay style, and you can tolerate toilet humor and a pretty bad story (With some nice lore), then pick up the Game of the Year version of Borderlands 2, as some of the DLC is good and some of it is bad (But all in all its good to have a bit of end game content to play around with ;D!)
Cheers!

After 530+ hours of playing this survival game, I cannot help but recommend it to CERTAIN PLAYERS.
Now first off, let us talk about what players I am speaking to. Rust is a very demanding game. What I mean by this, is that you will spend ungodly amounts of time in the game. Only certain players who have a good amount of time to spend (Hence why there are a lot of younger players) can truly flourish. This does not mean people with less time to spend will fail, it just may be more difficult for them to truly enjoy the game.
Secondly, you cannot get mad at people who steal your items. Most of the time people play on official servers, which are loaded with 200+ people. Community servers have a much lower amount of people, ranging from 10-70 usually. By playing on these smaller servers, you essentially make the game more "fun". You can relax a bit, knowing you won't get shot every 5 minutes. This ties into to the stealing items: people kill you because they don't want to work to get the items, and you would most likely kill a player to get items in Rust as well, don't try to deny it. Hell, it happens in society today. Think of a bank robbery.
Lastly, you must make friends in a server and survive together. Rust is more of a social survival game but this is a tricky must, because not everyone is honest. I recommend playing with IRL friends when you build a base together, but try to make allies by trading with people, talking with them, or even giving small gifts to them. Just don't be annoying. I've made over 40+ friends on my list from rust, and still talk with a good 15+ with them.
Overall, it is an amazing game. I truly recommend it. But please, prepare yourself when you play it. You will get killed. You will lose items. You will find toxic people.
Such is life in Rust.

Update: Just thought I would add something from the Wiki:
The first publicly available development build was released on December 16, 2013 during the alpha development stage through Steam's Early Access program at a cheaper price than when it is finally released. The price will increase as development continues until reaching the full release price. This alpha release is an early access build with a large amount of the features still in progress and the development team is targeting the release at an audience who want to be involved in what Hall called a "very barebones experience that is a platform for future development."
Release:
In November 2014, it was announced that the final release version of the game would be released in 2016.
In November 2017, the game was still in alpha development stage.
On November 28th 2017, a status report was released which disclosed that Dayz would not be coming out of alpha until 2018.
Reception:
The alpha release sold over 172,500 copies in the first 24 hours, totalling over US $5 million in sales. During peak sales, over 200 copies were being purchased per minute and after one week over 400,000 copies had been sold. The game reached a total of more than 1 million sales while remaining at the top of Steam's sales charts for two weeks in a row during their Winter sale despite it not being reduced in price. In an alpha review of DayZ, Rick Lane of Eurogamer commented positively on the new additions but said that the game may not be worth the current price until more features have been added. On the other hand, Craig Pearson of PC Gamer said that he had good experiences in DayZ and that it was already worth the price.

The first publicly available development build was released on December 16, 2013 during the alpha development stage through Steam's Early Access program at a cheaper price than when it is finally released. Characters are well written as is the humor (even if it is a bit purile), however the story is in general makes little sense in the context of the world and gets quite annoying in aditional playthroughs. Initial playthroughs are really fun especially with friends.
True vault hunter mode (second playthrough mode) either require friends or extremely good luck with weapon drops to maintain a decent pace. In this mode grey and green items are useless when you reach ultimate vault hunter mode and you need to start being very selective with purple weapons. Late game balance is almost non existant with only 1 or 2 builds of each character being viable, also the dlc characters have the worst balance and while they feel a bit op early and mid game they are fairly useless late game (though this depends on your playstyle and how flexible your willing to be with it, personally I don't think an RPG should be pushing you down a specific build).
Money is useless as the items in the shop are the worst you will find in the game unless your in the first hour or so, so you'll only use it to buy ammo or gamble, you lose a bit when you die but since there is nothing to spend it on who cares. Erridium, the games other currency is fairly useful early on and if you get the story DLC's (which I recomend as they are fairly well written and have less plotholes then the main story) they are used in endgame. Though I've complained alot it is a fun game and combat is generally satisfying but undeniably flawed.

After 530+ hours of playing this survival game, I cannot help but recommend it to CERTAIN PLAYERS.
Now first off, let us talk about what players I am speaking to. Rust is a very demanding game. What I mean by this, is that you will spend ungodly amounts of time in the game. Only certain players who have a good amount of time to spend (Hence why there are a lot of younger players) can truly flourish. This does not mean people with less time to spend will fail, it just may be more difficult for them to truly enjoy the game.
Secondly, you cannot get mad at people who steal your items. Most of the time people play on official servers, which are loaded with 200+ people. Community servers have a much lower amount of people, ranging from 10-70 usually. By playing on these smaller servers, you essentially make the game more "fun". You can relax a bit, knowing you won't get shot every 5 minutes. This ties into to the stealing items: people kill you because they don't want to work to get the items, and you would most likely kill a player to get items in Rust as well, don't try to deny it. Hell, it happens in society today. Think of a bank robbery.
Lastly, you must make friends in a server and survive together. Rust is more of a social survival game but this is a tricky must, because not everyone is honest. I recommend playing with IRL friends when you build a base together, but try to make allies by trading with people, talking with them, or even giving small gifts to them. Just don't be annoying. I've made over 40+ friends on my list from rust, and still talk with a good 15+ with them.
Overall, it is an amazing game. I truly recommend it. But please, prepare yourself when you play it. You will get killed. You will lose items. You will find toxic people.
Such is life in Rust.

Undertale is the best game currently in existence, but sadly, I am stuck with mixed feelings for the game where nobody has to die.
While Undertale seems to advocate peace and love, Toby Fox (the creator of Undertale) seems to not be serious about his themes. Much of what happens in the later parts of the game almost seem to outright reject all of the positive messages in the game. The only theme in this game that really works is DETERMINATION. This game is very successful at making you feel more determined although it makes you question why you should even be determined at all.
This game has more than enough hours of gameplay - you just have to want to play it in its entirety.
I have played the Mother series - Undertale's main influence - and Undertale manages to perfect and emphazise everything great within those games. This is easily twice as good as Mother 3, which actually seems to share the most resemblances with Undertale. (Mother 3's problem is that it pretended to be deep, but used only sadness to win over players.) Undertale still beats Earthbound, an RPG that I thought would never be surpassed, by a healthy margin.
Everything is emotional in Undertale and it sets a new standard for how games are produced. This game is full of MEMORIES. That is what every game should strive to be. But in addition to that, the entire game also manages to be incredibly human and emotional throughout. The fact that DATING was used as a minor element in the story is actually groundbreaking. However, if you lack an understanding of subtlety, you can mistake this game for simply being filled with jokes (somehow).
Another really noteworthy thing about the game is the programming itself. The manipulation of save files, closing the game and even renaming of the window's title happen while the game is playing. Even if it seems like your game has ended, more happens when you load the game, without the time stamp or location being changed. It makes me wonder how it could be done.
The combat system seems very risky, but it was done so well that I would probably prefer that every RPG mimicked Undertale's system. The battle sprites are huge and everything is amazingly well animated - making the characters and enemies feel very lovable, not to mention the incredible character art design itself. Every battle is absolutely filled with emotionally-charged tension and the regular enemies in the game are thankfully not too difficult to fight. The regular game is designed to be played at level 1, which does a lot to prevent immersion from being broken.
Even better, boss fights are surprisingly difficult, but as long as you stay determined and keep trying, everything just clicks.This is exactly what the game tells you to do and that itself is an unimaginable achievement.
It also helps that most people will be going through the same amount of difficulty considering that almost no one plays "bullet hell" games. (This game is a lot better than a bullet hell game because you are not just shooting a stream of fire for ten minutes while moving around. The gameplay quality and variety comparison makes the rest of the whole genre appear misguided.)
The graphics are definitely a step above other retro titles, even going so far as having mixed media art that works very effectively. Even the music is mixed media - some of it synth orchestrated and other songs 8-bit and 32-bit. Just about all of the music is the best of the best, which was another surprise. I am a huge, HUGE video game music fan and I have rarely heard any songs as good as this. It would be easy to argue that this is the best video game soundtrack ever.
"Bonetrousle", "Heartache", "Death By Glamour" and "Another Medium" are my favorite songs right now, but basically every song is equally supreme quality.
There are two HUGE problems, however......
The theme of the game about hope and pacifism is done perfectly minus one small, very key thing - there is no theme of NEW LIFE. New life would be making the world more fertile, gaining faith in something mystical, giving birth to new ideas, etc. The only thing we get by the end of Undertale is NEW LOVE. New love is used extremely effectively to show that non-violence is magic when combined with determination. However, love is only a bond - without anything long-term to use that bond for, it seems rather pointless. MATERIALISM is also a bit over-emphasized (this is copying the traditions of the Mother series) and this only furthers the player's lack of ability to understand what good works can ultimately be used for because the NATURAL WORLD is used almost entirely as a symbol throughout the game. The only exception that promotes green living is the vegetable enemy at the beginning of the game, but it is totally possible to miss that enemy in the first place and they are also one of the least sympathetic enemies. Therefore, the true ending of the game that makes everything happy just feels generic in spite of the cleverness, knowledge and originality laced through the rest of the game.
The second big problem greatly amplifies the need for the first problem to be resolved. This game introduces NIHILISM to a high extent. The ultimate bad ending, which you are only supposed to know to pursue after you beat the game, not only makes the overall game feel more horrific than anything, it breaks the balance of positivity by making strong, but subtle arguments to the idea of NIHILISM and people turning to acts of killing and destruction. To make things worse, the two wisest characters in the game are used to express this idea and it feels far more tangible than the peace in the best ending.
After exploring the game rather deeply, I found a secret conversation with another important character who basically tries to tell the player to embrace fighting physically (maybe even killing) as a necessary part of life. Maybe if this was given the pretext of talking about animals, that would make sense (although it would ironically get a lot more negative press), but this game basically shows us how you can use all of your effort to make a real difference without actually hurting anyone. The game tells us to be determined to change fate. Why the heck would one of the very last messages of the game be to deny that idea entirely?!
Thus, Undertale has ultimately betrayed its themes of positivity and a love of peace primarily for those who are not satisfied by the true ending's seemingly intentional weakness. Although these themes of darkness complete the game as a world inside of itself (not to mention the huge amount of alternative endings and choices that actually make a difference), there is no counterbalance of ideas to keep faith in to reject Nihilism and the meaninglessness of peace and existence as a whole. The flaws of this game make its major themes trivial in its last moments while Toby Fox's challenge to intentionally promote evil becomes stronger. This is a big shame and unfortunately something that a patch of the game is just unlikely to ever fix.
Because of this deep, but hopefully unintentional betrayal of its philosophy, this game is almost a promotion of evil more than good.

Final Verdict- 8.5/10
Borderlands 2 is still a hillbilly moonshiner sort of game, then, but it's the hillbilly at his canny, tinkering, big-dreaming best. It's the hillbilly at the peak of his powers. It's the hillbilly made majestic.
That's the spirit that made the first Borderlands great, too, of course, and that really came to the fore during the original game's add-on instalments. Dr Ned, General Knoxx, Claptrap's ramshackle uprising - these are the things that Borderlands 2 builds on the most, taking cues from the tighter campaigns, sharper jokes and more poignant, oddball asides. Questing, levelling, shooting, even driving: almost everything important has been improved while each little detail has been refined
t's a surprisingly good narrative, but it's not the real story at all. The real story is different for everyone, and for me it was about a man who was constantly waddling into battle slightly under-levelled and who really wanted to get his hands on a corrosive shotgun. The man was me, and the story had a happy ending. I finally hit the right level for the run-up to the end-game boss, and I finally found that shotgun I was after, too. Then I killed an awful lot of people with the corrosive bullets it contained.
There are plenty of improvements, then, but the most satisfying thing to note is that Borderlands has lost none of its untidy charm in the transition from unlikely hit to megabucks tent-pole. The storyline runs a touch deeper now, but it's largely resisted the lunge towards the blandly epic - and while the art sparkles, it's ducked the big-team slickness that can rub away at a game's personality.

Ive held off writing this review, during my time playing it, ive had ups and downs with it, some good updates, but mostly bad
In its current stable release, 0.58, there isnt much of a game.
Its the chernarus+ map, some bits of loot and a few thousand players online spread over many, mostly empty, servers.
There are no zombies, so no point to PVE
The animal AI has been removed so no hunting or various crafting options
The vehicles are bugged, some flip easily, passengers are desync'd beyond belief
the loot economy, while a slight improvement over previous releases, still seems unbalanced, coastal(spawn) areas dont respawn loot on a quicker timer than anywhere else on map, meaning it can be impossibly hard for fresh spawns.
There is a 'map swimming' glitch, cheaters paradise
The desync during PVP encounters makes PVP pointless, for example, on numerous occasions, shooting prone or standing people with no effect, only to see them get up or run off uninjured.
Awful clunky movements, delayed actions, random actions, horrible FPS in any populated or built up areas (10-20fps)
visuals, as you would expect from older engine/renderer, are starting to look dated when compared to say, FO4, they are in the process of building a new one from the ground up and implementing it
There is zero optimisation for this game. ZERO. DO NOT TAKE THE RECOMMENED/MINIMUM SPEC REQUIREMENTS AS GUIDLINES. The game only uses 1 CPU core, no multi threading, and doesnt matter if your using a titan gfx card or a toilet gfx card, there is very little adjustment to be made. There are 'fps guides' to try boost your fps, but you are not going to see anything pretty
For me tho, and for many others, the worst, and probably most discussed issue about this game, is the development progress.
This game is moving so slow.
The developers roadmap hasnt met a single point its set.
Status reports are vague, trying to be all pally pally, and avoiding any hard details on issues encountered and why deadlines not met.
Every PAX event see's a new 'road map', the latest being, that the game will be in beta in jan/feb/march 2016.
I'll eat my pants on you tube if that happens.

All in all, this game is awful.
wait until start of 2016, when beta isnt released, and you'll thank me, for saving you from what the rest of us suckers have had to endure

Made a review for this game around 4 years ago and was not of high quality so let me re-do it:
Campaign:
The core campaign features 4 characters (will get on to them soon). These characters are different from the orignal Borderlands, however they do make appearances.
The story follows the vault hunters on their journey to ultimately kill the games main antagonist, Handsome Jack.
This story spans over many large zones which will have many unique enemies in them and all areas have a very unique feel to them. The overall map is very large, so the quick travel feature is useful to navigate the map.
The campaign is rather long and can be played either, solo or co-op. There are 3 modes for the campaign each of which you will have to replay the missions, these modes are: Normal, True Vault Hunter and Ultimate Vault Hunter. Playing each mode will scale the enemies levels higher and allow you to obtain higher level gear. (For exampe the level cap is 72 and Normal mode caps at level 50 enemies and gear, which will not do any damage to level 72 enemies).
The characters you encounter throughout the story are unique and the dialog throughout the game is entertaining, which is one of the reasons I first came back and played this game over and over, accumalating over 800+ hours across PC, PS3, Xbox 360 and PS4.
Overall I would give the campaign an 9/10, as some missions can get repetitive, but it is still a very intriguing storyline.
Characters:
All 4 core characters and the 2 DLC characters all have their own unique skill which will allow different types of players an advantage during gameplay. The characters all have their own unique skill tree which can be upgraded to enhance their skill in different ways.
The different characters will suit different play types. I will give a brief breakdown of each character:
Axton (Commander): Weilds a deployable turrect that can be thrown down and upgraded to: stick to walls, rockets ect. This turret will shoot at enemies and distract them aswell.
Salvador (Gun Zerker): Salvador can duel weild (Gunzerk) 2 weapons at once and have increased firepower. Skill tree upgrades include: Chance to not use ammo, increased health ect. This is a tank type character.
Maya (Siren): Maya is one of the few sirens on Pandora (along with Lilith from the orignal Borderlands series), and has the ability to, 'phaselock', enemies which traps them and has them floating above the ground for an amount of time and players can attack the enemy without it attacking them. Skill tree upgrades include: Phaselock to revive players. Maya can be used as a sort of medic type character.
Zero (Assassin): Zero is an unknown character and his ability is that he can become invisible and not be shot at while invisbile of course. This will be a limited amount of time and shooting will remove him from his invisibile state. His skill tree can be upgraded to enhance stealth gameplay, such as extra sniper damage and Bore, which allows penertrating bullets to deal increaed damage. (This can be very overpowered if used correctly and one shot max level bosses with level 1 weapons)
Those are the 4 core characters.
Gaige (Mecromancer): Gaige can delpoy a robot that will float around near her and attack enemies. She can stack anarachy by killing enemies and this will be lost when reloading prematurely (Finishing the magazine and forecfully reloading will not lose this). Anarchy will increase damage but decrease accuracy.
Kreig (Psycho): Can weild a buzz axe which is an melee weapon and can be thrown. The buzz axe will do increased damage. (I have not played as Kreig too much upon achieving max level with him dont know to much about him.)
The characters are all very unique and allow a different play style each time and I can fault them.
I would rate the character selection 10/10 as they allow alot of replayability.
I wont go to in-depth about DLC, but there are 4 DLC packs all with their own storylines and introduce new areas and character and weapons and give a better understanding into why people have ended up in pandora and background on characters. These DLC packs are quite long and all introduce raid bosses to farm for loot.
There are also 5 headhunter packs all which have a single mission, which is quite long and introduce a new area and a boss to fight.
The weapon selection is very vast and there are different catergories in which weapons are ranked which are: White, Green, Blue, Purple and Orange, which are increasingly better in that order.
Pearlescent weapons are introduced in one of the level cap increase DLC's.
For a better idea of what weapons are good and where to get them I recommened checking out Yoteslayas youtube channel (Yoteslaya has passed away, RIP, but he was a devoted Borderlands 2 player and has very good guides on weapons!)
Overall this game is amazing and my favoruite game to play, however I have stopped playing as much as have so many hours in and completly maxed out it has started to get boring. Hoping for a Borderlands 3 release soon.
I cant thing of anything else to add as of now, will update if I think of anything.

"BRING ME A BUCKET, AND I'LL SHOW YOU A BUCKET!"
The screech of a Psycho on a mad, often suicidal rush is a sound familier to any veteran player who frequents the bandit camps of Pandora. Within the next three seconds, the same Psycho will be shot, slagged, electrocuded, partially corroded, burned, and finished off with a hatchet to the face. Overkill? Nope. Just business as usual.
Borderlands 2 is a great game marred by a few in-game details that ruin the fun for most everyone. For starters, the good. Borderlands 2 feels like a superhero comic. From the cel-shaded graphics to some hilariously over the top weapons, combat is fast, intense, and most of all fun. Borderlands 2 also stands as one of the few first person shooters on my list where the characters are genuinley likeable, and they do well in making an alien world feel remarkably real.
But when the fighting winds down the player is faced with long distances to travel between the handfull of fast-travel machines scattered throughout, often on foot, which wrecks the flow of gameplay as often the player needs to trek back and forth between where the mission is accepted and the actual mission itself. Giant boss-type enemies, most simply other enemies with the word "Badass" stapled in front, have a bad habit of appearing without prelude and tearing the player asunder, often after an intense firefight with said boss-type's little underlings. There are four unique classes to choose from, but it takes several level ups before their individual playstyles can become fully realized. Often times the first half to three-quarters of any playthrough consists of sniping from a distance and switching to another weapon to pick off stragglers or for the enemies who get a little to close, grinding for XP to unlock each character's true potential.
In spite of all that jazz, Borderlands 2 is still well worth your time, and astep and a half above most first person shooters of this day and age.

Let me start by saying you need a willpower of steel and harder patience than diamonds to get the full experience of this game.
Rust is an ambitious survival game that experiments with concepts most games of its genre would not tread upon. Radiation poisoning, cannibalism, and high scale pvp raids with towers to the skybox to get over your bases' walls will generally be the number one threat. Your experience with normal run of the mill FPSs won't help you here, as guns are extremely different in this game. You have no dot in the middle of the screen telling you where you're aiming. Which means you have to decide if you have enough time to stare down your iron sights at your target; which in turn can be the difference between life and death.
A great deal of the game is actually pretty realistic. Characters have death animations that vary depending on what you were killed with and where (I.E. A groin shot results in the last seconds of your life with your hands over your crotch.) You'll also suffer food poisoning from eating raw or spoiled foods, and sodium poisoning from drinking salt water.
Prepare for a tidal wave of scumbag players. Everyone is to be perceived as a threat unless you already knew the person prior. That's rule number one. And prepare for a deliciously salty hate message from the guy you just killed, because death results in the loss of EVERYTHING.
Overall, great game. 9.3/10 I'd give it. Definitely try it, but prepare to be ♥♥♥♥ed, painfully.

This game... oh wow, THIS GAME!
So before playing this game, I had heard of it but knew next to nothing about it. The most knowledge I had was that everyone's favorite character was this skeleton in a blue hoodie and that the game was an rpg. I had never seen any gameplay of it. Lucky me.
Now, I don't play a lot of RPGs. I have nothing against them but I always am the kind of guy to head directly for the story. I can't think of many (if any games) that motivated me into doing all the side quests.
But Undertale was different. See, even if it basically is an RPG, everything you do relates to something else. And even the "distractions" manage to keep you emotionally invested or are quick and not time consuming.
The battles are also different to most RPGs. Rather that just standing still, waiting to get hit or just press a counter button at the right time, you actually have to test your reflexes in some bullet hell. It really adds to the fun and the tension of the game.
But that's not the major strength of Undertale. See this game... knows how to hit you hard. It knows exactly how to tone itself. Make you laugh, make you cry, make you feel determined, etc. You will get emotionally invested in these characters. I can promise that.
And the game is what you make of it. I know a lot of people say that but I mean it here. Everything carries wait in this game. Everything. And that adds to the player's investment into the game.
There are some hits to the fourth wall here and there, but rather than using it to pull you out of the experience, it makes you feel like the game itself has a mind of it's own and that it's coming out at you. You ARE part of this world. Your decisions impact it hard and the game makes you know that.
The game starts to make you reflect on the type of person you are, or at least the type of gamer you are. There is a strong moral impact the game leaves on you and that (to me) is what true art really it.
Oh no! This game is meeting all of my standards!

To the viewer,
Undertale is a little indie JRPG developed by Toby Fox, aka "Radiation", known for his Earthbound Halloween ROM hack and composing music for the popular webcomic Homestuck. I would like to be one of the many to say that this is his magnum opus, his most well-made and well-written work in any given medium, if not the best indie video game ever developed. I could write an entire college-level essay about not only how this is a great video game, but a work of interactive art that can only be achieved through this special medium. Sadly, however, to speak of this game in such a high manor would require spoiling significant portions of the game, so I will refrain from doing such. Instead, dear viewer, please take my word that this game is not your time, but the price tag on the game itself is an insane bargain. $10 for an experience unlike any other video game published to date, with great writing, innovative combat system, mostly well designed graphics (I'll get into that later), and a soundtrack that both captures the essence of its spiritual predecessor EarthBound and modernizes it in such a way that it feels fresh and unburdened by its past.
The only thing I can really warn you about, viewer, is that Undertale has had time to accumulate a fanbase that, from the outside looking in, can be labeled most positively as "dedicated" and most negatively as "rabid and delusional". Whatever or whoever disagrees with the notion that Undertale is a perfect game is usually verbally torn to shreds or damnd to being ignored. I will be one to say that the game is not perfect, but it is so close to perfection that its flaws are frequently overshadowed. Whatever flaws that this game has is subject to what the player sees as a flaw, even those who are blind to such flaws.
I would recommend this game to anyone who enjoys good narrative and a meaning to their actions within the game. The ability to spare one's opponents play a role in the plot that I will not mention because doing so would be doing the developers an injustice to their work. Please trust me, the common man, that Undertale is a game for just about everyone and that you will not regret your decision of purchasing this game, if you do so.
Thank you for taking the time to read this recommendation, dear viewer,

Borderlands 2 is a very fun game to play, by yourself and with three other friends due to the co-op. It has a nice feel to the game with the cel shaders and the fact that nearly every weapon you pick up is pretty much unique. The campaign is enjoyable and always keeps you interested, with the changes of scenery and the variety of new enemies. The four player co-op works very well, up to three other people are able to join your place in the campaign and help you with areas you are stuck on.
The only downsides to the game are the fact that once you win the game the first time, to get to the level cap you have to play the game again with gets rather repetitive (especially if you have the DLC which makes the level cap up to 70). Another downside is the fact that the legendary weapons are very rare and you have to spend hours farming the bosses to find one.
Overall, this is a great game to play with your friends for the price (especially when it's on sale). You can have some very fun and enjoyable moments with them through the campaign and I highly recommend this game.

Borderlands 2 is still a hillbilly moonshiner sort of game, then, but it's the hillbilly at his canny, tinkering, big-dreaming best. It's the hillbilly at the peak of his powers. It's the hillbilly made majestic.
That's the spirit that made the first Borderlands great, too, of course, and that really came to the fore during the original game's add-on instalments. Dr Ned, General Knoxx, Claptrap's ramshackle uprising - these are the things that Borderlands 2 builds on the most, taking cues from the tighter campaigns, sharper jokes and more poignant, oddball asides. Questing, levelling, shooting, even driving: almost everything important has been improved while each little detail has been refined
t's a surprisingly good narrative, but it's not the real story at all. The real story is different for everyone, and for me it was about a man who was constantly waddling into battle slightly under-levelled and who really wanted to get his hands on a corrosive shotgun. The man was me, and the story had a happy ending. I finally hit the right level for the run-up to the end-game boss, and I finally found that shotgun I was after, too. Then I killed an awful lot of people with the corrosive bullets it contained.
There are plenty of improvements, then, but the most satisfying thing to note is that Borderlands has lost none of its untidy charm in the transition from unlikely hit to megabucks tent-pole. The storyline runs a touch deeper now, but it's largely resisted the lunge towards the blandly epic - and while the art sparkles, it's ducked the big-team slickness that can rub away at a game's personality.

I remember when Minecraft came out thinking the low-res graphics looked kind of silly for modern gaming. Then I played it and realized part of the reason the graphics were so minimal was because of the depth the world made it a necessity. The 16-bit feel of the game ended up becoming endearing in its own quirky way. Similarly, Undertale uses simplistic graphics. Like with Minecraft the reason seems to be due to the depth of the world, though not in a literal sense here. The story is rich and rewarding. The characters are, as a whole, memorable and likeable. While the gameplay can take a little getting used to if you don't want to simply murder your way to victory or if you're unfamiliar with things like mechanics (they don't just fix cars!), it felt fresh especially when compared to other pseudo-RPGs that have come out lately.
If you enjoy stories, even a little, you should play this game. If you don't, you should still play this game and see if it can't change your mind.

Having played the first Borderlands game I came in expecting more of what I'd loved so much about the first game: tons of guns, cool abilities, and a lot of dark humor.
I have not been disappointed.
I will say that the main storyline feels less... involved than the first game. The Borderlands 1 had lots of missions and side missions in each of the areas that made you feel like the only competent "good" gunslinger in the area. It wasn't a bad thing, especially since it meant you had good reasons to explore everywhere beyond just seeing what's there.
With Borderlands 2 I find I'm really enjoying the story and the characters, but it feels a lot less personal. It's like they wrote it in such a way that it's obvious that any old player will do.
That's really the game's only weakness though.
The power trees are filled with just as much "OOH, I WANT THAT!" or more than the last Borderlands, the guns are extremely varied and still fun, and the look is just as cool as it should - like you're living in a comic.
And can I also add that Zero's special ability to disappear and then attack is SO satisfying? It hits all the right buttons for me, which isn't surprising since I love playing the long range, sneaky killer.
Overall the game is a blast to play, looks great, and has a really robust and enjoyable co-op. Definitely worth your coin.

If you haven't played this game yet, what are you waiting for? The gameplay hooks you in from the get go. The music is catchy and addicting, and the characters are so full of personality they're almost real.

Oh, Undertale. Ridiculously hyped up game with an army of rabid fans ready to defend it from anything; whether it be trolls, elitists or those who just all out hate the game.
The reason why such a huge following?
IT. IS. FANTASTIC.
Every aspect of the game is amazing, but the characters and storyline are absolutely phenomenal. Never has a game made me laugh, cry, and shout in anger as much as Undertale has. The characters are engaing, hilarious, and sometimes rather scarily relatable (looking at you there, Alphys) and I honestly don't think I've ever came across a game with such a high volume of puns. The storyline, especially during the pacifist route is full of twists and turns which will leave you staring at your computer screen, mouth hanging open, wondering what in the seven hells just happened.
The combat system, with it's bullet hell and rpg lovechild-esque mechanics is most certainly unique, and is definately at times rather infuriating; if you aren't so good at dodging particular attacks, it can get the tiniest bit repetitive, especially with random encounters, but this really doesn't detract from the quality of the game very muvch at all.
Undertale was a pleasure to play, and I'm sure it will be enjoyed by gamers old and young, and with varying levels of experience in the genre for years, if not decades to come. This is, in my opinion, one of the best games of the 2010's so far. Hats off to you, Toby Fox, and anyone else who had a part to play in bringing this amazingly bizarre vision to life.

10/10 hands down. The entire game is captivating. The characters are amazing; they're both charming and downright deadly all at the same time. It has a surprising amount of depth for a 16-bit game! Depending on how you play, you could have hours filled with terror or bittersweet bliss.
I had serious doubts about this game at first; it didn't seem like it could be all THAT entertaining. But I was wrong. DEAD wrong.
I tip my hat to the creators of this game.
You should buy Undertale. Because if you don't, you're gonna have a bad time.

THIS REVIEW MAY CONTAIN SPOILERS!!! I really enjoyed playing this game. the action is tense and enjoyable, the driving is mad and fast and the loot is INSANE. it is based on some vault hunters searching for the second vault. But their plan isn't that simple. Hyperion( a gun corporation used in the previous Borderlands, their guns increase accuracy as you shoot) is trying to stop you, they are led by a not-so-handsome Handsome Jack who is cocky and treats you like a freind, but actually detests you. This game takes you from futuristic cities, to fighting massive robots in aridlands. the guns are twice as interesting as in its predecesor, like a shotgun that when you reload it explodes! I really enjoyed playing the DLC, too, the character skins are interesting and funny, and the ones thata are different storylines have excellent varied gameplay and completely different enemies. In the DLC, if you play it in chronilogical order, you start in a small 'beach' town called Oasis wher you meet a person called Shade, who is slightly weird, he sets dummies up around Oasis with speakers on them with him talking with a personality and they talk to you slightly creepily. "early access" Im sorry but no, dayz has been in early access for over 2 years now. The developers dont put any love or quality into this game, they just release new guns, clothing and so called 'features' to this bug infested mess. Dont get me wrong, dayz is really fun with friends, but there is no synergy to what is actually going on in the world, the zombies are a side show as what it boils down to is a bunch of people running around in a baron world just shooting each other, its not a survival game, its a free for all deathmatch in an admittidly impressive large and graphically detailed world with zombies, i have enjoyed playing dayz and will jump into it every now and then for a few hours, however saying it is still in early acess is a crime as it is just lying to their customers. the games optimisation seems to have worsened in my case, im running a very high end pc and yet lag spikes are frequent in cities.
The atmosphere in my opinion is brilliant in dayz, its just totally silent, with the wind gushing, birds tweeting and other environmental sounds that really do make the world extrememly believeable, when you see another player there is no other feeling like it in any other game than dayz, its truly terrifying as you dont know whether that player will attack you or play nice (90% of players will just kill you). You feel the need to take care with every decision you make in this game as loosing your stuff to another player is a frustrating annoyance as you just end up spawning to then do it all over again. And sadly this game just feels like a boring chore most of the time, you shoot you spawn you loot you die you shoot you spawn etc etc...
Now on to the controls, i find the controls repulsive, theyre so clunky and it feels as though it is lagging every time my player moves, sometimes i find it hard to even do a simple task such as walking into a building. Its so sad for me to have to give this game the negative review as i dont think it is a bad game at all, its very fun, but theres just so many bad things going for it that have made me grow out of dayz now as its just the same stuff every time i jump into a server. I'd only subject people with a decent pc to buy this game, but if your rig cant handle it then dont bother as the low graphics are just awful and you cant see anything such as players, and the low fps you'll be recieving will screw you over in a firefight.
VERDICT
Dayz is simply beautiful, it has the look, the feel and the atmosphere, but the gameplay itself and the context of the world is simply dull, repetitive and down right frustrating at times. It is a shame im giving this game a thumbs down considering ive been through periods where i'd play it all night and day with a couple of friends, but it almost feels like bohemia is now just being lazy with the development of the game and counting up all the money which we have given to them..I do hope they fix this game and start releasing some really good content for it, fix the engine for a start because this game has the potential to be the best survival game ever made, but in its current state it simply just is not. :(

It follows a way that takes away the time you would spend on "experience grinding", gets rid of it, and allows you to prevail without harming anyone--making bonds along the way.
Don't let the hype get to you. Since no game can be deemed the greatest, just relax and immerse yourself in the game.
It's better if you experience the game with no expectations. Just play along the story, do what you feel is right, and let "DETERMINATION" take you on train of emotions.
Quirky, at times humourus, at times emotional; the game forms a connection between you and all of it's characters.
UNDERTALE, is a game that you will smile upon in the future when you look back to it.

Borderlands 2 (along with the first Borderlands) is, without a doubt, one of the most stylish games I have ever played.  There is something about it that just sets it apart from other games.  The story is awesome; it has some great moments, and some even better twists.  The writing is genius - I mean, whoever wrote these games deserves an big, fat trophy.  You get seriously involved with the characters (I have literally come to despise Handsome Jack - what a dirtbag!) and the story because of how well the writing draws you in and leads you along throughout the adventure.  The characters are among the most well-crafted I've ever seen in a game.  I can't get enough of Scooter - the guy is hilarious.  And even the nobody enemies you fight have excellent design and neat dialogue (I love when you kill a Rat with fire - "I SMELL DELICIOOOOOOOOUS!").  The graphics really have a unique flair, and are simply beautiful; Pandora is a gorgeous world, and you can tell the developers put a lot of care into designing it.  The multiplayer shooter gameplay is so much fun.  I can't tell you what I blast I've had beating down some skags with my buddies.
The one drawback I might mention is that I've often had trouble with the online gameplay with friends at time.  I'm not sure if it's just my network or what, but I get some serious lag when playing with buddies, and our sessions have shut down more than once.   When it works, it works really well, but, again, I've had a few issues with it.  But that really hasn't hurt my experience with the game that much.
Overall, I'd give Borderlands 2 my thumbs-up.  It's a fantastic game; you'll get hours and hours of great entertainment out of it.  I highly recommend it.

I've been trying to find a decent game to sink a whole lot of hours into for a long time. Late December 2013 and all everybody's talking about is this zombie survival game. No not the old one, the new one! DayZ STAND ALONE. And what do you know, most of this game you are going to be alone. It's sad to say but I've probably logged less than 50 hours of actual PvP in this game, looking for people is really all you can do that's not completely pointless. That wouldn't be half bad if finding somebody can take anywhere from 15-25 minutes to 2-4 hour spans of you sprinting through empty towns.
I paid for the game already like most people, so I have a slight interest in my investment. There has been almost zero progress since the only (rare) vehicle was added in .53, and that was EIGHT and a half months ago. Only recently have I gotten a steady 25-30 fps in town on my more than enough pc build. But even now PvP is based purely on luck with the large and random amounts of desync (enemy players can be displaced up to twenty or more feet at a moments notice) leaving little to no enjoyment to be had.
A large reason I got into this game was role playing. After watching so many role playing videos of the mod I was sure the community would fire right back again with interesting♥♥♥♥♥♥ Yet at this point in development most people have been playing for 100+ hours and know what DayZ really truely is, an incomplete game in every level except the map that they got from their big brother.
Pros:
ONLY game I've ever played where PvPvE worked so well (when zombies etc. work)

Since I turned slightly obsessed with the Borderlands-series, I couldn't hold myself back from writing my own review of this game. Its hard to comment on the second part of a game, so I’m trying to make it attractive even for people who are totally new to the Borderlands universe. (Sadly, this review ended up longer than I expected)

Short description copied from wikipedia to explain what kind of story you can expect (since I am not able to explain the beginning of the story as good as this by myself):

Vault hunting? Pandora? Eridium?
If you haven’t heard anything about those words yet - Don’t be afraid. Finishing the first game isn't a condition to play and understand what the plot is about - the only thing you need is to follow the dialog. Borderlands 2 continues five years after the story ending of its predecessor but still connects at the previous one at so many points - It even included the old vault hunters. - After all, you can enjoy an understanding and exciting story-telling without feeling slightly lost.

Your role in this game is simple: You slip into the role of the vault hunters to save Pandora, kill all the bad-guys and make the villains happy by solving their tasks. Discovering and exploring the planet, farming loot and blow everything up would make another short description what you have to do in this game. Sounds like fun, right?
The game gives you the option to choose between four (or six - if you bought the certain DLCs) new characters - the "Vault Hunters". All of them own skill trees and combat specializations - and their own special attacks which can be unlocked at Level 5. To survive in Pandora, you equip yourself with different types of weapons like for example: rocket launchers, SMGs or sniper rifles. After the time you unlock about four weapon sloths which accepts combining and switching different weapon types in combat.

The gameplay is based on a role-playing system with EXP, skill trees and rewards. After you reached Level 5, you archive a skill point for every level-up to upgrade your skills and modify your character after your preferred gameplay. Being able to reset your whole skill tree for a little amount of gold, makes it possible to try the heck out of the skill system. So you don't need to follow any strict skilling and can do whatever you want and choose that what you think could fit the best for you.
Something new in the game is called the "badass system". This system is a kind of reward system. You earn badass-rank by completing several types of challenges. After you earned enough badass-rank, the system rewards you with a "badass token". Those token can be spend on randomly selected stat upgrades (like "Critical Hit Damage", "Fire Rate" or "Reload Speed"). There are about 14 possible upgrade choices.
Like in the first game – it’s pretty much loot-hunting focused: finding stuff, comparing stuff and selling stuff. You will find yourself following this procedure like 80% of all our in-game time. All that is caused by the over 17,8 Million different guns and rifles in this game. All of them are created via a random generator. If you enjoy games like Diablo a lot - this might be interesting for you.

The world of Borderlands 2 is huge. Compared to its predecessor - the world is a lot more colorful and there is much more to explore after all.
The amount of quests and tasks is also enormous - So you are not forced to permanently follow the main-quest. Next to the scoreboard, you find several quest-NPCs on every map. Mostly they contain tasks like "kill that or that guy" or "collect 5x (insert item here)". That might sound boring - at first. In the game itself every quest got its own kinda entertaining plot and some of them even give you the option what you choose as your reward.

The Borderlands-series is well-known for its cel-shaded-style and cartoon-like effects.
Not only the humor, the dialog and story are crazy so what would better fit there than crazy graphics? That type of style was the best thing that the developers could choose for this FPS. It looks indeed like just taken out of a comic - flashy but detailed. And due high color contrasts everything turns surreal-looking. After a time you will also realize: Just whenever you press F12 for taking a screenshot, the picture turns out flawless. You can see and feel how amazingly designed this game is.
There isn't really a huge difference between Borderlands 1 and 2 on the graphics though. The textures are more HD than before and make the graphical upgrade visible. Now they even brought daytime simulation into the game. Killing enemies hasn't been this cool before, especially at night. The visible animations are also a kind of eye-candy.

Borderlands 2 is already fun in single-player mode but where it really shines is in the multiplayer aspect.
Up to four players can join a session. In those sessions - team work is the only thing that maters. Solving quests, fighting bosses or loot-hunting is more fun with friends than alone, trust me. The number of people inside a session also has influence on the power of the enemies.
With the purchase of this game, you get a crazy first-person-shooter like you have never seen before. Importantly, one of the best multiplayer shooter I have played. It combines a role-play modules with a bunch of colorful weapons and an extra of insane story. And goddammit, if you are into humor and especially black humor - this game is more than perfect for you. It’s a game that enjoys its special place between all the First-Person-Shooters that have been released during the past few years.
Sadly, its side-quests and task start to repeat after some time but you hardly recognize that due the huge amount of quests.

4K | GTX 1060 | Ultra Settings gameplay:
This game just gets better and better with each new content, some of the latest DLC's have been fantastic. It's a cool, smooth fast paced FPS that just keeps on giving. Just when you think you've found your perfect weapon, a new one is discovered. It's a great time sink and you'll find yourself coming back for more. Highly recommended!

Borderlands 2 is a well-made game. It has good graphics, it controls very well, and the gameplay is founded on an unbeatable formula of shootin' dudes and constantly upgrading. Unlike most comparable games, each upgrade actually feels like an upgrade. There are very few "+0.2% damage" boosts and plenty of "+10% damage while ON FIRE" boosts. Each skill changes your playstyle a bit, as their triggers are quite varied.
It's a more polished product than the first, but suffers greatly in replayability and balance. The missions remain unchanged between playthroughs with lots of dialog and standing around, which makes them a chore the second, third, and each successive time through. The game's focus on humor actually hurts it here, as the jokes grow stale and become more annoying than anything else. Additionally, your enemies seem to scale much faster with levels than you do, leading to a lot of extremely fast deaths. This makes certain character builds completely worthless after a certain level, and forces you into a specific set of effective playstyles.
Weapon generation is pretty lacking, too. Most weapons will be ridiculously ineffective, and all of the best weapons are pre-defined drops from specific quests and bosses. This encourages farming and metagaming rather than actually looting everyone you meet.
Despite all of its flaws, it's worth many, many hours of fun. Just don't expect it to hold your interest in the long-term. Even with all of the DLCs adding new areas and enemies, they do nothing to fix the balance issues.

Let's just start out with yes, play this game. Play it blind as well, don't watch a playthrough on YouTube. This game is best experienced blind.
This game is about a kid who has fallen down into the underground. The underground is where monsters where banished to after a war. You play as this kid and you are told not to fight the monsters, but to befriend them by Toriel, or as many people call her Goat Mom. However, you are also told that this world is kill or be killed by a flower named Flowey. You can either kill monsters or spare them, which determines your ending.
Now lets get to what people say about it. Is the soundtrack great? Yes. Are the graphics good? Most of the time. There are a handful of sprites that bug me a bit, but otherwise it is great pixel art. Many people say to play pacifist first, but usually don't give a reason. The genocide route (the one were you kill everyone) expects you to have played at least a neutral run first. It features gameplay mechanics barely explained in genocide, it is in general a lot harder, and you miss a lot of thew quirky dialog that the game excels at. Consider this a spoiler, don't consider this a spoiler, but
This game has become on of my personal favorite games for it's story, characters, and gameplay in general. I highly recommend you play it.
I almost forgot about the community. It's not as bad as fnaf, as they are bad for different reasons, but they can be annoying. They constantly request people to play the game and freak out if you do a genocide run first. Just ignore them, while it may be hard, that's probably the best idea.

I really enjoyed playing this game. the action is tense and enjoyable, the driving is mad and fast and the loot is INSANE. it is based on some vault hunters searching for the second vault. But their plan isn't that simple. Hyperion( a gun corporation used in the previous Borderlands, their guns increase accuracy as you shoot) is trying to stop you, they are led by a not-so-handsome Handsome Jack who is cocky and treats you like a freind, but actually detests you. This game takes you from futuristic cities, to fighting massive robots in aridlands. the guns are twice as interesting as in its predecesor, like a shotgun that when you reload it explodes! I really enjoyed playing the DLC, too, the character skins are interesting and funny, and the ones thata are different storylines have excellent varied gameplay and completely different enemies. In the DLC, if you play it in chronilogical order, you start in a small 'beach' town called Oasis wher you meet a person called Shade, who is slightly weird, he sets dummies up around Oasis with speakers on them with him talking with a personality and they talk to you slightly creepily. The end of DLC boss-battle requires you to be consumed by a large creature named the Laviathan, where you fight Captain Scarlett's pet, Roscoe, a cute name for a giant rakk hive!( a boss in the last Borderlands) You then get regurgitated by the Laviathan onto a ledge and you fight it. The second DLC is Mr. Torgue's Campaign of Carnage where you hacve to compete in a series of arena battles to be the first to find the THIRD vault. You have to fight a Piston, who is a complete cheater, he has a giant mechanical T-rex, while you have a turret, someone who can turn invisible, a duel wielding person and a magic ball that suspends people in the air. You also have to fight somebody called Motor Momma, who rides a motorbike that you have to destroy then you have to kill her who has a giant RPG. When I did this boss-battle, I was three levels below her, so by the time I had almost killed her, she had respawned so I had to give up! I have ran out of time on this review, but I shall review other points another time, but if iwere to rate this game out of 10, I would give it definetley 10/10!

The Borderlands series has a brilliant formula of wacky humor, countless guns, and RPG mechanics. Borderlands 2 has crushed its prequel with modified gameplay, gorgeous graphics, hectic music and an interesting story. While the sequel improved in every department, its story took me by surprise. The strong, unique, and diverse personalities you’ll meet through the well-paced story improves the entire experience. Most importantly, this gives life and excitement to the planet of Pandora, which was just a boring hunk of rock in the original game. The “Bazzilion” guns that Gearbox claimed Borderlands 2 will have was no joke, and it’s more than just a few minor tweaks in damage and accuracy. The guns will sometimes have a huge bayonet, a wacky reload animation, a crazy looking scope, and may not even have any recoil. When the critics can only complain about an imperfect user-interface, we can conclude that the gameplay is as addicting as we all hoped it would be. For fans of the original Borderlands, this is a no-brainer, but for those who are skeptical about the unique gaming experience that Borderlands 2 has to offer, it’s time to come to your senses and get in on the fun that you’ve been missing out on.
The Good
+Lots of great loot
+Humorous writing
+Awesome world
+An actual story this time
+Single-player is finally enjoyable
+Co-op is still king
The Bad
-Underdeveloped visual customization
-A serious lack of being able to approach enemy strongholds stealthily

I have unregretfully poured just a little over 400hrs into this game. It's been nothing short of amazing and definitely ranks amongst the Top 5 this generation. The gameplay, story, drop system and dialogue are MASSIVE (and I'm not exaggerating) improvements over the first game. The main quest doesn't feel as tedious, bland and empty as BL1, in which some will give you the chance to earn slight bonuses, consisting of stronger weapons, shields or even character skins.
One of the major overhauls I love the most is the Badass Rank. Completing levels of challenges will increase your BA Rank and give you a token whi you can apply to stat increase for better accuracy, longer duration of DoT effects (shock, fire, corrosive) or overall damage. And your BA Rank is applied to all characters that you create (my BA Rank is around 31,000 or so) so you can start off a new character and be extremely overpowered but in the long run it will pay off as True Vault Hunter Mode will greatly amp up the difficulty. More so with Ultimate Vault Hunter Mode (not recommended until Lv61 because of level scaling). You can also earn skins from these challenges as well.
Of the core classes available you have Axton the commando, whose Sabre Turret shreds up everything when deployed. Going down specific trees allows the turret to fire rockets, set of a radial nuke or even grant the ability to deploy 2 at once. Maya is a Siren, much like Lilith but instead of Phase Shifting for an advantage, she can use Phase Lock. Phase Lock surrounds the target in a orb when invested into skills like Elated, Sweet Release, Helios and Chain Reaction, you'll set the enemy on fire, drain health (and restore it to your friends) and transfer that orb to the next target. Gaige the Mechomancer (who was available as a preorder bonus before the game launched) has Deathtrap. Deathtrap is basically your scout who'll rip apart anything in sight and his abilities are further amplified when going down the Best Friends Forever tree. I've invested a few points into BFF myself but I'm more partial to Little Big Trouble. LBT primarily focuses on Shock damage, in which some weapons (and shields) can make Gaige literally invincible.
There's much more I can say here but I'll wrap this up with: If you see it on sale, better yet the GOTY Edition which includes all of the DLC (not the paid skins) you are definitely getting a huge bang for your buck. 10/10.

This game made me unable to read the word "spaghetti" while keeping a straight face.
In all seriousness though, I strongly advise you to stop reading now as the best way to experience this game is as blind as possible. I give it a 9/10.
--------
- Has better humor than your average Borderlands game
- Has music on par, if not better than, Binding of Isaac + Wrath of the Lamb.
- Has the least repetitive (while staying coherent) gameplay I've seen in a RPG.
- Has the biggest amount of characters you'll get attached to I've seen in a single game.
- Gives you choices that actually matter over the course of your game.
- Respects your intelligence and gives no "stupid" tutorials. It teaches you mechanics cleverly.
- Has 3 completely different endings with their respective final boss.
- Has more spaghetti than pretty much every game you might think of COMBINED.
So why a 9/10 and not a 10/10? Well, I would have liked the option to make the text scroll faster, but it's mainly because as a player, you might naturally want (and be able to) work your way to a particular ending, but even if you meet all conditions, the game arbitrarily forces you to complete/witness another ending first, if this is your first run of the game. I say arbitrarily because from what I've read of it, I don't see any reason why the plaer would need to complete a different ending first to see this particular ending, but maybe I'm wrong. If so, I'll modify this rating.

I have unregretfully poured just a little over 400hrs into this game. It's been nothing short of amazing and definitely ranks amongst the Top 5 this generation. The gameplay, story, drop system and dialogue are MASSIVE (and I'm not exaggerating) improvements over the first game. The main quest doesn't feel as tedious, bland and empty as BL1, in which some will give you the chance to earn slight bonuses, consisting of stronger weapons, shields or even character skins.
One of the major overhauls I love the most is the Badass Rank. Completing levels of challenges will increase your BA Rank and give you a token whi you can apply to stat increase for better accuracy, longer duration of DoT effects (shock, fire, corrosive) or overall damage. And your BA Rank is applied to all characters that you create (my BA Rank is around 31,000 or so) so you can start off a new character and be extremely overpowered but in the long run it will pay off as True Vault Hunter Mode will greatly amp up the difficulty. More so with Ultimate Vault Hunter Mode (not recommended until Lv61 because of level scaling). You can also earn skins from these challenges as well.
Of the core classes available you have Axton the commando, whose Sabre Turret shreds up everything when deployed. Going down specific trees allows the turret to fire rockets, set of a radial nuke or even grant the ability to deploy 2 at once. Maya is a Siren, much like Lilith but instead of Phase Shifting for an advantage, she can use Phase Lock. Phase Lock surrounds the target in a orb when invested into skills like Elated, Sweet Release, Helios and Chain Reaction, you'll set the enemy on fire, drain health (and restore it to your friends) and transfer that orb to the next target. Gaige the Mechomancer (who was available as a preorder bonus before the game launched) has Deathtrap. Deathtrap is basically your scout who'll rip apart anything in sight and his abilities are further amplified when going down the Best Friends Forever tree. I've invested a few points into BFF myself but I'm more partial to Little Big Trouble. LBT primarily focuses on Shock damage, in which some weapons (and shields) can make Gaige literally invincible.
There's much more I can say here but I'll wrap this up with: If you see it on sale, better yet the GOTY Edition which includes all of the DLC (not the paid skins) you are definitely getting a huge bang for your buck. 10/10.
