I never take time to write Steam reviews, but I have to this time.  Why?  As of posting this, 97% of the steam reviews are positive, and the negative reviews are downvoted to Hell.  If I could do a "neutral" recommendation, I would.  But I am opting for a thumbs down because A) That 97% symbolizes why I am writing a review, and B) While this was a good game that I enjoyed playing somewhat, I absolutely wouldn't recommend it to most people.
On point A: This game needs to be taken down a peg on the internet in order to spare consumers like me.  I thought I was about to walk into a game with masterful game design and/or incredible writing.  The writing WILL NOT satisfy everyone, and the game play was good, but not Earth-shattering.  I would not have spent 10 dollars on this game at this point in my life if the information out there about this game were a lot more grounded.
Which leads to point B: All of that was coming from someone who enjoyed it.  I would be outright tilted if I disliked the game.  And just as I easily understand why there are some who love it dearly, I am certain that some would hate it and a huge number of people won't really enjoy it.  Why?  Because it's a polarizing game.  It's a story driven game whose writing is some of the campiest, strangest stuff out there.  I didn't use those words negatively.  It isn't BAD writing.  But it isn't writing that I would universally recommend.  Some people eat the aggressive silliness up.  Not everyone will think Temmie is funny (in fact, I'd guess most people).
Here's my breakdown:
Loved:
- The music was superb.  Best part of the game.
- The concept of the traditional RPG overturned with a non-violence option was what drew me.  It's as novel and interesting as you think it will be, and the reason I ultimately like the game.
Liked:
- The combat.  Most turn-based RPG's are just downright boring.  Replacing this with little bullet-hell minigames for a game that is meant to be about enjoying a story anyways was a great idea.
Neutral About:
- Visuals.  They just weren't for me.  Some things were adorable.  Some things were funny.  Others were ugly and bland.
- Puzzles.  They were just okay.
- Some of the writing.  I chuckled occasionally.  I did want to see what would happen next usually.
Hated
- How the multiple endings work.  The neutral ending is lame and didn't fulfill me.  Especially when I looked up the other two, cooler endings.  This means I would have had to look stuff up beforehand in order to get a good ending.  I definitely don't want to play through the whole thing again, nor do I want to watch someone else do it on youtube.
- Some of the pacifist fights.  Even though I praised the pacifism above, there are moments where it isn't handled well.  They are meant to be puzzles where you perform the right series of actions on the "enemy" in order to get them to stop fighting you, but there were a number of times where it was absolutely not intuitive to figure out, and I would be very annoyed when I'd look up what stupid thing I was supposed to do.
- Some other aspects of the writing.  Mostly the dialogue.  Many of the jokes fall flat.  The fact that every character is so dramatic will also grate on you after a while.
This is a good game.  I enjoyed it because of the superb music and the nontraditional RPG format.  But it is far from 97% good in my eyes.  And even though I absolutely understand why it would be a 97% darling in the eyes of some, you're kidding yourself if you think the majority of people will like it nearly as much as that.
I hope there will be more games like this - story-rich games where your choices matter.  I did a pacifist run and I loved every minute of it!

When I first heard about this game, I thought it's going to be perfect, but I'm going to try to explain here why it was good for me and why it wasn't.
To start off, the biggest issue DayZ has, and has pretty much had it from the beggining of early access, is the engine. The engine was out of date way before DayZ got into early access. The performance for most people sucks and the engine also is restrictive for developers in some aspects. The server-side performance is also terrible and at least the devs are working on it. Also, there is a lot of cheating in DayZ, which I thankfully haven't experienced for some time now, but it's still there and it will probably never be completely gone, but the devs have worked on it and it is certainly a lot better than it was. The worst time (as far as I remember) was around May 2014, when the game was quite literally unplayable because there was so much teleporting, wallhacking, guns with endless clips, etc. I can't say exactly how it is right now because I haven't had much time for playing games lately, but it is definetly a lot better and I haven't seen a cheater for a couple of months, if not more. Also, there are some occasional bugs and glitches, but they have fixed a bunch of bugs which were in the game when it got into early access. However, I don't complain much about this because it says when you buy the game and also every time you play the game that it is in early access, and the point of early access in general is for devs to see how people like their game so they usually only fix game-breaking bugs. You have to understand that DayZ was pushed into early access very early in the development and it still has a long way to go before being a finished game, so don't be one of those people who complain about the development taking forever.
That was pretty much all the bat things I had to say about DayZ. There is quite a lot of problems because the game was pushed out so early, but I still like the game. I don't play the game because it has a lot of content or because it looks pretty (none of this is true ofc), but I play the game because of the player interaction. I play the game because I love talking to other people and interacting with them, be it in the heat of the action when you're taunting the enemies or whatever, or when you're just casually strolling across Chernarus and come across an individual who makes you laugh, gives you the chills, or just straight up causes a situation which you later remember and laugh at. Those are the things you should play this game for and if you aren't looking for that, than you should probably not spend your money on this game because in that case you are probably not going to play it for a long time.
You might notice I have a relatively small amount of game time in DayZ, considering I bought it less than a month after it first getting into early access, but I've been through the good times and the bad times. That being said, I would recommend this game to everybody who, like me, wants to have fun interacting to other players and just generally surviving in Chernarus. At the same time I want to tell everyone who is looking for something completely else to think before spending money on this game, because there will be less people spreading frustrations and expressing their impatience regarding the development of the game. In the end, I would recommend watching a bunch of YouTube videos to everyone who is considering to buy this game, because everyone has a different taste and the best way to see if you will like the game is to watch videos, and there are definetly a lot of them. I certainly like the game a lot and a lot of other people share the same opinion and I hope a lot more people will come, but I know that I'm going to be playing this game for a while.

I don’t recommend at this time just because it’s one of the slowest in development and poorly organized games I have tried on early access. Though if you love early access games and do not mind one of the worst early access games I have played then I would buy it.

Can't recommend the game at all in it's current state.
The game runs like crap on decent hardware (i5 3570k, GTX970, 8GB RAM). On normal, I barely get above 30, let alone in built up areas.
The loot system has become so 'brutal' compared to the mod, it's no longer fun. Whilst I can appreciate Rocket's original vision, and the amount of guns in the mod could become silly at times, spending an hour searching for a gun or even a bag is painful, especially when half the time they won't be in usable condition. Couple this with then having to find ammunition and magazines to even use your weapons, it quickly becomes tedious.
Player mentality is absolutely garbage at the moment. The majority of players will kill you on sight, whether or not you're armed, or even have a bag on. Couple this with the snails pace at which you acquire loot, the game isn't tense, as it was meant to be, it's just straight up frustrating.
The way and rate at which the game is being updated is poor, in my opinion, and whilst I'm sure the fanboys will downvote my review for saying it, the game is barely any better than at release. 'Ooh, it's an alpha'. I'm fully aware of that, but considering we were supposed to be in beta by now, with a full release round the corner, fans who have been playing since the mod can't help but feel shafted by this release.
What's been added over the past two years is just a stone in the pond compared to many of the issues that are still prevelant, and much of the content from the original mod that is still missing. Yes, I know the new renderer is coming, etc., but until it does, and only if it significantly improves how the game runs AND causes content updates to speed up, will I consider changing this review.
This game doesn't deserve the 'Mostly Positive' rating it currently has on Steam. But just look at the positive reviews. Half of them are a joke, to DayZ's detriment.
If you enjoy spending 3 hours mindlessly pressing tab through the same empty interiors, hoping to find something you can use, only to get shot in the back by the very first person you encounter, by all means, buy this game.
If instead, you were hoping, after two years, for a slightly more polished version of the mod, with new, exciting features, stay well clear.
I will change this review when I see that the game has had enough progress made to warrant it, and I wholly anticipate the new renderer being as great as we've been told.

Let's forget about the roving bands of trigger-happy survivors. Let's forget about the evil rooftop snipers. Hell, let's forget about the zombie apocalypse.
The real apocalypse in DayZ is the famine! Apparently, the zombie apocalypse occurred just after the Food Rapture, and anything edible has disappeared and risen up to heaven to escape the sinners.
DayZ's loot system is an absolute travesty. Most of your gameplay experience consists of running around trying to search through bland, boring, barren and featureless buildings, and then starving to death before you've even run across a ruined book, let alone another living being.
The fact that there is no food anywhere is made even worse by the fact that the game allows you to live for only an hour of real-time gameplay tops without eating. Get ready to experience the fun of running around doing absolutely nothing for a full hour, only to die and respawn to repeat the same soul-crushingly boring experience ad nauseam.
Maybe if there was an ounce of detail put into the world, instead of copy-pasting the same carbon-copy vanilla room models, exploration would have been fun. But alas, the locations in DayZ are about as piquant as room temperature tap water with a generous serving of Wonder Bread.
Combine this with the godawful performance issues and an inventory system so broken you often can't pick items up off of the floor (or, if the Nine Divines favor you and you actually pick it up, the inventory system often glitches and prevents you from equipping it), and you have one truly atrocious package.
This game has been 'Early Access' for two goddamn years now, and it shows zero signs of improvement. It's failed to fix the smallest balance issues, let alone the glitches and performance problems plaguing it.
Don't buy this game, even if a mad Irishman threatens to kneecap you if you don't play this joke of a game.

I never take time to write Steam reviews, but I have to this time.  Why?  As of posting this, 97% of the steam reviews are positive, and the negative reviews are downvoted to Hell.  If I could do a "neutral" recommendation, I would.  But I am opting for a thumbs down because A) That 97% symbolizes why I am writing a review, and B) While this was a good game that I enjoyed playing somewhat, I absolutely wouldn't recommend it to most people.
On point A: This game needs to be taken down a peg on the internet in order to spare consumers like me.  I thought I was about to walk into a game with masterful game design and/or incredible writing.  The writing WILL NOT satisfy everyone, and the game play was good, but not Earth-shattering.  I would not have spent 10 dollars on this game at this point in my life if the information out there about this game were a lot more grounded.
Which leads to point B: All of that was coming from someone who enjoyed it.  I would be outright tilted if I disliked the game.  And just as I easily understand why there are some who love it dearly, I am certain that some would hate it and a huge number of people won't really enjoy it.  Why?  Because it's a polarizing game.  It's a story driven game whose writing is some of the campiest, strangest stuff out there.  I didn't use those words negatively.  It isn't BAD writing.  But it isn't writing that I would universally recommend.  Some people eat the aggressive silliness up.  Not everyone will think Temmie is funny (in fact, I'd guess most people).
Here's my breakdown:
Loved:
- The music was superb.  Best part of the game.
- The concept of the traditional RPG overturned with a non-violence option was what drew me.  It's as novel and interesting as you think it will be, and the reason I ultimately like the game.
Liked:
- The combat.  Most turn-based RPG's are just downright boring.  Replacing this with little bullet-hell minigames for a game that is meant to be about enjoying a story anyways was a great idea.
Neutral About:
- Visuals.  They just weren't for me.  Some things were adorable.  Some things were funny.  Others were ugly and bland.
- Puzzles.  They were just okay.
- Some of the writing.  I chuckled occasionally.  I did want to see what would happen next usually.
Hated
- How the multiple endings work.  The neutral ending is lame and didn't fulfill me.  Especially when I looked up the other two, cooler endings.  This means I would have had to look stuff up beforehand in order to get a good ending.  I definitely don't want to play through the whole thing again, nor do I want to watch someone else do it on youtube.
- Some of the pacifist fights.  Even though I praised the pacifism above, there are moments where it isn't handled well.  They are meant to be puzzles where you perform the right series of actions on the "enemy" in order to get them to stop fighting you, but there were a number of times where it was absolutely not intuitive to figure out, and I would be very annoyed when I'd look up what stupid thing I was supposed to do.
- Some other aspects of the writing.  Mostly the dialogue.  Many of the jokes fall flat.  The fact that every character is so dramatic will also grate on you after a while.
This is a good game.  I enjoyed it because of the superb music and the nontraditional RPG format.  But it is far from 97% good in my eyes.  And even though I absolutely understand why it would be a 97% darling in the eyes of some, you're kidding yourself if you think the majority of people will like it nearly as much as that.

Undertale has wacky humor and a compelling story. While the jokes can be a little bit slow and/or unoriginal sometimes, the comedic element of the game is amusing and entertaining for a majority of the game. The Neutral route is a little short, but has a lot more freedom than the other two routes. If you  want to fight and save specific people, you should play this mode. The Pacifist route adds a new element of love and friendship to the story that is surprisingly engrossing. This route will leave you feeling warm and fuzzy inside, and will have you smiling the entire time. The Genocide route is very dark, and disturbing. Within seconds of starting this route, the lighthearted music is replaced by a suffocating silence, and the humor disappears. If you play through this mode, you will found yourself feeling guilty and angry. Overall, Undertale is a great game that is well worth your money and your time.

Undertale - it's the game you've heard so much about. And all of the buzz? The game certainly deserves it (*see edit at bottom). Undertale is one of the most eye-opening games I've played that has more to offer than entertainment.
Pros:
+Lovely 8-bit style
+Memorable characters
+Interesting story
+Incredible soundtrack
+Unique gameplay style
+Different endings
+High replayability
Cons:
-Can really hit you in the feels.
The game essentially has 3 endings based on 3 different runthroughs of the game: You have a pacifist ending (good), a neutral ending, and the infamous genocide ending (bad). However, the endings can be altered a bit, depending on which runthrough is played first.

Undertale offers players a lovely story with humorous dialogue, characters with unique personalities, an interesting way of interacting with monster encounters, and the story has a moral to it.

Undertale is definitely worth it's full price (I purchased it on sale for around $7). I would even recommend purchasing the game and soundtrack bundle (you'll fall in love with Toby Fox's music).

In conclusion, I have to say Undertale ranks among my favorite games I've ever had the pleasure to play. If you have yet to pick it up, you're definitely missing out.
*Edit
I did play the game with very little to no expectations. I believe that is the best way to go into the game (for at least your first playthrough) and have your own actions define your gameplay experience.I actually went into the game feeling negative about it (because I heard stories about its dreaded fandom), but I believe that going in completely blind to the story helped turn my opinion around.
**Edit
I finished the genocide run, which I'd reccommend if you're a heartless ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. It went by really quick, but took me about 15 hours; probably 70% of that was fighting one specific character. But it really offers more story to the game and can help fill in some gaps.

This game is, in my opinion, one of the most innovative and groundbreaking video games to come out in the last ten years.  Quite a bold statement, right?  After all, there are many games like this one, games with a retro flavor or quirky humor or whatever first impressions the screenshots are giving you.  When I bought this game, it was with great reluctance as most games like this tend to be try-hard, self-referential wank fests in my experience.
I was dead wrong.  This game isn't like any other because it uses the medium of video games to subvert, deconstruct and question everything about video games.  Sure, other games have attempted this kind of thing before, but none to my mind have achieved it with the same level of depth and enjoyability.  On top of all the metagame philosophy and form-breaking questions is a deeply heartfelt, hilarious and engaging world that can be immediate and metaphorical at the same time.  Add to the mix a gameplay system that's inherently fun and unique along with AN INCREDIBLE SOUNDTRACK and you've got, well, a classic in the making.
I would only recommend that you pass on this game if you're determined to hate it.  If that's the case, you obviously won't enjoy it.  If you give it a chance, however, you might be just as pleasantly surprised as I was.

Welcome to Rust, the brutal, survival game that will have you tearing your hair out, laugh and cry, all on the same evening.  If you like games such as ARK, then this title is worth investigating. It offers extremely attractive graphics, full nudity plus a great and amazingly easy to use and follow HUD.
It is worth noting that you can't create your character, you will be given a random character of gender, creed and size.  If you are new to Rust I recommend finding a young or nearly empty server while you gain your feet.  Rust is a no mercy game.  Someone in full armour and the best weapons will not think twice about icing a guy who is naked, with a rock and new.
You have the freedom to build on almost anything and wherever you like. In water, up mountains, dry land.  The building system is simple and easy to use while providing the ability to build complex structures and upgrading materials used.  You learn with each new build better ways to construct strong bases that are harder to penetrate.
Rust for me was completely immersive, I found myself playing until the early hours without noticing.  Be aware this game is dramatically improved with friends and doesn't really work as a lone survival.  This is amazing for teams, communicating, working together, hunting in packs, bringing down choppers or racing for airdrops.
I love the freedom you have in choosing how to play:
- Be brutal, KOS and trounce them all.
- Play the nice guy, and then imprison them.
- RP a glorious city, trade and build stunning structures.
- Or just watch the Rusty world burn.
This game is in early access and there are bugs.  Bears clip through walls on the ground floor and kill you, rain clips through structures, items disappear through the ground and much more.  So it is worth bearing that in mind and not getting bent out of shape, trust me when I say, there are bigger issues to worry about.

It's a shame really that Garry doesn't priorities this in front of any form of weapon attachments and or a XP system.
In terms of value for your money: there is some, but perhaps not enough to justify its price. I'll let you decide whether Rust is worth your money or not.

I have played Rust off and on since it was released to Early Access over two years ago. I would say roughly 1/3 of my play time was in the original \"Legacy\" form of the game and the other 2/3 after it was rebooted. Rust for me is the type of experience which is marked by extreme highs but the vast majority of the game is spent doing dull resource grinding or being on the bad sides of its numerous shortcomings.
I find the development process also very challenging from a player perspective. Major changes are often made with what feels like very little balancing or pre-testing done. Other times there can be months with little more than what are basically new skins. Performance can rapidly sway patch to patch. While the game is in alpha, and I respect that, I would also expect that over time changes would have become more consistent. This just hasn\'t been the cause. At times it seems the community has the games direction on the mind more than its own developers.
There\'s a lot of potential to Rust. It still could reach it some day but at this time I would not recommend it.

Loved the game and put hundreds of hours into it. Random player models were cool and the constant stream of new content kept the game fresh and fun. Eventually I purchased a server specifically so that I could run my own and make a community that myself and like minded players could enjoy with modding tools making the game even more interesting. Things went great and I learned a great deal of admining through trial and error. Everything was awesome but my server simply died because the vast majority of my players were male and suddenly had female models. This was not well received and people became angry when I told them that I could do nothing to change it. The kicker was that the few female players on my server got male models and didn't want them anymore! As of writing this review, I have since quit playing rust along with the former players of my server simply because they don't give a choice between being a male or female within the game. I get that they want a player model to stay the same to avoid people misleading other players, but why not allow a one time choice of at least character sex so that people can have their individual player model and not create the issues of model switching? I love Facepunch but it seems that the whole system is made to make their jobs easier. Having complete random generation seems a lot easier than putting a little effort into some choice on the players part about their general mode. Not hating on the game, and if they ever do give a choice of at least gender I will be back, but it feels pretty bad to see a server and community I built over the months to fall apart because of something so simple.

This is a fantastic game. It is one of the best out there for survival sandbox games. I started out in the survival genre with ark survival evolved, and was instantly addicted. Rust, although very similar to ark, is very different in its own unique way. Rust is a game oriented around realism (although it is far from realistic). It has some beautiful graphics, beautiful lighting, and beautiful textures. If you can run the game (which takes a newer graphics card than most games) it will blow you away with the graphics. In addition, it is a fantastic survival sandbox for crafting, building, and pvping. There is nothing more satisfying than dropping a naked and taking all of their loot, or teaming up on a couple geared guys and winning all their gear. It's a game about cunning, creativity and domination. If you haven't already, please think about adding this to your steam library. It is a must have

About the Dev. Team
You hear a lot about "Devs" and what not. Short for developer. Basically, these people program the game and add in new content because, technically, the game is still being created, edited, and changed. Thus "Early access." Recently the dev team has been making some real poor choices, some consider. Instead of perfecting zombies and basic gear they jumped straight into making cars and whatnot. This is what some consider a flaw because the bae of the game is not yet completed. The persistance, meaning if I drop an item of clothing it stays there for a week until all servers reset, what not finished until some time later. They are just making choises that are all over.
Potential
This game has a good ammount of potential. If everyone came back it would be of more value, more money might be sunk into it, and overall there would be more fun. Basic economic rules apply as follows: Dayz is like a fax machine; if everyone in the world has one, then you can fax stuff to anyone in the world. Seems valuyble, right? But when people are havng a couple of errors and feel that mailing the faxed message would be faster, they stop buying the fax machine until only you and granny have a fax machine. Being that granny is old, doesn't understand tech, and doesn't like you annyways, the fax machine holds no value. Such is Dayz. Now that less people play, it is less fun unless you find a not full but nearly full pvp server. If it is hard to find people, oh well. The kill is that much better. But really, if more people play it is more fun. Potential still there, regardless of how many peple say the game is dead.
What this turns you into
When I first played Dayz I went onto the most populater servers and tried to say hi to everyone. Soon enough, people would just kill me on sight. Then I started beating fresh spawns up as a fresh spawn myself. Then I got better, found weapons easier, and basically started killing on sight. If they don't start talking in two seconds in any situation them *bam*. If they don't see me, and I say hello, and they do anything even remotely fishy, *bam*. If they draw, *bam*. Basically this game turns you into a monster. BUT you still have fun. Learn the hotspots for pvp in the new updates and you're golden.
Thanks for reading, looking for some DayZ fun or Ps2 or total war fun, look me up.

Welcome to Rust, the brutal, survival game that will have you tearing your hair out, laugh and cry, all on the same evening.  If you like games such as ARK, then this title is worth investigating. It offers extremely attractive graphics, full nudity plus a great and amazingly easy to use and follow HUD.
It is worth noting that you can't create your character, you will be given a random character of gender, creed and size.  If you are new to Rust I recommend finding a young or nearly empty server while you gain your feet.  Rust is a no mercy game.  Someone in full armour and the best weapons will not think twice about icing a guy who is naked, with a rock and new.
You have the freedom to build on almost anything and wherever you like. In water, up mountains, dry land.  The building system is simple and easy to use while providing the ability to build complex structures and upgrading materials used.  You learn with each new build better ways to construct strong bases that are harder to penetrate.
Rust for me was completely immersive, I found myself playing until the early hours without noticing.  Be aware this game is dramatically improved with friends and doesn't really work as a lone survival.  This is amazing for teams, communicating, working together, hunting in packs, bringing down choppers or racing for airdrops.
I love the freedom you have in choosing how to play:
- Be brutal, KOS and trounce them all.
- Play the nice guy, and then imprison them.
- RP a glorious city, trade and build stunning structures.
- Or just watch the Rusty world burn.
This game is in early access and there are bugs.  Bears clip through walls on the ground floor and kill you, rain clips through structures, items disappear through the ground and much more.  So it is worth bearing that in mind and not getting bent out of shape, trust me when I say, there are bigger issues to worry about.

Borderlands 2 is a great game! This sequel of Borderlands 2 really sucked me in to the Borderlands franchise, being my first Borderlands game. Despite no past knowledge of the game, it was a great journey with no dependency on an understanding of the previous game. The cartoonish style of the game lend themselves to the fast-paced shooter game, softening some of the harsher themes with a comedic tone, although after some conversations with other fellow game lovers, it has been established that the art style may be an acquired taste. The gameplay is fast paced from the get go, with the introduction featuring the love-hate character CL4P-TP (Claptrap) previously seen in Borderlands. From then on your led into the first of many adventures. A great improvement from the first game, and much desired feature regardless, is the top-quality voice-acting really adding that touch of life to the game, throughout the game. There is also a mini-map feature which for some, may be a great improvement on the compass feature in the first game.
Each quest is a real gem and sidequests are always tinted in humour, quests range from kill-quests, objectives and collect quests. Along the way you can earn badass tokens completing challenges, some which you may just stumble open, and many of which require you to interact with your environment which really rewards exploration whilst still showing that the game doesn't take itself too seriously. There are some challenges completable by doing puzzles and there are a few Easter eggs and jokes scattered along the way. Looting can be a bit problematic as someone can simply pick up what they want in the game, but if you've got some cooperative friends, it's just down to talking it out. Connecting up with friends has proved simple and easy, with all of my Borderlands 2 playthrough being with friends, so no issue there. Weapons, shields, class mods are all varied and greatly aid in personalising your playstyle, making the loot system very rewarding. The inclusion of eridium and enemies hidden within loot means that looting never gets boring or monotonous.
The character customisation is astronomically better than the first game, with the inclusion of heads and a greater range of colour schemes. DLC's have been released introducing additional characters Gaige (Mechromancer) and Krieg (Psycho), new skins and heads to customise your characters and more content and levels to beat in the game. Levelling is greatly rewarding with skill points rewarding at each level from 5 onwards, the talent trees are the same format as Borderlands but feel to be more important and interesting. After the first playthrough it almost becomes less about your initial skill and more about how you can customise your character through the skill tree. Additionally after your first playthrough, you can run through the game on higher difficulty with the chance of better loot. Through the use of the "Stash" you can pass beloved items through to your other characters and pretty much twink them out! The characters are made even more lovable and wacky with the inclusion of voice-acting for certain moves, looting, fight for your life, duelling and idling, though there is are no subtitles for these lines for the hard of hearing. Though a big thumbs up for the rest of the games subtitles! The music is fun although sometimes overwhelming what with the constant bombardment of gun noises and voice-acting.

What can I say about Borderlands 2 that hasn't already been said? It strives to be "more than" in all respects, pushing every boundary that it can find. Blacker humor (Shooty Face, anyone?), more hectic combat, wider varieties of enemies, and a greater number of weapons than you've encountered in every other game you've ever played put together. The DLC ranges from "okay" to "why can't all DLCs be this good?". Borderlands 2 even puts in a valiant attempt to add an end game (with raid bosses, of all things), which is all but unheard of in a First Person Shooter, even with the RPG elements.
My largest complaint about this game is that in order to push your characters to the level cap, you'll have to beat the storyline over and over again in True and Ultimate Vault Hunter Modes. Unless you just want to pick one of the six vault hunters as your main and ignore the others, you can easily have played through the first few chapters of the game ten or more times before maxing out a character, making successive playthroughs almost tedious.
That being said, Borderlands 2's flaws are few and far between, in my eyes. It can make you pull your hair out in frustration and then five minutes later have you laughing until you have a stitch in your side. The wild mania that is Borderlands 2 is an experience that no gamer should miss.

Borderlands 2 is a great game! This sequel of Borderlands 2 really sucked me in to the Borderlands franchise, being my first Borderlands game. Despite no past knowledge of the game, it was a great journey with no dependency on an understanding of the previous game. The cartoonish style of the game lend themselves to the fast-paced shooter game, softening some of the harsher themes with a comedic tone, although after some conversations with other fellow game lovers, it has been established that the art style may be an acquired taste. The gameplay is fast paced from the get go, with the introduction featuring the love-hate character CL4P-TP (Claptrap) previously seen in Borderlands. From then on your led into the first of many adventures. A great improvement from the first game, and much desired feature regardless, is the top-quality voice-acting really adding that touch of life to the game, throughout the game. There is also a mini-map feature which for some, may be a great improvement on the compass feature in the first game.
Each quest is a real gem and sidequests are always tinted in humour, quests range from kill-quests, objectives and collect quests. Along the way you can earn badass tokens completing challenges, some which you may just stumble open, and many of which require you to interact with your environment which really rewards exploration whilst still showing that the game doesn't take itself too seriously. There are some challenges completable by doing puzzles and there are a few Easter eggs and jokes scattered along the way. Looting can be a bit problematic as someone can simply pick up what they want in the game, but if you've got some cooperative friends, it's just down to talking it out. Connecting up with friends has proved simple and easy, with all of my Borderlands 2 playthrough being with friends, so no issue there. Weapons, shields, class mods are all varied and greatly aid in personalising your playstyle, making the loot system very rewarding. The inclusion of eridium and enemies hidden within loot means that looting never gets boring or monotonous.
The character customisation is astronomically better than the first game, with the inclusion of heads and a greater range of colour schemes. DLC's have been released introducing additional characters Gaige (Mechromancer) and Krieg (Psycho), new skins and heads to customise your characters and more content and levels to beat in the game. Levelling is greatly rewarding with skill points rewarding at each level from 5 onwards, the talent trees are the same format as Borderlands but feel to be more important and interesting. After the first playthrough it almost becomes less about your initial skill and more about how you can customise your character through the skill tree. Additionally after your first playthrough, you can run through the game on higher difficulty with the chance of better loot. Through the use of the "Stash" you can pass beloved items through to your other characters and pretty much twink them out! The characters are made even more lovable and wacky with the inclusion of voice-acting for certain moves, looting, fight for your life, duelling and idling, though there is are no subtitles for these lines for the hard of hearing. Though a big thumbs up for the rest of the games subtitles! The music is fun although sometimes overwhelming what with the constant bombardment of gun noises and voice-acting.
A solid game which focus a lot on squad based mechanism.

Other times there can be months with little more than what are basically new skins. Performance can rapidly sway patch to patch. Ah Borderlands... How many hours did I spent in the original game, playing online with my friends or with random people? The time just flew by.
AND NOW THAT EPICNESS IS BACK!
You will not believe just how much improvment this game brought. The visuals are a step forward, the customization reached a new height, but given how limited it was on the first one it is not that surprising...
And the the guns! My God, the guns. They are bigger, better, faster.... You see where I'm getting at.
Borderlands 2 is, overall, much better made then the first one.
However that is NOT the same as saying that 2 surpassed the original. Though Borderlands 2 has a better visual, gameplay, physics, it lacks greatly in the atmosphere, character design and dialogue.
The morbid and depraved feel that the original game had was somehow cut in half in its sequel, giving place to a more colourfull and joy filled atmosphere. The characters, though clearly still from the same bag as how they were introduced, have, saddly, lost what made them unique. Saddly I noticed this far more on my Borderlands character of election, Roland.
But he is not the only one, Claptrap, that "funny little robot", though explained, turned from, indeed, funny, to plain obnoxious, with only a handfull of rememberable dialogues.
Of course not all of the characters in this game turned out bad. The perfect example of this is Tiny Tina. And now this is where a lot of people will start shouting and asking if Claptrap is obnoxious, how come Tina isn't?
The answer is quite simple, good character design. Unless you invest some time towards finding out the story of this character, you won't know just how much this little girl is, I dare say, a must for both the game, and future content that may be released. She adds a new level of depth to the story, and actually makes you stop and think...
Other then that there is, though very rarely, a difficulty spike. Which isn't entirely bad since it keeps you on your toes. Wish there was more sounds, like the sound of wind, rakks flying by, something that would increase to the level of the atmosphere, rather then that music, which in my opinion could be better.
The story... It felt rushed. Let me express myself better. If you search the wiki, you'll know that there is A LOT of content that isn't revealed to the player in the games. Stuff that doesn't affect the game, but could affect how you see the characters. You can find the reasons as to why they are on Pandora, etc... And on that note, they could of have easily made a much longer game. Getting to the game's climax, the people who played it know what I mean, was a huge achievment and should be considered as such, it would be an epic pause to the narrative, if not for the game itself. Think Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix. At the end, we had lost more then what we had won, but instead of savouring that moment, the game rushed to the ending. Borderlands 2 can, in fact, create several moments in which it leaves the player to simply pause and collect their thoughts, pondering about what happen and what is bound to occur in the near future. Saddly it fails to use those moments to best create an intense atmosphere.
*sigh* Alright this took a turn down the wrong path... I wanted to say good things about it, but so far all I had was the guns, Tiny Tina, the guns, the visuals, the guns, some dialogues (yes, some are actually pretty well made, and give space for speculation and fan theories)... Oh, there is Gaige! Which is quite possibly the best playable character to walk on the surface of Pandora! Let's see, what else...
The customization of your character and your vehicles, the DLC, which again I fail to understand just why they didn't release the whole package on day one....
The gun fights themselves seem more... dynamic, easily going from a sniper duel between you and your friends against a group of psychos or nomads, to fight face to the face, don't forget, once you are that close, a shotgun is your best friend.
And then there is the guns! And no, I cannot, I simply cannot stress this enough, The guns in these game, specially snipers, are beyond.... everything! You have guns for everyone, small ones, big ones, ones that shoot red orbs of light that incenerate people, that bounce of the walls and go back to the enemies, that have a seeker bullet that zooms in on your target... The list goes on.
And this is for the weapons themselves, you still have the grenade mods, the shields, that now have more diversity. Just about everything that made the first Borderlands sell, is back in Borderlands 2 in force!
And to be honest, just what else do you need? This is the kind of game that is meant to be played with someone, the multiplayer experience is far superior to that of single player. This game IS a just and more then propper sequel to the game we all played for so many hours. This is the sequel we've been waitting for.
So grab your friends and join the hunt for the Vault(s)!

A game for the masses. The casuals, the hardcore and the lurkers.
Are you walking around endlessly, wondering what to do? Did you decide to check out this game, but yet aren't sure?
Do you want a game experience, that'll include hours upon hours, of hilarity and a good co-op and solo experience?
Borderlands 2 is just for you.
The game introduces you, and within the first minute you greet Claptrap. A robot you'll grow either fond of, or find to be like "Pinky" in Pinky and the Brain.
The voice acting in this game is beyond imagination, and the hilarity and focus upon entertainment and comedy is higher than I've ever experienced before.
Characters such as Tiny Tina, Marcus, Lillith and many more, greets you with a little cutscene, explaining their personality spot on. You'll get a specific, individual feeling about all of them, and you'll get to experience why.
The game introduces you to a story quest-line, but as you venture into the game, you'll quickly come to realize the numerous amount of side-missions available. The majority of those aren't of no reason, and feel dull and boring. No, in fact, many of them still focus on the great dialogue, and the exceptional story this game is so very known for.
The gameplay runs smooth, is very polished and introduces you to great characters, an RPG-type feeling, great opportunity to play with friends or just people you spoke with in the past. Even as far as new people!
There's great community groups, and easy ways of meeting other Borderlands 2 players.
If you find yourself getting lonely in Pandora, you can find new friends any moment you wish!
When you fight your way through the normal difficulty, you are quickly introduced to the second, more difficult experience that is "True Vault Hunter Mode" (and later the third difficulty; Ultimate Vault Hunter Mode), which will drastically increase in difficulty. You'll find some bosses seemingly impossible in a surprising manner, and normal Psychos, Varkids, Bullymongs and many more to swarm up on you, quickly making you a dead-man walking. An easy target.
But that's not it. When you think it gets close to unbearably difficult, you are introduced to the REAL game. The challenge that will or won't prove you worthy. But not to worry, you have lots of side-missions to prepare you for the challenges ahead, and tons of knowledge to learn about your class individually.
The endgame is filled with world-bosses, designed to be slain with friends, but could potentially be slain alone.
Seraph vendors selling some of the greatest loot, Tcoins giving you opportunity to buy legendary weapons in bucket-fulls, if you decide to invest your time in the game.
Rare loot, that you can farm for many hours, but still feel totally hyped about, jumping around once you finally see that pistol dropping.
The game also introduces you to several classes; Axton, Salvador, Maya and Zer0. (Plus Krieg and Gaige from DLC)
All with seperate skill-trees, ultimate-ability and playstyle.
Out of these classes, you are sure to find one that suits your individual taste in gameplay, and you'll soon find yourself growing incredibly fond of your character.
If you played the first Borderlands, you will find it funny that the old classes; Lillith, Brick, Mordecai and Roland are mission-givers, and support you as you venture into Pandora. Not only the old classes make a comeback, you'll also greet characters such as Scooter and Angel.
With genius dialogue, touching moments, awesome explosions, epic guns, polished gameplay, incredible voice acting and some of the best comedy in any game I've ever tried, I decide to rate this game with a well deserved 9/10, and certainly my zeal of approval.
Any fan of a game that supports individual playstyle, decisions and expectations will surely enjoy this game!
There aren't many flaws in this game, but I have to mention the few there is.
You can find yourself jumping around, trying to skip over a mountain to get to your objective in a quicker manner, but unfortunately see yourself getting stuck in a hole, having to save and quit, and start the past perhaps 10-15minutes over. (You will not lose your experience-progress, and I see this as a rather small flaw.)
The chances of a boss dying just as it jumps away, leading to it flying in the air is very slim, well, barely a possibility... But unfortunately it can happen that your loot will then fly off in the distance, impossible to find again. Either that, or it literally flew out of the map. Again, a very small flaw, that you possible won't ever see happening to you, but sure if a possibility.
When you progress in this game, there is a usualy flawless save-system, but it can be problematic. If your game bugs out just before another "checkpoint", you could end up having to spend those 10-15minutes again. I haven't found myself getting a roll-back, losing the XP I gained in the meantime, but I've heard of such.
The dialogue can be interrupted by talking to another characters at times, and you have no way of listening to it again, untill you get to next difficulty, or replay.
No seperate loot table (both a good and a bad thing, but when playing online, you can easily find people looting EVERYTHING there is, so you're left boned!) - There is a way to dupe items though, so if you co-op, you can essentially both get the item, if that's how you prefer it.
Unfortunately, this is a written review, so I will finish off here. And if you've read this far, I'm sure you're already filled in enough, so you feel ready to enjoy the unlimited amounts of fun and one of the most superior game experiences out there!
If you haven't yet gotten this game, I cannot do anything, but tell you: GET THE GAME. NOW.
It's amazing and unbelieveable- An experience you NEED to have!
Rating: 9/10, and my zeal of approval!
Pros:
- The dialogue in this game is beyond awesome.
- Gameplay is smooth, both for the casual and the hardcore.
- For both the social and the loner.
- Has one of the best villains ever!
- Ingenious eastereggs.
- Oceans of both story and optional missions.
- 100+ hours of incredible content.
- Lots of DLC to enjoy.
- A lot of endgame material.
Cons:
- Little to few bugs, glitches and exploits.
- Save-system can be problematic.
- No character-customization.
- Loot-system seems clunky to some.
I hope you enjoyed reading my review, and I hope I've inspired you to try out this amazing game!

When I first heard about Undertale, before it was actually released, it was getting a lot of negative press. Later, after it was released and some of the vitriol had died down, I heard that it was great, and worthy of Indie Game of the Year nomination. I had to see for myself.
The first thing I have to say is, I love the soundtrack. The mellow synth tunes take me back to the 16-bit console days of my youth, and the frantic and high energy battle music is very pokemon-reminiscent. Needless to say, I've had the whole soundtrack popping in and out of my head all day for the past week and a half.
I had a lot of fun talking to all the NPCs, which is one of my favorite things to do in RPGs - to talk to all the town NPCs and see what kinds of interesting things they have to say. The random humor you find in every interactable always hit me by surprise.
One thing I learned very early on is that Undertale is an RPG that attempts to defy all the tropes that define what an RPG is. Nothing ever seems to be as it is, and I'm hard pressed to say that there are no useless items in the game, even though the game tries to convince you that there are.
The boss battles are challenging. I like how color plays an important role in how the soul controls function. I actually found the game to be quite difficult until I switched from Keyboard/Mouse to an Xbox One controller, at which point I found that fights became significantly easier for me. I didn't find the puzzles terribly challenging, but I was also playing on the normal setting. I don't know if they get any harder as the difficulty rises.
The game really takes you on an emotional roller coaster. One minute you're laughing at the crazy antics of Sans and Papyrus, and the next you are hit with heavy-hitting themes like responsibility, consequences, death, social anxiety, unrequited love, and more. It's way more than just a game about chosing to kill or not kill.
The replayability on the game is high. I've only been through it once, and already I'm considering another playthrough to achieve a different ending, and the chance to find more secret stuff that I undoubtedly missed my first time around.
Final Verdict: Undertale is a work of art. Meant to be experienced and digested within a few hours, it's easy to appreciate the simplicity of the game on surface, but it has enough depth to give it a "thinker" status in my books. The gameplay is (most of the time) fun and engaging regardless of whether you prefer combat or pacifism. The soundtrack is hands down amazing. The art is well illustrated, and the graphics are what you might expect from a pixel-based RPG, though the game does make excellend use of space in both the foreground and background. In closing, Undertale is anything but Underrated, and it deserves all the praise it gets.

What can I say about Borderlands 2 that hasn't already been said? It strives to be "more than" in all respects, pushing every boundary that it can find. Blacker humor (Shooty Face, anyone?), more hectic combat, wider varieties of enemies, and a greater number of weapons than you've encountered in every other game you've ever played put together. The DLC ranges from "okay" to "why can't all DLCs be this good?". Borderlands 2 even puts in a valiant attempt to add an end game (with raid bosses, of all things), which is all but unheard of in a First Person Shooter, even with the RPG elements.
My largest complaint about this game is that in order to push your characters to the level cap, you'll have to beat the storyline over and over again in True and Ultimate Vault Hunter Modes. Unless you just want to pick one of the six vault hunters as your main and ignore the others, you can easily have played through the first few chapters of the game ten or more times before maxing out a character, making successive playthroughs almost tedious.
That being said, Borderlands 2's flaws are few and far between, in my eyes. It can make you pull your hair out in frustration and then five minutes later have you laughing until you have a stitch in your side. The wild mania that is Borderlands 2 is an experience that no gamer should miss.

Rust is an interesting Minecraft-like game with relatively advanced graphics, Game mechanics makes it feel realistic, at least at first. Hunger, thirst, and health levels need to be monitored after respawn. Strunggling for staying alive is definitely enjoyable for those short periods of time. Large reserves of food and water possible to consume prevent this aspect drom being irritating later on.
The next intriguing thing is that the character respawns with not even a part of colting, which need to be crafted each time. After a few minutes of uninterrupted game, player is able to buidl a simple shack and lay a sleeping bag there to have a constant point of respawn and hopefully a safe storage.
This is where the real fun part begins in my opinion. Developing a dwelling requires a combination of material gathering, blueprint hunting and securing obtained items. All three aspects are well balanced, so the game remains interesting until hitting the technology / space / server lifespan limit.
There are some aspects that could be corrected by now, even though the game is currently in alpha version. The most troubling defects are items falling through the ground (like some weapons, tools, granades), shooting, melee mechanics, large client-server traffic and missing terrain textures. Even considering these errors I find the game most interesting and I'll certainly be watching it develop.

Possibly the best expansion to Farmville to date!
Borderlands 2 takes off where Farmville leaves you wanting more! Ever wanted to have the redundant upkeep that farmville offers, but the mindless casual gaming experience of a first person shooter? WELL WISH NO MORE! For Borderlands 2 offers you that and much much more!
Not only can you farm in first person POV,  but by stroke of pure genius Gearbox and 2K games have managed get rid of pesky dialogue and storylines that seem to clutter up so many titles of any (AND EVERY LOL) genre.  Farm endlessly to get an EVEN BETTER WEAPON than before! Now you can use this weapon to continue mindlessly pressing right trigger (Left mouse button for stupid PC enthusiasts) in order to get an EVEN BETTER GUN!  Once you have the desired gun of choice... YOU CAN MINDLESSLY PRESS RIGHT TRIGGER AGAIN AND DO IT EVEN BETTER THAN THE LAST TIME!
I personally get disgusted when development teams take the time to clutter up your gameplay experience with a purpose.  Who even needs that??? And what's even better? Assuming you haven't hung yourself in your closet after realizing that your life has hit a new low... You can even explore NEW MAPS! These maps will consist of more WoW tier missions such as "GO TO OTHER SIDE OF MAP AND GET GUY WITH GUN",  "SHOW UP AT LOCATION AND MAKE SHOOTIES AT THIS GUY!", and who can forget the timeless classic mission "GO ACROSS MAP AND PRESS RIGHT TRIGGER OVER AND OVER AGAIN!" (still stuck on that mission, btw).
If these unique features weren't enough,  2K games and Gearbox have made it a point to upgrade the graphics substancially from "Silly and cartoonish" to "Silly and cartoonish + PhysX" for the percentage of the population that invested in an Nvidia card! That's right! You can now see small additional details while you are farming and pressing right trigger on endless loop!
The first time I played this game I was a little disappointed, as Gearbox decided to not allow me to import my Red Pepper fields directly from Farmville.  But after a while I grew to like it even more! Now I have six pistols (ALL IN WHICH FIRE ANY TIME I PRESS RIGHT TRIGGER),  Several items that give you health regeneration (FOR WHEN YOU NEED TO FARM JUST A LITTLE LONGER BUT DON'T SEEM TO HAVE THE HEALTH RESOURCES TO DO SO), and of course multiple types of grenades (FOR WHEN YOUR RIGHT TRIGGER FINGER IS SLIGHTLY SORE FROM EXCESSIVE USE)!
They even added the illusion of an RPG element to it by letting you level up and add all sorts of trivial stat boosts to your character! This way you can pretend to relate when people discuss wordy role playing games with you.  I personally have never been able to make it past the opening credits on a game like that.. TALK ABOUT BORING LOL!
I also recommend  this game to anyone who especially favors colors, sounds, loud noises, bright flashy lights, or when people make silly faces at you (SOMETIMES DAD CAN MAKE ME LAUGH A LOT WHEN HE MAKES A SILLY FACE AT ME LOL!!). This game will leave you on the edge of your wheelchair and ALWAYS screaming for more (which often sounds like "MOM I POOPED AGAIN")!
I give Borderlands 2 "FIVE DROOL CUPS UP" for combining my favorite facebook RPG (Farmville), and my favorite doctor prescribed activity to improve on my relatively impaired motor functions.  With any luck, we will rid the world of games with substance, and get everyone on a healthy rotation of charismatic cartoony CoD clones!

If you could bottle childlike innocence, pop culture comedy, and an engaging fairytale story and sell it as an 8 hour long game, you'd get Undertale.
When I first heard about Undertale, before it was actually released, it was getting a lot of negative press. Later, after it was released and some of the vitriol had died down, I heard that it was great, and worthy of Indie Game of the Year nomination. I had to see for myself.
The first thing I have to say is, I love the soundtrack. The mellow synth tunes take me back to the 16-bit console days of my youth, and the frantic and high energy battle music is very pokemon-reminiscent. Needless to say, I've had the whole soundtrack popping in and out of my head all day for the past week and a half.
I had a lot of fun talking to all the NPCs, which is one of my favorite things to do in RPGs - to talk to all the town NPCs and see what kinds of interesting things they have to say. The random humor you find in every interactable always hit me by surprise.
One thing I learned very early on is that Undertale is an RPG that attempts to defy all the tropes that define what an RPG is. Nothing ever seems to be as it is, and I'm hard pressed to say that there are no useless items in the game, even though the game tries to convince you that there are.
The boss battles are challenging. I like how color plays an important role in how the soul controls function. I actually found the game to be quite difficult until I switched from Keyboard/Mouse to an Xbox One controller, at which point I found that fights became significantly easier for me. I didn't find the puzzles terribly challenging, but I was also playing on the normal setting. I don't know if they get any harder as the difficulty rises.
The game really takes you on an emotional roller coaster. One minute you're laughing at the crazy antics of Sans and Papyrus, and the next you are hit with heavy-hitting themes like responsibility, consequences, death, social anxiety, unrequited love, and more. It's way more than just a game about chosing to kill or not kill.
The replayability on the game is high. I've only been through it once, and already I'm considering another playthrough to achieve a different ending, and the chance to find more secret stuff that I undoubtedly missed my first time around.
Final Verdict: Undertale is a work of art. Meant to be experienced and digested within a few hours, it's easy to appreciate the simplicity of the game on surface, but it has enough depth to give it a "thinker" status in my books. The gameplay is (most of the time) fun and engaging regardless of whether you prefer combat or pacifism. The soundtrack is hands down amazing. The art is well illustrated, and the graphics are what you might expect from a pixel-based RPG, though the game does make excellend use of space in both the foreground and background. In closing, Undertale is anything but Underrated, and it deserves all the praise it gets.

I used to defend this game. I used to state "It's still in EA, be patient."
It's evident to me now that the developers pulled a Sean Murray before he was even known.
The core mechanics of the game, the very simple movements of the player, the zombies, and vehicles relative to the game's world, are still very broken even after 4 years of development. Yes, while the core parts of the game, the vital lifeblood of DayZ has stagnated, the developers have done two good things.
They made the game look pretty and sound pretty.
Whoopdi-♥♥♥♥ing-doo.
Environment changes are cute and flashy and♥♥♥♥♥♥ but they are worthless while the core mechanics are still broken. DayZ will be releasing their beta soon on a new game engine, which has been over-hyped for over two years now. But I am not holding out for hope. There's a reason this game's community has died. No other successful EA game has had a drop off like this.
DayZ is not finished, and it is never going to be finished.
Let me walk you through the DayZ experience: you play for days gearing up, maybe getting killed a couple of times along the route. Then you reach Tisy at a good time. You get full army gear (because there's no reason to ever bother wearing anything but full army or ghillie), and then you build up a camp. Over time you collect every item worth collecting.
You collect all the medical supplies you can find even though they are completely useless and you will never use any of them outside of bandages/rags.
You will collect all the farming supplies even though you will never use them because why bother?
You will collect every gun, but you'll only ever use a glock/FNX or an AR or Winchester/Blaze 95.
You will collect every article of clothing but only ever wear the army set.
And then it happens. The game wipes persistence. The camp you spent weeks perfecting is gone. All that work made worthless.
So you run to Tisy, get an AK, and just start killing players until that gets boring, then you quit the game and regret spending 30$ on it.
Constant server wipes, game breaking bugs, random death glitches in a game that has permadeath, buggy zombies in a zombie game, buggy vehicles that cannot be driven, and OP Godly wolves that can teleport through walls and tank 15 axe swings to the skull each. This is what DayZ is.
Playing DayZ on day one of EA and playing it today offers an identical experience, which means in four years of development, despite all the fancy new ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t they added, we haven't made any meaningful progress.

When I bought this game, it was on sale for $15 way back when. That's an absolute bargain. It definitely lived up to being a full priced $60 game; so if you're getting it on sale, it's a steal. The big question would be "Should I get this or the GOTY edition?" Of course, as a fan of the game, I'd say GOTY all the way if you know you're going to want all the DLC and extra features. If you're unsure about the game itself, I'd recommend getting the regular version first. If you like it, you can always get the season pass which includes almost all the DLC you'd get with the GOTY edition.
The game is as advertised: Shoot, get loot, level up. The pacing is well done and it has a variety of enemies to keep the combat fresh. Think you've got killing loaders down? Wait until 3 or 4 different types show up the next fight. Boss fights are very well done. I'm very critical of games for their boss fights because I want them to be epic and a real challenge. There are certainly a couple ways to cheese through some bosses, but overall, the bosses in the game are very satisfying to fight.
I've actually spent quite a bit of time playing with a friend of mine from Germany (from the US myself) and other than the expected problems one would have connecting to halfway around the world, the game actually plays fairly well.
The story is one of the better stories I've seen in video games in a long time. To put it simply, you have to stop a guy named Handsome Jack. In spite of a very simple plot, there's some elements involved that are actually quite deep. Certainly caught me by surprise. Also, you do NOT have to play Borderlands 1 to understand the story. It would help, but just a bit. I'd say you might be missing out on 5-10% of the little references to the first game.
To sum it up, awesome game. Definitely one of my all time favorites now. Great dialogue, great characters, great gameplay, great replayability, great co-op action and great experience all around. I'll admit, some of the humour may turn off some people, but it's right up my alley. I think I've covered all the high points, hoped this helped you to make an informed decision. Cya!

How to start... Undertale is a fantastic game that I'd reccomend to just about anyone. The charm of the game lies in its characters and humor, as well as the universe's sentience that it is a video game. Between making friends with foes, bad skeleton puns, and an easy to pick up battle system, Undertale is a fantastic casual gaming experience with a lot of depth. HOWEVER, be careful of the fandom. Spoilers are everywhere on the internet, as well as people who will tell you there's only one proper order to get the various endings of the game in. Part of the Undertale experience is figuring out how your actions affect the universe, and everyone in it. The game loses some charm if those aren't decisions that you make for yourself. All in all, Undertale is certainly worth the money, and a game I can heartily reccomend to just about anyone!

Wow. That was a journey. As I am quite the impressionable girl, I was brought into this supposedly amazingly structured world filled with feeling I've not felt in a long time. I didn't expect much at first, but even within 5 minutes of actually playing the game, I was giddy. I was enthusiastic about playing as much as possible when I could. This feeling reminded me of playing the old Pokemon Mystery Dungeon games as a child. It was surreal.
Now on to what makes it such a great experience for not only me, but the thousands of other people who have played this game. Firstly, the way it presents itself. I went into the game nearly blind, knowing only the monster/human backstory, expecting some sort of quirky rpg that would be memorable, but not exactly phenomenal. It seemed friendly and cutesy, despite the horrifying murder attempt by Flowey.
I teared up. I have not teared up during a movie or video game since the aforementioned PMD series, though this time it was near the end of the second "generation" of the PMD games. I felt sad that I had to leave Toriel. Crying of laughter at the antics of Sans and Papyrus. Then, the looming threat of what was to come when I met Asgore. Awkward comparisons between myself and a few characters were a real hit it in head that showed me how real these characters are. No character (at least aside from some of the random monsters you talk to) was bland or stayed their welcome to long. It felt realistic. Sure flying a jetpack up a mountain of tables to get a can isn't exactly realistic, but you get the point.
Now that I've finished rambling about the things I personally loved, I'll now talk about the things that are good, regardless of what I think of them. The soundtrack is amazing, with it's collection of 9 songs. Though seriously, I feel that this changing around of one song into five was a good thing, as you'd pick up on these similar aspects and have a feeling of "Oh yeah, I did that thing that *wasn't* meaningless and mundane. The execution of emotional and funny moments is akin to a great book, or even a conversation with a friend. It all felt very real. If I were to continue onwards, I'd just be like a broken record, because I find this game outstanding.
I would definitely recommend this game to absolutely anyone that wants to play a fun and quirky game that has so much more to it than the "Nostalgia RPG" connotation people are giving it.

When I bought this game, it was on sale for $15 way back when. That's an absolute bargain. It definitely lived up to being a full priced $60 game; so if you're getting it on sale, it's a steal. The big question would be "Should I get this or the GOTY edition?" Of course, as a fan of the game, I'd say GOTY all the way if you know you're going to want all the DLC and extra features. If you're unsure about the game itself, I'd recommend getting the regular version first. If you like it, you can always get the season pass which includes almost all the DLC you'd get with the GOTY edition.
The game is as advertised: Shoot, get loot, level up. The pacing is well done and it has a variety of enemies to keep the combat fresh. Think you've got killing loaders down? Wait until 3 or 4 different types show up the next fight. Boss fights are very well done. I'm very critical of games for their boss fights because I want them to be epic and a real challenge. There are certainly a couple ways to cheese through some bosses, but overall, the bosses in the game are very satisfying to fight.
I've actually spent quite a bit of time playing with a friend of mine from Germany (from the US myself) and other than the expected problems one would have connecting to halfway around the world, the game actually plays fairly well.
The story is one of the better stories I've seen in video games in a long time. To put it simply, you have to stop a guy named Handsome Jack. In spite of a very simple plot, there's some elements involved that are actually quite deep. Certainly caught me by surprise. Also, you do NOT have to play Borderlands 1 to understand the story. It would help, but just a bit. I'd say you might be missing out on 5-10% of the little references to the first game.
To sum it up, awesome game. Definitely one of my all time favorites now. Great dialogue, great characters, great gameplay, great replayability, great co-op action and great experience all around. I'll admit, some of the humour may turn off some people, but it's right up my alley. I think I've covered all the high points, hoped this helped you to make an informed decision. Cya!

Spawned.
I open my sleepy eyes, as if I was asian, I viewed and wondered around the area that is now my soon to be home. Not understanding what true beauty it was to come, I found a rock, I gripped the beautifully shaped fossil, caressing it while it lay, resting in my soft but firm hands. I look into the unknown surrondings, viewing what resources I could possibly craft with this essential tool that I've just stumbled upon. I spot a bright but dim forest in the distance. Currently, surronded by mountains behind my back and jagged rocks to my sides, I look around for any other resources that I can gather while I'm pondering over this beautiful and majestic landscape. I viewed a rock so shiny, that it appeared to be as if the sun is sitting right in front of me, but it was a rock, covered in yellowish gradient, highlighting the very beauty that is bestowed right in front of my alerted eyes. I use the unforgettable tool that will eventually help me survive, I hit the rock. Bags of ores come out of the unkown rock by my feet. I inspected the ore. Sulfur.
After finding my way around this beautifully crafted map, I found a place to build my home. I've been gathering resources and other materials for weeks now, not spending any of it. Whilst searching for more materials such as Stone, Charcoal, Wood, Metal Ore and Sulfur Ore, I spotted my first animal in the wild. A Bear. Prior, I found my perfect place for my home, I crafted a wooden bow. Made out of oak wood and flax which I crafted into string, by a road, growing miraculously on its own. I knew this is the bow that will save my life and produce food for myself while surviving alone and scared. I then proceeded to craft arrows made out of oak wood and sharpened rocks that I've been collecting, I crafted my first arrow. I then continue to create more arrows as to which I knew it would soon save my life.
Once spotting the bear, I unholstered my bow, cocked a arrow and pulled back as if my life depended on it. Naked, the only thing I had besides the weapon, was my backpack, which was filled with all the materials that I've been collecting. I put manmade tar on the tip of my arrow, sparkling black it was, I put the excess tar back into my bag. I looked in the bag and pulled out a torch. I lit it from gun powder I've salvaged from an abandonded house, near the shore, I sparked the torch and lit the tip of my arrow on fire. I once again cocked back as hard as ever on my bow, aiming it towards the bear, while it sits, eatting a carcass of what it seems to be a human. I closed my left eye, my right eye focusing on my pray, I let the arrow go. The firery arrow, soaring threw the wind, sparks flying off the of tip of the arrow. Bullseye. I hit the bear in the neck, but it did not go down, it was stunned.
I quickly pulled back another arrow but this one was not on fire, I projected it once more, hitting the bear right in the middle of its ribs. It was mad. Myself, being on top of a rock, feeling secure and safe, I cocked back another arrow, thinking it would be the kill shot, I let go once more, striking the bear in the fohead. Borderlands 2 is a fun game. I laughed a lot during the story and every quest is filled with amazing voice acting. During your travels you'll meet many interesting and fun characters. Alongside the main story you have a bunch of fun epic quest arcs, some shorter than others but equally rewarding and interesting story behind them. You rarely feel like you are grinding or wasting your time with any of them.
The RPG elements gives depth to the gameplay and lets you customize your experience. All classes have a unique skill tree that lets you specialize in how you want to play. The endless amounts of different weapons also gives some aspects of uniqueness to your character but you'll soon find that they are more of the same.
The first person shooting is very well made. All weapons have fun effects and traits to them like exploding like a grenade when you reload or why not a shotgun that fires swords? Most enemies have a decent amount of health so you really want to land those crits. Some bosses however have a ridiculous amount of health points and makes the fight uninteresting and boring.
You can only fast travel from a number of fast travel stations. There's often very few of them and you sometimes feel like you're running from a to b for no reason. You sometimes find yourself at the wrong side of the map and have to run a long distance to get to the nearest fast travel station. There are however car stations here and there but the handling of the cars are so bad it's almost not worth to bother with.
Overall it's a great experience and there's content for more than 200h. I strongly recommend that you play co-op with some friends because you'll get more loot and they can give you a helping hand when you get downed.

It's one of the best games I've ever played! The story is amazing and well done. It's not a long game once you know what you're doing, but I've replayed this about 7 times now and don't find myself bored with the game at all. The story still makes me laugh, cry, and cheer as I progress through the game and I know it'll continue to do so for a long time, and I hope it will do the same for anyone else who plays Undertale.
Every character has a purpose and effect the outcome of the game depending on the player's choices. The characters don't feel like they were just tossed in with some dialog, Toby put a lot of feeling into the creation of every single character. The characters remind me of people I know in my own life, which is probably the same for others too, and that may give me some bias towards Undertale, but hey that just makes it all the more fun to play.
The music goes along perfectly for each area, battle, and character, and it's great to listen to outside of the game (I would say I wish I had bought the Game+Soundtrack together, but IMO this game deserves the extra few dollars for buying them separate).
The humor is on a whole new level. I don't know where Deadpool is at, but this game's 4th wall has been relentlessly shattered multiple times at the perfect moments. The jokes can be very corny, but it goes with the characters' personalities and the convenience of the jokes. Trust me, you'll either laugh out of humor or sheer disappointment.
TL:DR - There is none. The game is all about dialog, and if you can't read a simple review "You're going to have a bad time." I'll stop... Seriously though, the story is fantastic, the jokes are hilarious and corny, the soundtrack is one of a kind by far, and the characters are well defined and feel like actual characters! There's a reason Undertale is on most people's Top 5 Games list, including my own.
