Oh my gosh this game is so much fun! I loved the original when it first came out back in 2009. It was one of the first video games I tried. I had a hard time considering playing this game, knowing how much I truly enjoyed the first. I pre-ordered the game, and could not have been more wrong about not wanting to try it from the start. Borderlands 2 takes the world of Pandora to a whole new level. With a brand new set of playable characters, a flashback as old characters become NPCs, some familiar faces and places of the original, and an awesome villain that you want to hate but truly can't, you'll lose track of time as you immerse yourself in this totally redesigned world of Pandora. Gearbox has really prepared a truly awesome sequel.
The guns in this game are truly awe-inspiring. They've added so many cool, new guns that can be purchased or found while looting. They've improved the number of varieties and made elements like shock weapons and corrosive weapons more useful in the game. It's surprising how the first, which already had so many weapons, was able to add even more weapons to the game.
The new playable characters are so diverse and unique from the original game yet they still retain the original feel of the first game that made those characters so popular. Even the two DLC characters, Gaige and Kreig, add so much to the game. They are both new characters unlike the Borderlands world would ever expect to have and became some of my favorite characters to playthrough with. The trees are organized so much better and seem so much more useful for gameplay as well. Each spot you pick, you are actually able to tell impacts your character.
The world of Pandora is colored beautifully but still retains the feel of the Borderlands 1 world we loved so much; just with better coloring, lighting, and effects. I wanted to truly explore every area of Pandora just to see how dynamic this world had become and how different areas were shaded, colored, and weathered different. It was truly an experience I enjoyed, just looking at the diverse world around me that I felt like could be real.
Handsome Jack is an amazing addition to the game. He truly has some of the best and wittiest lines and his voice actor did such an amazing job with his dialogue. You wanted to hate him, but you couldn't. He's such an awesome villain and one to certainly never let your back turn towards.
Borderlands 2 is truly an amazing game that you should try. It will draw you in the minute you start playing and keep you holding on through every twist and curve the main and side quests offer you. You will loot to your hearts delight, shoot many bandits, and fight your way through each challenge the world will bring you. I recommend this game highly.
Good job Gearbox. You've truly outdone yourself with this one :)

No doubt you've already read countless reviews and heard every single mechanic about this game if you haven't already played it.
If you haven't- please don't let the fantastic reviews or the toxic fanbase put you off. Both of those often make me stay the heck away from popular games, but for some reason after watching half a Let's Play of Undertale I finally decided to buy and play it myself.

My first play through (as I mentioned, I had watched half a let's play before playing so I knew the basics for getting a pacifist run) I got 9 hours of play time. If I was gross enough to play a no-mercy run I'd easily have another 9 on top of that.
I would never have thought 9 hours would be enough to make me care deeply about every single pixellated character, but god-damn do I. I've never had problems with barrelling through legions of cute RPG monsters before, but suddenly the thought of attacking a single one fills me with dread.
It's a damn cheap game with an interesting (and pretty deep) storyline, a brand-new take (for once it's true) on RPGs, a ton of lovable characters and one of THE best soundtracks I've ever heard.
It won GOTY for a reason. If you haven't played it already, why the heck not?

REVIEW #2
Two years and poor grammar made me want to revisit this review.
DayZ is one of those games I keep coming back to, but every time I do, I leave feeling frustrated, exasperated, and disappointed. Since I last wrote my review, some of the problems I listed have been addressed, many have not, and brand new grievances have since bloomed.
So let's begin with a short list of reasons as to why you should not consider purchasing DayZ, this is a tl;dr for people who don't want to spend time reading the meat of this review.
Cons:
Poor performance across a broad range of hardware
Slow development cycle
Dated graphics
Persistent bugs and glitches
Distinct lack of content when compared to the DayZ mod
Poor UI
Poor community
Poor control scheme
I'll dissect the earlier complaints below, feel free to leave if you just needed that list.
Poor performance:
So why does DayZ Standalone suffer? It is after all a standalone game using the new Arma III engine, oh but wait it's not. DayZ SA uses a modified version of Real Virtuality 3 called 'Enfusion,' whereas Arma III uses Real Virtuality 4. The problem with Enfusion is that apart from a few quality of life adjustments to melee combat, graphical fidelity, and physics, it differs very little from RV3. This means DayZ SA has all the performance issues of the DayZ mod, such as poor fps in populated areas. While you may find your fps is higher in the Standalone than the mod or Arma II, it is still shockingly subpar on even enthusiast hardware. But so what right? Just turn the graphics settings down if it's bothering you that much. Well the graphical settings don't actually do all that much to change performance, they can certainly tank it but turning everything to the lowest settings will often net you fewer than 10 frames inside the cities. There are countless online guides which require .ini editing to enable developer graphical settings in a desperate attempt to raise fps, this is simply unacceptable. These performance issues become an even bigger problem when you realise how much they affect the fine movement required in DayZ. Aiming, inventory management, and interacting with objects are notoriously fiddly at the best of times, requiring good mouse control; but when the game is chugging along at 18fps in Elektro town centre it can feel impossible to shoot a target. What's more is other people could have paid for absolute cutting edge hardware that can almost reach the mythical 60fps target, giving them an absolute advantage over you in a firefight. If you're going to buy DayZ, prepare to fork out anywhere between £300 - 500 on new hardware.
Slow development cycle:
For an example on how to develop a game see Rust, a game not dissimilar to DayZ. The playrust website features weekly community and development blogs, accompanied by a bi-weekly update. The devs at Facepunch never fail to deliver on this, not without warning at least. DayZ on the other hand will often go months without a word from the dev team. A good example of this is the time it took between DayZ v0.60.133913 and v0.60.136348. The first version was released on the  20/07/16, and the second on 28/11/16. That's 4 whole months for a very minor update, not what you would expect for a game claiming to be in Early Access, a stage of game development where new features are a priority and new builds are released almost weekly. There have been some improvement to this slow cycle since, but don't expect too much from Bohemia.
Dated graphics:
Granted, DayZ was released in 2013, but as it is in alpha adjustments to graphics can be made at any time, that is what a true alpha stage is for. Despite being moved to a 64-bit client with enhanced lighting effects, DayZ still manages to look tacked together with inconsistent texture quality and almost plasticine character models. The game doesn't use any new graphical effects such as new anti-aliasing methods, or any of  what were unique selling points of Directx11. The game looks bland, and even with high anti-aliasing settings suffers from a blurriness of detail at distances and persistent jagged lines. The only good thing I have to say about DayZ's art style is the saturated and realistic colours, but good luck on enjoying these for more than an hour as you'll soon be wounded and seeing the world in black and white anyway.
Poor mechanics and persistent bugs and glitches:
This section could be very very long, so I'll just refer to some of the more common bugs, and question why day 1 glitches still haven't been fixed. If you buy DayZ prepare to see floating train tracks, prepare to see players and zombies clipping through walls, prepare to randomly lose loot when you drop it on the ground as very often it won't show up. Prepare to *clears throat:
Freeze to death after walking in a puddle
Break your legs falling 1 foot to the ground
Instead of falling, simply glide to the ground as physics do not exist in this game
Spam the same key over and over in a bid to get your character to do something (see vaulting)
Starve to death in 30 minutes
Die of dehydration in 30 minutes
Join server after server looking for loot that was all collected days ago
Get lamped by zombies that completely miss you
Completely miss all your melee attacks despite what the animation showed
Fall through staircases and get stuck forever
Bleed to death from a zombie's gentle pet (only bandages will stop bleeding, we all have leukemia apparently)
Obliterate your vehicle after a fender bender with a small shrub
Lose your mind
Lose your sanity
Uninstall this game
I'll add more to the list as and when I remember.
The point is, this game has a lot of issues, and many have existed since the game was first released. Despite several changes from Bohemia including new animations, and endless changelogs claiming to fix bugs, this game is still riddled with irritation and frustration. Further, what does work, is frustrating anyway. Bohemia don't seem to understand there needs to be a balance between fun and realism. DayZ is intended to be a realistic game, as was Arma II before it, but there is nothing realistic about inventory management, particularly with a UI like DayZ's. IRL if I am thirsty, and want to drink from my canteen, I will just do it, without thinking, I will reach to my belt or bag, pop the top off and have a drink, it's automatic, it's easy. In Dayz you must open your inventory, and right click on the canteen, and then drink it. It's not intuitive, it's not natural, it's artificial when compared to say a drink canteen keybinding. And this is persistent throughout, between chambering rounds and yeah at one point simply reloading, you'll find yourself in the UI more than the game, fiddling with prompts while a bandit shoots at your feet.
Lack of content:
Compared to the mod there are less guns, vehicles and general items. The only thing SA has on the mod is locations and junk items. Who can forget 2014 where all we received all year were useless cosmetics that served no gameplay purpose. If you bought the SA for planes and helicopters you will be disappointed.
Poor Community:
Rampant fanboyism and a fervent defense of griefing does not a good community make. Criticising DayZ is sacrilege and you will be lambasted by the Bohemia Brigade wherever you post it. The problem with attacking other players isn't so much the combat, it's the motivation. Often bandits will shoot fresh spawns with no gear simply because they can, not because they need to, or even if that spawn is aware they are there and a threat. This puts people off the game, and installs a ceiling on new players, making it very hard to climb up.
Poor Controls:
I touched on it earlier with the UI complaints but interacting in DayZ is all about character position and being lucky enough to catch your mouse in the right place, expect to stand near a door looking around for the sweetspot where yes you can press middle-mouse and open it.

Welcome to Undertale,
A game which tries it's hardest to break the conventions of the video game. A game that makes it feel as if it's entire goal is for you to explore yourself rather than the world that you, the player character, have been thrust into. The first question it asks is "Who are you?" It asks your name, and you decide who you'll be when you pick said name.
I found that it is a game of personal growth, and achievement rather than of the character's growth and achievement. It's a challenging game, with the biggest thing to stop you from doing everything is the time you put into it. This is a very small game if you try to beat it, but if you try to learn it, it's quite massive, with options and missable dialogue, and characters that can be humorous no matter how many times you view them.
This game is enjoyable the first time, so long as you're open to different choices in control and how to play. This first time I played through this game, I took the true pacifist route. It made me so satisfied, (happy wasn't quite the right term there.) that I HAD to play on a different computer in order to play again, I didn't want to remove some happiness from what is effectively lines of cope programmed to show pixels and a quirky font depending on who is talking.
The second time, I decided I wanted to do a genocide run... As I started, the ruins was the easiest to go through. I had done it, and killing the boss of the ruins was quite underwhelming, I was hoping for something different, something to give me more determination, but I wasn't really satisfied with killing it.
As I went on, the game got more and more dark, it went from this happy, quirky game, into a living nightmare. I was told I was gonna have a bad time by a character pretty early on in the game. To be honest, he was right. I was having a bad time, but not because it was hard, it was because of all of that of which I stand for, all of my heart told me to stop, to not keep going about half way through, I kept going because I was determined. When more and more of the game started making me feel worse and worse, I started wishing to turn around, and re-do it all. It finally climaxed when I reached the final boss of the genocide route.
I decided that it was high time for me to finally learn what I was getting into. I cheated myself out of the disgust, and looked it up, and I found out that it wasn't worth it. All of that hard work, all of that extra work that I planned on doing, I wouldn't be able to reconcile with myself for finishing the genocide run for that reward thereafter. I used the ultimate ability of the main character of the game, the ability to use saves to load her "DETERMINATION" to an earlier time to try again at a specific part of the game. I decided against doing the run that left one's hand caked with dried blood, I decided that I wasn't that type of person, and turned my save around. This game deserves all of the respect it is given, (although the fanboys might be a little exaggerating of it) and most of all, it deserves the time people have decided to put into it. This game is a good purchase if you're into the story of a game, or if you're into characters. If you want to take your time out to try and solve one of this games theories, DON'T. You'll only end up spoutting non-sense or coming up with a premise of a !crack-fic.
TL;DR
Buy the game if you want good characters or story, don't buy the game if you want the standard RPG. Be warned, this game will make you work for your happy AND your bad endings though.

REVIEW #2
Two years and poor grammar made me want to revisit this review.
DayZ is one of those games I keep coming back to, but every time I do, I leave feeling frustrated, exasperated, and disappointed. Since I last wrote my review, some of the problems I listed have been addressed, many have not, and brand new grievances have since bloomed.
So let's begin with a short list of reasons as to why you should not consider purchasing DayZ, this is a tl;dr for people who don't want to spend time reading the meat of this review.
Cons:
Poor performance across a broad range of hardware
Slow development cycle
Dated graphics
Persistent bugs and glitches
Distinct lack of content when compared to the DayZ mod
Poor UI
Poor community
Poor control scheme
I'll dissect the earlier complaints below, feel free to leave if you just needed that list.
Poor performance:
So why does DayZ Standalone suffer? It is after all a standalone game using the new Arma III engine, oh but wait it's not. DayZ SA uses a modified version of Real Virtuality 3 called 'Enfusion,' whereas Arma III uses Real Virtuality 4. The problem with Enfusion is that apart from a few quality of life adjustments to melee combat, graphical fidelity, and physics, it differs very little from RV3. This means DayZ SA has all the performance issues of the DayZ mod, such as poor fps in populated areas. While you may find your fps is higher in the Standalone than the mod or Arma II, it is still shockingly subpar on even enthusiast hardware. But so what right? Just turn the graphics settings down if it's bothering you that much. Well the graphical settings don't actually do all that much to change performance, they can certainly tank it but turning everything to the lowest settings will often net you fewer than 10 frames inside the cities. There are countless online guides which require .ini editing to enable developer graphical settings in a desperate attempt to raise fps, this is simply unacceptable. These performance issues become an even bigger problem when you realise how much they affect the fine movement required in DayZ. Aiming, inventory management, and interacting with objects are notoriously fiddly at the best of times, requiring good mouse control; but when the game is chugging along at 18fps in Elektro town centre it can feel impossible to shoot a target. What's more is other people could have paid for absolute cutting edge hardware that can almost reach the mythical 60fps target, giving them an absolute advantage over you in a firefight. If you're going to buy DayZ, prepare to fork out anywhere between £300 - 500 on new hardware.
Slow development cycle:
For an example on how to develop a game see Rust, a game not dissimilar to DayZ. The playrust website features weekly community and development blogs, accompanied by a bi-weekly update. The devs at Facepunch never fail to deliver on this, not without warning at least. DayZ on the other hand will often go months without a word from the dev team. A good example of this is the time it took between DayZ v0.60.133913 and v0.60.136348. The first version was released on the  20/07/16, and the second on 28/11/16. That's 4 whole months for a very minor update, not what you would expect for a game claiming to be in Early Access, a stage of game development where new features are a priority and new builds are released almost weekly. There have been some improvement to this slow cycle since, but don't expect too much from Bohemia.
Dated graphics:
Granted, DayZ was released in 2013, but as it is in alpha adjustments to graphics can be made at any time, that is what a true alpha stage is for. Despite being moved to a 64-bit client with enhanced lighting effects, DayZ still manages to look tacked together with inconsistent texture quality and almost plasticine character models. The game doesn't use any new graphical effects such as new anti-aliasing methods, or any of  what were unique selling points of Directx11. The game looks bland, and even with high anti-aliasing settings suffers from a blurriness of detail at distances and persistent jagged lines. The only good thing I have to say about DayZ's art style is the saturated and realistic colours, but good luck on enjoying these for more than an hour as you'll soon be wounded and seeing the world in black and white anyway.
Poor mechanics and persistent bugs and glitches:
This section could be very very long, so I'll just refer to some of the more common bugs, and question why day 1 glitches still haven't been fixed. If you buy DayZ prepare to see floating train tracks, prepare to see players and zombies clipping through walls, prepare to randomly lose loot when you drop it on the ground as very often it won't show up. Prepare to *clears throat:
Freeze to death after walking in a puddle
Break your legs falling 1 foot to the ground
Instead of falling, simply glide to the ground as physics do not exist in this game
Spam the same key over and over in a bid to get your character to do something (see vaulting)
Starve to death in 30 minutes
Die of dehydration in 30 minutes
Join server after server looking for loot that was all collected days ago
Get lamped by zombies that completely miss you
Completely miss all your melee attacks despite what the animation showed
Fall through staircases and get stuck forever
Bleed to death from a zombie's gentle pet (only bandages will stop bleeding, we all have leukemia apparently)
Obliterate your vehicle after a fender bender with a small shrub
Lose your mind
Lose your sanity
Uninstall this game
I'll add more to the list as and when I remember.
The point is, this game has a lot of issues, and many have existed since the game was first released. Despite several changes from Bohemia including new animations, and endless changelogs claiming to fix bugs, this game is still riddled with irritation and frustration. Further, what does work, is frustrating anyway. Bohemia don't seem to understand there needs to be a balance between fun and realism. DayZ is intended to be a realistic game, as was Arma II before it, but there is nothing realistic about inventory management, particularly with a UI like DayZ's. IRL if I am thirsty, and want to drink from my canteen, I will just do it, without thinking, I will reach to my belt or bag, pop the top off and have a drink, it's automatic, it's easy. In Dayz you must open your inventory, and right click on the canteen, and then drink it. It's not intuitive, it's not natural, it's artificial when compared to say a drink canteen keybinding. And this is persistent throughout, between chambering rounds and yeah at one point simply reloading, you'll find yourself in the UI more than the game, fiddling with prompts while a bandit shoots at your feet.
Lack of content:
Compared to the mod there are less guns, vehicles and general items. The only thing SA has on the mod is locations and junk items. Who can forget 2014 where all we received all year were useless cosmetics that served no gameplay purpose. If you bought the SA for planes and helicopters you will be disappointed.
Poor Community:
Rampant fanboyism and a fervent defense of griefing does not a good community make. Criticising DayZ is sacrilege and you will be lambasted by the Bohemia Brigade wherever you post it. The problem with attacking other players isn't so much the combat, it's the motivation. Often bandits will shoot fresh spawns with no gear simply because they can, not because they need to, or even if that spawn is aware they are there and a threat. This puts people off the game, and installs a ceiling on new players, making it very hard to climb up.
Poor Controls:
I touched on it earlier with the UI complaints but interacting in DayZ is all about character position and being lucky enough to catch your mouse in the right place, expect to stand near a door looking around for the sweetspot where yes you can press middle-mouse and open it.

Oh my gosh this game is so much fun! I loved the original when it first came out back in 2009. It was one of the first video games I tried. I had a hard time considering playing this game, knowing how much I truly enjoyed the first. I pre-ordered the game, and could not have been more wrong about not wanting to try it from the start. Borderlands 2 takes the world of Pandora to a whole new level. With a brand new set of playable characters, a flashback as old characters become NPCs, some familiar faces and places of the original, and an awesome villain that you want to hate but truly can't, you'll lose track of time as you immerse yourself in this totally redesigned world of Pandora. Gearbox has really prepared a truly awesome sequel.
The guns in this game are truly awe-inspiring. They've added so many cool, new guns that can be purchased or found while looting. They've improved the number of varieties and made elements like shock weapons and corrosive weapons more useful in the game. It's surprising how the first, which already had so many weapons, was able to add even more weapons to the game.
The new playable characters are so diverse and unique from the original game yet they still retain the original feel of the first game that made those characters so popular. Even the two DLC characters, Gaige and Kreig, add so much to the game. They are both new characters unlike the Borderlands world would ever expect to have and became some of my favorite characters to playthrough with. The trees are organized so much better and seem so much more useful for gameplay as well. Each spot you pick, you are actually able to tell impacts your character.
The world of Pandora is colored beautifully but still retains the feel of the Borderlands 1 world we loved so much; just with better coloring, lighting, and effects. I wanted to truly explore every area of Pandora just to see how dynamic this world had become and how different areas were shaded, colored, and weathered different. It was truly an experience I enjoyed, just looking at the diverse world around me that I felt like could be real.
Handsome Jack is an amazing addition to the game. He truly has some of the best and wittiest lines and his voice actor did such an amazing job with his dialogue. You wanted to hate him, but you couldn't. He's such an awesome villain and one to certainly never let your back turn towards.
Borderlands 2 is truly an amazing game that you should try. It will draw you in the minute you start playing and keep you holding on through every twist and curve the main and side quests offer you. You will loot to your hearts delight, shoot many bandits, and fight your way through each challenge the world will bring you. I recommend this game highly.
Good job Gearbox. You've truly outdone yourself with this one :)

Welcome to Undertale,
A game which tries it's hardest to break the conventions of the video game. A game that makes it feel as if it's entire goal is for you to explore yourself rather than the world that you, the player character, have been thrust into. The first question it asks is "Who are you?" It asks your name, and you decide who you'll be when you pick said name.
I found that it is a game of personal growth, and achievement rather than of the character's growth and achievement. It's a challenging game, with the biggest thing to stop you from doing everything is the time you put into it. This is a very small game if you try to beat it, but if you try to learn it, it's quite massive, with options and missable dialogue, and characters that can be humorous no matter how many times you view them.
This game is enjoyable the first time, so long as you're open to different choices in control and how to play. This first time I played through this game, I took the true pacifist route. It made me so satisfied, (happy wasn't quite the right term there.) that I HAD to play on a different computer in order to play again, I didn't want to remove some happiness from what is effectively lines of cope programmed to show pixels and a quirky font depending on who is talking.
The second time, I decided I wanted to do a genocide run... As I started, the ruins was the easiest to go through. I had done it, and killing the boss of the ruins was quite underwhelming, I was hoping for something different, something to give me more determination, but I wasn't really satisfied with killing it.
As I went on, the game got more and more dark, it went from this happy, quirky game, into a living nightmare. I was told I was gonna have a bad time by a character pretty early on in the game. To be honest, he was right. I was having a bad time, but not because it was hard, it was because of all of that of which I stand for, all of my heart told me to stop, to not keep going about half way through, I kept going because I was determined. When more and more of the game started making me feel worse and worse, I started wishing to turn around, and re-do it all. It finally climaxed when I reached the final boss of the genocide route.
I decided that it was high time for me to finally learn what I was getting into. I cheated myself out of the disgust, and looked it up, and I found out that it wasn't worth it. All of that hard work, all of that extra work that I planned on doing, I wouldn't be able to reconcile with myself for finishing the genocide run for that reward thereafter. I used the ultimate ability of the main character of the game, the ability to use saves to load her "DETERMINATION" to an earlier time to try again at a specific part of the game. I decided against doing the run that left one's hand caked with dried blood, I decided that I wasn't that type of person, and turned my save around. This game deserves all of the respect it is given, (although the fanboys might be a little exaggerating of it) and most of all, it deserves the time people have decided to put into it. This game is a good purchase if you're into the story of a game, or if you're into characters. If you want to take your time out to try and solve one of this games theories, DON'T. You'll only end up spoutting non-sense or coming up with a premise of a !crack-fic.
TL;DR
Buy the game if you want good characters or story, don't buy the game if you want the standard RPG. Be warned, this game will make you work for your happy AND your bad endings though.

Here's a little REAL story that I've endured over the time I played this beautiful game from many years ago when this game was first created.
Spawned.
I open my sleepy eyes, as if I was asian, I viewed and wondered around the area that is now my soon to be home. Not understanding what true beauty it was to come, I found a rock, I gripped the beautifully shaped fossil, caressing it while it lay, resting in my soft but firm hands. I look into the unknown surrondings, viewing what resources I could possibly craft with this essential tool that I've just stumbled upon. I spot a bright but dim forest in the distance. Currently, surronded by mountains behind my back and jagged rocks to my sides, I look around for any other resources that I can gather while I'm pondering over this beautiful and majestic landscape. I viewed a rock so shiny, that it appeared to be as if the sun is sitting right in front of me, but it was a rock, covered in yellowish gradient, highlighting the very beauty that is bestowed right in front of my alerted eyes. I use the unforgettable tool that will eventually help me survive, I hit the rock. Bags of ores come out of the unkown rock by my feet. I inspected the ore. Sulfur.
After finding my way around this beautifully crafted map, I found a place to build my home. I've been gathering resources and other materials for weeks now, not spending any of it. Whilst searching for more materials such as Stone, Charcoal, Wood, Metal Ore and Sulfur Ore, I spotted my first animal in the wild. A Bear. Prior, I found my perfect place for my home, I crafted a wooden bow. Made out of oak wood and flax which I crafted into string, by a road, growing miraculously on its own. I knew this is the bow that will save my life and produce food for myself while surviving alone and scared. I then proceeded to craft arrows made out of oak wood and sharpened rocks that I've been collecting, I crafted my first arrow. I then continue to create more arrows as to which I knew it would soon save my life.
Once spotting the bear, I unholstered my bow, cocked a arrow and pulled back as if my life depended on it. Naked, the only thing I had besides the weapon, was my backpack, which was filled with all the materials that I've been collecting. I put manmade tar on the tip of my arrow, sparkling black it was, I put the excess tar back into my bag. I looked in the bag and pulled out a torch. I lit it from gun powder I've salvaged from an abandonded house, near the shore, I sparked the torch and lit the tip of my arrow on fire. I once again cocked back as hard as ever on my bow, aiming it towards the bear, while it sits, eatting a carcass of what it seems to be a human. I closed my left eye, my right eye focusing on my pray, I let the arrow go. The firery arrow, soaring threw the wind, sparks flying off the of tip of the arrow. Bullseye. I hit the bear in the neck, but it did not go down, it was stunned.
I quickly pulled back another arrow but this one was not on fire, I projected it once more, hitting the bear right in the middle of its ribs. It was mad. Myself, being on top of a rock, feeling secure and safe, I cocked back another arrow, thinking it would be the kill shot, I let go once more, striking the bear in the fohead. The bear running towards me, ran up a 90 degree rock and slaughtered me. Thanks Rust for being glitchy as ♥♥♥♥. :)

Undertale is a story-driven, bullet-hell, rpg with an amazing 50 song+ soundtrack designed by indie developer Toby Fox, and it's a good one at that. The game features a complex combat system that has four action options; Fight, Act, Item, Mercy. Now you may be familiar with two of those options but Undertale brings a fresh take to the rpg genre by giving you the option to resolve combat scenario's with peaceful alternatives. Undertale is an rpg where NOBODY has to DIE if you don't want them to and that in and of itself gives you a great idea of what you're exactly getting.
Yes and No. The game has a lot of similiarties to RPG's but is fundamentally more of a bullet-hell. The premise of the game's combat mainly relies on dodging white pellets in a small square box. Aside from this Undertale does share a lot of similiarties to other RPGs such as a character-centric narrative and stat progression.
Undertale's story is set in a fictional underground comprising of a society of monsters who have been banished from the surface after a long war against humans. You, a human who has fallen down into the underground, must journey through this dungeon to find your way back to the surface. Along the way you meet many different monsters, all featuring an array of personalities, and often having an effect on the games outcome. Toby fox leaves nothing to be desired in his story, and from start to finish it is absolutely captivating. Witty narrative, immersive personalities, and a
are all but just a few words to describe this incredible game.

Undertale.
Pros:
- Good soundtrack.
No, seriously. Go give it a listen.
- The combat.
It's a bit weird, but I found it to be pretty okay once I got used to it.
You have to time your attacks, but you also have to dodge enemies' attacks.
By the way, the enemies are pretty bullet-hellish. That's what makes it -really- fun.
- The story, plot, and characters.
If you're playing Undertale and you already know what's going to happen, it wouldn't be a good experience anymore. The story, plot, and characters are pretty much what's going to keep you going if the combat and graphics don't cut it for you. It's an emotional, crazy, fun ride.
- Dialogue.
Just get past the "tutorial section" and you'll know what I mean.
Neutral Points, Also may be Cons:
- Graphics.
I'm a big fan of pixel art and stuff, but I'm pretty sure not everyone is.
Plus, combat is in black & white, which also might not appeal to everyone.
- Game length.
I went through it pretty fast, but that's mainly because I was binging it and didn't really stop to look around and explore. I'd say a regular playthrough would last around 2.5 - 3.5 hours. Though, I'd say the game length doesn't matter; the content does.
Stuff and Verdict:
I'm trying my best not to spoil anything because Undertale is meant to be played through blind. Seriously. Knowing what to do and knowing what happens because of what you did will take away a LOT of the enjoyment from the game. If you do plan on buying the game, avoid spoilers. Don't go on any subreddit or watch an LP of a YouTuber. Pick up the demo, see if you like it, then pick the game up. Once again, Undertale is an experience that'll stick with you for the rest of your gaming life if you do decide to grab it.
Score: 9/10.

+High replayabity.
Cons:

The game has a lot of potential and could become something amazing in the distant (VERY DISTANT) future. At every new patch i hop on to see what has changed and to see if that the game has made new progressive. The game still runs like crap and does look awful at time, but the gaming experience is slowly becoming more enjoyable. The devs have gone through stages of having tons of high grade loot spawning everywhere (recently) to literally no loot at all which is a shame, but hey it's still aplha to be honest. I wish that if the devs didn't just rush out the game in it's very early life stages (trees looked like thin little sticks haha) to rob our money then people might of gave it less hate, but that is the devs fault and now they are paying the price for it with less and less people buying it. The streamers make it seem so cool and EPIC! but without other mates you'll realize how lonely and un-exciting it really is sorry. On the bright side hackers are about as rare as finding a heli crash site with it's full millitary loot intact hahaha. If i was you i would wait until it's beta if you don't like 1/8 finished games, or wait until it's full release as right now the devs are only robbing us effectively. Undertale is an exceptional game.  It is incredibly charming and funny and deep.  It made me smile, it made me laugh, it made me angry, it made me feel genuinely clever, it made me feel like a badass, it made me feel like a helpless child, it made me grieve, it made me feel disgusted with myself as a player, and it damn near made me cry on a couple occasions.  Despite all those selling points, it is very difficult for me to write a convincing recommendation without spoiling anything due to the fact that I, with the entirety of my being, suggest that anyone going in to this game, do so blindly and with as little knowledge of the game as possible so that they may experience all the things that I did as purely as possible.  However, I understand that some may be hesitant to blindly invest in something they know nothing about, so this is my recommendation to you:
Read up on Steam’s refund policy, which can be found here:
At the time of writing, Steam’s policy is that you may return a game so long as you submit a request for return within fourteen days of purchasing the game and you’ve played less than two hours of the game; therefore:
Once the timer goes off, decide if you wish to return the game or not.  Within the first hour and a half of the game, you get an excellent taste of three of the game’s four selling points – the mechanics, the humor, and the music.
(Oh, and a small suggestion once you’ve purchased the game: right click on it in your library, go to Properties, then the Updates tab, and then at the bottom, make sure you uncheck the box marked “Enable Steam Cloud synchronization for Undertale.” It ended up causing me some issues)
Then allow me to expand on those three points.
Undertale uses a combination of systems for the “combat” mechanics.  When attacking, you are required to hit your attack button at just the right time for bonus damage and when under attack, you dodge your opponents’ attacks in a style reminiscent of bullet-hell games.  Even as someone who is not a fan of bullet-hell games, I enjoyed this very much.  Throughout the game, there are slight variations on these mechanics which keep this aspect of gameplay fresh and interesting.
At times, this can be a very light and humorous game.  Just like the gameplay mechanics, the kind of humor gets varied throughout the game as well.  From cheesy puns to slapstick humor to just plain-old humor because I don’t know how else to describe it, this game covers a fair scope of different types of humor.  There were some times where I felt that the game was just being random to try and elicit a cheap laugh, but that’s okay since the variety in humor means that you’re not overexposed to one specific element of humor the entire game.
The music was stellar and complimented the game well; I still find certain tunes getting stuck in my head.  There’s not much to say about this point; it has to be experienced on one’s own.

I played this again recently after I bought this game near enough day 1 on release, and really apart from extra content I can't see that they've really resolved any of the main structural problems. Zombies still are basically broken (to the enxtent they've had to remove them from the game), vehicles are in but buggy as hell and that goes for most of the other features in the game. In short this game still has a long way to go before it becomes an enjoyable game for me.
Basically I'd wait for them to do a final release for the game and then do what they had to do with Arma 3 and patch the hell out of it to actually get it to a state where it has a decent fps. So in other words come back in about 2017-18 and check progress.
**So here I am in August 2017 I've played a few extra hours what's new? Well I don't know if maybe some of you are old enough to remember Monty Python and the Holy Grail, but there's a scene where John Cleese is  like 100m away from running toward these guards and not getting any closer. The guards are looking at him then to each other like 'err... wtf' kind of way. Then suddenly blam he's right on them! Well I was delighted to be reminded of this in DayZ a Zombie was following me and I was like those guards 'cool he's 100m away I've got thinking time'. Boy was I mistaken when he magically appeared next to me. So Zombies are still broken then (this wasn't the only observed error in 3 or so hours of gameplay). In fairness however they are at least back in the game and do somewhat actually acknowledge buildings now (when they're not clipping through them) so there has been some improvement in the 2 years since I wrote this review. Hey maybe in another 2-3 years I can review the completed game!
In general the game's UI still seems at best clunky with it's own internal logic that works, but is just annoying to use. If you're used to ARMA games it's ok (ok is the best way to describe it), but if not it's like you have to put together a weird holistic puzzle.**

Borderlands 2
I just bought Borderlands 2 in Autumnsale and I really ask myself why I didn't buy it sooner. I already played the first part of Borderlands and I just liked it. The 2nd part is even better.
The Story
I just bought it and don't have that much time, but the part I've already played is really great. It's a big world with many locations and groups of bandits. I like games with so much background to study, but you don't need to know what's actually going on in Pandora. It doesn't harm the gameplay if you aren't interested in the backgrounds.
I think it's also great, that you meet all the playable characters from the first part(like Roland, Lilith,...)
The Controls
The Controls are just like in every other videogame on the PC, but what I didn't like is that you can'T control cars with w-a-s-d but with w-s and the mouse. But driving like that can be really funny, especially if you play with some friends.
The graphics
I can't really say anything about graphics because my PC isn't very young anymore and I can't play it on the highest graphic. But for my stanard the graphic is good. The game doesn't try to look like it was real, but it is more comic style.
The atmosphere
The atmosphere is really great. Even tough the game is in comic style you may feel like you are in there. The action never stops because you are all the time surrounded by monsters or bandits.
The Multiplayer
In the multiplayer you can play the story together with your friends. If another player joins the monsters become stronger. multiplayer is REALLY fun. I can't describe it but I think it's about 5 times more fun if you play with friends. If you knife or hit them you can challenge your friends by dueling.
But I think the developers could even make more out of the multiplayer like searching the other one and eliminate him or hunting challenges but it's also very much fun to play the story together.
The conclusion
To sum up I really enjoy Borderlands 2 and I'm going to play it more soon. The Story is great, driving cars is much fun, I can't really say anything about graphics, the atmosphere is great and the multiplayer is the best thing in game.
I can only recommend the game to everyone and I would definitely buy a third part of the series.

EDIT: It's now September 2017 and my recommendation of DayZ still stands. Last March I jumped into ARK and spent over 1000 hours having a lot of fun and a whole bunch of grind. I played PVE because the build/grind/kill/lose-it-all path ain't my thing. I also was on their official servers since I wanted unpredictable interactions with whomever got on the server - not just known friends or RP players. With all the yak on the DayZ reviews relating to its release I think it is worth mentioning that the way the ARK devs did it makes the DayZ devs appear as simple, honest country folk with regards to LYING TO YOUR PLAYER BASE. That's a big part of my coming back to DayZ.
Many DayZ reviews ignore the 'computer science' part of its development and that's understandable since most of its players are ignorant about programming. The conversion of the original ARMA II mod to the various subsystems and engine to be used in the released game is about like having your skeleton and major organs replaced while you are awake and using them. Or imagine driving a car while a mechanic rebuilds it at the same time. Ignorance is not bliss, merely the fuel for unrealistic expectations and armchair generals.
Anyway, I need to get back in game.
ORIGINAL REVIEW: I've got several hundred hours in this game. Playing solo or in a very small team is my preference. In that time I've probably have interacted with less than 50 other players since I'm more inclined to play PvE in a zombie/survival/apocalypse game than run around and kill other players on sight or engage in semi-organized battles. Just because I don't seek out direct player interaction does not mean that other players' presence in the game means nothing - it is very important since they might want to kill and eat me. This makes a continual level of tension in every game regardless of the server population. Three times I've been killed by the only other player on a server and it's not been in common looting areas. Right now in the .58 stable release there are no zombies while the devs work on some programming issues so it does make it a lot calmer  - and the players less alert. There will be a new learning curve when the zombies come back. Since this is an Early Access Alpha stage game in development I am not one to sit around and judge the performance of the developers. In fact, that is the biggest negative to DayZ - the vocal minority of whining children (regardless of actual age) that can't read the numerous articles about what games in alpha stage are really about. The players at this stage are not customers - we are lab rats. The devs should change the player avatars to big white lab rats as a constant reminder of the stage of development (and I'll change my game name to Ben).
Never have I put so many hours into a single game and I started in the 70's with PONG. I've certainly gotten my money's worth out of DayZ (that is not even a full game yet).
Ask ten players what they like about DayZ and you can actually get 10 very different answers. My likes don't really matter. This game allows each player to search out their own sweet spot.

In it's current state (12/12/15) no, I would not recommend this game. Let me explain why.
At the game's moment in time, it's VERY unfriendly to computers- especially those with weak GPUs. No matter what they say about the recommended requirements, they are lies. This game is SUPER unoptimized at the moment and is just a ♥♥♥♥♥ to run. Even on my GTX 950 (also paired with some handy launch commands) it struggles to keep a steady 40 FPS at most times. Mind you that I keep the game on the lowest settings posible, and it has pretty harsh drops when you enter cities; mostly 20 FPS drops. I've also heard mention from AMD users that this game is just completely unplayable, so if you're running an AMD build, don't even consider buying this game until they debug the game and optimize it for both Intel and AMD hardware. While the devs ARE CURRENTLY WORKING ON OPTIMIZATION, I still feel like these framerates should be ironed out already. Cities are still usually 20-30 FPS even with the -newui enabled and semi-low settings.
As far as newbies coming into the game, I think this game won't really appeal to them because of the fact that this game souly depends on the user doing his/her own research to figure out how the game works. There are no tutorial stages, no etiquitte, no instructions, nothing. The game forces you to go to the Steam User-Created Guides, or YouTube for help. Granted, this is how I got into the DayZ community on YouTube and Steam, I still think it's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t how much I struggled at first- and how much I STILL struggle even with these 40+ hours on my account.
The community and players in the game can be both great, but also very negative at times. For example- I've met two players today, 1 of which was suicidal and wanted me to kill her (which I did), but the other guy... that guy, was the first friendly guy I've ever met. He was asking about a friend who radioed in earlier and asked if I knew where he should go. He was a good guy and I gave him some food (because he was a fresh spawn) and sent him on his way. Even though there ARE good people in this community, there can be a bunch of♥♥♥♥♥♥♥who will kill at any cost. In the same day, I was killed from behind while drinking some water from a fountain. He gave me no warnings, didn't imprison me, nothing. Just a clean, straight kill from behind. I've also had a group of two kill me just for saying "Hi" in the chat.... So yeah...
With that being said about the community, I wish people had a little bit of ♥♥♥♥ing humanity. JUST A LITTLE BIT! I can't even begin to tell you how many times I've met up with some person on the side of the road just to have a short and friendly conversation with him/her and then he/she proceeds to hit me in the head once and i'm knocked out cold while they take all my gear that I worked so hard getting. This not only discourages me playing the game, but it makes me never ever want to go to high pop servers and kill EVERYONE I MEET ON SIGHT because I cannot trust ANYONE in this mother♥♥♥♥ing game. Call me crazy, sure, but when you realize that NO ONE IS EVER FRIENDLY, you'll never want to befriend ANYONE.
Bugs are riddled so much throughout this game. I know that the devs don't like to refer them as "bugs", but that's really what they are. I've lost so many characters because of ♥♥♥♥♥♥ bugs- I lost a recent month-old character because I walked up a flight of stairs and got desynced off and fell to my death. Desync is even worse in 0.59 now that it's stable. Regardless of desync, I still see the occasional hacker in the ground or some zed hit me randomly out of nowhere (sometimes even when there isn't a zed around, I'll randomly be attacked). Developers are still trying to fix these common issues that SHOULD have been fixed months- no, YEARS ago.
The game can just be more of a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥rather than be fun
I'll admit, I have fun playing this game, but I get anxiety because I'm afraid a person will jump me, either take me hostage and steal my♥♥♥♥♥♥ or will kill me and loot me for all the♥♥♥♥♥♥that took me weeks, if not months to gather up. I have definitely gotten addicted to this game, dispite my newbie-ness and dispite all the issues I've come across. I still find some way to enjoy this game. I will DEFINITELY reccommend this game when it reaches an ACCEPTABLE STATE. Right now, it's just WAY too buggy and glitchy to even be considered a game.

First off, I've always been a big fan of DayZ. And still am. But in this state as it actually is, I can not recommend the standalone. I've been playing the mod for Arma 2 for some time before all the hype started and with pleasure I watched it getting better (most of the time) with every update released. I could not wait for the standalone release with enhanced graphics, animations and stuff, as the mod-version already gave me some of my funniest, scariest and most exciting and satisfying moments I ever had in a game! And it was the only game I felt like paranoid while playing.
Like:
At night crashing with a bike into a couple of zombies, falling off, braking legs and getting chewed upon.
Playing taxi: Driving around all day in a bus, picking up all the players on the way.
Running from an axe-wielding psychopath mumbling weird things about god and jesus saves.
Hunting other players, wielding an axe and mumbling strange things about god and jesus saves.
Generally scaring the **** out of other players, without killing them.
Trying to discover the mysteries of ...phsshhh..... Green Mountain (with a can of mountain dew).
Hunting and eating all the animals.
Grabbing a helicopter, being unable to fly stable and crashing into the next tree or building just to be kicked off the server for causing a large explosion. Relogging and wondering why you spawned just next to the crash site with all your health and inventory fully intact.
Being chased by zombies for what felt like hours until you met another player and managed to make them chase him instead of you.
Build a tent or two. Gather weapons, ammo, food and water in such amounts that you could survive for months. Manage to repair a vehicle, drive to your tent and accidently drive OVER your tent, flattening it, destroying all the stuff inside immediately. Feel like wanting to drive over and flatten your PC, too.
Now, the standalone seems to have lost nearly all of it. Sure, graphics are better, animations are smoother. The game runs much better since the last recent updates. But much I loved about the mod is missing in the standalone.
Zombies have been temporarily (?) removed, I've never seen working vehicles, helicopters and bikes too. The loot system is terrible. It seems like motorcycle helmets, jumpsuits, chemlights and duckt tape are the most common items. The inventory and quickkey system is kind of weird and VERY buggy. I lost many stuff and weapons just by dragging things around.
The game runs more or less smoothly now with fewer lags, but still not as good as the mod-version. I know, better engine, better graphics and anims. But still not flawless.
Many of the new items are just for punishing and terrorizing other players. Also some game mechanics like feeding rotten fruits to a handcuffed prisoner. Your punishers can keep you alive for how long they want and you can't just respawn as a fresh player to escape your terrible fate. Might be funny for a short time if you're on the right side, but if not... well... it kind of ruins your game experience. And your fun to play.
Another thing that is annoying for me: I do not like that there are only very few "official" or "hived" populated servers. Most populated servers have special settings or mods enabled and so you cannot carry over your hardly earned stuff to another server when your desired one is down or at some times has too few players.
I still play from time to time but there is less much fun to experience than before the standalone.
In my opinion, DayZ Standalone has mutated into a large world PVP or Clan/Gangwar only. No need for friendly or solo players. Be in a group or you're just prey and a toy for all the others.
So, everybody who hasn't yet played DayZ should rather consider spending his money for Arma 2 and installing the mod instead of buying this standalone. It offers all you get from this one and so much more. Plus you're free to install enhanced mods like Origins or play on one of the many user-created islands.

First off, I've always been a big fan of DayZ. And still am. But in this state as it actually is, I can not recommend the standalone. I've been playing the mod for Arma 2 for some time before all the hype started and with pleasure I watched it getting better (most of the time) with every update released. I could not wait for the standalone release with enhanced graphics, animations and stuff, as the mod-version already gave me some of my funniest, scariest and most exciting and satisfying moments I ever had in a game! And it was the only game I felt like paranoid while playing.
Like:
At night crashing with a bike into a couple of zombies, falling off, braking legs and getting chewed upon.
Playing taxi: Driving around all day in a bus, picking up all the players on the way.
Running from an axe-wielding psychopath mumbling weird things about god and jesus saves.
Hunting other players, wielding an axe and mumbling strange things about god and jesus saves.
Generally scaring the **** out of other players, without killing them.
Trying to discover the mysteries of ...phsshhh..... Green Mountain (with a can of mountain dew).
Hunting and eating all the animals.
Grabbing a helicopter, being unable to fly stable and crashing into the next tree or building just to be kicked off the server for causing a large explosion. Relogging and wondering why you spawned just next to the crash site with all your health and inventory fully intact.
Being chased by zombies for what felt like hours until you met another player and managed to make them chase him instead of you.
Build a tent or two. Gather weapons, ammo, food and water in such amounts that you could survive for months. Manage to repair a vehicle, drive to your tent and accidently drive OVER your tent, flattening it, destroying all the stuff inside immediately. Feel like wanting to drive over and flatten your PC, too.
Now, the standalone seems to have lost nearly all of it. Sure, graphics are better, animations are smoother. The game runs much better since the last recent updates. But much I loved about the mod is missing in the standalone.
Zombies have been temporarily (?) removed, I've never seen working vehicles, helicopters and bikes too. The loot system is terrible. It seems like motorcycle helmets, jumpsuits, chemlights and duckt tape are the most common items. The inventory and quickkey system is kind of weird and VERY buggy. I lost many stuff and weapons just by dragging things around.
The game runs more or less smoothly now with fewer lags, but still not as good as the mod-version. I know, better engine, better graphics and anims. But still not flawless.
Many of the new items are just for punishing and terrorizing other players. Also some game mechanics like feeding rotten fruits to a handcuffed prisoner. Your punishers can keep you alive for how long they want and you can't just respawn as a fresh player to escape your terrible fate. Might be funny for a short time if you're on the right side, but if not... well... it kind of ruins your game experience. And your fun to play.
Another thing that is annoying for me: I do not like that there are only very few "official" or "hived" populated servers. Most populated servers have special settings or mods enabled and so you cannot carry over your hardly earned stuff to another server when your desired one is down or at some times has too few players.
I still play from time to time but there is less much fun to experience than before the standalone.
In my opinion, DayZ Standalone has mutated into a large world PVP or Clan/Gangwar only. No need for friendly or solo players. Be in a group or you're just prey and a toy for all the others.
So, everybody who hasn't yet played DayZ should rather consider spending his money for Arma 2 and installing the mod instead of buying this standalone. It offers all you get from this one and so much more. Plus you're free to install enhanced mods like Origins or play on one of the many user-created islands.

A peasant is a member of a traditional class of farmers, either laborers or owners of small farms, especially in the Middle Ages under feudalism, or more generally, in any pre-industrial society. In Europe, peasants were divided into three classes according to their personal status: slave, serf, and free tenant. Peasants either hold title to land in fee simple, or hold land by any of several forms of land tenure, among them socage, quit-rent, leasehold, and copyhold.
The word "peasant" is—and long has been—often used pejoratively to refer to poor or landless farmers and agricultural workers, especially in the poorer countries of the world in which the agricultural labor force makes up a large percentage of the population. The implication of the term is that the "peasant" is uneducated, ignorant, and unfamiliar with the more sophisticated mannerisms of the urban population.
The word "peasant" is also commonly used in a non-pejorative sense as a collective noun for the rural population in the poor and under-developed countries of the world.
Etymology
The word "peasant" is derived from the 15th century French word païsant, meaning one from the pays, or countryside; ultimately from the Latin pagus, or outlying administrative district.
Social position
Peasants typically made up the majority of the agricultural labour force in a pre-industrial society. The majority of the people in the Middle Ages were peasants.

This is personally my second favorite game I've ever played. Beautiful map, decent combat (apart from the occasional desync), and the stories. The stories are what make the game, that a long with the people. I have so many experiences that  are hilarious, sad, maddening, enjoyable.
Exp- I was runnning in Elektro and my legs randomly break, turns out someone shot me with a mosin from very far away, he approaches, bandaging me and handcuffing me. Apologizes over and over, ends up hearding me to a near by industrial building. I contact my friends on team speak, for an hour Im in a hostage situation, three of my buddies are engaged by the kidknappers squad, he leaves to help. I break my restraints and charge into battle, for 45 minutes we are in a raging fire fight in the heart of Elektro, more people join, soon enough we have almost the whole server in a civil war. Almost three hours of war, blood, children screaming, the cry of women looking for their mssing children.
Finally we have a peace treaty, me and my former assailent meet in city center, our armies behind us. We come to an agreement, my clan was to move to cherno, they would go to beri. Sudden mic chatter "NEVER SURRENDER." I turn, my second in command has a double barrel aimed at me, squeezes the trigger. All hell breaks loose, almost everyome dies. Total experince was about 6 hours or so, one of the best experiences I have ever had in gaming.
People need to understand that yes it is glitchy, yes there is a very large number of bandits and scum, sometimes youll die for no reason. Seeing the hype this game received via social media and YouTube, I was initially very skeptical. As soon as I was an hour in, I couldn't stop. I played halfway through Earthbound before starting Undertale to better understand one of its major inspirations and Undertale has added so much of its own charm and mechanics through gameplay and story. Undertale's dialogue is quite reminiscent of the Paper Mario series at certain parts, too.
I was made aware of pacifist and genocide runs before playing and completed both in that order - say what you will about the fans who are 'too emotional' about Undertale, but the endings of both playthroughs were very powerful for me.  My only criticism is grinding being quite tedious during the genocide run, but the reason for it makes a lot of sense when you know the story.
If I could play it again, I would. If you decide to play this game, read up on how to achieve pacifist and genocide runs and NOTHING ELSE. DO NOT spoil the story for yourself. It really is a game - no, an experience - where you need to jump in completely blind.

I think this game is very good. Extremely good.
When I hear people complaining how overrated it is I honestly can't imagine what game they played, but it can't have been this one. I do admit, though, what makes it not just good but exceptional, is the replayability of it. I see how, if you just played through it for the first time expecting mind blowing stuff, you might be a bit confused. Not that the first play though isn't great, but there are some major strengths this game has (that I've never seen done before?) that you will miss if you don't do a second, even third, playthrough. And the game itself is just short enough for that to not be too dull.
Not to mention lovable and unique characters, and a stellar soundtrack!

Rust is one of those games that at first glance seems simple in it's nature but is in fact packed with a tonne of gameplay filled with various mechanics that will have you hooked for hours. Along with the obvious PvP component, Rust offers players the ability to truly survive in a hostile world by base building, hunting, gathering, and exploration. While at the time of writing Rust is still Early Access, it has an extremely active development team pushing out updates every other week with excellent new content or tweaks to play with. I would highly recommend Rust to anyone who's looking for a survival game to play that has so many options it really is a one size fits all kind of game.

Funny, bloody, unorthodox, and well-written are words do this game justice. This game is different, but the same, as it's previous installment. It is as agreeing as it is contradictory to the original Borderlands, the style of the genre and the mixture of RPG elements with gritty, dark shoot 'em up gameplay makes for a crescendo of awesome. Easter eggs galore, not a single moment went by that I didn't laugh my♥♥♥♥♥off at a vague reference to everything from MacBeth to The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy. The dry, melancholy humor and sarcastic satirical dialogue (In both actual gameplay and cutscenes) bombard you with every new quest, challenge, and firefight. Subtitles are recommended, you really do not want to miss anything the intrinsic and well thought out characters have to say. This game is the best possible outcome for a sequel to Borderlands, and it makes your mind think what they could cook up for Borderlands 3.

Seeing the hype this game received via social media and YouTube, I was initially very skeptical. As soon as I was an hour in, I couldn't stop. I played halfway through Earthbound before starting Undertale to better understand one of its major inspirations and Undertale has added so much of its own charm and mechanics through gameplay and story. Undertale's dialogue is quite reminiscent of the Paper Mario series at certain parts, too.
I was made aware of pacifist and genocide runs before playing and completed both in that order - say what you will about the fans who are 'too emotional' about Undertale, but the endings of both playthroughs were very powerful for me.  My only criticism is grinding being quite tedious during the genocide run, but the reason for it makes a lot of sense when you know the story.
If I could play it again, I would. If you decide to play this game, read up on how to achieve pacifist and genocide runs and NOTHING ELSE. DO NOT spoil the story for yourself. It really is a game - no, an experience - where you need to jump in completely blind.

Not to mention lovable and unique characters, and a stellar soundtrack!

Now I know I just gave it a thumbs down, but I don't think it's a bad game.    It has it's flaws yes, for example it's buggy, it hasn't been properly updated in forever, and your character is the biggest wimp ever always complaining about weather, food, water, etc just to name a few, but I don't feel as if the game deserves as much hate as it gets on a regular basis.   It's fun in the sense that you are a pathetic little weakling going up against people who can and will kill you in an instant just to find out if you had anything of value to them, not only do you have to face them (and the trolls), but you also have to survive your natural needs, and zombies!     It's the fact that everything is against you and you have very few things that will work out for you that I think makes this game fun.   To me, reguardless of what other people say, this is one of the most realistic games you'll find, not because of the graphics or the situations, but rather the true and utter helplessness that you, somewhat, experience going through the world, in this era (especially in America) people would have as much chance of survival in a post-apocalyptic world, where it's you versus everything mind you, as that wimp you have to play as.     To sum up a book and a half, the game has many flaws, but do to the fact that it is so realistic in the sense that if anyone in the real world were in the same situations as the character you play as, they would be just as big of a wimp, if not more of one, so this mess of a game is good in my books.

Now I know I just gave it a thumbs down, but I don't think it's a bad game.    It has it's flaws yes, for example it's buggy, it hasn't been properly updated in forever, and your character is the biggest wimp ever always complaining about weather, food, water, etc just to name a few, but I don't feel as if the game deserves as much hate as it gets on a regular basis.   It's fun in the sense that you are a pathetic little weakling going up against people who can and will kill you in an instant just to find out if you had anything of value to them, not only do you have to face them (and the trolls), but you also have to survive your natural needs, and zombies!     It's the fact that everything is against you and you have very few things that will work out for you that I think makes this game fun.   To me, reguardless of what other people say, this is one of the most realistic games you'll find, not because of the graphics or the situations, but rather the true and utter helplessness that you, somewhat, experience going through the world, in this era (especially in America) people would have as much chance of survival in a post-apocalyptic world, where it's you versus everything mind you, as that wimp you have to play as.     To sum up a book and a half, the game has many flaws, but do to the fact that it is so realistic in the sense that if anyone in the real world were in the same situations as the character you play as, they would be just as big of a wimp, if not more of one, so this mess of a game is good in my books.

Borderlands 2, just like the first game, is a first person shooter with RPG elements. However Gearbox went out of their way to really put as much new content into the game as they could. In the first game each of the 4 different characters had only one tree of skills to select. In Borderlands 2 they have 3 trees and instead of 4 characters there are 5. I ended up playing as the Siren again like I did in the first so I will be reviewing from that character’s perspective. The Siren’s main skill, the phaselock (which is the ‘f’ key for all characters) is an ability that holds enemies in the air while you shoot at them. The skills she has vary from improving that main skill (health recharge by killing the phaselocked enemy, longer duration and even after you kill the enemy the phaselock goes to find another one), improves weapon elemental effects and the Siren’s overall health and shield. She also has several abilities that can improve the team you are with if you are playing co-op.
There are so many different kinds of guns it is ridiculous. I wasn’t even able to see maybe 1/1000th of the different weapons that are in this game. Each gun even can have its own special ability e.g. the weapon being thrown as a grenade when the player needs to reload, having a quicker or unique reload function and even guns that will talk. Like most RPGs these weapons come as massive amount of loot that enemies drop that vary in color depending on their rarity. I only reached level 36 by the end of the game so I only had 2 Orange weapons but they were both very good.

The story starts off with the player riding a train somewhere on Pandora in which Handsome Jack rigged to explode. Claptrap finds you and has you follow him to Sanctuary the main rebel city in the game. All this time Angel is trying to get you to stop Jack from force opening the vault in order to get the power from ‘The Warrior’ that is inside. For the most part you are doing various quests that follow the story and you end up meeting and helping out all the original vault hunters from the first game. But other than that the story is pretty straight forward and fairly simple. What really makes the story and side quests special is the dialogue and characters themselves.
Each NPC in the game feels like a legit character that gearbox took a lot of time creating a personality for. Every time claptrap speaks or someone makes fun of him I can’t help but laugh. Even Handsome Jack has a funny personality in a sick twisted sort of way. Without the characters Borderlands 2 would more than likely be a bland fetch quest RPG with no real attachment.



Now Borderlands 2 has its own style of graphics that sets it apart from many other games. It uses a cel shaded (it is spelled that way with one ‘l’) graphics that makes it very colorful and cartoonish feeling. All the different areas feel unique and awesome which is more than the first game can say. In Borderlands 1 the areas were all pretty much the same, dry desert with lots of rocks and caves. In Borderlands 2 that isn’t the case, there are many different settings for the different areas and they all feel different.
On top of that Gearbox did a fine job with the audio. As mentioned before the dialogue is outstanding and the voice acting is very well done. Because there are so many guns in this game they all need their own individual sound and Gearbox delivered on that one. Each different make and model have different sounds for the reloading, the shooting and when you have one of those special guns they even talk. Where the game shines due to the sound effects and voice actors it fails with the music. The music is just there in the background, is extremely quiet and doesn’t seem to ever really change. I was kind of disappointed because they had such a great trailer for the game mentioning 100% more “Wub Wub” but there was no such music in the game.


Overall this game was a great successor to an already great series however it didn’t improve a few things that the first game had problems with as well.

You should play this game and learn as little as you can before you do. It will be a better experience that way.
This is a "meta-game" type of game wrapped in an oldschool rpg with random battles. And perhaps the first really succeful "meta-game" game out there. Soon, I am sure this post-modern game genre will need its own tag.
Graphics are not great, but fitting, and most of all very creative. It is this creativness and new thinking that is the brilliance of the game. But I was not impressed with the art-style. And it really does not sell the game well. You have to be patient the first part of the game before anything interesting actually happens. It really has a slow start and it was only the knowledge that this game would eventually be great that kept me playing. Otherwise I would soon have turned it off and never returned.
Mechanics. Absolutely frustratingly dull and repetitive. This is one of the worst parts of the game. If you like random battles you might be fine, but the battles so quickly get repetive, and once you have gotten the gist of the REASON for the fights they just become an annoying obstacle that stands between you and the story. Yes, there are many creatures that are all different but the concept is not, and so the monster variation does not save this very repetive game mechanic. The IDEA is novel and interesting, and the way the mechanics are displayed are very creative. I love the "meta" here. Well, you have to find out for yourself. Fantastic ideas. Really dull mechanics.
One unforgivable point is the fact the game only has specific save points. That means a lot of repeating certain dialogs and events before you beat a certain boss, and that gets old REAL fast. It is never fun to see the same (sometimes long) dialog over 10 times, if you for example have a hard time with a boss.
Music is an interesting one. At first I wasn't very impressed, but I still appreciated the creativity of the music. But it got on me more and more as I played. It is quite varied, both in style and complexity. It also really varies in quality. Sometimes some quite bad midi music is used, and sometimes the productions quality is really high. In any case, the music really ads a deep emotional layer to the game and never feels out of place. It makes the game much more enjoyable.
Story is the best part of this whole game and worth the admission alone. It is not so much the story itself, but how you interact with it, and the turns it takes. I don't want to spoil anything so better less said. But this game is really deepening the perspectives of games, the player, and what a game can do. It has some great self-reflecting humor as well.
