This is a "meta-game" type of game wrapped in an oldschool rpg with random battles. And perhaps the first really succeful "meta-game" game out there. Soon, I am sure this post-modern game genre will need its own tag.
Graphics are not great, but fitting, and most of all very creative. It is this creativness and new thinking that is the brilliance of the game. But I was not impressed with the art-style. And it really does not sell the game well. You have to be patient the first part of the game before anything interesting actually happens. It really has a slow start and it was only the knowledge that this game would eventually be great that kept me playing. Otherwise I would soon have turned it off and never returned.
Mechanics. Absolutely frustratingly dull and repetitive. This is one of the worst parts of the game. If you like random battles you might be fine, but the battles so quickly get repetive, and once you have gotten the gist of the REASON for the fights they just become an annoying obstacle that stands between you and the story. Yes, there are many creatures that are all different but the concept is not, and so the monster variation does not save this very repetive game mechanic. The IDEA is novel and interesting, and the way the mechanics are displayed are very creative. I love the "meta" here. Well, you have to find out for yourself. Fantastic ideas. Really dull mechanics.
One unforgivable point is the fact the game only has specific save points. That means a lot of repeating certain dialogs and events before you beat a certain boss, and that gets old REAL fast. It is never fun to see the same (sometimes long) dialog over 10 times, if you for example have a hard time with a boss.
Music is an interesting one. At first I wasn't very impressed, but I still appreciated the creativity of the music. But it got on me more and more as I played. It is quite varied, both in style and complexity. It also really varies in quality. Sometimes some quite bad midi music is used, and sometimes the productions quality is really high. In any case, the music really ads a deep emotional layer to the game and never feels out of place. It makes the game much more enjoyable.
Story is the best part of this whole game and worth the admission alone. It is not so much the story itself, but how you interact with it, and the turns it takes. I don't want to spoil anything so better less said. But this game is really deepening the perspectives of games, the player, and what a game can do. It has some great self-reflecting humor as well. Also, the game goes down many routes. You can end the games in many ways. Re-play value? Absolutely ;)
I enjoyed this game, and enjoyed the new ideas. I don't think it is the best thing I have played, and I found the mechanics really boring. Nevertheless I very much enjoyed the experience and I am happy games are trying new ideas like this. It is a very good game. Definitely try it, but don't listen to the hype. Better that way.

The game is, in short, about a human who falls underground to a world of monsters, and thats really it right? Well, think of the game like...
No, I mean, think of the game like, The Stanley Parable, except, 16 Bit and with monsters, and... nevermind. The game takes everything and I mean EVERYTHING you do, and keeps it throughout the rest of the game... Whatever monster you kill, whatever choice you make... Has an impact on the end of the game. And guess what? Play through the game again, and all the characters seem to know you...
Not only is the story great, but the music in this game is so good... Seriously, go listen to it, you won't regret it! But I digress. Every character exists for a reason. Every character has their own unique personality, and they are all relatable (Except for them being mosters) But, you get the idea. Allow me to give an example. In the game if you go into a character's house, some may know him as "Papyrus", has a TV, and if you turn it on, he says that his favorite show is on. That same character that runs the show appears later on in the game, as an "antagonist" for lack of a better word. Thats how deep the story is, and like I said, every character exist for a reason, so everything fits together.
I give undertale a 9/10, its a great game that everyone should experience. If you don't like it, you're entitled to that. But for me, this game was great!

I HATE to give this game a negative review. Believe me, it has its charm.  I want to love it.  I can see the potential the idea DayZ is built upon has.  But the game, I feel, hasn't really gone anywhere.  In fact, for the time being it has taken a turn for the worse.
We all love a good survival game, and hell, you throw zombies in there it boosts the experience even more.  Unpredictable player encounters bring the gamer to their most entertaining moments!  But DayZ, despite having the skeleton of greatness we all know it has, just drops the ball in a lot of different ways.
Here's a typical game experience on a crowded, persistent server:
-You spawn on a beach near Elektro.
-You run for about five minutes, searching houses on the outskirts of town.
-You find a shirt, a meat tenderizer, a battery, a can of bacon, and craft a stone knife.
-You start running past a factory.
-There's some guy with a cowboy hat standing in the doorway of a shed.
-You run up and hit the wave hand gesture.
-"Don't worry, I'm friendly" the other player says, pulling a gun from his back.
-You turn, and get a couple steps.
-Your screen goes black.  "You're dead." fades ominously onto the monitor.
-You some teenage kid's voice as you stare at the screen, he barrages you with various obnoxious comments and tells you about how he'll enjoy cannabilizing your gonads.
-You hit respawn (that all took you from 15-20 minutes).
-Now you're in the mountains somewhere.
-You run for a good ten minutes without encountering anything.  Your fps wavers pretty bad in this time.
-You find a seemingly isolated town and manage to get a gun, bullets, food, and other decent gear.
-You follow the road.  Who knows where you're goin?  The map is massive.  You run for about ten to fifteen minutes without encountering anybody or anything.
-Ahead you see another smaller, remote town.
-You loot a couple buildings.  A few of the items can't be picked up for whatever reason.  Some of them are floating in the air.
-You leave a building and suddenly run into someone who has recently spawned.  All he has is a sledgehammer.
-He screams in his prepubescent, grating voice, "I'M GOING TO **** YOU!"
-You pull out your gun and fire round after round as you circle each other, but not even the shots seemingly aimed right at him make contact.
-He hits you once, and then manages too get you again.  Screen goes black.  You are unconcscious, and then the words fade in.  "You are dead."
-You spawn again.
-You go hardcore.  You spend hours getting the best gear, avoiding all interaction, and only venturing to areas that are not so popular.  You see a couple dudes and pick them off from a distance.
-Suddenly your gear starts falling off on its own.  You try to put it back on but it keeps falling off.
-You stand there naked for a moment, and then a couple dudes that seem to be hovering appear out of nowhere in full military gear.
-The hackers kill you.  After hours of work getting gear, avoiding the few people you've seen.
-You spawn again.  Around you are various apartment buildings.

In the end it's that hot girl you decided to invest your time, interest, and money in, but just ends up being bit bat♥♥♥♥♥♥crazy.  Potential at first sight, but wholly a disappointment.

I started playing awhile back (late 2013 or early 2014 I think), and since then there have been some positive changes. Servers now have a more balanced amount of loot available.  There's a variety of weapons, clothes, and so on, plus there have been additions such as vehicles (limited to very glitchy trucks), and servers that support 50 players at a time.
But now, at version .58, I've just played about four hours on  down day.  The player versus player dynamics are just as good as usual, I didn't encounter any hackers at least to take the gear I'd accumulated over hours, and the loot doesn't seem too abundant, and not too sparse, but the real kicker about my experience today has been that I didn't encounter a single zombie or animal.   I mean, regardless of whether of not that's a temporary state of the game, why should I be bothered to play a zombie survival game if there aren't any zombies?
When I started out back in the day, I remember being chased by them everywhere.  They had them in civilian clothes, and some in S.W.A.T. geddup, and even these infected that sort of hopped around.  Now I don't encounter one anywhere near the most popular spots in DayZ, and I didn't find any in the less visited towns further inland.  I used to run along the coast and see zombies chasing livestock, and some poor, unarmed new spawn that had three on his tail.  The game experience, despite all the gear and other additions, has made a serious turn for the worse by cutting back on the undead, particularly to this extreme degree.
I'd  put off purchasing DayZ at least for the time being.  As much as I really want this game to be recommendable, I just can't advise anyone to fork out thirty bucks for it in its current state.  WAIT until it reaches 1.0, and then see if its reached a better state.  WAIT until they have some kind of sale, and you can pick up DayZ for a cheaper price.
I might switch my review if the game improves, but for now I can hardly play it.  I'm at a point where I'll check in every so often, but that's it.  So, in my humble opinion, I'd say look elsewhere to spend your money.  Best of luck to the developers, though.  I can't express how much I want this game to improve.  But who can say where it'll be in two years.  The community could be completely dead by that point.
I should also mention that the game's technical performance is pretty bad.  I have a connection speed of about 100 Mbps, and I turn the game down to the lowest video quality, and it still lags to the point where it's frozen for a few moments.  I don't know if that's because of my hardware.  I've got an AMD quadcore, and an NVIDIA 9800 video card, plus 4 GB of RAM.  Even so, I've heard other players say the game can run poorly even if you do have the newest equipment.

During my last two game sessions, on different servers, I found myself wandering aimlessly. After two hours I found a damaged soda can, a terrible hat, and one other player who immediately punched me to death. Not a single zombie.
I endured this hoping that some legitimate gameplay may arise, but it did not. Yes there are people who go in with friend groups and have an enjoyable time, but I can't help but think they are deluding themselves.
Please do not buy or play this game.

THIS REVIEW IS A BIG 'OL BUCKET'O'SPOILERS, you've been warned.
I've been through phases with this game; after I recently beat it I thought extremely highly of Undertale, but then the magic seemed to fade, and then now it's growing on me again. After I beat the games neutral and true pacifist endings I loved it all. Everything felt right, from the music to even the graphics. I didn't know why, but it felt like a perfect game to me, and I loved it.
Then everything changed (when the fire nation attacked) after about a week to month after that, the magic wore off and the people online who HATED Undertale started seeming more and more correct. I didn't understand WHY I liked the game, so I started not liking the game at all. The graphics started looking ugly, the music started seeming repetitive, and the gameplay became too easy; even sans had gotten easy to me.
Then a three of my favorite youtubers : Yahtzee (Zero Punctuation guy), Jim Sterling, and John Bain (Totalbuscuit) all put this game as there number one game of 2015, so I felt wrong about Undertale again, because if the game had sucked those three reviewers wouldn't all have liked it so much. It took a few more hours of introspection than I'd like to admit to come to my conclusions about why I like Undertale again now as well as why it gets so much praise from the internet.
Here's a list of my conclusions (also you REALLY shouldn't read these if you havn't palyed the game):
1) The music: yeah this one is simple but it's worth mentioning. The music in Undertale is ALL very well made and used. It's intense during hard fights (Megalovania), happy during success (Bring it in Guys), and even tearjerking when it's appropriate (His Theme). I can't think of a single time when the music conveys the wrong emotion or goes against the flow of whatever else is happenning, except when it's on purpose (Unneccessary Tension). The use of both chiptune and actual instruments helps as well by increasing the contrast between small and large parts, mid-game and final bosses for example.
2) The visuals: okay they may be very low resolution and seem ugly at times, but it still works with the characters. The fact that most of the NPCs you meet are monsters allow for some amazing creativity with how they look, much more than humans would. Papyrus looks wacky, Toriel looks kind and nice, and Temmie looks, well Temmie-ish. Also the environments get beautiful if you take the time to look at them after you leave the ruins; the forest in the background of Snowdin, the core looming in the background in Hotland, and pretty much all of Waterfall is very pretty in my opinion. The use of much higher resolution textures for omega flower also helps him stand out from anything so far, as well as the rainbow effects of Asriel and screen blackouts of Sans.
3) The writing: this game has a charm like few others. The narrator, who some say is the fallen human but we'll get into the theories later, has such a personality to them. They'll judge you when you mess up, congradulate you everytime you succeed, and say more puns than even sans would care for. The writing is another critical component to the whole atmosphere that Undertale always manages to have, along with the music, visuals, story, gameplay, and lore.
4) The story: this is simultaneously a turn-off for a lot of new people and one of the best parts of Undertale. The game starts off very small, as in you fell down a hole and want to get out, which is why many give up on the game early on before the world can fully envelope them. But as the game progresses the story unravels it becomes so much more. You learn about the basic story of Asriel and the fallen human, and then it only escalates from there from the protagonist's actual name to learning that Flowey is Asriel. There are so many different plot twists of different sizes and importance that I couldn't list them all here.
5) The characters: Undetale has some of the best character designs that I've seen in a while. They all radiate personality to the point where some even get obnoxious because of it. There are plenty of comics and the like that seem cannon because of how well Undertale portrays these characters. I always really like anything that I could find out about Napstablook or, later on, Sans. The feel real and nomatter what you do they have an in-line reaction for it. You can bring an umbrella to Sans, force Papyrus to fun to his kitchen and back to his living room to fast for his legs, and even get Undyne so mad during her fight by taunting her that she checks to see if it's not a prank.
6) The lore: the lore of Undertale is kinda similar to the lore of Dark Souls; only the people who spend hours looking for small details can get anywhere, and then other people just look it up from them. There are so many tiny details that are easy to miss about the history of monsters and what happen's before you arrive that I'm pretty sure I still don't know MOST of what happenned. For example: one of the more recent things I learned was that Toriel carried the fallen human's body to the ruins when she left, and that explains the empty coffin, need of her to take care of those flowers, and part of the importane of golden flowers. that didn't even touch on Gaster.
7) The total understanding and abuse of the demographic: this is another reason why Undertale click's with some better than others. If these don't fit you, the game won't seem as mystical. The are plenty of nods and prods to the players of Undertale depending on what you do, and most of them come from Flowey. If you kill Toriel and reset he'll call you out on it, he points at the people who don't do the genocide run and just watch a video about it, and the fallen human even directly tells YOU about your ignorance when you start acting above consequences.
8) The demolition of expectations built up by other games, including Undertale itself sometimes: this game has a fourth wall like no other. Many features commonly thought to be part's of any RPG turn out to be canon parts of the universe. Omega Flower can save and load you file, Asriel knows about your resets, and even Sans figured out about how you're screwing with the timeline. There 'are also smaller ones like not being able to sell items to most shopowners and you not actually naming the character you play as.
9) The unanswered questions: the room left to theorize about this game is wide open, from the murky past of Asriel to a character that most people don't even find, Gaster, there are plenty of places to come up with theories about the game and its characters, which only helps interest about it.
10) Gameplay: the part designed before any other, according to the creator Toby Fox. The actual combat works well and doesn't get boring easily due to the puzzle like friending system, timing based murder system, and bullet hell based dodging system that constantly keep you on your toes. The mechanic of befriending or beheading monsters plays in directly to the game's main message; be nice. It was made in opposition to how most RPGs are just grinding fests about getting better numbers than your opponent. The much happier ending is obtained by becoming great friends with everyone and helping them overcome their inner demons. The worst is gotten by grinding the the monsters you can find to dust, which is what Toby didn't like about other games.
I could probably go on for much longer and more indepth than that aboujt Undertale but considering it's about 2:30 AM right now and I've pretty much reached the character limit I'm going to try to wrap up my thoughts. I do regard Undertale very highly right now, especially because I have a much better understanding of why. I like everything about it, but if I could change one thing, it would be to add hard mode because it's too easy for me now, but I suppose that's a point Toby was trying to make, he made a lot of points in Undertale.

Oh boy, I'm not going to make any friends off this review. Yeah, I...I don't really CARE about Undertale, but it's not the game's fault, not entirely anyway. The rabid fanbase has slowly driven me further and further and further away from Undertale until the point that I cannot connect with the game at all and I just give up. It's been ridiculously hyped, LPed to hell and back, and theorized until there's no theory left unaddressed.
That said, I really do want to like this game. It has most of what I need: Fun gameplay (Not compelling, but enjoyable enough), oustanding soundtrack (At least 3 years since 2010 that we've had indie gems with awesome soundtracks, like Dust and FTL), interesting story (But I'm NOT playing through the game 3 times for the different endings), charming characters (No "Stay With Toriel" BIttersweet Ending still bugs me), and SOME replayability (Not enough for me).
But...No matter what I say positively about the game, I can't connect with it in the same way I'm able to with Dust: An Elysian Tale. The story feels like it has no driving force besides "Hey, destiny said you need to keep moving forward, so you should keep moving forward" and, incoming bombshell, the game's fanbase PREVENTS me from playing it. If I try to share my experiences with an Undertale player, they'll almost inevitably spoil a really big fight like Undyne, Mettaton, or even the infamous Sans Pure Genocide Run and kill any tension to the story BECAUSE I know exactly who I'm going to be forced to fight depending on what run I go for. (SPOILER WARNING: HOOT HOOT, PUT IT ON MUTE)
I just can't do it. Stay determined?... ...... .........No. No longer. Frisk, may you find peace in the Pacifist afterlife.

Pretty good game. Since I can't be bothered to write an essay on it, I'll break it up into sections
COMBAT: Intuitive and working, it's an intesting system that combines bullet hell with normal RPG mechanics and does it well. It's a shame to see intuitive design get ruined, but here it was played out incredibly. Can't get enough.
STORY: It would be better without the filler characters (Muffet, Shyren, etc.). It definetly is a great story, but it needs some polishing-up. It's emotional and deep, but horribly cliche in its execution. I also do see the appeal in the quirky silliness of the game combined with the dark overtones and plot, but personally I find it to kill any shred of immersion that this game hoped to achieve. I'm not saying that the game should be Max Payne 3 levels of helpless, but not so polar in theme. That, and this polar theme has no real gradient, just a sudden slam from one extreme to another (i.e.
.) any sort of story flow this game hoped to achieve was ruined, but it's still a great story; just fragmented across the game.
GRAPHICS: cutesy and good-looking, but somewhat glitchy in certain scenarios
LEVEL DESIGN: Goes from good to high-school computer  programming project. Lots of areas are perfectly designed and pullled off, but some look awkward and surreal. The conveyor belts tend to screw around with where you're allowed to go (i.e. clipping through the level by forcing a conveyor belt to push you into and through a wall by moving sideways along it).
PUZZLES; not intuitive at all. A first grader could solve these puzzles. It's an interesting mechanic but it's never elaborated on except to develop a character.
Difficulty; this game is easy. Now of course, I spent a good year beating all 6 levels of Terry Cavanagh's Super Hexagon, so I might be "better than average" so to speak. This wouldn't be a problem if there was a way to change the difficulty, but all their really is is speeding up the game through external programs or buying the game-breaking Tem Armor halfway through the game. Normally I'm not one to care for "Shoot & Loot" games, becuas they generally don't have a very good storyline, but Borderlands somehow breaks that barrier by having an open-world shoot & loot game, but with a compelling storyline.

Undertale
Rating - A+
Genre - RPG
Creator - Toby Fox
Review
Undertale was a hyped game for quite some time until we all finally were able to play it and the wait was definately worth it. The rich story , the awesome characters and the concept executed so perfectly just adds it up to a great game. The combat system doesn't work like a traditional RPG , however this doesn't mean the game is bad but instead of attacks and such you can ACT , FIGHT , or use ITEMS then you can SPARE them those are the 4 things you can do.
If you FIGHT then you are playing the game on the GENOCIDE route. Not fighting , but instead ACTING will put you on the PACIFIST route. The different routes also make the game have alot of re-playability.
The game itself has great pixel graphics , funny jokes , good secrets and the AMAZING story is great.
The story itself (SPOILERS AHEAD) Is a very heart-warming tale of a human waking up in a world of monsters you play as the human , you will meet amazing characters with lots of personality giving the game a way more real feeling to it you go through multiple areas each one more detailed than the last , and I am not going to lie I cried playing this game.
The Ending of the game is A very big plot twist (SPOILERS NOW) Where Flowey (The first character you meet in the game) kills King Asgore (King Of The Monsters) and becomes OMEGA FLOWEY and with even more detail where the game will crash frequently as Omega Flowey is "Breaking The Game".
Personally I think the soundtrack is probably one of THE BEST soundtracks in a game EVER and I ain't lying!
Overall Undertale is a great game and I urge anyone who enjoys any kind of RPG or pixel-graphic game to play THIS GAME.

This game is amazing! It's a character-driven RPG with humor, good gameplay, and great presentation! It's a fun experience    that leaves you with a nice feeling afterwards. One recommendation that I'd make, is don't watch let's plays of this game, at least until you beat it. Avoid spoilers, and please, play this game! You won't regret it!

Borderlands 2. After playing through one hour of the first game, I turned it off. I found it to be repetitive, buggy, bland. I saw this in the Summer Sale for £5. My friend said it was amazing, so I thought what the hell. I am so glad I brought it.
The Humour is ALOT better than the first game. (Tiny Tina!). The graphics are alot more colourful and varied than the first game. There is hardly any glitches in the game, which really annoyed me in the first game. The story actually has a good few plot twists that fit in well with the RPG elements of the game. Actually, the RPG elements are very good. I like loot based games such as Diablo 3, Torchlight, and I'd say that Borderlands 2 is on par with them games. Also, the in game UI is also alot better, and they added a mini map. A MINI MAP!
The world surprised me as well. The characters in the game are some of the best video game characters ever produced. All of them are memorable.
Overall, I loved Borderlands 2 and was one of my favourite games of the 2012 releases. It is a vast improvement over the first game and is a very replayable game as well.
I give Borderlands 2 a 5/5.

Almost everything I loved about the original Borderlands is here in BL2. I say almost because the only thing that’s missing is some of the charm and humour of the original. But BL2 is still a great game, and it improves on the original in one area -- the variety of enemies. Again the visuals and sound design are impressive. There are plenty of maps to explore as you complete the numerous missions. The combat is well-balanced and challenging without being frustrating. And there are, as advertised, “bazillions” of weapons (too many, in my opinion -- it’s gets a bit tedious deciding what to keep and what to sell or dump). And it’s a great multiplayer game too, especially with friends. I guess it’s hard to match what was an excellent game first time around, but Gearbox have just about managed it despite not being quite as memorable as the first.

I bought this game with fairly low expectations; All these new early access-survival-crafting-PvP games seem buggy, half-finished and feature-lagging. They were all the same games to me. The graphics are decent but so poorly optimized that even a good mid-high end PC suffers massive FPS drops, the gameplay becomes repetitive and boring after a few hours and combat is more or less off the table as glitches and lag makes it nearly impossible to enjoy.
Even though the game has been out a few years now, I recently began to hear positive things about Rust in particular, and suddenly started seeing friends playing it. So why not give it a go - to at least give the old preconceptions a solid test. Luckily Steam offers a full refund within two weeks of the purchase and as long as you haven't played the game for more than 2 hours, so why the hell not try it out?
Expecting to play it for two hours to then return it, I booted it up, found a somewhat random official server with a decent ping and then began to mess around with the graphics settings for an hour trying to optimize it as much as humanly possible. I then played it... And played... And played... And suddenly 6 hours had gone by - eliminating my chance of a potential refund. Still with a hint of scepticism and a pinch of regret I then decided to find a proper server to start on for real (wasn't to happy about the one I initially found). I then stumbled upon a guy on the Steam forums who sought players for his new modded server. He seemed pretty cool and genuinely quite friendly, so I gave it a go.
Fast forward 2,5 weeks (and 92 hours of game time): I am now an admin on this server that has gone from 2 players to about 50 since I joined - and I'm ♥♥♥♥ing loving it! The game is fine, and has somewhat busted my negative assumptions about it, but what really keeps me going is the awesome community we have managed to establish.
I log on for the gameplay but I stay for the social aspect.
I only just started playing a few weeks ago - I have no idea how the game was before then, but NOW it runs smoothly on my 3 year old mid-high end PC. Combat works - not too laggy or glitchy. Gameplay is fairly varied and rewarding. The attention to detail is impressive considering the scale of the game. The game is generally quite intuitive (especially crafting and building) yet elaborate. And the developers seem active and occasionally adds some new features and/or bugfixes - even within the short period of time I have played.
I really like it. And granted my low expectations from the start, I'm very pleasantly surprised about how good it actually is. I haven't really tried any other games that shares the same genres as this, but one thing I can say is:
I definitely recommend Rust. 8/10

lets look at some facts.
Fallout 3, a great AAA game for its time, came out in 2008.
It took Bethesda 7 years of development, and re-development to finally give people Fallout 4 this coming november.
Now, the team working on DayZ have only been working on it for 2 years. They have also had members leave, and new people come on to the team. They are, as compared to Bethesda, a very small team. The smaller your team is, the longer development takes. With that said, it still took Bethesda 7 ♥♥♥♥ing years with a huge team to create Fallout 4.
The reality of it is this; it could be another 2-5 years before DayZ is finished, or at the least is out of Alpha. So, if you want to help that team along, and get to play a game that IS STILL BEING DEVELOPED, then by all means buy the game.
But if all you want to do is buy the game and then give it ♥♥♥♥ reviews then ♥♥♥♥ off. they have a very clear disclaimer telling you that the game is in its infancy.
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Bit of a side note here. It seems like people expected this game to be finished or be in Beta by now. What people seem to forget, is that this game was created from scratch. The DayZ mod for Arma was relatively easy to make, as they already had all the code and resources at their disposal. This is not the case for the Standalone people....This game has literally been created from the ground up with new code, new assets, and a smaller crew then the team that made Arma.
No one should under any circumstance compare the development life cycle of DayZ:SA to the DayZ Arma mod. Other than overall end goal, they share nothing in common. Different code, different assets, different team.

I bought this game with fairly low expectations; All these new early access-survival-crafting-PvP games seem buggy, half-finished and feature-lagging. They were all the same games to me. The graphics are decent but so poorly optimized that even a good mid-high end PC suffers massive FPS drops, the gameplay becomes repetitive and boring after a few hours and combat is more or less off the table as glitches and lag makes it nearly impossible to enjoy.
Even though the game has been out a few years now, I recently began to hear positive things about Rust in particular, and suddenly started seeing friends playing it. So why not give it a go - to at least give the old preconceptions a solid test. Luckily Steam offers a full refund within two weeks of the purchase and as long as you haven't played the game for more than 2 hours, so why the hell not try it out?
Expecting to play it for two hours to then return it, I booted it up, found a somewhat random official server with a decent ping and then began to mess around with the graphics settings for an hour trying to optimize it as much as humanly possible. I then played it... And played... And played... And suddenly 6 hours had gone by - eliminating my chance of a potential refund. Still with a hint of scepticism and a pinch of regret I then decided to find a proper server to start on for real (wasn't to happy about the one I initially found). I then stumbled upon a guy on the Steam forums who sought players for his new modded server. He seemed pretty cool and genuinely quite friendly, so I gave it a go.
Fast forward 2,5 weeks (and 92 hours of game time): I am now an admin on this server that has gone from 2 players to about 50 since I joined - and I'm ♥♥♥♥ing loving it! The game is fine, and has somewhat busted my negative assumptions about it, but what really keeps me going is the awesome community we have managed to establish.
I log on for the gameplay but I stay for the social aspect.
I only just started playing a few weeks ago - I have no idea how the game was before then, but NOW it runs smoothly on my 3 year old mid-high end PC. Combat works - not too laggy or glitchy. Gameplay is fairly varied and rewarding. The attention to detail is impressive considering the scale of the game. The game is generally quite intuitive (especially crafting and building) yet elaborate. And the developers seem active and occasionally adds some new features and/or bugfixes - even within the short period of time I have played.
I really like it. And granted my low expectations from the start, I'm very pleasantly surprised about how good it actually is. I haven't really tried any other games that shares the same genres as this, but one thing I can say is:
I definitely recommend Rust. 8/10

Borderlands 2. After playing through one hour of the first game, I turned it off. I found it to be repetitive, buggy, bland. I saw this in the Summer Sale for £5. My friend said it was amazing, so I thought what the hell. I am so glad I brought it.

The world surprised me as well. The characters in the game are some of the best video game characters ever produced. All of them are memorable.

I give Borderlands 2 a 5/5.

I guess it’s hard to match what was an excellent game first time around, but Gearbox have just about managed it despite not being quite as memorable as the first.

lets look at some facts.
Fallout 3, a great AAA game for its time, came out in 2008.
It took Bethesda 7 years of development, and re-development to finally give people Fallout 4 this coming november.
Now, the team working on DayZ have only been working on it for 2 years. They have also had members leave, and new people come on to the team. They are, as compared to Bethesda, a very small team. The smaller your team is, the longer development takes. With that said, it still took Bethesda 7 ♥♥♥♥ing years with a huge team to create Fallout 4.
The reality of it is this; it could be another 2-5 years before DayZ is finished, or at the least is out of Alpha. So, if you want to help that team along, and get to play a game that IS STILL BEING DEVELOPED, then by all means buy the game.
But if all you want to do is buy the game and then give it ♥♥♥♥ reviews then ♥♥♥♥ off. they have a very clear disclaimer telling you that the game is in its infancy.
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Bit of a side note here. It seems like people expected this game to be finished or be in Beta by now. What people seem to forget, is that this game was created from scratch. The DayZ mod for Arma was relatively easy to make, as they already had all the code and resources at their disposal. This is not the case for the Standalone people....This game has literally been created from the ground up with new code, new assets, and a smaller crew then the team that made Arma.
No one should under any circumstance compare the development life cycle of DayZ:SA to the DayZ Arma mod. Other than overall end goal, they share nothing in common. Different code, different assets, different team.

I may be a little late to the party, but I felt this was the least I could do for Toby Fox.
While this game is a true masterpeice and easily one of my favourite games of all time, it is certainly not perfect. That I would mainly chalk down the visual quality of the game. While the characters are beautifully and imaginatively designed, I feel like some areas of the overworld could do with more detail. Areas like the cave lantern room were nicely designed, but I feel like areas like the Ruins and Hotland could have done with more of this talent. The rest of these areas were passing, but I feel like a lot of areas could have really done with this extra shine.
The gameplay (in terms of the battle system) was very solid, and I really enjoyed all the different "modes" (as it were), and even developed favourites among these. The "ACT" system was very well-done too, with the choices tailor made to each monster and each would appeal to them in different ways. The moves the monster displayed also helped me learn more about their character and how to appease them; which is such an incredible amount of detail. The "FIGHT" system has little too it, which is ok, a standard RPG battle style which fit in well with its genre. A minor complaint was that the controllable character walked at a god damn snail's pace but with transport like the Riverwoman and the... blobs in Waterfall helped soften this, but I felt like more of these were needded around the world.
In regards to the plot, I was not fortunate enough to experience this game blind, but even so, when playing the game for myself, I still found it well-woven. I built such a genuine liking to the characters, and their motivations and personality were very real and compelling. Extra story elements I did not often indulge in finding, but I knew them nontheless and still found the over-arching story quite compelling.
The music is beautiful. Nuff said.
I think the thing that really sells this game to me is making me feel REALLY involved. All that 4th Wall breaking towards the end of each playthrough really shook and had an effect on me. While I cannot say I enjoy either route over the other, I think each route really embodies what it is about. The no mercy route... is well, merciless. It's frustrating (especially with Undyne and Sans), but I think that is the message the game wants to put across and my craving for the adrenaline of being to triumph over everything really is the desire for personal satisfaction despite killing everyone. The music is dark and everything is very iscolated, like the message is trying to convey. And, in the pacifist route... I truly felt loved and cared by all the characters. ALL of the main characters were truly lovable, and such a broad spectrum gave me lots of characters I generally wanted to see acheive their dreams. I love these guys so much that even after the Genocide Run, I want to go back and set everything straight, like the way I SHOULD have left it. This game really weighs on my moral obligation, and well, taught me that sometimes, just leaving things alone, following advice and trying your best to love everyone around you is the way to go. This game is sure to stay with me for a long time.
I respect you and your game, Toby.
May you make more (but plz don't make a sequel) and may more games be like this in the future.

When Undertale came out of nowhere, we were literally buried under the heaps of praise coming from gamers and critics alike. Now, that is usually what rings an alarm here and reason why I've decided to stay away from a game for a while. I've needed dust to settle because it wasn't hard to notice formation of fanboy armies who stomp and kill everyone who dare say anything negative about object of their appreciation. As much as I despise this kind of attitude, I'm a fanboy myself for some other♥♥♥♥♥♥so I can justify that kind of behaviour in a way.
During my almost four hour run, I've realized that Undertale is more of an eccentric interactive experiment than a game. It is piece of software that questions the basics of RPG genre and how we corelate to characters and worlds we inhabit during our playtime.
The game starts with a cliche: once there were humans and monsters. Monsters went underground and one human fell in a deep hole (in case you haven't figured it out - that's you) and is now stuck in monsterland. The Undertale plays like a NES game with much better music. Actually a great music, to be honest.
Turn based battles are what's really interesting about Undertale. You can attack physically or act in a way for a chance to avoid battle. Hints about your enemies are always displayed on the screen so you'll know what buttons to push (read: choices to pick) to try to avoid the battle. And when you're avoiding punches, Undertale throws interesting bullet-hell system. Avoid the bullets - save your HP.
Game also tends to break a fourth wall here and there and it 'remembers' your previous actions which guarantees more room for replayability and surprises in case you're in for it. This meta aspect of Undertale seems to be the most interesting one to many players and I have to say I find it quite gripping as well.
But why didn't I finish my first walkthrough and don't have any interest of even going for the second?
Being unique is also Undertale's worst enemy. Silly characters, wacky dialogues and jokes that tend to repeat themselves, all the goofs grow pretty thin at certain point. I've really tried to get into the game, feel it, experience Undertale for what it is, one of the highest rated games of all time. After two hours I've wanted to uninstall it. I gave it another push, another half an hour and another and another and then I said: "No, it's enough".
I simply don't feel it. I don't corelate to characters and they don't deliver any reason why I should listen to them talk, spare them, fight them or travel through their world. The underworld is bleak, filled with characters that turn cheap after a few smiles and no laughs at all.
Undertale is one of those games that have a certain appeal, but if you're not into humor that acts like meme/9Gag overkill, you can't force yourself to love it. I dig Monty Python, South Park, Seinfeld, Curb Your Enthusiasm, I can always rewatch Guy Ritchie's brutal drama comedies such as Snatch and Lock Stock and Two Smoking Barrels. That is (fortunately?) humor for me. Undertale unfortunately isn't and since it is solely based on its humor (80%) and turn-based-JRPG-battle with a spin (20%), I really can't recommend it.
Well, at least I've tried.

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

HOW HAVE I NOT WROTE A REVIEW FOR THIS GAME YET!?
There are very few games in this rare category I call TIMELESS.
These are the games you play for YEARS.
I did it with Mario Kart, Tribes 2, WoW, Planetside 2, and now Rust.
I started playing in December 2014 and hardly play anything else.
- REALISTIC looking OPEN WORLD.
- Build your own base however and wherever you want. I loved LEGOS to death when I was little and I love the idea of making your own persistent base in an online open world.
- Play SOLO or TEAM UP with random people or invited friends.
- PVP everywhere: In the field, at the town, at the airdrop, at someone's base, from your base, and BASE RAIDING.
- Ingame voice chat is realistic - your mouth moves in game when you talk and it can only be heard nearby (like IRL).
- Rewarding resource collection which can be tedious but you have to really earn what you want to make.
- Smart player community that figures out great base designs and sneaky little tricks/exploits to take down your great base :)
- Every month they keep improving the game.
- The devs communicate their progress with the community constantly via WEEKLY devblogs and Twitter. The weekly devblogs are EXTREMELY interesting insight into the process of new ideas, optimization, polishing, balancing, bug fixes, and curbing cheaters.
- The DEV TEAM is EXTREMELY TALENTED and COMMITTED to RUST.
- RUST is one of the most graphically beautiful and realistic games designed with a small dev team. Compares to AAA titles.
- The lead is Garry Newman who made one of the most successful sandbox mods for HL2. As such, RUST fully supports player mods and highly encourages them.
- Through the ups and downs, it's usually always fun or thrilling. From defending a big brand new base by yourself against a whole team of raiders (intense and sometimes traumatic) to being the last man standing and getting killed by some random with a spear (lol/cry)!
- Figuring out clever ways into someone elses base and designing yours against those vulnerabilities.
- I made some great gaming friends playing RUST.
- I have met many ruthless players and some really cool/chill RUST players.
- This is one of the most addictive games I know of.
- I have played on the public official servers occasionally but there ARE some very clever and persistent cheaters there that can circumvent the anti-cheat processes in place. Official servers DO NOT HAVE ADMINS.
- Most of my time is spent on Rustafied Main
which has had outstanding support for RUST!
- Rustafied community is great overall even though most are KOS and hostile, you just have to learn to play around it :) You eventually will make friends to teamup with.
-
posts updates outside of and alongside the devblogs and has active forums.
- Very few servers have as many active admins as Rustafied servers do. Rustafied also has a low-pop option and the special map servers.
- There are several other community run servers that might jive better if you are having problems on Rustafied or the Official servers.
- I HIGHLY HIGHLY RECOMMEND PRACTICING PVP on the Battlefield or Battle Royale servers! Learn the weapons, their rates of fire, their clip sizes, their range, their recoil, and which one's you like. Also learn when to play conservatively and aggressively without fear of losing hours of work.
- Performance is not consistent but the devs are constantly improving this - especially for fps drops around large bases and during firefights.
- Some players are toxic and others will poop-on newbies really hard. Some will act nice to get into your base and screw you over (kill you, change your codes, destroy everything, steal everything, etc). Then there are the cheaters that come out when the admins aren't on - usually getting revenge for dying or losing their base.
- There is a lot of finger pointing about cheating and a lot of sneaky cheaters using cheats conservatively to stay under the radar, but with just enough advantage to "pwn noobs".
- Every server does a map wipe once a month and Rustafied Main does a map wipe every week! This is due to technical issues keeping a server up with hundreds of player created bases. It does make it easy to skip playing for a week or two though and jump back in on a wipe day.
- To craft medium to advanced items requires learning Blueprints (BPs) which ARE A GRIND and don't carry over to other servers. Whatever server you decide to go with you will probably stay with once you have most of the BPs you need. The counter to this is to join a team/friends that are already established on another server so they can help you get most of your BPs pretty fast (since they already have them). This is also changing in a future patch to an XP system.

Got told by a major villain to stop playing the game because even THEY wouldn't be so cruel as to do that. So I'm here now. 10/10
You know ALL those Undertale memes that you're sick of hearing? Trust me on this: they hit MUCH harder when you're in the proper context.
Undertale is a game that lives on the strength of its writing, and boy howdy, DOES it deliver. The game's dialogue hits the entire emotional spectrum. To say more would be a disservice. Ditch your guides, click off your Let's Plays, this is a game that's MUCH better going in blind, but even for those who have seen dozens of important lines parroted across the internet as cheap memes... the writing hits the mark MUCH more often than it misses.
The combat system is basically Bullet Hell Lite. You avoid attacks like you would in Touhou, and you land them in a simple timing-based combat system. Dodging is, obviously, where the fun takes place, and despite the game feeling a bit too easy at times (I actually died more times to a mini-boss at the two hour mark than I did against the last three bosses in the game COMBINED) it works well.
You can end fights either by killing your foes or by finding ways to convince them to stop fighting. Finding the ways to "spare" opponents isn't too hard, at least most of the time, and eventually random encounters become a bit tedious, but the combat system gets the job done.
...Look. I'm going to level with you here. The main draw of the game isn't the GAMEPLAY. It's not bad by any stretch of the imagination, but it's not why the game EXPLODED in popularity. It's not the art style, either, though it's pretty solid. It's not even the music, even though it's AMAZING.
No, the reason Undertale became THE big surprise of 2015 was because of the writing. And sure, if you want to be robbed of context, if you want to divorce yourself from the REAL impact of the writing, there's no shortage of text dumps or Let's Plays. But what makes Undertale TRULY special is when YOU'RE the one at the wheel. That, alone, is worth the price of admission.
And when you're at the wheel... whether you're going to have a bad time or not is up to you.

Borderlands 2 is both a great improvement over the first one and a great game on its own. It maintains the structure of the first game, but adds new and improved characters with much better-structured classes and skill trees, a proper story and impressive graphics.
Borderlands 2 starts off a bunch of years after the first one. The vault has opened and there was nothing of value there...Just kidding! The opening of the vault actually released a powerful alien power which has drawn the attention of Hyperion Corporation's president: Handsome Jack, who is also an as*hole. That should be his name. As*hole Jack. So, this Jack guy completely enslaves the population of Pandora. His greed is almost as big as the number of guns in this game. Seriously, did I already mention it? The number of guns in this game is just amazing. I don't even know how much is 'bazillions', but that probably doesn't even exist and had to be made up just to count the amount of weapons generated in this game.
Again, you are a vault hunter. But Handsome Jack does not want anyone else going for the vault. He wants it all for himself, so one of his goals is to kill you, and one of your goals is to kill him. Throughout the game you'll meet Borderlands 1's main characters, such as Lilith and Roland, and you will help them achieve some of their goals. Roland is the leader of a resistance who is fighting against Hyperion forces but is pretty much losing, as far as you can tell. Without getting any further on the story, it basically just ties the loose ends that the disappointing Borderlands 1 ending had and develops beyong that with a good, solid story. All that without taking away from the gameplay and, of course, the humour.
Borderlands 2 can be played solo, but it is harder to do so than it was on the original game. This game is made to be played in coop, and it is SO much better. Of course the game is really fun solo too, but there's just no denial that the real fun is on playing with friends, selecting different classes and learning how to play with them to properly cooperate with others and create a great team.
I am trying really hard to search for a let down in this game, because there isn't. Maybe some quests are kind of repetitive and/or irritating, but those are mostly sidequests and should not be bothered with. So, Borderlands 2 is a wonderful experience and you should definitely buy it, ESPECIALLY if you have a couple of friends who also play it or want to play it.
+Good gameplay mechanics
+Beautiful graphics
+Way more variety in the game's world than the first one
+Infinite amount of weapons
+Well-written story
-Most of the side-quests are repetitive
SCORE: 94/100

You know ALL those Undertale memes that you're sick of hearing? Trust me on this: they hit MUCH harder when you're in the proper context.
Undertale is a game that lives on the strength of its writing, and boy howdy, DOES it deliver. The game's dialogue hits the entire emotional spectrum. To say more would be a disservice. Ditch your guides, click off your Let's Plays, this is a game that's MUCH better going in blind, but even for those who have seen dozens of important lines parroted across the internet as cheap memes... the writing hits the mark MUCH more often than it misses.
The combat system is basically Bullet Hell Lite. You avoid attacks like you would in Touhou, and you land them in a simple timing-based combat system. Dodging is, obviously, where the fun takes place, and despite the game feeling a bit too easy at times (I actually died more times to a mini-boss at the two hour mark than I did against the last three bosses in the game COMBINED) it works well.
You can end fights either by killing your foes or by finding ways to convince them to stop fighting. Finding the ways to "spare" opponents isn't too hard, at least most of the time, and eventually random encounters become a bit tedious, but the combat system gets the job done.
...Look. I'm going to level with you here. The main draw of the game isn't the GAMEPLAY. It's not bad by any stretch of the imagination, but it's not why the game EXPLODED in popularity. It's not the art style, either, though it's pretty solid. It's not even the music, even though it's AMAZING.
No, the reason Undertale became THE big surprise of 2015 was because of the writing. And sure, if you want to be robbed of context, if you want to divorce yourself from the REAL impact of the writing, there's no shortage of text dumps or Let's Plays. But what makes Undertale TRULY special is when YOU'RE the one at the wheel. That, alone, is worth the price of admission.
And when you're at the wheel... whether you're going to have a bad time or not is up to you.

HOW HAVE I NOT WROTE A REVIEW FOR THIS GAME YET!?
There are very few games in this rare category I call TIMELESS.
These are the games you play for YEARS.
I did it with Mario Kart, Tribes 2, WoW, Planetside 2, and now Rust.
I started playing in December 2014 and hardly play anything else.
- REALISTIC looking OPEN WORLD.
- Build your own base however and wherever you want. I loved LEGOS to death when I was little and I love the idea of making your own persistent base in an online open world.
- Play SOLO or TEAM UP with random people or invited friends.
- PVP everywhere: In the field, at the town, at the airdrop, at someone's base, from your base, and BASE RAIDING.
- Ingame voice chat is realistic - your mouth moves in game when you talk and it can only be heard nearby (like IRL).
- Rewarding resource collection which can be tedious but you have to really earn what you want to make.
- Smart player community that figures out great base designs and sneaky little tricks/exploits to take down your great base :)
- Every month they keep improving the game.
- The devs communicate their progress with the community constantly via WEEKLY devblogs and Twitter. The weekly devblogs are EXTREMELY interesting insight into the process of new ideas, optimization, polishing, balancing, bug fixes, and curbing cheaters.
- The DEV TEAM is EXTREMELY TALENTED and COMMITTED to RUST.
- RUST is one of the most graphically beautiful and realistic games designed with a small dev team. Compares to AAA titles.
- The lead is Garry Newman who made one of the most successful sandbox mods for HL2. As such, RUST fully supports player mods and highly encourages them.
- Through the ups and downs, it's usually always fun or thrilling. From defending a big brand new base by yourself against a whole team of raiders (intense and sometimes traumatic) to being the last man standing and getting killed by some random with a spear (lol/cry)!
- Figuring out clever ways into someone elses base and designing yours against those vulnerabilities.
- I made some great gaming friends playing RUST.
- I have met many ruthless players and some really cool/chill RUST players.
- This is one of the most addictive games I know of.
- I have played on the public official servers occasionally but there ARE some very clever and persistent cheaters there that can circumvent the anti-cheat processes in place. Official servers DO NOT HAVE ADMINS.
- Most of my time is spent on Rustafied Main
which has had outstanding support for RUST!
- Rustafied community is great overall even though most are KOS and hostile, you just have to learn to play around it :) You eventually will make friends to teamup with.
-
posts updates outside of and alongside the devblogs and has active forums.
- Very few servers have as many active admins as Rustafied servers do. Rustafied also has a low-pop option and the special map servers.
- There are several other community run servers that might jive better if you are having problems on Rustafied or the Official servers.
- I HIGHLY HIGHLY RECOMMEND PRACTICING PVP on the Battlefield or Battle Royale servers! Learn the weapons, their rates of fire, their clip sizes, their range, their recoil, and which one's you like. Also learn when to play conservatively and aggressively without fear of losing hours of work.
- Performance is not consistent but the devs are constantly improving this - especially for fps drops around large bases and during firefights.
- Some players are toxic and others will poop-on newbies really hard. Some will act nice to get into your base and screw you over (kill you, change your codes, destroy everything, steal everything, etc). Then there are the cheaters that come out when the admins aren't on - usually getting revenge for dying or losing their base.
- There is a lot of finger pointing about cheating and a lot of sneaky cheaters using cheats conservatively to stay under the radar, but with just enough advantage to "pwn noobs".
- Every server does a map wipe once a month and Rustafied Main does a map wipe every week! This is due to technical issues keeping a server up with hundreds of player created bases. It does make it easy to skip playing for a week or two though and jump back in on a wipe day.
- To craft medium to advanced items requires learning Blueprints (BPs) which ARE A GRIND and don't carry over to other servers. Whatever server you decide to go with you will probably stay with once you have most of the BPs you need. The counter to this is to join a team/friends that are already established on another server so they can help you get most of your BPs pretty fast (since they already have them). This is also changing in a future patch to an XP system.

Undertale has become one of the most hyped games in recentl months, and was recomended to me by a friend. I figured that it sounded fun, and ten dollars for a game isn't too bad, so now I'm here writing this review. I will be splitting this up into three catagories; Presentation, Fun, and Story. If you don't like my opinion, that's ok, just please don't try to shove your opinion down my throat.
Presentation: Visuals and Audio
The game is obviously going for a retro look here, and this is because it's trying to reference old rpgs like Gen 1 Pokemon and Earthbound. My biggest problem with this style is that it's an easy cop out for game makers to be lazy and just say  it's "retro" or "minimalist" in response to criticism. Now to be fair, some games can make it work, but most don't. Undertale does manage to pull it off well in some areas (like Waterfall and Hotland which are lovely) but in others is either unoriginal or looks lazy (Snowdin is admitally very pretty, but is basically every winter level in every RPG ever made. On the other hand, The Ruins has the opposite problem in that it is an intresting concept, but looks incomplete in many areas.) In terms of character designs, everyone is recognisable and looks nice, basically doing what they are supposed to do. Other than that, there isn't much to write home about the art style. The soundtrack is where the game really soars, and is easliy one the best parts of the game. My only complaint about the music is that I feel it would have been better with real instruments instead of chiptune. Overall, Presentation gets a 8/10.
Fun: Controls and Gameplay
The controls do what they do, but there really isn't much else to say about it though. Out-of-combat gameplay is bare bones, but definetly where I had the most fun, Everything and everyone can be interacted with, and while it isn't the height of comedy, some of the quips can be funny, and the game does a good job of giving exposition without shoving it down your throat. Puzzles on the other hand are a bit too easy, and I would have liked more of a challenge. In-combat gameplay is unfortunatly borin though. Basically you and your opponent take turns. On yours you can either use healing items, spare them, act, or fight. Fight to deal damage, Act to pacify monsters. Wash, rinse, and repeat until you kill the monster or you spare them. Now, this woulld actally be pretty fun, becuase each type of monster requries a different act combo to pacify them, and they each have different attacks to avoid. Unfortunately, the fights are ruined because the same enemies keep popping up over and over again. Soon, fights that were fun at first quickly become boring and annoying. This is made worse by the fact that random encounters are used, so you can't even avoid enemies. Fun gets a 6/10.
Story: Characters and Plot
This is where Toby Fox really put in the most effort. The characters are mostly likeable, and it helps make some of the worst gameplay bearable (especially because repetition and random encounters don't apply to bosses, who are all main characters or important side characters). Unfortunately, with the exception of four or five characters, it feels like character depth and growth was sacrificed for "quirky" humor like pop culture references and internet memes. While, slapstick, witty comments, and bad puns also are used and they are actually funny, it isn't enough for me to overlook some of the lame jokes made. As for the story, it isn't as complicated as fans would like you to think. While there are some plot twists and multiple endings, the story is fairly straightforward. However, if  you want to get the good ending, you have to reload your save after the neutral ending and go do stuff that should have been available the first time around, and if you want the bad ending, you have to do it last, or all other endings are ruined for you. This is bad game design, and enjoyability shouldn't be sacrificed for innovation when it comes to video games. But, the biggest flaw is the moral. Throughout Undertale, you are encouraged to be peaceful to solve problems, and are treated like a villain if you use violence. This wouldn't be a problem, except in most of these situations, the enemy is trying ot kill you, and you would be justified if you used violence to defend yourself. This very naive view of morality is also extended to the backstory of the game. It felt kind of like I was listening to propaganda when learning about the history of the world, even though the creator of the game makes it obvious that this is what happened. Overall, Story gets 7/10.
Conclusion: Undertale is a game that tries to criticze the gaming industry and community. While it does succeed in many areas, it also relies a lot on of the same mechanics and cliches it criticizes while also sometimes tripping it's own ambition. Now, I feel that the circumstances surrounding a creation has an effect on it. Undertale was mostly made by one person, and that is why I am being a bit lenient here. Undertale's final grade is a 7/10. If you're looking to have a good time, go ahead and buy this game. There are worst things to spend ten dollars on. If your're looking for the next Earthbound or Final Fantasy, look elsewhere.

After I played Undertale, I started looking back on other RPGs I've played in the past and asked myself "Why are people still making games like this and act like it's so unique and groundbreaking?" - You don't need 72 hours of content to get players hooked on your game. Yet, in this short amount of game time, Undertale expresses so much emotion and heart that other games take over 34 hours to do a fraction of the expression Undertale gives the player.

Borderlands 2 is both a great improvement over the first one and a great game on its own. It maintains the structure of the first game, but adds new and improved characters with much better-structured classes and skill trees, a proper story and impressive graphics.
Borderlands 2 starts off a bunch of years after the first one. The vault has opened and there was nothing of value there...Just kidding! The opening of the vault actually released a powerful alien power which has drawn the attention of Hyperion Corporation's president: Handsome Jack, who is also an as*hole. That should be his name. As*hole Jack. So, this Jack guy completely enslaves the population of Pandora. His greed is almost as big as the number of guns in this game. Seriously, did I already mention it? The number of guns in this game is just amazing. I don't even know how much is 'bazillions', but that probably doesn't even exist and had to be made up just to count the amount of weapons generated in this game.
Again, you are a vault hunter. But Handsome Jack does not want anyone else going for the vault. He wants it all for himself, so one of his goals is to kill you, and one of your goals is to kill him. Throughout the game you'll meet Borderlands 1's main characters, such as Lilith and Roland, and you will help them achieve some of their goals. Roland is the leader of a resistance who is fighting against Hyperion forces but is pretty much losing, as far as you can tell. Without getting any further on the story, it basically just ties the loose ends that the disappointing Borderlands 1 ending had and develops beyong that with a good, solid story. All that without taking away from the gameplay and, of course, the humour.
Borderlands 2 can be played solo, but it is harder to do so than it was on the original game. This game is made to be played in coop, and it is SO much better. Of course the game is really fun solo too, but there's just no denial that the real fun is on playing with friends, selecting different classes and learning how to play with them to properly cooperate with others and create a great team.
I am trying really hard to search for a let down in this game, because there isn't. Maybe some quests are kind of repetitive and/or irritating, but those are mostly sidequests and should not be bothered with. So, Borderlands 2 is a wonderful experience and you should definitely buy it, ESPECIALLY if you have a couple of friends who also play it or want to play it.

HOW HAVE I NOT WROTE A REVIEW FOR THIS GAME YET!?
There are very few games in this rare category I call TIMELESS.
These are the games you play for YEARS.
I did it with Mario Kart, Tribes 2, WoW, Planetside 2, and now Rust.
I started playing in December 2014 and hardly play anything else.
- REALISTIC looking OPEN WORLD.
- Build your own base however and wherever you want. I loved LEGOS to death when I was little and I love the idea of making your own persistent base in an online open world.
- Play SOLO or TEAM UP with random people or invited friends.
- PVP everywhere: In the field, at the town, at the airdrop, at someone's base, from your base, and BASE RAIDING.
- Ingame voice chat is realistic - your mouth moves in game when you talk and it can only be heard nearby (like IRL).
- Rewarding resource collection which can be tedious but you have to really earn what you want to make.
- Smart player community that figures out great base designs and sneaky little tricks/exploits to take down your great base :)
- Every month they keep improving the game.
- The devs communicate their progress with the community constantly via WEEKLY devblogs and Twitter. The weekly devblogs are EXTREMELY interesting insight into the process of new ideas, optimization, polishing, balancing, bug fixes, and curbing cheaters.
- The DEV TEAM is EXTREMELY TALENTED and COMMITTED to RUST.
- RUST is one of the most graphically beautiful and realistic games designed with a small dev team. Compares to AAA titles.
- The lead is Garry Newman who made one of the most successful sandbox mods for HL2. As such, RUST fully supports player mods and highly encourages them.
- Through the ups and downs, it's usually always fun or thrilling. From defending a big brand new base by yourself against a whole team of raiders (intense and sometimes traumatic) to being the last man standing and getting killed by some random with a spear (lol/cry)!
- Figuring out clever ways into someone elses base and designing yours against those vulnerabilities.
- I made some great gaming friends playing RUST.
- I have met many ruthless players and some really cool/chill RUST players.
- This is one of the most addictive games I know of.
- I have played on the public official servers occasionally but there ARE some very clever and persistent cheaters there that can circumvent the anti-cheat processes in place. Official servers DO NOT HAVE ADMINS.
- Most of my time is spent on Rustafied Main
which has had outstanding support for RUST!
- Rustafied community is great overall even though most are KOS and hostile, you just have to learn to play around it :) You eventually will make friends to teamup with.
-
posts updates outside of and alongside the devblogs and has active forums.
- Very few servers have as many active admins as Rustafied servers do. Rustafied also has a low-pop option and the special map servers.
- There are several other community run servers that might jive better if you are having problems on Rustafied or the Official servers.
- I HIGHLY HIGHLY RECOMMEND PRACTICING PVP on the Battlefield or Battle Royale servers! Learn the weapons, their rates of fire, their clip sizes, their range, their recoil, and which one's you like. Also learn when to play conservatively and aggressively without fear of losing hours of work.
- Performance is not consistent but the devs are constantly improving this - especially for fps drops around large bases and during firefights.
- Some players are toxic and others will poop-on newbies really hard. Some will act nice to get into your base and screw you over (kill you, change your codes, destroy everything, steal everything, etc). Then there are the cheaters that come out when the admins aren't on - usually getting revenge for dying or losing their base.
- There is a lot of finger pointing about cheating and a lot of sneaky cheaters using cheats conservatively to stay under the radar, but with just enough advantage to "pwn noobs".
- Every server does a map wipe once a month and Rustafied Main does a map wipe every week! This is due to technical issues keeping a server up with hundreds of player created bases. It does make it easy to skip playing for a week or two though and jump back in on a wipe day.
- To craft medium to advanced items requires learning Blueprints (BPs) which ARE A GRIND and don't carry over to other servers. Whatever server you decide to go with you will probably stay with once you have most of the BPs you need. The counter to this is to join a team/friends that are already established on another server so they can help you get most of your BPs pretty fast (since they already have them). This is also changing in a future patch to an XP system.

and I'd be willing to buy it for my friends for them to play with me. I've enjoyed this game every single month of development and can't wait to read the next devblog every week!

Updated for v0.60:
While zombies have returned to the game (still underwhelming) and loot has been rebalanced (still underwhelming), the biggest improvement is performance. v0.60 absolutely delivers on that front, no amount of hate can detract from that.
It's a much more playable game now thanks to this, but it's still maddening to play with friends when you can't even choose the general area of your spawn. As long as there are suicide glitches, and failing that, tall buildings and zombies, players will find a way to kill themselves to roll another spawn.
The dev team might as well abandon their losing battle and allow people to at least choose their spawn region a la ARK: Survival Evolved, because teamplay by far the strongest aspect of the game, and the only way this game has any longevity. It's a crime to make it so inaccessible.  If the apocalypse really happened, surely you would seek out your friends and neighbors, so why does a game that tries to have so hard to be realistic, a game that constantly adds half-baked systems like building and gardening, refuse the idea that people might survive the apocalypse with people who live near them?
Utlimately, it's still inferior to the Arma 2 mod in every way except for performance.  This is still a game that will be an alpha title forever, because the developers start things they'll never finish at their glacial pace before the foundations are even in place.
Original text:
A complete and utter betrayal of a game and fanbase by the developers.  The ARMA II mod was infinitely more complete than this game will ever be.  There's not even zombies in it anymore, because the development team literally could not be bothered to design a passable AI for zombies, yet they continue to sell the game as "DayZ" despite the "Z" element having been completely removed.  It's basically false advertising.
The best part about the DayZ mod was collecting guns, hunting for a car, then driving up north and mounting raids on their airfield and northern towns for better gear and resources.  That dream is dead as a doornail.  It's hard to find guns, much less ammo, you can find food but have to get a separate implement to open it, so you'll probably die of starvation moving from house to empty house looking for an implement.  And you'll never find a car.  So good luck walking up north to where all the fun stuff might still be.
The developers continue to add more roadblocks to make the survival element more realistic and difficult, but have failed to create systems or a world that is compelling to survive within in the first place, a world that's been completely stripped of anything that makes it more than the most boring, empty ARMA mod of all time.  The loot tables are completely at odds with even the character's most basic needs for survival.  A five year old could tell that about the game, and yet the developers do nothing about it.  The one new thing that's nice is the redesigned Chernarus map with more interiors, but with nothing meaningful inside them except 15 functionally-identical items of clothing, the gesture falls flat.  Plus the same old performance issues from the ARMA mod persist.
Do not buy this game in 2015. It's dead and should be allowed to die. There's no point to PvP, there's nothing to survive except boredom.  Bohemia should be ashamed for continuing to sell this farce.  This is the single worst abuse of the Early Access label in Steam's history, the progress is glacial, Early Access is not an excuse for such an offensively glacial development schedule, the subtraction of content over time, and other mistakes.  Early Access is not a blanket excuse for these things.  It is a promise to your purchasers that you will do right by them, and the developers have not.

Undertale is a great example that a game doesn't require 72 hours of content, hundrends of quests, or countless weapons and skills to be profound. After I played Undertale, I started looking back on other RPGs I've played in the past and asked myself "Why are people still making games like this and act like it's so unique and groundbreaking?" - You don't need 72 hours of content to get players hooked on your game. An average playthrough of Undertale takes 4 - 6 hours. Yet, in this short amount of game time, Undertale expresses so much emotion and heart that other games take over 34 hours to do a fraction of the expression Undertale gives the player.
The music is perhaps the most astonishing aspect of the game. It is vital to the game's aethestics and atmosphere. The melodies often sound like love-letters to classic video game music and battle themes, they're nostalgic but they also have their own uniqueness about them that still sounds contemporary.
The game changes narratiave based on how you interact with its world. Don't feel compelled to be a "Pacifist" as some fans would recommend, just be true to yourself and forge your own solutions to conflicts. Perhaps what's more important about this game is that it's just damn fun and it's actually comedic. It's not always a dark, self-loathing edgefest and that's really refreshing after years of popular media, especially video games, becoming so engulfed in creating a dark, edgy story.
The greatest thing about Undertale can't be properly expressed through words, you're going have to go and play it yourself! Enjoy the ride.
