There are plenty more unique and interesting weapons to choose from and even more loot than last time with better effects and style. Elemental effects are back with the new inclusion of “Slag”, which is actually a by-product of refined Eridium. Slag causes no damage on its own, but in fact covers its victims and causes them to take increased damage from subsequent attacks. Elemental damage is very useful again and slag really helps you dish out the pain, but the non-elemental damage weapons often deal greater single shot damage to make some great pistols and sniper rifles.
Two big improvements apart from the better loot are the new character skill trees and more interesting enemies to fight. You don’t feel as restricted by your skill choices this time around and it is more generalised damage now, so you don’t have to specialise as much in certain weapon types. Whilst the bottom skills in each tree are very useful I’ve noticed that almost any combination of skills are strong and viable, although some are stronger than others at the moment the foundations are fine and it’s more of a numbers game for any updating that needs to be done for balance. There is more variation in critical spots on some enemies and weaknesses to exploit. On some enemies (such as spiderants) this is vital for taking them down quickly because of the amount of armour and lack of damage you will do anywhere else on the body. Crystalisks for example require you to shoot the crystals on their legs to take them down quicker, which then count towards your money when you pick them up.
The soundtrack has a similar intensity to the first game but has taken on much more of what I would describe as a Bastion-esque atmospheric folk vibe for the most part and then takes on a lively electronic nature in several combat sections. This fits very well with the game and is more memorable than in the first Borderlands, in which the music wasn’t exactly bad either. The sounds of the creatures and weapons are also of high quality, similar to the first game. Some of the smaller weapons do sound a little bit weak but still suit the guns and the special animations and designs on some guns had cool sounds to go along with them. For example, I used a rocket launcher at one point that included a revolving chamber-like design that slowly spun up after you reloaded.
The graphics have improved, but for the most part it’s only moderate. Most of the improvement seems to be higher resolution textures, but the main difference between the aesthetics of the game is that the colours are much more vibrant and feel much better now. Gearbox promised to put special care into the PC version, which is evident and finally includes a slider to adjust the Field of View, making the game feel much better for my resolution (I chose a setting of 100 for 1920×1080). Plenty of PhysX effects on PC are included that look great and show that they’ve put a lot of effort into the “port” now.
The difficulty has increased a bit; you’ll have to think about what you’re doing more and possibly do some tweaking to your “build” for some parts. There is often a greater diversity in resistances and weaknesses in the enemies together (robots and some soldiers being armoured, for example), so you have to make sure you have multiple elemental weapons at hand to deal with them individually. For some reason, Gearbox decided to make death feel like much more of a penalty too. The death process involves more than just a teleporting animation back to a New-U station now, you also have to watch yourself drop to the ground, then teleport to the station and watch a cutscene of you materialising into existence. It’s quite frustrating to have to wait through, especially when you’re at a difficult section of the game. The bosses are more interesting and larger, however, with longer fights to provide a greater sense of achievement to match the difficulty of taking them down.
The maps are bigger and more detailed, with open areas and content everywhere. There is a greater variation in environments too, which makes the world seem much more expansive and like you’re actually traveling a fair distance in the world. While a good bunch of the quests are the typical collection situation there are still plenty of them that have enough character to them to feel fresh and worthwhile (even some funny easter egg quests to find). There is a quest for example that you can get from a bandit-looking guy who gives you the rather straightforward task of shooting him in the face…that’s it, but it’s quests like that that are the most fun in the game (depending on the person that may or may not sound like a bad thing, but I assure you it’s more the originality than substance that I’m referring to). There are lengthier fun quests which involve helping a cult that believe Lilith to be some sort of fire God, checking to see if Handsome Jack’s “Grandma” is okay, and both inviting people for and attending Claptap’s birthday party to name a few. Slot machines are provided for your gambling needs to use up your precious credit and gamble on getting better guns and rewards. You can even tip Moxxi at her bar, which eventually rewards you with unique weapons for your generosity.
In Borderlands 2 the story is better and much more developed, but I feel that’s mostly less by the choice of the player and more because the story involvement is more present by force. The player has to wait for characters to finish talking in many of the main story missions to progress, and if you don’t care too much about the story (which is very common in co-op play) it can be quite a hindrance.
Hyperion’s huge space station is always visible on the planet – a constant reminder of its presence and influence. The Hyperion soldiers and robots are dropped in from space; you can both see and hear as they’re sent down as obstacles on your adventure. Handsome Jack regularly contacts you, with taunts as a constant reminder of the force you’re up against and the force you need to stop. The relationship between the two of you swaps as you progress. His light-hearted demeanour at the start of the game is both amusing and instils a hateful determination to take him down, but as you continuously resist his attempts to stop you he realises that you’re a legitimate threat, and his laughter turns to anger. At this point you realise that you’re now laughing at him. You’re now in the position of pitying him as he protests. The reason that Handsome Jack is such an important part of the story for me that he’s the element that makes the story such a prominent part of the game. In the first Borderlands, the story was probably the last factor of the player’s enjoyment of the game – it was all about the guns and the characters.
I thoroughly enjoyed my time playing Borderlands 2, both 1st and 2nd playthrough. It took me about 40 hours to complete both playthroughs with about half of the side quests done (doing all of the side quests will probably be another 10-15 hours). There is plenty of replayability if you have friends to play with and cooperative play is the most fun way to play. I will say that the first couple of hours were rather boring, but once you reach Sanctuary and get better guns it’s worth sticking around. I feel that the story was admittedly saved only by Handsome Jack from being almost as easily overlooked as in the first game, but other than that it's pretty much the Borderlands 2 we've been waiting for.

As I ate my first meal I thanked the men, stating that I had only bought the game about a half an hour earlier and had absolutely no idea as to what I was doing.
The men then all turned toward me and I heard the tone in their voices shift.
"This is your first day?" One of them asked.
"Yes." I replied.
He then swiftly drew his fire axe and swung it with great might into the front of my skull.
Then he spoke the coldest words I had ever heard..
"Welcome to DayZ."

Whether or not it's usually the type of game you'd go for, it's going to be one of those games referenced in the years to come by almost every reviewer and game journalist as a testament to storytelling through gameplay, atmosphere building, and the power of a game's soundtrack.

It's worth anyone's time.

Borderlands 2 is a really funny, comical game (though much of the humor is dark). Though the Main quest line is rather short on its own, the game shines through with the optional missions. Playing every mission on a single character takes a decent amount of hours, and then there is all the DLCs that really add to the playability of the game before it can become dull.
The customisation is actually quite extensive, and there is a class for just about anyone. Multiplayer doesn't break the game either, compared to many other games (Magicka), and the multiplayer is directly playing with another person directly on their character's world.
The game has become repetitive for me after 130 hours of gameplay (I also have it on the Xbox 360), but for anyone looking at this game while on sale or has steam friends who play,  you can easily get 40 hours of fun out of it, and that is without the DLCs.

This game single-handedly spawned such a prolific and active (but slightly toxic) fandom. And for good reason..
If youre planning to play this game, its best to not know anything about the game. And its best not to take any advice from the people who have played/ watched this game. Why? Well, you never really know what to expect from it. Thats one of the best things about this game.
All I can say is go ahead and play this game. Play it right now if you like great stories.
Ive literally bought this game 3 times. And bought the soundtrack to sho appreaciation for this.
And I wont be expecting anything like this for years to come.
Anyways, here's my breakdown of the game.
Graphics: Imagine a NES game... now go back a couple of generations. Thats what this looks like.
Ok, even for a pixel rpg game, the graphics here are pretty bland. Environments can be a turn off. Especially on the first few levels. But there are times where the graphics and art style show some promise. Places like Snowin or Alphy's lab are really beautiful places. But these are a little bit rare. Suffice to say. It has its own charm, but still, pretty terrible grin emoticon
Story= (lim(x): 1/x as x approaches 0+)/10
This is a game where I really felt like I was friends with the characters. They're all so charming. All having their own sense of humor. All very well written. The dialogue is something you really can't get enough of. And you can sense there are some references to outside sources. References to spongebob, to anime, etc.
The game has a main narrative within the game world itself. But it has a secondary narrative that you see later on as you play. a narrative of YOU playing the game. And different playthroughs arent just different dialogue paths all meaning the same. They add another layer to the story. There ARE character you dont get to meet when you do a specific playthrough. Characters that are central to the story.
You feel all the feelings with this game. Laughter, Sadness, Fear (wayyyyyy better than most horror games), DETERMINATION, and strangely enough, it makes you feel loved within the game world itself.
Its all so well done..
Audio: Im broke 80% of the time and I still bought this game's OST.
I have listened to the OSTs everyday since I've played the game. Ive listened to a lot of the musical covers of the OST. I dont know. Maybe I have a problem. Maybe even an addiction to the music. But. Jesus, its so Good. Especially the themes of the Final Bosses.
Sound, well, it has its charm. Maybe above average. But pretty standard RPG ambient sound.
Gameplay: . . .
Well, The game has 2 major "phases". The 1st one is where you take control of the main character's body. And the second one is where you take control of the main character's soul. You go through the mini puzzles, collecting little.. um.. "frienddliness pellets"
You also have the choice to kill or to spare the characters within the game. Changing how each major character's perspective and attitude towards you.
Take that as you will :D
TL:DR:
Welp. I bought this game 3 times and didn't regret it. It's one of those games that come once in a blue moon. Go out and play it. It's a really great game.

Let me get the easy and mandatory stuff of the way:
The Graphics:
Okay so this is the same engine as 3 years ago. However, there are improvements, at least on the PC version. The physx is now able to display some cool visual effects. The improvements include
+hundreds of sparkles from explosion guns;
+ fire looks like fire now;
+the corrosion goo now oozes out on the ground and cascades down the slopes;
+ the battlegrounds are now littered with pieces of rocks and gravel (that do not disappear by the way);
the electric guns now display more sparkling effects;
+there is now some sun glare
+there is now aurora borealis
+there are some nice snow and desert effects
+the anti-aliasing has been greatly improved
+the day to night shift has also been improved
The Cons:
-the water looks pretty much the same though
-we still get Directx9
-Visually, everything about the game has been improved except that you still cast no shadow and you still can't see your legs
-The Resolution problem. okay so I thought I was playing with my native 1920x1080 resolution until I figured out (at level 10) that you needed to change the resolution one more time IN-GAME. Apparently, changing resolution in the game menu does squat. So I've been playing the crappy console 1080x720 whitewash resolution for about two hours before I figured out what was wrong. DON'T MAKE THE SAME MISTAKE.
-SLOW texture loading, just like in the first game. Whenever you enter a new are or go into a shop it will take a couple of seconds for textures to load. Thanks consoles!
Okay as for the gameplay:
It remains largely unchanged however there are improvements. The sprint effects are now more realistic. One of the things I liked is that it is MUCH MUCH harder to earn money now. I reached level 18 and rarely had more than $ 1500 bucks in my pocket. This is a breath of fresh air considering that you could easily rack up $ 200,000 by the time you hit level 15. ( I am not even mentioning the exploit of cloning artifacts and rejoining friend's game to essentially have infinite money). Also, I should mention that they now got rid of all those unnecessary zeroes, as in, there really is no reason to sell a gun for $ 254,620 when they could downplay the entire currency by a factor of 1000. Ergo, you would have to buy the gun for $ 254 instead.
The skill tree is somewhat the same from the first games with some similar perks.
They now added Eridium as currency, which is rare. Except you can only use it to upgrade your ammo/grenade/backpack capacity.
They haven't changed the driving. It is still a keyboard+mouse driving which still sucks.
They also now added caravans which can get attacked and then get looted for rare weapons.
The elemental effects largely remain the same. Fire is good against flesh and corrosion is now really effective against armor (robots don't have shield or health anymore, only armor). Also, robots are easily taken out when their limbs are blown off.
It seems like the auto-assist weaker than in the first game but it can still be felt.
The enemies are even more hilarious now. The voice acting is great (same goes for THE friendly NPCs), especially when you hear the midget armored goliaths talk. It's obvious they try to overcompensate for their vertical challenge by being extra badass. The enemies still do the barrel rolls, they still take cover and can spend up to 5 seconds and they can also jump from platform to platform. There are also the buzzers (make-shift propelled helicopters much like in the mad max movies) which are pretty fun to shoot down. It's even more fun when they sing the Ride of the Valkyries composition (from Apocalypse now), it's pretty amusing. Some midgets ride on each others' heads too.
I'm not too sure about the insects though. They are gross and disgusting to fight.
In general, it is still way more fun to fight humans or rather, the humanoids, rather than the robots and the beasties.
The weapons:
I'm not sure if it's me but it looks like they put more effort into adding more flare to almost every other gun. The seemingly random-generated stats are still there but at least gun skins look more flamboyant and peculiar. They also varied the standard appearance types somewhat. So, not every rifle gun is necessarily elongated for instance.
The story:
It's a continuation of the first story (perhaps a couple of years after opening of the vault) wherein The Handsome Jack, who is in charge of the Hyperion Corporation is attempting to open an even bigger vault and obtain control of the prehistoric monster to rule Pandora. The story has some twists, surprisingly and it's always welcome to see the good old friendly NPC's again.
In the end, perhaps this could quality as Borderlands 2 since it's a continuation of story and all, I just didn't really feel like it was a new installment all that much, a lot of things feel same, although it's a definite improvement over the old one. There is more narrative, more quests, new enemies, new artifacts, mods, etc. etc. But there is not necessarily more depth, perhaps it is so because of the type of game itself. However, there are plenty of comical and satirical moments that catch you off-guard. The game is also littered with easter eggs.

The game's major weakness: Practically everything is a spoiler. If you know little to nothing about this game, now is the time to play it.
Undertale is a twisted spin on RPGs with a retro art style.
The basic concept is that you don't have to kill any enemies if you don't want to. This creates many diverse ways the game can be played, which the creator has taken into account and planned for. With all these branching paths, it is best to go in knowing as little as possible to get a more personal feeling while playing, instead of simply looking up how to get the "best" ending. Looking up a walkthrough or watching a lets play really does invalidate the point of the game, so I can't stress enough how important it is to avoid spoilers.
Unfortunately, due to the game's massive success and popularity, most players, myself included, already know too much on their first playthrough and don't get the full experience.
The gameplay is built on very basic RPG elements, but they are actually incorporated into the story. There are a few weapons that all act mostly the same, you try to stop a white bar in the center of a meter to get the most damage. Not the most complicated system, but still somewhat challenging for new players. Enemies, on the other hand, have personalized attacks and optional ways to spare them. The real unique part of combat is that it becomes a bullet hell when enemies attack they player, and even this isn't always as straight forward as it seems. Depending on certain choices you make, this can be anywhere from stupidly easy to hair tearingly difficult. Outside of combat, there are many puzzles to get through in order to advance.
Aside from two bosses whos' solutions weren't immediately obvious and some optional puzzles I skipped the first time around, this game was a cake walk; but, there were some options I didn't take that would have enhanced the difficulty severely.
The game doesn't lack for beautiful scenery, if you can at all appreciate the pixel art style. Personally, I think the game looks amazing; but I know some people don't see pixel art as anything but an easier way to make a game. This game makes me question those people's sanity, as it is by far one of the most breathtaking games I've played.
The soundtrack is definitely one of the best features of the game, as the lead developer is moderately well known for their previous musical works. The music mostly sounds like chiptunes, with a smattering of realistic instruments in the background. The atmosphere is intensely amplified by the music, or lack thereof in some cases. However, if you are interested in buying it, be warned that many tracks are under a minute long. Almost all the songs are designed to loop, so most end up being shorter than they seem in game. This is mostly made up for with there being a staggering 101 songs on the album, and the sheer quality of the best songs. Maybe consider buying the official metal cover instead. It's more expensive, but it doesn't come with songs that are under a minute in length.
The story and lore of the land are top notch. I found myself deeply engaged when clues and backstory were provided; but I'm a sucker for those things, regardless. The world feels like a real place with a long history. There's lots of diverse areas,
with details and secrets hidden everywhere.
One major gripe people seem to have with this game is that the characters are too,"tumblry." I can understand where they're coming from; but it seems like a silly thing to complain about, and I didn't really notice anything too edgy. I found most of the characters to be very similar to people one might meet in real life, from angsty teens all the way to pushy salesmen.

Undertale reminds me of older video games that were amazing...Ones that you sat in your basement all day and played and never got up to eat or go to the bathroom from. When you play undertale you feel all warm and cozy because of all the lovably list of qwerky characters that you'll remember for your entire life, to the beautiful retro RPG style graphics.
Undertale is unique in many different ways, One way is the fighting mechanics. In undertale you can actually mercy your opponents if they wish not to fight making it possible for a playthrough where you dont have to kill a single thing. There are 3 different routes to play in undertale...The pacifist route where you kill no one, the neutral route where you kill some and let some live, and the famous genocide route where you kill every single character in the game. The game puts you through many interesting and cute areas where you meet new characters and face puzzles.
Now if you haven't had anything spoiled to you about undertale yet then you are lucky because undertale's community is pretty toxic. The less you know about the game the better. The storyline (without spoiling anything) is this...a long time ago a war broke out between monsters and humans, the humans were stronger so they sent the monsters underground and sealed them there with a magical spell. many years later you are a little girl who falls down into the underground. Thats pretty much all ill tell you before anything is spoiled. The storyline is incredible in this game and it's one of the main reasons so many people love it.
Now there is no voice acting in undertale, (except one line) instead there are lines of text in different fonts for different characters and different noises for each letter that pops up. But the one thing that is brilliant is the music in undertale. Holy♥♥♥♥♥♥the music is incredible in this game and it was all made by Toby fox (the creator, this guys got serious tallent) If you have a few extra dollars, please buy the soundtrack for this game...you wont regret it. Some songs are soft and slow and great for listening to on chill days and some songs are hardcore as balls (megalovania) that will get you pumped up for anything.
This game deserves its own section for its characters. One of the main reasons the story is so amazing is not only because of its amazing plot, its also because of the incredible list of characters that appear throughout your adventure in the underground. You've got toriel, the mother whos just trying to help you but you are so
to find your way up again. You've got flowey, cute on the outside and evil on the inside, however he has a bit of hope inside him for something good. You've got sans, (my personal favourite) the cool skeleton who loves life and tells really bad jokes, did I mention he's the most powerful character in all of undertale? You've got Papyrus, San's brother who really wants to become part of the royal guard and fight beside his hero, Undyne, the BEAST knight who runs the royal guard and protects the king of the underground from the humans. Theres so many other characters but those were just some of my personal favourites.

I was hesistant to buy it after reading some of the negative reviews (especially those that talked about people cheating or going on rampages killing everyone). Ignore those. I have played on 20+ servers with no problems at all. Many of the players were very helpful when I was starting out and some even gave me items/explained how to build stuff.
I now run my own dedicated server available to anyone online (Name: [East] North Carolina. Wiped 5/5. No Decay). I have about 10 active players and everyone works together and gets along...for the most part. Occasionally we kill each other, but mostly its a collaborative experience. We work on building and exploring. If you join a toxic server, leave and find another. Many of the community run servers are great. They have active admins and zero tolerance for cheaters. Find a server with lots of active admins and the cheating problem you read about will be non-existent.
It is clear Facepunch is working hard on this game. Since I have owned it, I have been a part of two "major" updates. While it is annoying it wipes the server, they address many glitches/random issues and add  new items/mechanics.
The game can be quite demanding on the computer, especially if you want to run it at max settings; however, they have many preset graphic settings from "fastest running" to "fantastic". I am running 2x 980ti's ftw model in SLI and get around 30-35fps at max settings at 4k. I am sure as they continue to optimize the game/improve NVIDIA and AMD support it will only get better. I am willing to bet they do not support SLI and that is part of the reason I cannot max out fps.
Take away:
I am 100% glad I purchased this game and am looking foward to what the future holds. While you may encounter cheaters/12 year-old boys who will try to kill you every chance they get, there are a lot of good servers out there with a great community. If you like games like MineCraft you will like this game as well.

There are plenty more unique and interesting weapons to choose from and even more loot than last time with better effects and style. Elemental effects are back with the new inclusion of “Slag”, which is actually a by-product of refined Eridium. Slag causes no damage on its own, but in fact covers its victims and causes them to take increased damage from subsequent attacks. Elemental damage is very useful again and slag really helps you dish out the pain, but the non-elemental damage weapons often deal greater single shot damage to make some great pistols and sniper rifles.
Two big improvements apart from the better loot are the new character skill trees and more interesting enemies to fight. You don’t feel as restricted by your skill choices this time around and it is more generalised damage now, so you don’t have to specialise as much in certain weapon types. Whilst the bottom skills in each tree are very useful I’ve noticed that almost any combination of skills are strong and viable, although some are stronger than others at the moment the foundations are fine and it’s more of a numbers game for any updating that needs to be done for balance. There is more variation in critical spots on some enemies and weaknesses to exploit. On some enemies (such as spiderants) this is vital for taking them down quickly because of the amount of armour and lack of damage you will do anywhere else on the body. Crystalisks for example require you to shoot the crystals on their legs to take them down quicker, which then count towards your money when you pick them up.
The soundtrack has a similar intensity to the first game but has taken on much more of what I would describe as a Bastion-esque atmospheric folk vibe for the most part and then takes on a lively electronic nature in several combat sections. This fits very well with the game and is more memorable than in the first Borderlands, in which the music wasn’t exactly bad either. The sounds of the creatures and weapons are also of high quality, similar to the first game. Some of the smaller weapons do sound a little bit weak but still suit the guns and the special animations and designs on some guns had cool sounds to go along with them. For example, I used a rocket launcher at one point that included a revolving chamber-like design that slowly spun up after you reloaded.
The graphics have improved, but for the most part it’s only moderate. Most of the improvement seems to be higher resolution textures, but the main difference between the aesthetics of the game is that the colours are much more vibrant and feel much better now. Gearbox promised to put special care into the PC version, which is evident and finally includes a slider to adjust the Field of View, making the game feel much better for my resolution (I chose a setting of 100 for 1920×1080). Plenty of PhysX effects on PC are included that look great and show that they’ve put a lot of effort into the “port” now.
The difficulty has increased a bit; you’ll have to think about what you’re doing more and possibly do some tweaking to your “build” for some parts. There is often a greater diversity in resistances and weaknesses in the enemies together (robots and some soldiers being armoured, for example), so you have to make sure you have multiple elemental weapons at hand to deal with them individually. For some reason, Gearbox decided to make death feel like much more of a penalty too. The death process involves more than just a teleporting animation back to a New-U station now, you also have to watch yourself drop to the ground, then teleport to the station and watch a cutscene of you materialising into existence. It’s quite frustrating to have to wait through, especially when you’re at a difficult section of the game. The bosses are more interesting and larger, however, with longer fights to provide a greater sense of achievement to match the difficulty of taking them down.
The maps are bigger and more detailed, with open areas and content everywhere. There is a greater variation in environments too, which makes the world seem much more expansive and like you’re actually traveling a fair distance in the world. While a good bunch of the quests are the typical collection situation there are still plenty of them that have enough character to them to feel fresh and worthwhile (even some funny easter egg quests to find). There is a quest for example that you can get from a bandit-looking guy who gives you the rather straightforward task of shooting him in the face…that’s it, but it’s quests like that that are the most fun in the game (depending on the person that may or may not sound like a bad thing, but I assure you it’s more the originality than substance that I’m referring to). There are lengthier fun quests which involve helping a cult that believe Lilith to be some sort of fire God, checking to see if Handsome Jack’s “Grandma” is okay, and both inviting people for and attending Claptap’s birthday party to name a few. Slot machines are provided for your gambling needs to use up your precious credit and gamble on getting better guns and rewards. You can even tip Moxxi at her bar, which eventually rewards you with unique weapons for your generosity.
In Borderlands 2 the story is better and much more developed, but I feel that’s mostly less by the choice of the player and more because the story involvement is more present by force. The player has to wait for characters to finish talking in many of the main story missions to progress, and if you don’t care too much about the story (which is very common in co-op play) it can be quite a hindrance.
Hyperion’s huge space station is always visible on the planet – a constant reminder of its presence and influence. The Hyperion soldiers and robots are dropped in from space; you can both see and hear as they’re sent down as obstacles on your adventure. Handsome Jack regularly contacts you, with taunts as a constant reminder of the force you’re up against and the force you need to stop. The relationship between the two of you swaps as you progress. His light-hearted demeanour at the start of the game is both amusing and instils a hateful determination to take him down, but as you continuously resist his attempts to stop you he realises that you’re a legitimate threat, and his laughter turns to anger. At this point you realise that you’re now laughing at him. You’re now in the position of pitying him as he protests. The reason that Handsome Jack is such an important part of the story for me that he’s the element that makes the story such a prominent part of the game. In the first Borderlands, the story was probably the last factor of the player’s enjoyment of the game – it was all about the guns and the characters.
I thoroughly enjoyed my time playing Borderlands 2, both 1st and 2nd playthrough. It took me about 40 hours to complete both playthroughs with about half of the side quests done (doing all of the side quests will probably be another 10-15 hours). There is plenty of replayability if you have friends to play with and cooperative play is the most fun way to play. I will say that the first couple of hours were rather boring, but once you reach Sanctuary and get better guns it’s worth sticking around. I feel that the story was admittedly saved only by Handsome Jack from being almost as easily overlooked as in the first game, but other than that it's pretty much the Borderlands 2 we've been waiting for.

Borderlands 2 is awesome. It's fun, full of content and humor, gorgeous at high resolutions, and well worth your money. For you Mac gamers out there, I should note that this game runs very well under OS X thanks to a great port by Aspyr.
First, I should note that I played the first Borderlands game, and I didn't enjoy it. So, when I purchased this game, I had low expectations for what I would be getting. Maybe that's why I was so blown away.
Graphics-wise, the game looks gorgeous. One of the biggest selling points (at least for me) of Borderlands is the amazing art style. Much like Team Fortress 2 and Jet Set Radio, the world of Borderlands 2 is convincing - a living, breathing, weighty, realized, but "cartoon" world. Little hints of humor appear here and there in the landscape - "Dook hut - No Fapping" signs, for example - and the landscapes and areas are a breath of fresh air from the typical dull-grey shooter fare we've become accustomed to over the past decade or so.
Areas and enemies are also greatly varied. While there are the typical grunt bad guys, you'll fight everything from plant life to angry midgets. Boss fights are quite fun as well, and since bosses drop the best loot, you'll find yourself fighting them often.
Borderlands 2 mixes up the typical FPS shooting mechanics, greatly benefiting the player. In addition to a wide variety of weapons, your character will gain unique abilities as you level up. The "builds" you can make with your character can vary their abilities, and thus your playstyle, greatly. Best of all, you can re-spec your abilities if you'd like to change your character up.
The grind for loot is a major part of this game. If you love hoarding weapons and items with various bonuses and abilities, you'll be at home in Borderlands 2. Any time you find a great weapon or item, it's like a small hit of dopamine that goes off in your brain. For that moment, you're satisfied, but you'll be back soon, wanting more.
DLC - I find the DLC in this game is good, though some have complained. If you purchase Borderlands 2, I would advise purchasing the Season Pass before you beat the game. The DLC's, especially the Tiny Tina DLC, greatly expand the world and offer more loot opportunity.
Finally, if you have friends (what are those?) who play Borderlands 2, you'll love playing co-op with them. Better loot, tougher enemies, and all that jazz.
Based on my experiences with Borderlands 2, I can't recommend this game highly enough.

Ah, Undertale.
I found out about this game through the sudden YouTube craze surrounding it and let me say, I was skeptical at first. I thought it was another Five Nights At Freddy's. Not bad, but relatively shallow in terms of gameplay and content. Oh man was I wrong. While one run of the game can be completed in 4-6 hours,  there's
many different ways to play it. The endings are all intriguing and satisfying, and it really makes you want to get to all of them.
At its core, Undertale is a standard RPG with one big change. You don't have to hurt anything throughout the course of the game. Not once. This core feature, along with the well-implemented decision-making, is really what sets it apart from other games. The combat is cool, nothing super amazing but it has a pretty fun and interactive way to dodge enemy attacks.
To avoid spoilers, I won't name off any of the characters here, but let me just say that Undertale has some of the best writing I've seen in a long time. There's humor scattered about, even just blatant observations of things that can make you laugh. No game's characters have stuck with me the way the Undertale's have. Each has their own unique, special personality and really stand out from the crowd.
Buy this game and buy it now. Even if you're not an RPG kind of person, trust me. Undertale is more than just your average RPG.

Let me get this out of the way first. I judge a game on a what I paid for it basis, and I demand 2 hours of solid entertainment per 5$ spent. This game has 1 play though that I like, the first one, and that first place through without dlc can clock in at 30-40 hours long depending on how sidetracked you get with side missions. On that metric alone, the game is worth getting.
HOWEVER, when you get to play though 2 or 3, that's when I stop enjoying the game altogether. See the game is a stats based game that focused on multiplayer and classes interacting with each other. The problem is the loot system in the game is competitive and unless you have 4 good friends you trust, or better yet, know in real life so you can punch them if they steal the good loot all the time, the better. The problem is I don't have good friends in real life who won't steal loot and like the game. So because of that I am forced to join random games if I want to play multiplayer, which just sucks.
Now why do I mention the multiplayer with play through 2 and 3? Probably because of how the enemies in the game gain so much health that even your most powerful shotgun at level 49 can't touch something at level 51. The exponential ramp up of stats out right kills all enjoyment I get out of the game prior to it, it demands that I play with outers, a point where the game fails if you don't have the close friend group.
I'm at level 51-61, I forget what my character is at because I haven't picked the game up in a while, but come Julyish the dlc went on a major sale, so I picked it up, wanting to play Tiny Tina's campaign. The thing is, I just can't find the will to play the game anymore. They made loot a painful grind at the high end, and then they took away the bee shield from shotguns with expedited the 1 in 100 kills some loot is. See that shield made a shotgun blast a 1 hit kill for many enemies, but you couldn't take damage, I have among the best snipers in the game, the best guns in the game (without hacking) but most of the time a headshot isn't a kill shot, a shotgun could take a full clip to kill one thing. Because of the reuse timer on your special ability, you are forced to hide for your life from even the weakest enemies because you just cannot kill them without it.
See other games like torchlight, diablo, and others get it. You don't die to the cannon fodder, sure sheer numbers can kill you at times if you aren't paying attention, and bosses can, but for the most part, its 1-3 slashes and its dead. This game? Melee is a joke, and even the most powerful of weapons can't kill enemies in 1-3 clips, much less shots, but they sure as hell can kill you in 1.
Play through 1 - 8/10
Play through 2 (pre bee nerf) - 6/10
Play through 2 (post bee nerf) - 4/10
Play through 3 - 2/10
I can't recommend the game passed the first play through and if you want to play for the high end and the "best guns" other games will do you better in the reward for your loot.

All the cools kids seem to be doing their "first few hours" of games, so I'll give it a go.
Joined a random public official server. I had next to no idea what I was meant to be doing, but I had a rock and three meters.  I spawned in at night on a small beach, so I instantly began to freeze and lost a bit of health. Following the coastline, I found many houses (in hindsight, they were all probably abandoned), and pilfered some pumpkins and corn from a small crop field. I then immediately hightailed it to the mountains and began cutting down some trees for wood. After about 45 minutes of running around and trying to figure out how to cook food, I died of food poisoning from stolen food after starving and drinking salty water.
Spawn back in again and this time I go straight to looking for food. I found some mushrooms but I guess they belonged to a guy as he shot me with an arrow. I managed to hide inside a bush, but I spent the next ten minutes hiding inside of it thinking he was still there, until I poked my head out and found out it was a horse. Didn't find any food but I found a player idling on the beach. Died of starvation.
This time, I went inland. There were a lot of gunshots in the distance and people getting angry over someone cheating. I got shot in the back by a guy with a bow, who then apologized thinking that I was a threat and let me go. For whatever reason I thought it would be a good idea to run towards the gunshots. Got scared and hid in another bush. I slowly snuck inside an empty house and took my bearing. Killed a horse (first kill!) and ate it over a fire in the empty shack. I then got out of the warzone and headed towards the beach. I was still pretty hungry so I needed to get some food. After following the beach for some time I found and killed a wild boar, who happily dropped four pork for me, enough to sustain me for a long time. After chasing down another boar, a man saw me, shot me, berated me for my sloppy fighting (despite never really ever fighting before) and then murdered me with my own spear.
I joined a new server (my dignity was low but spirits still high) and went exploring the forests. The people here (if there were people) were a bit more friendly, keeping their distance from me. I actually managed to make myself a bow, 100 arrows and a burlap suit. But food was another story. I searched every forest and valley for food and all I could find was the occasional mushroom. No deer, horse or boar to be seen. I pilfered another pumpkin farm and set to work building a base, only to be suprise attacked by a bear and killed. I did build a sleeping bag this time, but the bear just turned around and immediately killed me again anyway.
After 3 hours, 4 or so deaths and 6 or so kills, I think I'm done for the moment. This game is fun, but I don't think I can get too invested in it what with all the raiding and such.

Unlocking cool blueprints is fun, server wiping and losing everything is not. When there's a cool update I try to join in the fun, having to ignore abuse, russian, and russian abuse hurled at me. I try to avoid servers with hackers which usually results in me playing by myself.
However the gender forcing update has turned me away from this game completely. This has nothing to do with sexism, or misogyny. I just feel that choices like this belong in the hands of the players.
In short, I do not recommend this game, there are beter places to spend your money if you want a survival game, a decent community experience and the freedom to evolve your character as you wish.

Borderlands 2, the second installment in the Borderlands series, is much like its predecessor. It's filled with witty, raunchy humor, blood and gore, and even more guns. Yet despite all of these things, the game suffers from very repetitive gameplay and inconsistent writing. The guns do have variety, but the differences are negligable at best. The player customization, as far as aesthetics go, has improved a bit, but the classes the players are expected to choose from vary only slightly from the ones in the first game. The gameplay quickly becomes a "desk job" of killing everything in the area, rummaging through everything with a green light on it, rinse and repeat. Even the quests are seemingly pointless. The player is forced through so many quests that have very little motivation on the part of the player to accomplish that they become boring and uninteresting. I found myself finishing the quests simply to hear some of the well written, witty humor that the game's characters have, but that's about it. The missions were just bridges between dialogues. If you enjoy Call of Duty, but not the annoying children that populate the online play, then Borderlands 2 is right up your alley. The game sustains entertainment for +/-20 hours of gameplay, but quickly becomes boring and repetitive, even with the addition of DLC.
An absolute blast with huge improvements from the first game. Multiple playthroughs are challenging and completely worthwhile. 400+ hours in and I'm not bored with Borderlands 2 yet.

Borderlands 2 is a game for those that enjoy the feeling of finding awesome equipment hidden in a massive pile of other stuff.
Sure, you don't NEED to go in-depth with this game.  On the first playthrough you can get by with just picking up gear as you travel along, choosing stuff that looks better than your current gear, and maybe occasionally buying something in the vendor that looks handy.  The deeper you go down the rabbit hole however, the more there is to discover.
The story is decent for a First Person Shooter (albeit one with RPG elements), and dialogue is often amusing to a degree.  Handsome Jack, the main antagonist is a cartoon villain with M rated attitudes.  He believes, or at least pretends to believe that he is the good guy, and you are just a "Filthy Bandit.".
Graphically, the game has a lot more variations in design and color scheme than it's predecessor (which was brown, brown, and a bit of color here and there).  Cell shaded graphics with thick, graphic novel like outlines is the style of the game, and does a good job of separating it from the average FPS.
Now, on to the gameplay itself!:
Action is often fast paced and exciting.  So long as you don't allow yourself to get too far ahead of the enemy levels, you'll find battles where you have to fight hard to win.  The game does a decent job of easing you into the various elements, such as different gun types (Pistol, SMG, Assault/Combat Rifle, Shotgun, Revolver, Rocket Launcher, and Sniper Rifle), the importance of a good shield, grenade mods (alter the way your grenade behaves, including damage bonuses and special effects), Class Mods (Class-specific devices which can boost skills, and have other effects like increasing fire rate with specific weapon types), and lastly Relics (Device which generally boost damage or defence in some way).  Equipment rarity is also made fairly clear.  It goes White, Green, Blue, Purple, Magenta, Orange, Seraph, and Pearlescent.  The final two rarities (Pearlescent and Seraph) are special.  Seraphs require you to have at least one of the season pass DLC to obtain (and you need all 4 of the Season Pass DLC to obtain all the Seraph rarity items), and as to Pearlescent rarity weapons, you need to be in Ultimate Vault Hunter Mode (Playthrough 3) for them to have a chance of being spawned.  Don't assume that a blue is automatically better than a green rarity item, even at the same level.  Experiment!
Playable Characters and Skills:
There are 4 included playable characters, and two DLC characters.  Each class has it's ups and downs, and a special game changing skill unique to them.  For example, Salvador (Gunzerker) will dual-wield guns when his action skill is active, meaning TWICE THE FIREPOWER.  Axton (Commando) drops a turret, which damages enemies and draws aggression away from you.  Maya (Siren) locks an enemy's movements for a short time, allowing you to get in free hits.  Zer0 turns invisible for a few seconds and launches a decoy, and his first attack made whilst in this mode does increased damage.  The DLC characters are Gaige (Mechromancer) who launches a flying robot that attacks nearby enemies, and Kreig (Psycho); a schizophrenic musclebound maniac that will whale on everything within reach with increased offensive and defensive capabilities and can even throw his axe at more distant targets.
Aside from the action skills unique to the character, there are various other skills that you can put points into, and have an effect on gameplay in some way.  For example, increasing fire rate or damage for a few seconds after a kill is made.  Each character has 3 skill trees, each ending with a final gamechanging skill modifier.  For example, Zer0's Bloodlust (Melee) tree ends with the Many Must Fall perk, which will instantly re-deploy the hologram if he kills the enemy with one melee strike.  As mentioned before, Class Mods unique to a character class will boost certain skills.  It's possible for them to go as high as +6, meaning some skills can be boosted to 11, as the normal limit on points you can put into most skills is 5, though some skills are only 1 (those usually affect the way you play).
Plus, there is a gun that shoots swords....EXPLODING swords...In DLC4 (Tiny Tina's Assault on the Dragon Keep).  So yeah, there is that too.
I hope you found my review useful, even if it might be a bit messy XD

All jokes aside, the internet ruined this game. Furries, tumblr, and other degenerate types completely took the characters, story, and setting and ran with it, flooding the internet with their terrible fanfiction, matchmaking, and theories, so if you already know the story, characters, setting, and whatnot because you spent too much time on the internet, dont even bother buying it. Its a simple, cute, funny, crazy game, but as far as actual GAMEPLAY goes, it's just simple (yet sometimes difficult) bullet hell sequences. The only difference is the wacky enemy encounters and the off the wall actions you can take, the story and dialogue is what really makes it, so if you already know everything thanks to autistic fanbase, you're not gonna get much out of it except the occasional chuckle. I played this with friends and we had a great time snickering at all the crazy stuff, and I loved the game so much I made the mistake of searching for discussions and art of it online... And that's when I realized how cursed Undertale is with it's terrible fanbase of cringeworthy internet troglodytes. This game deserves to be experienced with its innocence intact, so for the love of god, stay away from the internet discussion boards about it, and just play it, have a good time, and remember it as that quirky little adventure that that you giggled at.
TL;DR Great game, not mind blowing or lifechanging by any way, just fun, but the absolutely terrible fandom has overhyped it so much, it's doomed by its own popularity amongst ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and weirdos.

First thing I gotta tell ya: Borderlands 2 is hi-la-rio-us.
Second thing I gotta let ya know: The art style is awesome.
It's 100% pure, juicy, cell-shaded yumminess that fits perfectly with the game's tone. Funny.
I have to admit, I didn't get Borderlands 2 the "legit" way at first (I don't constantly have game money to throw around) so it says something about how enraptured (haha, get it, Bioshock, 2K...) I was when I tell you I actually BOUGHT IT(!!!) after playing half the game off-Steam. It is the first title I picked up in the series, and I got it because I'd heard good things from my friends. It was a multiplayer, shooty, very pretty game so I thought, "Why not?" and got it during the summer sale for ten bucks. I started playing, and I loved it. I played the heck out of it for about two weeks. Shooting, looting, guns ("No refunds!"), awesome quests, and funny challenges (to get Badass Tokens, if you can believe it). What more could a girl want? A lot of people rave about the multiplayer, but I prefer the single player. It's quieter, you don't have anyone stealing your hard-earned stuff, and the pop-culture references + ridiculous tasks are enough to keep you giggling for at least the first single-player playthrough.
Did I mention you can play this game up to 4 or 5 times, getting higher level loot and harder bosses? Pretty darn cool, although I must say it gets a bit boring playing the same story again and again. I am seriously loving this game, though, and I try to mention it to my other gaming friends because not enough people have caught the BL2 disease! I'm eagerly waiting for the Winter Sale to get some steals on the DLC, especially Tiny Tina's Assault on Dragon Keep, which is based on DnD. :D
I'd say 9.5/10.

Rust is the defining survival/gatherer game, and it has been under development for quite some time. I also receives very regular updates, and from what I understand the developers communicate with the community a lot. However, I cannot recommend this game in its current form.
The game is predominently PvP, and with that comes all the ugliness of an anonymous community. You will be shot, stabbed and stomped on with no reason or provocation, other than it's "fun" to do so. You will spend hours fortifying a base, only to have someone C4 it to heck while you're offline.
This game needs more coherent and meaningful PvE dangers. So far you have randomly placed wildlife, only two of which will attack you. You also have a patrolling helicopter that may occasionally hunt you down. It's not enough, and coupled with other environmental aspects, are all easily mitigated or avoided.
Originally the game had radiation as a theme, with irradiated towns and wildlife. The game really needs to expand on that theme, and introduce things such as herds of irradiated creatures that roam the world. Events, such as spikes of radiation, radioactive dust storms, large irraditaed creatures attacking etc. I commented a while back that Rust would be awesome if it included the cannibals from The Forest. Rust needs something like that, so it can have a PvP mode for people that like that kind of thing, and a PvE mode for people like me, who prefer cooperation against an ever increasingly hostile world.

Spawn in naked in a random location on a procedurally generated island & start collecting resources for your very first house. Make basic tools & learn how to make more advanced gear and weapons. Meet people in-game, make friends & get betrayed for the first time. Lose everything due to mistakes you made. Learn from your mistakes & build the next house in a better location with appropriate safety measures. Form a clan & declare war on other clans. Cooperate with smaller clans. Attack & destroy critical parts of an enemy base, steal everything they’ve got & return home with more stuff than you had before.
Rust is really the ultimate FPS survival experience right now. It surpassed competitors like DayZ a long time ago in terms of performance, stability & content. I spent 20€ on this game and that’s an investment that really paid off. It’s given me loads of entertainment and since the developers Facepunch add more content to the game on an almost weekly basis I’d argue that this is probably the best early access title on the market & it’s already better in many ways than many full price games out there.
The developers are very active on social media like Reddit. They respond to feedback, give insight on what they've got planned & reasoning behind changes. It's very refreshing to see developers that are this engaged with their community.
The only downside I can think of is that it’s a very hard game for players that play alone. Even the developers said that it’s not meant to be played alone. You’re supposed to “make friends or die” pretty much. Don’t let that put you off though. It’s easy to meet other players in-game & team up. And keep in mind that you WILL make mistakes that lead to your demise. Accept it & learn from your mistakes.
TL;DR
Good game
Amazing with friends

The story kind of continues where the last game ended but this time we have new Vault hunters, new enemies and a new Vault. The story is great and offered me many hours of playtime.

Rust = Survival of the fittest
If you want a game about peace, love and dancing in poppy fields then this game is not for you :) So for all the negative reviews about a toxic community I would simply suggest that you don't understand the nature of this game.
Everything you do in rust needs to be assessed from the perspective of "how will this benefit me, and what is the risk" so when you find another player you need to asses the risk in wanting to have a nice talk with a random player who appears "wink wink" to be friendly as this may result in having your brains blown out. In rust you need resources to build, if you "steal" another players resources i.e. (blow their brains out and take from there corpse) you can build faster and protect yourself better. There is also an advantage to forming a group but this comes with its own risk i.e. could I tolerate this squeakers voice for more than 10 minutes, will he betray me, is he utterly useless, is his cod piece bigger than mine. :)
Every encounter is a adrenaline fuelled adventure leaving your heart pounding and your butt cheeks clenched, oh and either the euphoric thrill of victory from defeating an enemy or resisting the urge to punish the keyboard when you get shot. No other game I know of lets you grind your enemies into dust quite like rust, first you kill them, then chop the body up for meat, then destroy their base, then take all the resources they spent hours collecting, and last up dinner time "fillet of enemy" whilst telling the guy you killed your eating him in chat :).
You start with nothing but a rock and a torch but with enough time and dedication you can build an empire. You don't need a team to survive in rust although it does make it easier. Anyone can have a big base with all the trimmings if you play smart.
I have over 1200 hours in this game and have only every seen a few hackers, if you play on a server with active admins they will ban the hacker immediately. If anyone wishes to buy the game but does not want to play alone then add me on steam and you can join my group of players and we can give you the rust crash course.

Borderlands 2 is a game for those that enjoy the feeling of finding awesome equipment hidden in a massive pile of other stuff.
Sure, you don't NEED to go in-depth with this game.  On the first playthrough you can get by with just picking up gear as you travel along, choosing stuff that looks better than your current gear, and maybe occasionally buying something in the vendor that looks handy.  The deeper you go down the rabbit hole however, the more there is to discover.
The story is decent for a First Person Shooter (albeit one with RPG elements), and dialogue is often amusing to a degree.  Handsome Jack, the main antagonist is a cartoon villain with M rated attitudes.  He believes, or at least pretends to believe that he is the good guy, and you are just a "Filthy Bandit.".
Graphically, the game has a lot more variations in design and color scheme than it's predecessor (which was brown, brown, and a bit of color here and there).  Cell shaded graphics with thick, graphic novel like outlines is the style of the game, and does a good job of separating it from the average FPS.
Now, on to the gameplay itself!:
Action is often fast paced and exciting.  So long as you don't allow yourself to get too far ahead of the enemy levels, you'll find battles where you have to fight hard to win.  The game does a decent job of easing you into the various elements, such as different gun types (Pistol, SMG, Assault/Combat Rifle, Shotgun, Revolver, Rocket Launcher, and Sniper Rifle), the importance of a good shield, grenade mods (alter the way your grenade behaves, including damage bonuses and special effects), Class Mods (Class-specific devices which can boost skills, and have other effects like increasing fire rate with specific weapon types), and lastly Relics (Device which generally boost damage or defence in some way).  Equipment rarity is also made fairly clear.  It goes White, Green, Blue, Purple, Magenta, Orange, Seraph, and Pearlescent.  The final two rarities (Pearlescent and Seraph) are special.  Seraphs require you to have at least one of the season pass DLC to obtain (and you need all 4 of the Season Pass DLC to obtain all the Seraph rarity items), and as to Pearlescent rarity weapons, you need to be in Ultimate Vault Hunter Mode (Playthrough 3) for them to have a chance of being spawned.  Don't assume that a blue is automatically better than a green rarity item, even at the same level.  Experiment!
Playable Characters and Skills:
There are 4 included playable characters, and two DLC characters.  Each class has it's ups and downs, and a special game changing skill unique to them.  For example, Salvador (Gunzerker) will dual-wield guns when his action skill is active, meaning TWICE THE FIREPOWER.  Axton (Commando) drops a turret, which damages enemies and draws aggression away from you.  Maya (Siren) locks an enemy's movements for a short time, allowing you to get in free hits.  Zer0 turns invisible for a few seconds and launches a decoy, and his first attack made whilst in this mode does increased damage.  The DLC characters are Gaige (Mechromancer) who launches a flying robot that attacks nearby enemies, and Kreig (Psycho); a schizophrenic musclebound maniac that will whale on everything within reach with increased offensive and defensive capabilities and can even throw his axe at more distant targets.
Aside from the action skills unique to the character, there are various other skills that you can put points into, and have an effect on gameplay in some way.  For example, increasing fire rate or damage for a few seconds after a kill is made.  Each character has 3 skill trees, each ending with a final gamechanging skill modifier.  For example, Zer0's Bloodlust (Melee) tree ends with the Many Must Fall perk, which will instantly re-deploy the hologram if he kills the enemy with one melee strike.  As mentioned before, Class Mods unique to a character class will boost certain skills.  It's possible for them to go as high as +6, meaning some skills can be boosted to 11, as the normal limit on points you can put into most skills is 5, though some skills are only 1 (those usually affect the way you play).
Plus, there is a gun that shoots swords....EXPLODING swords...In DLC4 (Tiny Tina's Assault on the Dragon Keep).  So yeah, there is that too.
I hope you found my review useful, even if it might be a bit messy XD

First thing I gotta tell ya: Borderlands 2 is hi-la-rio-us.
Second thing I gotta let ya know: The art style is awesome.
It's 100% pure, juicy, cell-shaded yumminess that fits perfectly with the game's tone. Funny.
I have to admit, I didn't get Borderlands 2 the "legit" way at first (I don't constantly have game money to throw around) so it says something about how enraptured (haha, get it, Bioshock, 2K...) I was when I tell you I actually BOUGHT IT(!!!) after playing half the game off-Steam. It is the first title I picked up in the series, and I got it because I'd heard good things from my friends. It was a multiplayer, shooty, very pretty game so I thought, "Why not?" and got it during the summer sale for ten bucks. I started playing, and I loved it. I played the heck out of it for about two weeks. Shooting, looting, guns ("No refunds!"), awesome quests, and funny challenges (to get Badass Tokens, if you can believe it). What more could a girl want? A lot of people rave about the multiplayer, but I prefer the single player. It's quieter, you don't have anyone stealing your hard-earned stuff, and the pop-culture references + ridiculous tasks are enough to keep you giggling for at least the first single-player playthrough.
Did I mention you can play this game up to 4 or 5 times, getting higher level loot and harder bosses? Pretty darn cool, although I must say it gets a bit boring playing the same story again and again. I am seriously loving this game, though, and I try to mention it to my other gaming friends because not enough people have caught the BL2 disease! I'm eagerly waiting for the Winter Sale to get some steals on the DLC, especially Tiny Tina's Assault on Dragon Keep, which is based on DnD. :D
I'd say 9.5/10.
TL;DR - Buy Borderlands 2. You probably won't regret it.

Rust is the defining survival/gatherer game, and it has been under development for quite some time. I also receives very regular updates, and from what I understand the developers communicate with the community a lot. However, I cannot recommend this game in its current form.
The game is predominently PvP, and with that comes all the ugliness of an anonymous community. You will be shot, stabbed and stomped on with no reason or provocation, other than it's "fun" to do so. You will spend hours fortifying a base, only to have someone C4 it to heck while you're offline.
This game needs more coherent and meaningful PvE dangers. So far you have randomly placed wildlife, only two of which will attack you. You also have a patrolling helicopter that may occasionally hunt you down. It's not enough, and coupled with other environmental aspects, are all easily mitigated or avoided.
Originally the game had radiation as a theme, with irradiated towns and wildlife. The game really needs to expand on that theme, and introduce things such as herds of irradiated creatures that roam the world. Events, such as spikes of radiation, radioactive dust storms, large irraditaed creatures attacking etc. I commented a while back that Rust would be awesome if it included the cannibals from The Forest. Rust needs something like that, so it can have a PvP mode for people that like that kind of thing, and a PvE mode for people like me, who prefer cooperation against an ever increasingly hostile world.

Borderlands 2 is easily one of the finest shooters on the market today, the sheer innovation that the Borderlands franchise brought to the genre in 2009 is staggering and as a huge fan of both Diablo-esque AARPGs and first person shooters I must say that if you haven't played this game your doing yourself a huge disservice.
+ Great visuals: Borderlands 2 isn't Crysis by any means but it isn't trying to be either, it's colorful and vibrant and makes for an extremely beautiful gaming experience it's visuals are somewhat dated but somehow always come out looking perfectly acceptable.
+ Replayability: The game features a random loot generation system which insures that the items you're awarded are never qute the same through each playthrough, that coupled with multiple difficulty levels, a large skill tree for each character, multiple characters, and several different effective builds for each character really makes the game feel slightly different each way you choose to play it.
++ Multiplayer: The multiplayer in this game is top notch, several games on the market today tend to make multiplayer feel either tacked on or they make it a chore to play with other people, this game has wonderful 'drop in drop out' gameplay that makes it to where any player regardless of level or gameplay progression can play together.
+ Optimization: As someone who has played this game on both a high end gaming computer (Intel/Nvidia based PC) and an entry level gaming computer (AMD based PC) I can testify that it runs quite well regardless of what you're trying to run it on, the only time I had trouble running it was when I was attempting to use AMD hardware with PhysX which is Nvidia's proprietary physics engine.
- Accessibility at this point it the game's life cycle: Since the game's release there have been several DLCs released for the game which may make picking it up now seem a little daunting and expensive.
- Borderlands 2's kind of humor: I personally loved the game's humor but some may find it immature and silly, even at it's most serious there is still some underlying comedy to it.
- Loot ninjas: When playing online the loot that is dropped by the enemies is not dropped for each individual character but the group as a whole which has led to people stealing all the loot and immediately leaving the match.
- Repetition: Though the loot system and character system tend to keep things fresh for the most part some may find the gameplay repetative as you will often end up shooting your way through hordes of the same enemies and bosses.
8.5/10
Reasonable Price Point: I bought the game when it first came out so I paid full price and I've bought each DLC as it's released (Apart from the alternate colors/costumes) and I don't have a bit of regret I would say the reasonable price point would be anywhere in the $50 to 60$ USD range.

Holy balls, where do I begin?
This game is beyond amazing. The greatest first-person shooter ever envisioned, filled with pop-culture references and comedy, with a lighthearted spin that every game should take a leaf out of.
The story begins with a man called Handsome Jack. You meet him as a industrious and hilarious guy, but his motives become clear. He's serious. He's also one of the greatest villians in video game history.
This game has HEAVY RPG elements and is not for those that wish for a pick-up-and-play shooter. This game sucks your time out through a straw. Gun choices are almost infinite (87 bazillion) making no specific gun the one that is the greatest. Voice acting is splendid, enemies are varied and hilarious (I'M GONNA MAKE YOU MY NEW MEAT BICYCLE!) and the world is huge. Tons of replay value as well, including 2 new game plus modes and 4 extensive DLC missions.
So, if you like shooters, if you like RPGs, if you like comedy, or if you just love video games in general, give Borderlands 2 a whirl. You won't regret it. I'm known for my dislike of first-person shooters, but this game blew me away and is now one of my favorites ever.
Now get out there, and let the great journey of shooting and looting begin!

Spawn in naked in a random location on a procedurally generated island & start collecting resources for your very first house. Make basic tools & learn how to make more advanced gear and weapons. Meet people in-game, make friends & get betrayed for the first time. Lose everything due to mistakes you made. Learn from your mistakes & build the next house in a better location with appropriate safety measures. Form a clan & declare war on other clans. Cooperate with smaller clans. Attack & destroy critical parts of an enemy base, steal everything they’ve got & return home with more stuff than you had before.
Rust is really the ultimate FPS survival experience right now. It surpassed competitors like DayZ a long time ago in terms of performance, stability & content. I spent 20€ on this game and that’s an investment that really paid off. It’s given me loads of entertainment and since the developers Facepunch add more content to the game on an almost weekly basis I’d argue that this is probably the best early access title on the market & it’s already better in many ways than many full price games out there.
The developers are very active on social media like Reddit. They respond to feedback, give insight on what they've got planned & reasoning behind changes. It's very refreshing to see developers that are this engaged with their community.
The only downside I can think of is that it’s a very hard game for players that play alone. Even the developers said that it’s not meant to be played alone. You’re supposed to “make friends or die” pretty much. Don’t let that put you off though. It’s easy to meet other players in-game & team up. And keep in mind that you WILL make mistakes that lead to your demise. Accept it & learn from your mistakes.

Diablo With Guns, that would be the best way to describe this game.
As a Single Player game it's not bad at all, the Story is Great, it's got a good Longevity to it, but the meat of the game is the Loot and the challenge that it offers.
The game offers serevall classes and all of them can be modified to your liking, either be a Solo Hunter or a Party Healer and Buffer, it's your choice and the best part is that each class was it's own playstile and not just a simple change of main type of weapons.
The Game engine is well optimized (even with PhysX, it is one of the games that best uses it and with the least impact on performance), and the Online is Great, unlike the first Borderlands, the second one deals much better with your progress in a Single Player Game and your progress with a Co Op Game (let's say you finish a quest in Co Op that you did not even got near in Single Player... when you unlock said quest, or quests, in your Single Player, the game will go "oh hey! You already done that Online, want to skip that?").
Most of the DLC are worth it but... if you need to choose, as for story driven DLC... Tiny Tinas is the best one!
As for the DLC classes, well... it's a matter of playstile, I can't help you with that, the Mechnonancer is a pet focused class and the Psycho is a Melee class.
Overall, it's a good Single Player game and a Great Co-Op Game, one of the best in that regard.

The game play can be repetitive, but for some reason, I can't put it down. Leveling up doesn't incur the same exhilaration that other loot grinders/dungeon crawlers do, seeing as all but one of your skills are passives. But there's a couple of things that keep me coming back to this game. It's the massive amounts of loot, and the bigger-and-bigger enemies that you face.

Borderlands 2 is not as good as the first game. Oh, sure, it's got a better (more emotional!) story, more diverse maps, more vehicles, a cool head and skin system, more gun types and effects, and is just all around a bigger, more varied experience, but it's not... well, okay. The first game wasn't a great shooter. Borderlands 2 isn't either. It mostly relies on simply pointing and clicking. The stats all ultimately determine how quickly an enemy's health bar diminishes in size. It's not as if we're playing Half-Life or Halo or FEAR or Bulletstorm or something, because we're not. We're playing a game that's about loot.
Too bad the loot drop ratios are so bad. I don't know why they're worse than they were in the original game, but I do know that in my hundred-some hours of play, I only managed to pick up four or five orange items. That seems wrong. Borderlands 2 is the first game that made me seriously consider using CheatEngine. Me, I don't like cheats unless they're humorous, but Borderlands 2's drop ratios are so frustrating, requiring needless, endless grinding from players, that I found myself kinda going "yeah... let's make things more like they were in the first game."
The story is great. I've mentioned that. I should mention it again. It's great. Best of all is Tiny Tina's Assault on Dragon Keep, which is apparently the only DLC developed entirely in-house at Gearbox (the others were apparently outsourced, which might suggest why they're all kind of terrible in terms of level design, pacing, and the like and only worth playing for the humor--Hammerlock's Hunt is easily the worst one), which actually kinda makes me feel emotions and stuff that I don't normally like feeling in video games.

This game needs more coherent and meaningful PvE dangers. So far you have randomly placed wildlife, only two of which will attack you. You also have a patrolling helicopter that may occasionally hunt you down. It's not enough, and coupled with other environmental aspects, are all easily mitigated or avoided.
Originally the game had radiation as a theme, with irradiated towns and wildlife. The game really needs to expand on that theme, and introduce things such as herds of irradiated creatures that roam the world. Events, such as spikes of radiation, radioactive dust storms, large irraditaed creatures attacking etc. I commented a while back that Rust would be awesome if it included the cannibals from The Forest. Rust needs something like that, so it can have a PvP mode for people that like that kind of thing, and a PvE mode for people like me, who prefer cooperation against an ever increasingly hostile world.

Borderlands 2 is easily one of the finest shooters on the market today, the sheer innovation that the Borderlands franchise brought to the genre in 2009 is staggering and as a huge fan of both Diablo-esque AARPGs and first person shooters I must say that if you haven't played this game your doing yourself a huge disservice.
+ Great visuals: Borderlands 2 isn't Crysis by any means but it isn't trying to be either, it's colorful and vibrant and makes for an extremely beautiful gaming experience it's visuals are somewhat dated but somehow always come out looking perfectly acceptable.
+ Replayability: The game features a random loot generation system which insures that the items you're awarded are never qute the same through each playthrough, that coupled with multiple difficulty levels, a large skill tree for each character, multiple characters, and several different effective builds for each character really makes the game feel slightly different each way you choose to play it.
++ Multiplayer: The multiplayer in this game is top notch, several games on the market today tend to make multiplayer feel either tacked on or they make it a chore to play with other people, this game has wonderful 'drop in drop out' gameplay that makes it to where any player regardless of level or gameplay progression can play together.
+ Optimization: As someone who has played this game on both a high end gaming computer (Intel/Nvidia based PC) and an entry level gaming computer (AMD based PC) I can testify that it runs quite well regardless of what you're trying to run it on, the only time I had trouble running it was when I was attempting to use AMD hardware with PhysX which is Nvidia's proprietary physics engine.
- Accessibility at this point it the game's life cycle: Since the game's release there have been several DLCs released for the game which may make picking it up now seem a little daunting and expensive.
- Borderlands 2's kind of humor: I personally loved the game's humor but some may find it immature and silly, even at it's most serious there is still some underlying comedy to it.
- Loot ninjas: When playing online the loot that is dropped by the enemies is not dropped for each individual character but the group as a whole which has led to people stealing all the loot and immediately leaving the match.
- Repetition: Though the loot system and character system tend to keep things fresh for the most part some may find the gameplay repetative as you will often end up shooting your way through hordes of the same enemies and bosses.
8.5/10
Reasonable Price Point: I bought the game when it first came out so I paid full price and I've bought each DLC as it's released (Apart from the alternate colors/costumes) and I don't have a bit of regret I would say the reasonable price point would be anywhere in the $50 to 60$ USD range.
