By this time, you have probably heard something about Undertale, due to the massive hype train about it.  Whether it is showing up in image macros, youtube videos, or various in-jokes, it is clearly a massive internet sensation.  I will do my best to try to cut through the hype and get to the core of the matter.
Undertale is an RPG based on games from the 16-bit era (SNES/Genesis) with elements of bullet dodging games.   The mechanics are fairly straightforward - walk around and interact with characters, occasionally getting into turn-based combat.   The combat interface features option for attacking the monsters, which uses a timing minigame, running, and using items.   The innovation comes in the ability to perform a variety of actions toward monsters.  Choosing certain actions will convince the monster that you are friendly, and can end an encounter without you or the monster dieing.  This awards you with gold, but does not award XP.  When it is the monster's turn, there is a brief dodging minigame. This gets tougher as the game progresses, but the game is not a bullet hell.  I've been okay even on my low LV run, despite being pretty bad at bullet dodging.
The graphics of Undertale are mostly 16-bit sprites, and pretty well done.  The game looks well put together, but don't 3D graphics or photo realistic designs.
The musical score for this game is one of the best I have heard in an indie game.  It's a nice blend of 16-bit retro tunes and a wide variety of musical styles ranging from symphonic to jazz to rock to polka.   Sound effects are otherwise fairly basic.  Each character has a particular sound effect for their voice, making it possible to recognize them, but there is almost no voice work in the game.
Undertale's hype is built almost entirely on its story.  It has a large number of ending variations.  Every boss you kill or spare changes the outcome of the game.  It is indeed possible to live up to the game's tagline of being the RPG where no one has to die, and that is a very satisfying if challenging outcome.  You can also kill every single monster in the game, which is challenging for its own reasons.   The game has a message to it, but it is not preachy or really self-righteous about it.  The game just treats monsters in random encounters like characters as opposed to being just a source of XP.  It also takes into account game mechanics in the story - saving and loading is something that happens in the world of the game.
Characters in Undertale are highly memorable.  Toriel and Flowey (both of who show up in the first few moments of the game and are on the cover art) are both very interesting characters with a solid amount of backstory available to explore. Writing is clear and easy to read, and the game's humor is pretty impressive.   I have written this with the intent of not spoiling the game, and it is best experienced unspoiled. (I read spoilers beforehand and wish I hadn't)
If this sounds at all interesting to you, I recommend buying Undertale.  It is well worth $10 US, the soundtrack is great, and when it is on sale it's a steal.

This game is beyond amazing. The greatest first-person shooter ever envisioned, filled with pop-culture references and comedy, with a lighthearted spin that every game should take a leaf out of.

Tons of replay value as well, including 2 new game plus modes and 4 extensive DLC missions.
So, if you like shooters, if you like RPGs, if you like comedy, or if you just love video games in general, give Borderlands 2 a whirl. You won't regret it. I'm known for my dislike of first-person shooters, but this game blew me away and is now one of my favorites ever.

borderlands 2,  the second game in the game series that invented a new game genre (loot 'n' shoot) , is a game of many genres, it has some heavy RPG aspects, switching out equipment every few seconds and upgrading your character as you level up and gain new points.  I'm not going to divulge the plot to you, although the game has one it can be a little weird to follow, especial if you do the DLCs out of order or before completing the game, all i will say is there there are plenty of opportunities to kill everything multiple times and even revisit places that you may have strolled into 5 levels to low and gotten thoroughly destroyed by even the simplest enemies there ( oh yes the RPG revenge feeling ).
If the borderlands franchise name alone dose not make you want to buy this game consider some of the DLC and the interesting things the game devs are doing to keep it fresh and exiting over a year after its original release.
the game has several DLCs that add huge areas with their own quest lines,  unique enemies, loot and new quirky characters, the best of which in my opinion is "Tiny Tina's Assault on Dragon Keep" wherein the player is pulled into a re-imagined version of Dungeons and Dragons, with the worst dungeon master of all time, the DLC is so different from the rest of the game and from borderlands as a whole that it really dose feel like a new game entirely, a strange and stupid sense of humour and some over the top ridiculousness all inside some nice FPS Dungeon and Dragon-ing with a deep, dark undertone. Along with that DLC there are many many more, giving more loot enemies and even level cap increases for those who have several hundred hours to spend and DLCs are (at time of writing) are still being made with several more set for release in the coming months.
After a few hours in game you will encounter the Hub town an if you look around you might find a nice shiny golden chest, this is a special loot chest that gives rare, powerful and level dependant loot, the gimmick to this chest is that the user must go to outside websites such as gearboxes facebook and twitter to find "shift Codes", which when entered into the extras menus give rewards such as unique loot, free costumes and golden keys for the aforementioned chest.
Community challenges have been added, requiring people to sign up for the chance to get awesome loot, these challenges require registered members to kill certain enemies or bosses to acquire extra awesome loot for all involved, these update weekly giving goals for the entire community to work together by murdering a crap tonne of bandits and skags. All of the DLCs plus the community features combine to mean that even after 100 hours there are still so many things to do and most players wont get to all of them but it is still fun trying and the game gives a great co-operative experience, teaming up to fight the super mega bosses or even going head to head in duels for acclaim, money or gambled loot.
Basicly there is no reason why anyone shouldn't buy this game, great game play , 100s of hours of fun game play, endless potential for fun and frustration. This game gets a 100% recommendation from me. Shoot and Kill . (also buy the DLC season pass to save money :P)

By this time, you have probably heard something about Undertale, due to the massive hype train about it.  Whether it is showing up in image macros, youtube videos, or various in-jokes, it is clearly a massive internet sensation.  I will do my best to try to cut through the hype and get to the core of the matter.
Undertale is an RPG based on games from the 16-bit era (SNES/Genesis) with elements of bullet dodging games.   The mechanics are fairly straightforward - walk around and interact with characters, occasionally getting into turn-based combat.   The combat interface features option for attacking the monsters, which uses a timing minigame, running, and using items.   The innovation comes in the ability to perform a variety of actions toward monsters.  Choosing certain actions will convince the monster that you are friendly, and can end an encounter without you or the monster dieing.  This awards you with gold, but does not award XP.  When it is the monster's turn, there is a brief dodging minigame. This gets tougher as the game progresses, but the game is not a bullet hell.  I've been okay even on my low LV run, despite being pretty bad at bullet dodging.
The graphics of Undertale are mostly 16-bit sprites, and pretty well done.  The game looks well put together, but don't 3D graphics or photo realistic designs.
The musical score for this game is one of the best I have heard in an indie game.  It's a nice blend of 16-bit retro tunes and a wide variety of musical styles ranging from symphonic to jazz to rock to polka.   Sound effects are otherwise fairly basic.  Each character has a particular sound effect for their voice, making it possible to recognize them, but there is almost no voice work in the game.
Undertale's hype is built almost entirely on its story.  It has a large number of ending variations.  Every boss you kill or spare changes the outcome of the game.  It is indeed possible to live up to the game's tagline of being the RPG where no one has to die, and that is a very satisfying if challenging outcome.  You can also kill every single monster in the game, which is challenging for its own reasons.   The game has a message to it, but it is not preachy or really self-righteous about it.  The game just treats monsters in random encounters like characters as opposed to being just a source of XP.  It also takes into account game mechanics in the story - saving and loading is something that happens in the world of the game.
Characters in Undertale are highly memorable.  Toriel and Flowey (both of who show up in the first few moments of the game and are on the cover art) are both very interesting characters with a solid amount of backstory available to explore. Writing is clear and easy to read, and the game's humor is pretty impressive.   I have written this with the intent of not spoiling the game, and it is best experienced unspoiled. (I read spoilers beforehand and wish I hadn't)
If this sounds at all interesting to you, I recommend buying Undertale.  It is well worth $10 US, the soundtrack is great, and when it is on sale it's a steal.

Summery: Has a steep initial learning curve, gameplay experience varies by the attitude of other players on each given server.
Longer:
Naked and alone, with a rock for company you must find a source of food in the next 20 mins or die. A naked man accosts you with his rock, he ignores your pitiful attempt to claim that you are friendly, the wild light of hunger burns in his eyes. After a vicious struggle you brain him with your rock. Deciding that low on health you have no choice but to resort to cannibalism, you butcher his corpse (with the rock), and seek out wood to make a camp-fire to cook a lovely bit of leg on.
Later, and replete from your breakfast, you explore a dilapidated power station. A crazed naked lady chases you with an axe, luckily a quick spear throw to the head saves you from becoming a snack. You have lunch and gaze lovingly at your new axe.
Later still, you have a house with good views over rolling fields, its all going rather.... BEAR!THERES A BEAR! ARGHARGH ARGHHHHH!
Respawn at your sleeping bag (deployable spawn point), HOW THE HELL DID THE BEAR GET INTO MY HOUSE?!OH GAWD ARGHARGHHHHH.....
Later after having rebuilt your supply of tools and kit you head out for a swift bit of hunting, a naked man throws a spear through your head and butchers your corpse while singing over voice chat.
A Lady wearing a wolf head shoots you at close range with a shotgun.
Wolves eat you.
You starve to death.
You awake trapped in a spike pit.
Sever (dependant on sever) Chat is often a litany of banal and repetative racism and homophobia (As with many other multiplayer games).
And so on.
You will die a lot – this is fun. Challenge = FUN.

The fast travel system and vehicles minimizes the amount of time walking from place to place that's required, keeping you focused on killing enemies.  Cell shaded graphics are neat, but your mind starts to overlook it in the midst of an intense fire-fight.
Lots of side quests keep it interesting and extend play time.  Random finds and low level orcs sometimes leave rare or high-level items to make it worthwhile to kill everything you see and leave no stone unturned.
Enemies sometimes don't level up very well, so a character that has completed lots of side quests can breeze through the main quest too easily, but the story is enough to keep things engaging.

This is one of the best games of 2015.
It's not because of the gameplay or the graphics, as they're quite simple yet efficient, or the amazing chiptune music it has, but it's because of the novelty and the experience it offers. The story is superb and the characters are captivating.
There are few games that can mess with your emotions like this one. It's full of memorable moments. Not killing the enemies is much more fun than I thought it could be.
The only bad thing I can say about this game is the fandom (or, to be fair, just a part of it). Sometimes there will be something super clever and unusual that will blow the mind of a lot of people, and some of them can't handle it. It's the kind of the problem that "My Little Pony: Friendship is Magic", a girls cartoon whose creators decided to put real content instead of the usual bimbo drivel, has. The fans mean well, but if some of them bothers you, just ignore and take the game for what it is.
It's not an expensive game and despite only having up to 30 hours content it's worth the price. And even though the soundtrack is the same price of the game, it might be worth it too.

I can't fathom how good this game is. A truly heartbreaking/ warming game, Undertale has to be one of the most wonderful     JRPGs that I've played-- a JRPG where your actions DO have consequences, consequences much bigger than stealing from the shop in Link's Awakening. Despite its pixelart game style that can be compared to that of the Earthbound series, Undertale is one that'll pull at the heartstrings, regardless if you play the Genocide route or the Pacifist one. You'll start to grow genuine bonds to all of the characters you come across, be it Sans to Mettaton. Just be warned, if you play the Genocide route... well, you're gonna have a bad time. ;) With that said, I rate Undertale a full 10/10 (because screw IGN.) This is a game you NEED to play, regardless if you don't like JRPGs.

Guns. Numbers. RPG elements. Explosions. Blood. Gore. Death. Humor. Story. Co-op. Borderlands laid waste to all other games in the shoot-n-loot genre, and Borderlands 2 blows the orignal out of the water.
First of all, the procedurally generated gun system is both amazing in technology, and a challenging mistress to work with. You'll have to actively choose what weapons are going to give you a tactical adavantage for all your missions, and how best to approach all and any situations.
The class system really shines in co-op and gives you a huge range of ways to destroy your opponents, be it with sentry guns, Siren abilities, or good old-fashioned buzzsaw blades on the end of a stick. Co-op is a challenging, exciting and an overall fun experience.
Story. Many modern games struggle to find a good villain. Perhaps the only true examples of good villains in recent games are the Joker and the Riddler in the Arkham franchise. Handsome Jack definitely holds his own against the greats, and you'll find youself loving and hating that "handsome ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥" all throughout the game. Whether it's when he whispers random insults into your echo communicator or screams about the time he spooned a guy's eyes out between fits of laughter, you're going to miss him once you've wiped him from the face of Pandora.
A fantastic sequel to the original co-op shoot-n-loot extravagansa.

Guns. Numbers. RPG elements. Explosions. Blood. Gore. Death. Humor. Story. Co-op. Borderlands laid waste to all other games in the shoot-n-loot genre, and Borderlands 2 blows the orignal out of the water.
First of all, the procedurally generated gun system is both amazing in technology, and a challenging mistress to work with. You'll have to actively choose what weapons are going to give you a tactical adavantage for all your missions, and how best to approach all and any situations.
The class system really shines in co-op and gives you a huge range of ways to destroy your opponents, be it with sentry guns, Siren abilities, or good old-fashioned buzzsaw blades on the end of a stick. Co-op is a challenging, exciting and an overall fun experience.
Story. Many modern games struggle to find a good villain. Perhaps the only true examples of good villains in recent games are the Joker and the Riddler in the Arkham franchise. Handsome Jack definitely holds his own against the greats, and you'll find youself loving and hating that "handsome ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥" all throughout the game. Whether it's when he whispers random insults into your echo communicator or screams about the time he spooned a guy's eyes out between fits of laughter, you're going to miss him once you've wiped him from the face of Pandora.
A fantastic sequel to the original co-op shoot-n-loot extravagansa.

Im running through a forest nothing in sight it is dark and raining no flashlight no ammo and definitely no food wondering if a zombie is going to take my life away. A few hours later it is now day with no rain and not a single zombie in sight nor town to gather supplies I die with no food and water. This is Dayz a game set in a zombie apocalypse where the only thing you can do is survive. Dayz is a giant world and on normal circumstances id say that is a good thing. However today is not the day to lie. When you make a game like dayz you have certain options and ways you can go about doing them you can make a world populated full of zombies and big places to search and gather supplies. or you can make a giant sized map with few zombies very small cities and more trees than you know what to do with. Over half the hours I have put into dayz was spent running on a road with no end in sight looking for a city or town to scavange hell a zombie to fist fight would have been nice. However one key and huge issue I have run acrossed in this game is just how empty it is. With such a giant map where are the towns? where are the cars on the roads? AN WHERE THE HELL ARE THE ZOMBIES. See zombies in this game have a spawn area it seems most if not all of them only spawn near towns or cities nowhere else which some would say is realistic however with how populated the world is that is not true. The game prides itself in being a game about surviving a zombies apocalypse however it's more of a food and water apocalypse than anything and this saddens me. Expecially since the game is so beautiful and the gameplay is so fitting and well done. However at the end of the day no matter how beautiful a game is or how well the controls feel there needs to be a hook a feeling that your doing something better than running down a long road full of nothing but this game does not have that. Dayz though beautiful and well put together only deserves what it puts out in entertainment wich is a 5/10. I hope one day I can change this an that they update an change these huge key problems but till then I cannot give it more of my time and I cannot tell others to put there time into it.

To start, this is one of the best, if not the best, games I've played. The story is very well written. It goes beyond just what the characters say and do. It has meaningful messages in there as well. The way it wraps around you and then surprises you, it's all very well done. This game is a fun one to play. The characters are quirky, and there are plenty of jokes to laugh at. The fighting system is unique with its Fight/Mercy options, and how you move to dodge attacks. The classic art style is a nice way to present the "innocence" feeling you get throughout the game. The music here is wonderful, and when coupled with the powerful story, I may have nearly cried. Undertale has high replay value as well, as you will want to explore more, AND play differently to view the different endings. Highly recommended!

Hello everyone,
I don't even know where to begin describing DayZ...
About a year ago, I purchased DayZ at the price of $30.00 dollars in hopes of having a great time playing this game with a friend of mine who also had the game. He convinced me to purchase the game, and after watching all the amazing and nicely orchestrated videos on this game from YouTube, I finally purchased the game. At that time I was running the game on an Intel Integrated Graphics Card.
IMPORTANT NOTE** If you do not have a good gaming PC that can't handle medium to high end graphics, do not purchase this game. My first huge mistake that I made was that I did not realize how CPU depended this game is and since I was playing on an Integrated Graphics card, my game was toast. Even after reducing everything to minimal settings (which by the way makes DayZ look worse than Minecraft and GTA 3), I was still only getting 15FPS outside of cities.
My initial reaction, was that even though I had the FPS lag, it wouldn't be that bad and I could continue playing with a friend of mine. So I hop in game, and the first major problem (in my opionon) appears: I am no where near my friend. Since this is a game that is supposed to be played majority of the time with other friends, I was expecting some type of option for my friend and I to spawn near each other. Well guess what fellas... there is no option for that. And because of this, majority of the time you spend on DayZ will be to find your friends without dieing! It's a pain in the ✇✇✇ to spend half a day to find a friend and go through that process once again when you die. I feel as if something should have been done about this, but nothing has and nothing will be done about this major issue.
I should mention here that after about 6 months of playing DayZ, I purchased a new gaming computer. This did make DayZ feel a lot different since I did not have FPS lag anymore, but the game was still broken and the cons outweighted the pros.
This was the initial problem right from the start, but as I played DayZ with my friend for a few months, more and more things were beinging to catch our attention. It started with the updates... even though updates should make the game more enjoyable for players, the DayZ updates actually break the game even more. Ever since I have been playing DayZ, all the updates that have come out have only broken the game even more. Some examples include, but are not limited to: removing vegetables and fruits from the game, removing zombies from the game, removing various ways of transportation, etc. I know that these seem like minor things, but after you play the game for such a long time, they really start to add up and it gets more and more frustrating. I really hoped that the developers (if there is actually more than one) would actually update the game and make it more enjoyable for its players, but from my experience and other people, these updates do not fix the game in any way, but rather continue to make it even more broken.
Guns, guns, and even more guns. DayZ is supposed to be based on a realistic setting of a post-apocalyptic era, yet the guns used in this game are all old fashioned guns that are overpowered and not consistent. Even though the game does feature numerous types of guns and ammo, the penetration and trajectory of these bullets are ridiculous compared to real life. I do not want to go into more detail about this. Bottom line here is that the firearms in this game are unique, yet also nonrealstic.
Even after giving this game a few chances and playing over 100 hours on it, I definitely do not reccomended this game to any new people who want to play DayZ. The price has gone up by $5.00 in the matter of one year, even though the game has continued to worsen. There are much better games out there that you can buy for this money and be more satisfied. There is an update that is supposed to come out soon that introduces new ways of transportation over this vast map, but I highly doubt that this is true. I believed that this game had a great potential, but after seeing how slow things are moving and with updates coming out only once every two-three months I feel as if this game is on the edge of collapse.

Hello everyone,
I don't even know where to begin describing DayZ...
About a year ago, I purchased DayZ at the price of $30.00 dollars in hopes of having a great time playing this game with a friend of mine who also had the game. He convinced me to purchase the game, and after watching all the amazing and nicely orchestrated videos on this game from YouTube, I finally purchased the game. At that time I was running the game on an Intel Integrated Graphics Card.
IMPORTANT NOTE** If you do not have a good gaming PC that can't handle medium to high end graphics, do not purchase this game. My first huge mistake that I made was that I did not realize how CPU depended this game is and since I was playing on an Integrated Graphics card, my game was toast. Even after reducing everything to minimal settings (which by the way makes DayZ look worse than Minecraft and GTA 3), I was still only getting 15FPS outside of cities.
My initial reaction, was that even though I had the FPS lag, it wouldn't be that bad and I could continue playing with a friend of mine. So I hop in game, and the first major problem (in my opionon) appears: I am no where near my friend. Since this is a game that is supposed to be played majority of the time with other friends, I was expecting some type of option for my friend and I to spawn near each other. Well guess what fellas... there is no option for that. And because of this, majority of the time you spend on DayZ will be to find your friends without dieing! It's a pain in the ✇✇✇ to spend half a day to find a friend and go through that process once again when you die. I feel as if something should have been done about this, but nothing has and nothing will be done about this major issue.
I should mention here that after about 6 months of playing DayZ, I purchased a new gaming computer. This did make DayZ feel a lot different since I did not have FPS lag anymore, but the game was still broken and the cons outweighted the pros.
This was the initial problem right from the start, but as I played DayZ with my friend for a few months, more and more things were beinging to catch our attention. It started with the updates... even though updates should make the game more enjoyable for players, the DayZ updates actually break the game even more. Ever since I have been playing DayZ, all the updates that have come out have only broken the game even more. Some examples include, but are not limited to: removing vegetables and fruits from the game, removing zombies from the game, removing various ways of transportation, etc. I know that these seem like minor things, but after you play the game for such a long time, they really start to add up and it gets more and more frustrating. I really hoped that the developers (if there is actually more than one) would actually update the game and make it more enjoyable for its players, but from my experience and other people, these updates do not fix the game in any way, but rather continue to make it even more broken.
Guns, guns, and even more guns. DayZ is supposed to be based on a realistic setting of a post-apocalyptic era, yet the guns used in this game are all old fashioned guns that are overpowered and not consistent. Even though the game does feature numerous types of guns and ammo, the penetration and trajectory of these bullets are ridiculous compared to real life. I do not want to go into more detail about this. Bottom line here is that the firearms in this game are unique, yet also nonrealstic.
Even after giving this game a few chances and playing over 100 hours on it, I definitely do not reccomended this game to any new people who want to play DayZ. The price has gone up by $5.00 in the matter of one year, even though the game has continued to worsen. There are much better games out there that you can buy for this money and be more satisfied. There is an update that is supposed to come out soon that introduces new ways of transportation over this vast map, but I highly doubt that this is true. I believed that this game had a great potential, but after seeing how slow things are moving and with updates coming out only once every two-three months I feel as if this game is on the edge of collapse.
The final decision is up to you... but as a player who has over 120+ hours on DayZ, I would reccomend to everyone to hold on to your money and spend it on something else.

Team up with up to three other players for four-player online goodness or go old-school with two-player split-screen couch sharing mayhem as you spend hours leveling up your character and equipping them with one of the millions of badass weapons. Borderlands 2 features a new visually stunning array of procedurally generated guns, shields, grenades, artifacts, enemies and more. Choose one of the four new character classes to be taken through a carefully crafted and connected story to all new and surprising environments across the living planet of Pandora. Make new friends, arm them to the teeth and fight alongside them on your relentless quest for revenge and redemption.

My favorite game on Steam so far; Borderlands 2 boasts a good story, excellent DLC, mechanics, unique graphics and all for a good price. However, although all these are its good points and there are hardly any negative points, the game requires a powerful setup to run smoothly. Disregarding the fact that it made me depressed, made me go from functional to a hopeless wreck, it still has the worst ending I've seen in any video game, which ruined the rest of the (honestly unpolished and full of plot holes) story. The gameplay was fun, though not nearly as hard and bullet-hell like as I originally believed and feel it's lacking.
I know that almost no one will have the same negative reaction, the same degree of contempt, that I have for the end of this game. I know many of my friends love this game, despite its flaws, or what I am convinced are flaws. But personally... I would have been better off never having played this game.

When DayZ gets it right it is a brilliant game. For a game where a lot of the time not much happens it has got my heart rate going more than any other game. Stumbling into a group of bandits or getting trapped on the roof of a building by a horde of zombies really is tense knowing one mistake and you will loose a character that you have spent hours with.
However those moments are few and far between and getting fewer.
I haven't seen a Zombie in probably about the last 10 hours of game play. I don't know if this is something they are doing as part of development or a bug but without it the whole game play mechanic of 'do i risk going into that zombie infested town for loot' is gone. With that gone all that you have left is the excitement of chance encounters with other player but the amount of players seems to be dwindling because of these frustrations meaning this is becoming less common now as well.
With these parts of the game gone what you are left with is a survival game that doesn't stack up mechanically to other pure survival games on the market.
This game had such potential but with so little progress after 3 years I cant see this game going much further.
On a side note if you are looking for a survival game with PvP elements i recommend having a look at ARK. There's base building, almost weekly updates and you get to ride a freaking dinosaur.

Borderlands 2 is a massive shooter that is best experienced in co-op mode, but if you want to play by yourself, it's worth every penny. The action is hectic, the pacing is great (well, maybe besides some of the optional quests which squeeze everything that's possible out of a given location in the game, thus making it a bit tedious. The NPCs are amusing and the cast itself is varied, delivering some great and memorable dialogue. The comic book-esque graphics is definitely something different, but in a good sense, and it also works well with keeping the light-heartedness going, even though the story gets suprisingly grim every now and then. Overall, this is a must have game for anybody who wants pure fun.

Borderlands 2 is one of the rare triple A games that doesn't take itself very seriously. Its gameplay is okay, its combat and RPG mechanics are mediocre, and its endgame content is grindy and repetitive. But, what makes this game special is its environments, characters, and how they react with one another.
Possibly Anthony Burch's magnum opus (seriously, go watch Hey Ash, Whatcha' Playing), the writer creates memorable and fantastic characters. The antagonist is just someone you love to hate, and its writing and voice acting is definitely on par with the famous antagonist from Farcry 3. And then, there's Tiny Tina, one crrrrazy little mother ♥♥♥♥er! With all of this, the game has a fantastic sense of humor. For example, when reviving a downed ally in co-op, you might say things like "Wow, um... do you work out?"
Its environments are beautifully crafted. Set pieces and events makes the world vibrant. Crazy things happen during the main campaign, and it makes you love (and hate) Pandora that much more.
Its combat gets repetitive, but during the main campaign, it stays fresh. Most importantly, though, is that it is entirely different from those CoDs and BFs. It definitely stretches what FPS's can do.
Unfortunately, its extensive amounts of DLC and TWO Season passes does mar this otherwise great game. If you do not have the DLC's, you cannot level up your character after certain levels. Online, this effectively means you're seggregated from people who do. So that really sucks.
All in all, this is a great game. Beautiful environments, great story, and excellent characters.
A great game that you can never get tired of playing!

I never thought I'd ever write a review on steam. Here I am, writing one.

I don't want to list any pros and cons of this game and rather tell about the impression itself. As of now I've finished Undertale once, and I am left mind♥♥♥♥ed in more ways that I'm comfortable with. The game plays you as much as you play the game. While the graphic in itself isn't impressive, it doesn't need to be. The art and the design are gorgeous. The music is beautiful and never felt out of place. The character have a deep personality and, while sometimes pretty annoying, queer or outright strange, you can't bring yourself to dislike them. Each of those parts blend together so well, that I couldn't imagine Undertale being anything different than it is.
Undertale is a game about investment. How you play it is up to you. How much you invest, in time, in emotion. And the more you invest, the more you will get in return. Take your time. Enjoy it. And then enjoy it again, because you can't get the full experience in just one playthrough.

This game has a huge fanbase, which is what got me to look at it. Now, I know that can do the complete opposite for some people, but this is honestly a great game.
First off, the humor. It ranges from random and spontanious (not people screaming "I LIKE PICKLES" random. that's not funny) to very well pulled off pop culture humor (mostly the Undernet. I love Alpys). That may not be your cup of tea, but it's definately mine.
Next, the characters. Oh, how I love the characters. They're all funny, yet some are kinda deep, and they're all well executed.
Literally, for some of them.
*budum tisk*
The story is simple, yet complicated, and very emotional at times. That sums it up.
The battle is great. Most of you probably know about the "You don't have to kill anything in the entire game" mechanic, but you never truly understand it until you actually play it. It's awesome. And the fighting is fun.
Bosses can get tedious at times, but that makes it even more rewarding when you kill (or spare) them.
If you're not one for pixely graphics, I totally understand. But the pixels don't get in the way of anything. In fact, I'd go as far as to say they might be necissery to the game.
It's overall a pretty fun game, and I recommend it hugely.

After having played Borderlands 2 for over 300 hours (I only spent ~260 hours in Skyrim), I can safely say that this game is awesome.  The writing and dialogue have caused bouts of rib-splitting laughter and so many "I understood that reference!" moments.  The folks at Gearbox software really did well with this game.
The graphics are classic Borderlands "comic-book" style with strong outlines and vivid colors.  Admittedly, it's been years since I played Borderlands 1, but in my opinion the gameplay is improved over Borderlands 1 and it seems like the maps are larger with more ambient objects and sounds.  I've spent hours just roaming to find the random objects that Gearbox placed for the completionists like myself.
The True/Ultimate Vault Hunter Modes add end-game challenges that will test your patience (Badass Psychos, I'm looking at you.)  If you're on the fence about this game, buy it.  Especially if you catch the Game of the Year version on sale.  You definitely won't regret it.  (Unless laughing at Handsome Jack's jibes breaks a rib, then you might....nah not even then.)
P.S.  You *must* play Tiny Tina's Assault on Dragon Keep DLC.  That is *the* funniest thing I've ever played.

This game is near flawless. With exciting AND addictive game-play that stays fresh even past the 2nd play-through I am never bored with this Game. Especially considering how easy it really is to play with Friends. I do wish it was more possible for people of different Level ranges to play together but we cant have it all.
In stark contrast to the first Borderlands, the story is actually compelling and the superb voice acting makes it hard not to be drawn in. The Humor plays a big part as well and never feels out of place in the abstract Borderlands Universe.
The Graphics look great on both high and mid range Systems, offering highly stylized Graphics that still have a touch of Realism. In closing I must commend Gearbox Software for their love-letter to the PC community. This Game truly deserved Game of the Year. “You're gonna be my new meat bicycle!” 100/100

I never thought I'd ever write a review on steam. Here I am, writing one.
That in itself should tell enough about how much this game impressed me.
I don't want to list any pros and cons of this game and rather tell about the impression itself. As of now I've finished Undertale once, and I am left mind♥♥♥♥ed in more ways that I'm comfortable with. The game plays you as much as you play the game. While the graphic in itself isn't impressive, it doesn't need to be. The art and the design are gorgeous. The music is beautiful and never felt out of place. The character have a deep personality and, while sometimes pretty annoying, queer or outright strange, you can't bring yourself to dislike them. Each of those parts blend together so well, that I couldn't imagine Undertale being anything different than it is.
Undertale is a game about investment. How you play it is up to you. How much you invest, in time, in emotion. And the more you invest, the more you will get in return. Take your time. Enjoy it. And then enjoy it again, because you can't get the full experience in just one playthrough.

It goes without saying I have a love/hate relationship with this game. On one hand I've been thrown into a deadly world with bandits trying to ride me as a meat bicycle where avoiding proves very challenging. On the other, I'm in an environment that rewards me for progressing forward with the promise of shiny new loot.
The later stages of the game are hard, very hard, and it really stops me wanting to play the game. Yet if I am willing to make the effort and progress just that little bit further, I might find myself with a brand new weapon that shoots out lightning, or a new shield that explodes like a boss upon equipping it. There's very much a sense of "Tug-of-war" going on here and I think this game is just good enough to make you want to keep playing.

After 2 years, amazing improvements:
- The fps got steady, i remember when i had problems between 30-60, now it's constantly under 30.
- The loot is everywhere, you can start a fashion presentation.
- They added so many guns , that you'll have to loot 3 cities to get bullets for your gun. More exploration.
- Now everyone desyncs so fights are well balanced. Remember when you would've desync alone ?
- People can only glitch in the church. No worries God sees and eventually will punish them. Except if they have a different religion and they get praised, that's another story.
- Now it feels like a real survivor game , you need to loot 5 hours to get in a gun fight or at least try to get there. Elseway you can always run after someone that has a mossin. Note: apparently the pursuit can take a bit , as it's impossible to hit someone who is running and has tons of gear on him while you only have an axe. But no worries eventually one will die of hunger. Another note: a lot of random people can join you in this pursuit, so you can team work, like taking turns on who runs after the guy and who gets to eat. (Credit Lirik for this idea).
- Zombies struggle to survive also. There are times when i don't see one for hours. Makes me wonder if Britney the zombie is still alive :(.
- Apparently everyone shoots in the leg. But don't worry, you'll still get the kill as the "crawler" has many obstacles in front of him, like getting in a house. So don't worry it's mostly kill secured.
Keep it up, and the price even "upper".

"WARNING: THIS GAME IS EARLY ACCESS ALPHA.
YOU WANT TO ACTIVELY SUPPORT DEVELOPMENT OF THE GAME
TO HANDLE WITH SERIOUS ISSUES AND POSSIBLE INTERRUPTIONS OF GAME FUNCTIONING." I think this warning says enough to get the point across yet people still buy the game and do nothing but complain about it. It's a game in development and♥♥♥♥♥♥will most definately happen while you're playing that will upset you. Sometimes games that are supposed to be finished have their problems. When it's finished and the issues persist, THEN you can cry like babies that you wasted your money and you've been cheated by the developer. Frankly, I would much rather see the developer push back release until everything is just right instead of following the status quo and releasing incomeplete garbage.
EDIT: 6/11/16 A new update currently in experimental testing brings a new game renderer and other offerings. The new renderer boosted frame rates. Gains of over 40 to 50 fps are common on most machines, some better machines offering over 100 fps. Player controller revamp, new player animations and many other features are in progress. Still, players are complaining, they always will. Do not listen to the nay sayers. DayZ is worth the time and money. After it is finished it will deliver the entertainment you crave, without a doubt. The future of DayZ is certainly bright.
My review? DayZ was the start of a new breed of MMO. There have been MANY other games attempting the same recipe but I haven't yet seen one that compares to the feeling of DayZ. It's been a rocky development but I see it heading in the right direction. Bugs, sure. Crappy situations, absolutely. I recommend this game to anyone who like shooters, comedy, replayability or anyone who has friends.

Во-первых, живой и нескучный сюжет. Вернее, собственно сюжет традиционен для такого рода игр, но он раскрывается и преподносится так живо, так стремительно, такими мощными мазками ярких красок, что хочется выведать еще и еще и невозможно оторваться. Ключевая заслуга в этом принадлежит блестящей плеяде персонажей, тщательно и с любовью выписанных как в переносном, так и в прямом (комикс же!) смысле.
Во-вторых, масса квестов, изредка повторяющих друг друга, но тем не менее увлекательных и - что немаловажно - познавательных. Каждый из них принесет вам ту или иную награду (кредиты, оружие, снаряжение, и т.п.), а иной раз и бесценную информацию об окружающем мире. Кстати, мир этот можно исследовать до морковкиного заговенья.
В-третьих, по-настоящему здоровый и хороший юмор (хоть далеко не всегда оригинальный). Не исключаю, что пользователи русской версии страдают от несовершенства перевода... А может, и не страдают.
В-четвертых, уйма самого разного оружия. Неисчислимое множество оружия. Бездна оружия. Что любопытно, зачастую те или иные "пушки" по ТТХ различаются гораздо меньше, чем по внешнему виду, но на поверку выходит, что внутренние особенности весьма и весьма существенны и связаны, в том числе, с видом противника, против которого это оружие применяется. Против живой силы незаменим в прямом смысле огнестрел, а также классические дробовики; роботы и прочие железяки воют от энергетического воздействия; также техника крайне чувствительна к кислотному и шлаковому урону, и т.д. и т.п. С учетом постоянно развивающегося действия, открытия новых локаций и врагов, это не позволяет обзавестись набором "любимчиков" и таскать только их. Приходится регулярно тасовать арсенал, со слезами выбрасывать когда-то незаменимый дробовик и брать такой же, но другой, жертвовать "шлаковым" оружием в пользу "огненного" или наоборот, и т.д. и т.п. То же самое относится и к снаряжению: например, один щит дает большое количество энергии, но сильно уменьшает запас здоровья, а другой имеет меньший заряд, но зато поглощает вражеские снаряды и пополняет ими ваш патронташ, и т.д. А можно не выбрасывать, а сложить все в хранилище. что в Убежище.
В-пятых, элемент РПГ. Прокачиваться можно и нужно. Нельзя пренебрегать никакими заданиями, позволяющими увеличить здоровье, усилить силовой щит, ускорить перезарядку, повысить точность, развить спецспособности вроде перехвата пуль или припадка халковской ярости. Иначе к первому же серьезному боссу вы выйдете с голой задницей, хотя до этого с легкостью расправились с дюжиной более мелких (не зная еще, что они мелкие). Можно уйти, прокачаться таки и вернуться как Терминатор.

I want to like this game.
No, actually, I want to love this game.
Rust has the kind of building simulation I've been waiting for since the emergence of the craft-your-own-world genre. Extensive blueprint systems allow players to collect and piece together amazing things from raw materials, and there is just enough scavenging to keep things interesting. Graphically, Rust is well beyond several games of this type. It combines with an open-style sandbox that can be enjoyed by several players which would, ideally, form a vibrant, active, always-online community.
That is, it would, were it not for the community.
I've seen that some players have compared the general game community to cancer, and I wouldn't say it's an unfair comparison. That said, I think a more accurate description of the Rust community at large would be to say they're like a case of anal herpes. They're nothing if not a consistent, incurable pain in the♥♥♥♥♥
Upon spending more than a few minutes on any given server, new players will notice there are mainly two types of player in this game. The first treats the game like Minecraft, happily setting about building magnificent structures, and some of them are really fantastic. Skilled builders can really show off the best points of the system, creating intricate constructions that really show what an open concept and a creative mind can accomplish.
These players are the minority.
The other type of player in this game treats everything as a low-rent Call of Doody, whereupon discovering other players sharing a map, they proceed to clip through walls (or just shoot through them as though they were nonexistent) and run about happily defecating all over everything. Nine out of nine servers tested has returned positive for this breed of cancerous anal herpes.
Sadly, this game breeds that kind of player like inbreeding breeds low IQs.
If you have the ability to piece together your own dedicated, private server, by all means, grab this game and mess around with your friends. If you're stuck on public servers, well.. just don't get stuck on public servers. You're better off playing other games.

Note: I have played many more hours of Rust on another account, I do have expereince with the game.
I am shocked at the practices that this company is getting away with. I played Rust towards the beginning of its popularity, and now coming back, and seeing that gender and race are random, and cannot be changed, has made me give this review.
The reason that I bought Rust was for the survival elements, and I still think it accomplishes as being a social survival game.  I bought Rust to help the game devs work on this game, to update it faster, and add new features. This game is still in Early Access, and I don't see it leaving Early Access soon either, it is progressing, but what "features" they have added are not always features. Specifically as I mentioned race and gender being entirely random, with no way to even re-roll your character. We all put up with having the same stock white male model originally because it was Early Access, and new. I don't think anyone expected it to last very long. Now we have the same amount of choice (none) but by giving us these attributes without any say in the matter, is a ridiculous practice for a game company. They have implemented a feature, without giving the users access to it. I feel like I have been ripped off, and I cannot believe that people are still buing this game with the practices that this company has shown over the past 3 years (!) of development.
They want to make the claim, that like life, you are dealt these things with no say in the matter, and while that is true, video games are an entirely different concept. People play games to escape the world, this means playing a character like themselves, to connect with the character, or playing as a different character, and being able to role play as this character. By making this random, they are going to effectively make many people upset, like myself, for no reason, since they have the ability to give us a choice, even if it was a one time choice, that would be acceptable to me, and I do not know why there is not a choice. I bought this game expecting that updates would give us these choices down the road, since these options are a staple of any game within the genre, since I would consider it a role-playing game, since it is set in a world unlike our own.
The reason it is such an issue, is they are insisting on the realism of Rust, but the main reason it is not realistic at all, is that we are forced to view our characters in full, everytime we go to our inventory screen. This completely breaks any immersion for me, even with a basic inventory screen would not break my immersion, since it is so internalized, but seeing my character is just awkward, and results in this disconnect with the character. It feels that the game devs are attempting some sort of psychological experiment on the users, by implementing random forced race and gender, and seeing how users react. The way that humans work (besides transgendered individuals) is that people have no reason to be uncomfortable in their own bodies to hardly any degree. Usually we want to improve ourselves, but that is direct with ourselves, we still want to be ourselves, just a better version. By forcing these things, they create a disconnect between the gamer, and the game. Even if the gamer doesn't want to play a game with a character like themselves, they usually have a mental image of the character that they do want to play as. This disconnect results in many being directly affected to different extents, but still affected.
The devs could fix this in many ways, but their stubbornness regarding the race issue (which has been the same for about a year) has made them to do nothing. I have no faith in this company or Garry Newman, I am actually shocked that he thinks that the Rust sales grew 74% with female models and forced gender, was a combination of both factors. It was probably bought by many who thought they would have a choice, or just didn't care, since they could view the nude female character models. Having accumulated over 2600 hours in-game, I must say DayZ has passed the longevity test and then some. In terms of the multiplayer interactions present and the size of the map, DayZ has the "replayability" of games such as Skyrim, Fallout 3 and GTA5 all rolled into one.
Let's get a few kinks out of the way before I continue with my praises of such an important game in my personal gaming development.
1. It's alpha and has been for a long time. It's a little behind schedule and those of us who bought into the game in the first few days or months have seen just how far it has come. It IS proceeding slower than our expectations, but aside from a few iterations of failed stable versions in the 0.40s and early 0.50s this game has kept me coming back.
2. It isn't optimized, yes it's alpha, but even with a super rig, you're still going to suffer some FPS fails and desync that will annoy you.
Back to why I recommend this game:
1. Combat realism, it is by far and away the most intense, adrenaline-milking, pulse-destroying game I have ever played. The combat can and will get you addicted, I am pretty sure I've briefly experienced something like PTSD after a marathon 6 hour session of non-stop fighting. When you're dead, the effect is mostly permanent. Wave goodbye to your gear unless you were fighting on the coast and are lucky to get a close spawn, which is pretty rare.
2. Map size, it's huge. It's mindnumbling huge and it's beautiful. I have visited every location on the map in my time in game and they're adding new locations every couple of patches. The beautifcation of the game is progressing in a very real and tangible fashion. Even though I have visited every location on the map, I have still not travelled through half the forests that seperate the cities and countryside.
3. It's emersive. You can get lost in the game and in the world. I wrote a novel for my Masters in Creative Writing inspired by my experience in DayZ as a lonewolf in the northern reaches of the map. It really takes you to another place.
4. Survivalists or combat junky, there is a space for you here. You can live out in the sticks, farming and hunting or you can bring your game to the high traffic areas and shoot anything that moves, its up to you.
5. It's stacked in favour of group formation. As in reality, this is no different, the bigger your group, the better your chances of surviving. Lone wolf combat against groups is only realistically possible via long ranged tactics. Group on group battles are the most amazing things you can experience in game and taking down a small group, solo, is so difficult that once accomplished you'll experience a feeling akin to getting a nuke in COD:MW2 days.
I highly recommend this game. It is not for the faint-hearted and it is not for sufferers of "sense of direction impairedness."
I continue to be impressed 2600+ hours in!

Undertale has a bullethell-fighting system, so for most fights, you're a red heart who can move freely in a box while avoiding white object that might hit you. Later in the game you experiance different ways of fighting, and the colour of your heart changes with it.

With you're choices, you can either make friends with them, which the game rewards you for, or you can kill them, which really just sucks for you. Based on your actions, you can get three different endings with three different bosses.
The way the game looks is uh... actually one of the worse things. While most of the characters look ok for a RPG, some just look awful. One of the worst is the Main Character, you. But by far the worst sprite is near the end of one of the three endings, I won't say who, but they look like a marshmellow stuffed inside some clothes, which is sad when compared to how great they can look in other scenes.
I enjoyed Undertale, but I think the way to enjoy it most is to do all three routes, and then do the happy ending again, well, unless you did it last. And remember, use some MERCY.

As I have now become aware of how it works, and the sheer stupidity of it as a mechanic, I'm going to be pursuing a refund on this purchase.  Its absolutely ridiculous to me that they would force this decision upon people, and they don't appear to be concerned about changing their course of action.
Games these days SHOULD NOT be gender locked, ever.  Black Desert Online was partially bad BECAUSE so much of the classes were gender locked, and I refused to play it for this reason as well.  This game has, somehow, taken it a step further by FORCING a gender upon you based on something outside of your control, and giving you absolutely no ability to change it.
Therefore, I'm not going to recommended this game any longer.  I wanted to get a few of my friends interested in purchasing it and giving it a go with all the new gameplay/mechanics, but that will no longer be happening.
I sincerely hope the developers take the time to truly think over how irrational of a decision this was and will revert the change or offer some way to swap, or I can't image myself trusting any of their game decisions in the future.

Having accumulated over 2600 hours in-game, I must say DayZ has passed the longevity test and then some. In terms of the multiplayer interactions present and the size of the map, DayZ has the "replayability" of games such as Skyrim, Fallout 3 and GTA5 all rolled into one.
Let's get a few kinks out of the way before I continue with my praises of such an important game in my personal gaming development.
1. It's alpha and has been for a long time. It's a little behind schedule and those of us who bought into the game in the first few days or months have seen just how far it has come. It IS proceeding slower than our expectations, but aside from a few iterations of failed stable versions in the 0.40s and early 0.50s this game has kept me coming back.
2. It isn't optimized, yes it's alpha, but even with a super rig, you're still going to suffer some FPS fails and desync that will annoy you.
Back to why I recommend this game:
1. Combat realism, it is by far and away the most intense, adrenaline-milking, pulse-destroying game I have ever played. The combat can and will get you addicted, I am pretty sure I've briefly experienced something like PTSD after a marathon 6 hour session of non-stop fighting. When you're dead, the effect is mostly permanent. Wave goodbye to your gear unless you were fighting on the coast and are lucky to get a close spawn, which is pretty rare.
2. Map size, it's huge. It's mindnumbling huge and it's beautiful. I have visited every location on the map in my time in game and they're adding new locations every couple of patches. The beautifcation of the game is progressing in a very real and tangible fashion. Even though I have visited every location on the map, I have still not travelled through half the forests that seperate the cities and countryside.
3. It's emersive. You can get lost in the game and in the world. I wrote a novel for my Masters in Creative Writing inspired by my experience in DayZ as a lonewolf in the northern reaches of the map. It really takes you to another place.
4. Survivalists or combat junky, there is a space for you here. You can live out in the sticks, farming and hunting or you can bring your game to the high traffic areas and shoot anything that moves, its up to you.
5. It's stacked in favour of group formation. As in reality, this is no different, the bigger your group, the better your chances of surviving. Lone wolf combat against groups is only realistically possible via long ranged tactics. Group on group battles are the most amazing things you can experience in game and taking down a small group, solo, is so difficult that once accomplished you'll experience a feeling akin to getting a nuke in COD:MW2 days.
I highly recommend this game. It is not for the faint-hearted and it is not for sufferers of "sense of direction impairedness."

Okay, so I haven't gotten that far in the game yet, but I really don't like how heavy/guilty this game can make you feel. I understand that you don't have to kill anyone to progress in the game, but I struggled at one point. I literally could not figure out any other way on my own to defeat the opponent. I had to cheat and look it up online, cause i knew i didn't have to fight them. I think what really threw me off was the fact that you have to keep trying your options in the game, even if you've already tried them, otherwise you may miss what you're supposed to do.
I do like the game. I like the style, the characters, and the fact that you don't have to kill anyone. I don't like the fact that the only way that you can figure out what the obstacle is is by either playing through the same freaking fight over and over until you get the result you want, or by giving in and looking it up online.
TL:DR: I enjoy this game for its design, but I don't appreciate the amount of guilt it can lay on you if you can't figure out the non-violent route in a fight on your own.

**Updated because I had to think about it for some time. I gave it a thumbs down last time due to some mixed emotions I had with it.**
Old review (The thumbs down review):
I have to admit that the game is quite charming, the soundtrack is very well done, and it plays with your emotions. However, I'm not pleased with having to pay for this game. You can play games like this for free on Gamejolt, and other indie gaming sites. I also do not see what the big deal of this game is all about. I see Undertale related posts everywhere on Deviantart and Tumblr, and those artists/people are saying that this game is godly and amazing. But for me, personally, it's just another ordinary game, and don't see what the hype is all about. There are other games like this made by classic gaming companies.
New review (The thumbs up review):
Gotta admit that I'm feeling pretty neutral about this game. I still don't see what the big hype of it is all about. Steam really needs to do something about their recommendation options.
Positives:
- Charming characters.
- Excellent soundtrack.
- Neat art style.
- Plays with your emotions.
- Addictive gameplay, depending on your taste in genre.
Negatives:
- The price. I find it to be too expensive. For a game like this, I think it deserves to be at least 3-6 dollars.
- The fans. They treat the game like it's godly. I just don't see what all the hype is about. I see fan art, fan games, etc. made everywhere I go. Games like this have been made before, just a bit different and not too story-driven is all. People need to learn to broaden their horizons and research.
My overall feelings, though, are neutral but are more on the positive side. What ruins the gameplay experience for me, though, is the fandom. Funny how when something becomes a fad, it can mess with your emotions on whether you want to fully like it, or not.
I would recommend the game for your own experience. But what I won't recommend about it is listening to the die-hard fans of how godly it is, and for how much the game's worth. Maybe get it when it's on sale, or something. I made the mistake of buying it at full price, and regret actually paying that much for it.

Let's not pretend that this game is not a phenomena. Like it or hate it, there's no disputing that this game is probably one of the biggest indie releases to date, regarding sales and sheer popularity. Basically anyone with a Steam account, or socail media, or anyone that uses the internet in general, has heard of this game. So, with this review, I'm not going to pretend that most people out there have not heard of this game and are completely clueless to it. Everyone talks about this game to a near obnoxious level, so the goal of my review is to try and convince anyone out there that's scepticle, that's completely uninterested because of how annoyed they are about hearing about it, that's completely turned off by the game and turn away from it simply because Tumblr has jumped straight into its trash chute. Because here's the thing. The worst thing about this game is its popularity. So again, my goal with this review is to not recommend, but IMPLORE that you listen and take my words into consideration. Because despite how much flack this game has gotten (when you forget about the immense praise it actually gets), this game is worth it. It deserves to be remembered, and I fully believe it can stand the test of time.
So with all of that established and out of the way, here's where I answer the main question. 'What is so great about Undertale?'. Well, a lot of things when you look at it all from a technical level. The story is very well thought out, written, and paced, the characters are all memorable (and despite a lot of opinions, very multi-dementional. It's called subtlty, people, these characters are "tropey" because that's only their outward appearance.) The music is fantastic, the gameplay is really fun and unique, and almost constantly changes the rules on you. It almost NEVER gets repetitive like a lot of standard RPG's usually are. That is... Depending on how you play. I'm sure most people already know what I'm talking about, the option to either FIGHT or SPARE. This is where most people get their experience spoiled and I know a lot of you out there know exactly what I'm talking about.
"NO, DON'T FIGHT, WHAT THE HELL IS WRONG WITH YOU!"
"YOU'RE PLAYING THE GAME WRONG, "YOU'RE GONNA HAVE A BAD TIME!""
I know how it is. Backseat gamers are super annoying. But here I am, a massive Undertale fan saying PLAY HOW YOU WANT. Your first time through, do what you feel like doing. It's a part of the experience, don't worry about what others say. Yes, your actions weigh heavily on the outcome of the story, and it's done in a way that actually MEANS something to the story of the game. But you are still a person playing a video game. It's YOUR experience, so treat it that way.
But again, getting back on track, 'What is so great about Undertale?'. Yes, all the technical aspect of the game are good and appealing, but what has gotten it so much hype? How is it that some consider it, quite literally, to be "one of the greatest games of all time"? There are so many out there that say that it's unfathomably overrated and should be thrown away and forgotten because no one will stop talking about it. "It doesn't deserve the hype". This is where most people, even die hard fans of the game, can't explain why it's NOT overrated. This is what's disapointing to the smaller group of people that love this game, such as me. The ones that love it for the entire point of the game. The thing that Toby Fox himself wanted players to see.
Undertale is one of those rare games that not only try to push the boundaries of what video games as an artform are capable of doing, telling a story and giving an experience, but also exceed its attempt. No other game before has done the things Undertale has done quite like Undertale. There are similar concepts used in other things that have come before, but still. Nothing quite like Undertale has done. Because Undertale doesn't use these unique concepts, which I will not explain and leave whomever is interested to find out for themselves, as a gimmick. An experiment or something new to try out. It takes full advantage of what it does and uses it in the context of the game's lore and story. It's something that, I as a player, brought me into this game's world and story far deeper than any game has done before. It made me feel literally a PART of the story. Some would say that's digging way too deep into fiction, but that's the thing. That is what I love about this game.
It has been a pretty long amount of time since I have played a video game and actually FELT like I was a part of it. Like I was IN it. That's something I always felt as a kid playing games, I always really felt like I was in whatever world I was experiencing, and I always felt like I actually knew the characters personally. Because that's just what happens when you're a kid. Fiction isn't so far from reality. And that is one of the biggest things that Undertale does right, with absolute flying colors. It takes that feeling, that suspension of disbelief that only a child could have, and uses the concepts and the way it tells its story to fully immerse the player like that. This game made me feel like I was 9 years old again, playing some of my first really good games for the first time again. That's what I think so many people love about this game, even those that don't fully realize it. That's what makes Undertale so great.
For those thinking about, or about to go into this game, even after all the hype and all the spoilers being thrown out there without any care, going in and expecting this absolute grand masterpiece of a video game, and point out every little tiny flaw and subjective thing that you don't like and feel the need to criticize the game for it, to the finest, sharpest detail possible... Just play the game. Pretend you're 9 years old again, and just experience the game. That's about the best thing you can do when playing Undertale.

I want to like this game.
No, actually, I want to love this game.
Rust has the kind of building simulation I've been waiting for since the emergence of the craft-your-own-world genre. Extensive blueprint systems allow players to collect and piece together amazing things from raw materials, and there is just enough scavenging to keep things interesting. Graphically, Rust is well beyond several games of this type. It combines with an open-style sandbox that can be enjoyed by several players which would, ideally, form a vibrant, active, always-online community.
That is, it would, were it not for the community.
I've seen that some players have compared the general game community to cancer, and I wouldn't say it's an unfair comparison. That said, I think a more accurate description of the Rust community at large would be to say they're like a case of anal herpes. They're nothing if not a consistent, incurable pain in the♥♥♥♥♥
Upon spending more than a few minutes on any given server, new players will notice there are mainly two types of player in this game. The first treats the game like Minecraft, happily setting about building magnificent structures, and some of them are really fantastic. Skilled builders can really show off the best points of the system, creating intricate constructions that really show what an open concept and a creative mind can accomplish.
These players are the minority.
The other type of player in this game treats everything as a low-rent Call of Doody, whereupon discovering other players sharing a map, they proceed to clip through walls (or just shoot through them as though they were nonexistent) and run about happily defecating all over everything. Nine out of nine servers tested has returned positive for this breed of cancerous anal herpes.
Sadly, this game breeds that kind of player like inbreeding breeds low IQs.
If you have the ability to piece together your own dedicated, private server, by all means, grab this game and mess around with your friends. If you're stuck on public servers, well.. just don't get stuck on public servers. You're better off playing other games.

**Updated because I had to think about it for some time. I gave it a thumbs down last time due to some mixed emotions I had with it.**
Old review (The thumbs down review):
I have to admit that the game is quite charming, the soundtrack is very well done, and it plays with your emotions. However, I'm not pleased with having to pay for this game. You can play games like this for free on Gamejolt, and other indie gaming sites. I also do not see what the big deal of this game is all about. I see Undertale related posts everywhere on Deviantart and Tumblr, and those artists/people are saying that this game is godly and amazing. But for me, personally, it's just another ordinary game, and don't see what the hype is all about. There are other games like this made by classic gaming companies.
New review (The thumbs up review):
Gotta admit that I'm feeling pretty neutral about this game. I still don't see what the big hype of it is all about. Steam really needs to do something about their recommendation options.
Positives:
- Charming characters.
- Excellent soundtrack.
- Neat art style.
- Plays with your emotions.
- Addictive gameplay, depending on your taste in genre.
Negatives:
- The price. I find it to be too expensive. For a game like this, I think it deserves to be at least 3-6 dollars.
- The fans. They treat the game like it's godly. I just don't see what all the hype is about. I see fan art, fan games, etc. made everywhere I go. Games like this have been made before, just a bit different and not too story-driven is all. People need to learn to broaden their horizons and research.
My overall feelings, though, are neutral but are more on the positive side. What ruins the gameplay experience for me, though, is the fandom. Funny how when something becomes a fad, it can mess with your emotions on whether you want to fully like it, or not.
I would recommend the game for your own experience. But what I won't recommend about it is listening to the die-hard fans of how godly it is, and for how much the game's worth. Maybe get it when it's on sale, or something. I made the mistake of buying it at full price, and regret actually paying that much for it.

Let's not pretend that this game is not a phenomena. Like it or hate it, there's no disputing that this game is probably one of the biggest indie releases to date, regarding sales and sheer popularity. Basically anyone with a Steam account, or socail media, or anyone that uses the internet in general, has heard of this game. So, with this review, I'm not going to pretend that most people out there have not heard of this game and are completely clueless to it. Everyone talks about this game to a near obnoxious level, so the goal of my review is to try and convince anyone out there that's scepticle, that's completely uninterested because of how annoyed they are about hearing about it, that's completely turned off by the game and turn away from it simply because Tumblr has jumped straight into its trash chute. Because here's the thing. The worst thing about this game is its popularity. So again, my goal with this review is to not recommend, but IMPLORE that you listen and take my words into consideration. Because despite how much flack this game has gotten (when you forget about the immense praise it actually gets), this game is worth it. It deserves to be remembered, and I fully believe it can stand the test of time.
So with all of that established and out of the way, here's where I answer the main question. 'What is so great about Undertale?'. Well, a lot of things when you look at it all from a technical level. The story is very well thought out, written, and paced, the characters are all memorable (and despite a lot of opinions, very multi-dementional. It's called subtlty, people, these characters are "tropey" because that's only their outward appearance.) The music is fantastic, the gameplay is really fun and unique, and almost constantly changes the rules on you. It almost NEVER gets repetitive like a lot of standard RPG's usually are. That is... Depending on how you play. I'm sure most people already know what I'm talking about, the option to either FIGHT or SPARE. This is where most people get their experience spoiled and I know a lot of you out there know exactly what I'm talking about.
"NO, DON'T FIGHT, WHAT THE HELL IS WRONG WITH YOU!"
"YOU'RE PLAYING THE GAME WRONG, "YOU'RE GONNA HAVE A BAD TIME!""
I know how it is. Backseat gamers are super annoying. But here I am, a massive Undertale fan saying PLAY HOW YOU WANT. Your first time through, do what you feel like doing. It's a part of the experience, don't worry about what others say. Yes, your actions weigh heavily on the outcome of the story, and it's done in a way that actually MEANS something to the story of the game. But you are still a person playing a video game. It's YOUR experience, so treat it that way.
But again, getting back on track, 'What is so great about Undertale?'. Yes, all the technical aspect of the game are good and appealing, but what has gotten it so much hype? How is it that some consider it, quite literally, to be "one of the greatest games of all time"? There are so many out there that say that it's unfathomably overrated and should be thrown away and forgotten because no one will stop talking about it. "It doesn't deserve the hype". This is where most people, even die hard fans of the game, can't explain why it's NOT overrated. This is what's disapointing to the smaller group of people that love this game, such as me. The ones that love it for the entire point of the game. The thing that Toby Fox himself wanted players to see.
Undertale is one of those rare games that not only try to push the boundaries of what video games as an artform are capable of doing, telling a story and giving an experience, but also exceed its attempt. No other game before has done the things Undertale has done quite like Undertale. There are similar concepts used in other things that have come before, but still. Nothing quite like Undertale has done. Because Undertale doesn't use these unique concepts, which I will not explain and leave whomever is interested to find out for themselves, as a gimmick. An experiment or something new to try out. It takes full advantage of what it does and uses it in the context of the game's lore and story. It's something that, I as a player, brought me into this game's world and story far deeper than any game has done before. It made me feel literally a PART of the story. Some would say that's digging way too deep into fiction, but that's the thing. That is what I love about this game.
It has been a pretty long amount of time since I have played a video game and actually FELT like I was a part of it. Like I was IN it. That's something I always felt as a kid playing games, I always really felt like I was in whatever world I was experiencing, and I always felt like I actually knew the characters personally. Because that's just what happens when you're a kid. Fiction isn't so far from reality. And that is one of the biggest things that Undertale does right, with absolute flying colors. It takes that feeling, that suspension of disbelief that only a child could have, and uses the concepts and the way it tells its story to fully immerse the player like that. This game made me feel like I was 9 years old again, playing some of my first really good games for the first time again. That's what I think so many people love about this game, even those that don't fully realize it. That's what makes Undertale so great.
For those thinking about, or about to go into this game, even after all the hype and all the spoilers being thrown out there without any care, going in and expecting this absolute grand masterpiece of a video game, and point out every little tiny flaw and subjective thing that you don't like and feel the need to criticize the game for it, to the finest, sharpest detail possible... Just play the game. Pretend you're 9 years old again, and just experience the game. That's about the best thing you can do when playing Undertale.
