The main problem is that you CANNOT go 30+ minutes without having an entire gang of friends with you, even then that's a push, because people just kill you constantly, before you can even get any supplies or clothing. I played with a friend, we survived a little and got some sleeping bags. And then, BANG BANG we're dead. And you cannot defend yourself with but a mere rock; Not to mention how nearly everywhere is blocked from building, due to bases already being there! To sum up, this game is decent, but not worth £15 at all as you're not getting your money's worth from it, you're getting 50 pence's worth. You die, and die, you play as a bald person of the opposite gender, and the map is so bland and all the same, with the big red rusted sphere being the main place out of it all, mainly. So; No, do not get this game right now, wait for it to become a real game and not alpha (if that's ever going to happen, release date is 11 Dec 2013.. 2013!) or wait for everything to be on sale again, like at Christmas, get it dirt cheap. I got a refund for my purchase of this game, and I am glad of it.

For ten euro, there's so much to pick up from this game. Undertale isn't your traditional pick up, play and put back in your shelf game. Partly because it's only avaliable digitaly, but mainly because It's a game that sticks to you. And impacts you.
The world of Undertale is alive. It's breathing. And by alive, I don't mean the game world is huge, or looks impressing graphically. Quite the opposite actually. The game world in itself isn't impressing in scale, and the game looks like a game straight from the SNES era. What truly makes the world of Undertale feel so alive is it's characters and world-building.
Every character is so lovable, charming and distinct to the point where you almost view them as real persons. And the writing in the game is so fantastic, it's hard to stop playing or thinking about Undertale once you're hooked. The characters actually remember your actions and reacts to them, just like a real person would do. The characters are some of the most lovable in a video-game, and it explains the endless stream of fan-fiction and fan-art for the characters of Undertale. Undertale is the kind of game where you loose yourself in the experience, loose track of time and absolutely love it. Or hate it. Depending on YOUR actions.
And that brings me to my next point.
Undertale is a game where you make choices. Real, heavy choices. And the choices you make actually matter. Not just within the next ten minutes of gameplay, but for the whole experience. As I said, the characters remember everything you do. The game has no less than three diffrent endings, each one playing out significantly diffrent compared to the others. To understand the full plot, and the full greatness of Undertale you have to get all of them. The replay-value is fantastic.
The consequence of such a living world, meaningfull choices and so lovable characters makes for a game incredibly easy to immerse yourself into. And Undertale abuses this to the max.
Did I meantion that the writing in this game is incredible? It really is. I meant it.
The story has so many twists and turns and breaks the norm in so many ways, to the point that you never know what's gonna happen next. This game has some of the absolute most hearth-wrenching and hearth-warming moments in video-game history, and often you don't even see them coming. I wont spoil anything, but this game will make you laugh through your tears.
As you may have heard, I've mentioned the word experience many times throughout this review. And that's because that's just what Undertale is. This game will make you love yourself. Or absolutely hate yourself. The game toys with your feelings, and it's fantastic.
But what about the gameplay?
Well, Undertale surely doesn't dissapoint.
The combat system is fast-paced and robust, with each fight being like a puzzle on it's own depending on how you choose to handle the situation. The way you fight also change drasticly depending on which enemy or boss you're fighting, which makes every fight memorable.
And oh, did I meantion this game has a killer soundtrack? The game's tracks fit their scenes perfectly, and are a huge part of the game. The games track contributes to the experience immensly, and makes the emotional moments of Undertale hit even harder. Which is a rare thing these days. The boss tracks are also some of the most epic, awesome, hearth-pumping tracks I've ever heard.
Just listen to some of these tracks.

Ok, I understand tons of people love this game but... I seriously just can't.
Let's at least start with the stuff I did like:
- The gameplay is rather unique (more on that soon)
- Multiple paths to choose from
- Some humour at points (more on that soon too...)
- Some character designs are rather neat
- Homosexual relationships are mentioned (which is really amazing!) And the main character is androgynous, which is really good for me especially.
Ok... I'm pretty hard pressed to think of any really good positives, so I'll just spout out the stuff I didn't like:
- Combat, while unique, is boring and tedious
- Characters personalities are not that impressive, seem to have a few simple traits and never seriously develop
- Music isn't exactly impressive. It suits the tone sometimes, but only in certain places. No tracks are very memorable. This is a real shame for me considering I'm a musician myself, and I compose a lot of chiptune style music.
- The humour gets old fast.
- Dialogue is repetitive. Seriously, saying the word "determined" every 5 minutes makes me more determined to put this game down and play another game.
- Killing characters starts off emotional, but after the first 2 or 3 the emotional impact wears off. Bear in mind I consider myself very emotional, so this disappointed me greatly.
- The pace of the game is way too slow, and some battles are tiresomely long to the point that they are not worth it no matter what path you take.
- The tutorial segment is too long. It'd be good if there was more to the game, but there isn't. The game doesn't let you do anything for yourself for ages.
- There isn't any kind of satisfaction for keeping characters alive. The only time you feel satisfied is when you kill a character, but even then, their deaths become pointlessly drawn out.
- The graphics seem too simple. They seem lazy and there isn't any kind of charm.
- A single playthrough isn't that long at all (and considering everything above, one playthrough is more than enough)
- The world doesn't feel alive. At all.
I probably missed like 20 other things.
You can probably guess I don't like this game very much at this point. However, at this point I would like to say, for every negative in this game, there is a positive side to it. Likewise for every positive, there's a negative. Some characters feel more alive than others, and some characters get small humorous moments, but nothing really feels particularly special for them. Certain parts feel way too comical for their own good. Dialogue is generally so repetitive, but it gets good when it stops trying to repeat itself. There isn't any satisfaction in sparing an enemy, but sometimes this leads to more interesting conversations with characters. Killing opponents very quickly becomes meaningless, as there isn't really a reason to keep them around, but that means the game at least has some satisfying moments. Basically, everything good in this game is also bad, and everything bad is good, but in this game, the positives do nothing to outshine the negatives. The bad stuff just seems to come forth and take over, and the positives get drowned out because even though they are there, they don't make the game fun at all.
Bear in mind this is just my opinion. Honestly, I think that Undertale is a good game, but it's nothing special, and it's not anything I'd reccomend. I didn't enjoy it, but apparently most other people did, so it really depends on who you want to follow. For me, this was probably the most disappointing game I've played in... years... probably ever... but hey, that's just me.

Great price, great writing, great music and great gameplay. I don't think there's much I can say to sell someone on Undertale at this point, other than to say "you know all those overly positive reviews you've already read? They're correct.".
I've replayed this game several times through, and as someone who typically waits years before replaying games, this is probably the highest praise I can give it. And at the very least, the price should be reason enough to try it out and see what everyone's been talking about.
One thing I think is important to note is that I played the demo before playing the game - and I disliked it. I didn't think I'd bother playing the full game because the demo bored me. Then a friend encouraged me to play and gifted me a copy. I was actually quite worried I was going to end up disliking it based on the demo (also the first area of the game). After getting out of this area, the Ruins, I absolutely fell in love with the game. Since then, I have even bought a copy of the game for another friend!
I have seen a few people drop the game partway through the Ruins for the same reasons I nearly did - they're not super exciting. But once you get through them, the game gets infinitely better. So my recommendation is to stick through the Ruins if you're not quite feeling it and then spend some time in the next area of the game, Snowdin, before making your final call. It's a shame the least enjoyable part of the game is the very beginning as it's best for a game to grab people at the start or else it risks losing them.

Ok, I understand tons of people love this game but... I seriously just can't.
Let's at least start with the stuff I did like:
- The gameplay is rather unique (more on that soon)
- Multiple paths to choose from
- Some humour at points (more on that soon too...)
- Some character designs are rather neat
- Homosexual relationships are mentioned (which is really amazing!) And the main character is androgynous, which is really good for me especially.
Ok... I'm pretty hard pressed to think of any really good positives, so I'll just spout out the stuff I didn't like:
- Combat, while unique, is boring and tedious
- Characters personalities are not that impressive, seem to have a few simple traits and never seriously develop
- Music isn't exactly impressive. It suits the tone sometimes, but only in certain places. No tracks are very memorable. This is a real shame for me considering I'm a musician myself, and I compose a lot of chiptune style music.
- The humour gets old fast.
- Dialogue is repetitive. Seriously, saying the word "determined" every 5 minutes makes me more determined to put this game down and play another game.
- Killing characters starts off emotional, but after the first 2 or 3 the emotional impact wears off. Bear in mind I consider myself very emotional, so this disappointed me greatly.
- The pace of the game is way too slow, and some battles are tiresomely long to the point that they are not worth it no matter what path you take.
- The tutorial segment is too long. It'd be good if there was more to the game, but there isn't. The game doesn't let you do anything for yourself for ages.
- There isn't any kind of satisfaction for keeping characters alive. The only time you feel satisfied is when you kill a character, but even then, their deaths become pointlessly drawn out.
- The graphics seem too simple. They seem lazy and there isn't any kind of charm.
- A single playthrough isn't that long at all (and considering everything above, one playthrough is more than enough)
- The world doesn't feel alive. At all.
I probably missed like 20 other things.
You can probably guess I don't like this game very much at this point. However, at this point I would like to say, for every negative in this game, there is a positive side to it. Likewise for every positive, there's a negative. Some characters feel more alive than others, and some characters get small humorous moments, but nothing really feels particularly special for them. Certain parts feel way too comical for their own good. Dialogue is generally so repetitive, but it gets good when it stops trying to repeat itself. There isn't any satisfaction in sparing an enemy, but sometimes this leads to more interesting conversations with characters. Killing opponents very quickly becomes meaningless, as there isn't really a reason to keep them around, but that means the game at least has some satisfying moments. Basically, everything good in this game is also bad, and everything bad is good, but in this game, the positives do nothing to outshine the negatives. The bad stuff just seems to come forth and take over, and the positives get drowned out because even though they are there, they don't make the game fun at all.
Bear in mind this is just my opinion. Honestly, I think that Undertale is a good game, but it's nothing special, and it's not anything I'd reccomend. I didn't enjoy it, but apparently most other people did, so it really depends on who you want to follow. For me, this was probably the most disappointing game I've played in... years... probably ever... but hey, that's just me.

Great price, great writing, great music and great gameplay. I don't think there's much I can say to sell someone on Undertale at this point, other than to say "you know all those overly positive reviews you've already read? They're correct.".
I've replayed this game several times through, and as someone who typically waits years before replaying games, this is probably the highest praise I can give it. And at the very least, the price should be reason enough to try it out and see what everyone's been talking about.
One thing I think is important to note is that I played the demo before playing the game - and I disliked it. I didn't think I'd bother playing the full game because the demo bored me. Then a friend encouraged me to play and gifted me a copy. I was actually quite worried I was going to end up disliking it based on the demo (also the first area of the game). After getting out of this area, the Ruins, I absolutely fell in love with the game. Since then, I have even bought a copy of the game for another friend!
I have seen a few people drop the game partway through the Ruins for the same reasons I nearly did - they're not super exciting. But once you get through them, the game gets infinitely better. So my recommendation is to stick through the Ruins if you're not quite feeling it and then spend some time in the next area of the game, Snowdin, before making your final call. It's a shame the least enjoyable part of the game is the very beginning as it's best for a game to grab people at the start or else it risks losing them.

It took every ounce of D E T E R M I N A T I O N that I had left not to go outside and burn them to dust.
About a day later, I finished the True Pacifist run for the first time.
I looked outside, at the field of sunflowers, and I actually shed a few tears.\
And I promised myself that as long as I lived, I would never harm another flower in my life.
Undertale is my GOTY for 2015, ladies and gentlemen. And it's because a flower made me cry.

Okay this will be my first actual super serious game review! (or a wall of text review)
As a Dark Souls fanboy, I've been looking to play souls-like game.
The reason why I making this review is because I recently played Dragon's Dogma☠ and I keep thinking that the game doesn't feel like a souls game and it felt like 3rd person Diablo/PoE with fun combat.
So I thought, what is a souls-like game?(I know some people hate the term 'souls-like' but hear me out.)
Then Undertale crossed in my mind, both games has similarities that enhance my gaming experience.
Let's see...
Both games requires you to use your brain to fight most enemies even the easiest one, it isn't just button mashing and hoping you didn't get hit because of RNG.
It rewards you for being good.
Both games rewards you for exploring the areas, there are some optional areas that will reward you when you explore it.
In both gamess, most areas are connected and the map feels huge because of it.
When you died to a boss, the game will treats you that you have fought the boss so you could skip the dialouge for a straight up gameplay.
The lack of quest marker also improves the games, it doesn't force you to explore, instead you explore the world by your own will.

After played Dark Souls, now I hate manual saving that take too long just to save a game, thankfully in Undertale it is so fast it felt seamless.
Plot twist!
I think most of those lists I wrote are just the icing on the cake.
The actual cake is actually good musics, interesting characters, fun bossfights and engaging story!
Basically, I just want to point out the similarities of both games, or... I just can't stop praising this game and I had to write long review about it.

If you enjoyed the first Borderlands then this will fill like the mega deluxe sequel to it. Gearbox doesn't change up the formula much. It's just more of the good stuff. More highly detailed levels. More classes to play. More guns and interesting gun stats (like throwing your guns like grenades when you reload!). More Story. Way more jokes from the crude, to the ludicrous, dark, and ironic.
I have three criticisms but they are small. First the level designs are very highly detailed with scale. Some areas have seven floors and often times you can see multiple floors at the same time. It can be hard to process every thing that is happening at once. Second the NPCs talk over each other. If you want to hear what they say just stop moving. If you trigger another conversation it will just completely cut off the other one with no hope of retrieving it. Some of the areas are really long and you can easily be killing guys for up to an hour before another plot exposition. Maybe I'm just ADD but you can easily forget what was going on.
Over all Borderlands 2 is very very good with over 30 hours of content. I finished this game and felt like I could easily find another 15 hours and that's before all the extra DLC. The co-op in this game is no joke either. The enemies scale accordingly so it's not a cake walk and working together is a must in this shooter.  Easily worth it at full price. Pretty much a must buy at $15.

The only things that is slower than DayZ's development is the zombies in DayZ. The AI/threat level of the zombies is very bad. If a server performs well enough for them to not teleport all over the place, they are slow and weak (~10 hits to kill a player). They pose no threat once you get a decent melee weapon, and are especially easy to kill with guns, assuming there isn't any lag. I thought this was supposed to be a game about surviving the zombie apocalypse... if they pose no threat, why are the survivors killing each other? Why are we even playing this game to begin with then? Why not any of the survival games on steam with far better AI/Environmental threats and loads more content.... I'll get to that shortly.
While feature rich, the UI is very clunky and unintuitive. You will be taught even the simplest of tricks 10-20 hours into your gameplay if you don't read up on the wiki for an hour or two before you play(because there is no tutorial for most of these features).
The core gameplay is still buggy and poor. Each new feature they add feeling like a placeholder for something greater. As a Dark Souls fanboy, I've been looking to play souls-like game.
The reason why I making this review is because I recently played Dragon's Dogma☠ and I keep thinking that the game doesn't feel like a souls game and it felt like 3rd person Diablo/PoE with fun combat.
So I thought, what is a souls-like game?(I know some people hate the term 'souls-like' but hear me out.)
Then Undertale crossed in my mind, both games has similarities that enhance my gaming experience.
Let's see...
Both games requires you to use your brain to fight most enemies even the easiest one, it isn't just button mashing and hoping you didn't get hit because of RNG.
It rewards you for being good.
Both games rewards you for exploring the areas, there are some optional areas that will reward you when you explore it.
In both gamess, most areas are connected and the map feels huge because of it.
When you died to a boss, the game will treats you that you have fought the boss so you could skip the dialouge for a straight up gameplay.
The lack of quest marker also improves the games, it doesn't force you to explore, instead you explore the world by your own will.

After played Dark Souls, now I hate manual saving that take too long just to save a game, thankfully in Undertale it is so fast it felt seamless.
Plot twist!
I think most of those lists I wrote are just the icing on the cake.
The actual cake is actually good musics, interesting characters, fun bossfights and engaging story!
Basically, I just want to point out the similarities of both games, or... I just can't stop praising this game and I had to write long review about it.

I've loved every hour and kill in this game.
Borderlands 2, obvious sequel to ''Borderlands'' is honestly one of my favorite games ever (and i'm a pretty hardcore gamer myself). This is a fantastic blend between RPG and FPS. In a vast and amazing open world approprietly named ''Pandora''. Every meter of this game has so much to offer, so many guns (87 Bazillion!), so many locations and so many enemies. Borderlands 2 is a never ending experience with lots of fun.
The Hyperion Corporation desires to obtain the Vault Key to awaken ''The Warrior'' for mass extinction. And it's leader, Handsome Jack, will do anything to make this happen. Your job is to make your way through and stop this from happening. While doing this, you have tons of side quests, you'll meet tons of old friends and find lots of easter eggs and references.
Factions:
The Bandits will be your main annoyance. As generic bandits, they'll give you a struggle throughout the game. They don't care about no ''Vault Key'', pssshhhh, they just wanna see some blood! Nomads, Psychos, Marauders, Midgets, Rats, Goliaths and Bruisers are what define Borderlands as a whole and if Borderlands 3 is a thing, they will undoubtedly appear and cast the same fame.
Hyperion Corporation is the strongest faction, the so-to-speak leaders of Pandora. With Engineers, Loaders, Constructors and Soldiers, Hyperion will give you one hell of a bad time if you do not have the appropiate weapons and level.
Crimson Raiders are who you work for. Lead by the main cast of the first Borderlands, Roland, Lilith, Mordecai and Brick. The Crimson Raiders are who want to stop Jack. On here, no one ever does anything except you. So essentially you are your own faction to stop it all.
And obviously, Wildlife. There are too many iterations of these to write them all. The Wildlife can be seen in almost every location. Spiderants, Varkids, Crystalisks, Threshers etc. These are particularly the main annoyance, at least for me. You'll encounter them almost anywhere that's not Hyperion terretory.
Those are all the Factions. What else is there?
Leveling up: The game consists on an XP system that depending on your level and the enemy's, you'll get rewarded with a certain amount of XP once they die. There are also other ways to get XP: Completing missions, completing long term accomplishments (open 5000 boxes, pick up 750 weapons etc.)
XP and levelling up is what makes the game unique and hard to an extent.
Guns: Borderlands 2 uses a similar Item randomization like Diablo III. In Borderlands 2, there are aproximately 17,000,000 different types of weapons. They all can vary in: Scope, Type of bulets, Type of Melee, Rarity, Firing Rate, Accuracy, Recoil, Reticle etc. The probability of you finding the same gun twice is pretty damn small.
Rarity: There are 5 different types of rarity: White, Green, Blue, Purple, Orange.
White being least rare and Orange being rarest. These can all vary between guns, grenade mods, shields, class mods, relics, heads and skins. However these do depend on level, for example: A level 1 orange is a lot worse than a level 50 white.
Rarity in Borderlands 2 makes Farming a big role in the game. If you wanna get better stuff you better get used to doing stuff like this. Farming can be: Killing a boss, saving and quitting and doing it again until you have something you like, this can also be done with a chest. Everytime you save and quit chests and enemies go back to their original state.
Side Quests: Quests are essentially what make up the game. But I mean side quests. Side quests help you level up faster, get better stuff and know more about the game. You may ignore these, but that's not very smart and could make your Borderlands experience awfully slow an painful. Side Quests are just as importat as Main Story missions.
There is much more to offer, but i've got only so many characters left.
I hope you've enjoyed this giant and rather small summarize of the game. Borderlands 2 has much more to offer! Please consider buying Borderlands 2.

How to review this game... Its not for everyone.  If you want to play a survival game where you can actually survive, you might want to look elsewhere!  Rust is cruel and unforgiving.  You are going to get beaten to death by naked people with rocks.  You will be shot in the head trying to get enough wood to build a campfire.  You will experience frustration.  Despite that, Rust is my absolute favorite PC game.  You can play the game in so many different ways... Updates are almost every week, and many times they are loaded with content.  NPCs are only so smart in other survival games, but surviving from other players... they are a true challenge to survive from.  I definitely recommend this game!

I do recommend this game.
Since my original review, Rust has gone through yet another iteration, and most of my primary criticisms have either been addressed or are heading in the right direction.  Rust still needs some work on PVE (spoiled meat mechanics, more requirements on hydration), game mechanics (electricity? vehicles?) and customization for people who run servers.  Not everyone wants to play Rust 8 hours a day and PVE can be a huge grind, but Facepunch responds and iterates on player feedback.  PVP seems solid right now.  Base building and raiding seem "fun" and good enough for now.  Pathfinding and AI is being fixed, which should resolve many complaints and perhaps lead to other fun things.  I can say the game continues to strike a balance between beautiful and performant, fun and strategic, and even though it goes down directions that I think aren't fun, overall (3/4 years) it has been well worth the money and time spent playing.  I recommend this game because the developers do respond to the mountain of feedback they get from the community, and seem to care about the game being successful.
Forced monthly wipes are still a problem to me, but if you want a faster game that's more casual, two week and one month wipe cycles are good.  However, this limits the scope of this game's true potential.  All the other game mechanics have been seen in other games like Ark and 7DTD.  Unlike those games, Rust has better PVP and is at least on average, more performant and beautiful.

Undertale, “the friendly RPG where no one has to die.” When a game makes you feel bad for killing monsters and makes you consider not killing any more, then it definitely does something right!
The story goes that both monsters and human once ruled over earth, living together, until war broke out between the two races. The humans defeated the monsters and drove them to the depths of Mt. Ebott, trapped with a magic spell. You appear on a bed of golden flowers, and are greeted by a flower, and taught about friendliness pellets. Afterwards, you can choose to massacre every monster you meet, or choose to show mercy to your opponents. Your actions of killing or mercy will shape the way the game progresses, as well as how others view you. The dialogues, and even the music of the game will become happier or distorted based on your killings or acts of mercy. With that said, there are a few endings that can be achieved within the game, some being more satisfying than others; some feeling like you are cutting onions, and some just for the cold hearted. What makes these outcomes to impactful, and sometimes sad, is the way the monsters react to the player’s actions, and sometimes questioning your actions and making you feel like a monster for the things you do. This is also true when you do immoral things like take more than one candy from a bowl of candy that says “take one please”.
Gameplay is very easy to catch on to, and is like one of those old time rpg games like Earthbound. Your goal is simple, but complex, just get through the game(through any means necessary). Your initial goal, or why you are there are not stated, but you can assume you fell down the mountain (as seen in the opening). Your real goal is to play the game as you like, exploring this unique world of monsters and see what it has to offer.  While you explore the world, you will have numerous random encounters with monsters, in which you are a heart that must avoid monster’s attacks, and will die if you take too much damage (causing you to restart at your last save). Pretty easy to understand and play, but a bit difficult to master, as some of the later encounters will be a lot more difficult to dodge seamlessly, and may prove to require a bit more thought and endurance to overcome, rather than just one lucky turn. The game itself is not too difficult, in that it does not have any difficult puzzles to do, and no grinding is required to win the game, as the game can be beaten without killing a single thing.

The visuals are all a bit old timey, but that does not take away from the experience. As for the audio, there are a wide variety of songs that make the game very fun while in combat scenarios. The beginning music was a bit new to me, as I did not think it would have the old retro type of music, but it surprisingly worked well and was not monotonous, and seemed to match the backdrops, and battles very well.
Why would I include a characters section in a review? The answer is, because they are such an integral part of the game, otherwise it would be like any other rpg, with the exception of the option to spare your opponents.  The characters are what make this game so memorable. It’s not the fact these characters are super likeable, since you may end up disliking or even hating some of them, but the fact these characters will end up growing on you in the end. Without such a unique and hilarious cast of characters, the player would not feel any real motivation to spare them, or any remorse if the player decides to kill any of them. They are in all respects to this game, the driving force that makes it so popular and why it causes many (if not all) it’s players to shed tears.

If you enjoyed the first Borderlands then this will fill like the mega deluxe sequel to it. Gearbox doesn't change up the formula much. It's just more of the good stuff. More highly detailed levels. More classes to play. More guns and interesting gun stats (like throwing your guns like grenades when you reload!). More Story. Way more jokes from the crude, to the ludicrous, dark, and ironic.
I have three criticisms but they are small. First the level designs are very highly detailed with scale. Some areas have seven floors and often times you can see multiple floors at the same time. It can be hard to process every thing that is happening at once. Second the NPCs talk over each other. If you want to hear what they say just stop moving. If you trigger another conversation it will just completely cut off the other one with no hope of retrieving it. Some of the areas are really long and you can easily be killing guys for up to an hour before another plot exposition. Maybe I'm just ADD but you can easily forget what was going on.
Over all Borderlands 2 is very very good with over 30 hours of content. I finished this game and felt like I could easily find another 15 hours and that's before all the extra DLC. The co-op in this game is no joke either. The enemies scale accordingly so it's not a cake walk and working together is a must in this shooter.  Easily worth it at full price. Pretty much a must buy at $15.

Ein durch und durch geniales Spiel. Handsome Jack ist einer der besten Bösewichte seit langem, mir gefällt er sogar noch besser als Vaas aus Far Cry 3. Aber auch außer dem überdurchschnittlich bösen (wer hätt's gedacht?) Bösewicht bietet das Spiel viele tolle Momente.
Das ganze Spiel basiert auf der Theorie "abge♥♥♥♥terer kränkerer shidd ist gar nicht mehr möglich". Es wird an jeder Ecke übertrieben, bitterböser zynischer Humor angewandt und auf den beiden höheren Schwierigkeitsgraden wird es richtig anspruchsvoll.
Allen voran möchte ich auf Tiny Tina eingehen. Sie ist ein NPC, den man schon ziemlich zu Beginn des Spiels kennenlernt. Auf der einen Seite kindlich und niedlich, auf der anderen Seite brutal, vor nichts zurück scheuend, durchtrieben und eine Sprengstoffexpertin. Egal was passiert, sie hat immer den passenden Spruch auf Lager und abgesehen von dem "Arschgaul" hat sie den größten Lacher auf meine Lippen gezaubert, und das ist bei meiner Art von Humor nicht wirklich leicht.
Die Grafik ist gewöhnungsbedürftig, aber unterstreicht den abge♥♥♥♥t verrückten Stil des Spiels nochmals.
Das Item-System ist sehr motivierend. Man möchte immer eine bessere Knarre (von denen es bekanntlich noch Bazillionende mehr als schon in Teil 1 gibt), Schilde oder Artefakte finden. Auch durch die unterschiedlichen Seltenheitstypen (Legendarys, Selten, Schrott, etc.) und oftigen Spezialeffekten der Items wird das System nochmals motivierender als es ohnehin schon ist.
Das erste Playthrough dauert etwa 25 bis 30 Stunden, ab dem zweiten mal sollte man deutlich mehr Zeit einplanen, so habe ich etwa 60 Stunden gebraucht.
Die Charakterklassen sind gut ausbalanciert und alle spielen sich sehr flüssig. Es gibt keine unfaire Skills, also kommt es wirklich nur auf den persönlichen Geschmack des Spielers an.
Borderlands 2 ist ein klasse Spiel, das ordentlich Langzeitmotivation bietet. Die Dialoge, Handsome Jack, die verrückten Sprüche der Gegner und auch alle anderen Szenen sitzen perfekt und bringen jeden zum Lachen. Außerdem fetzt das Gameplay und so vergehen die Stunden wie im Flug.

All in all, a really great game. Handsome Jack is one of the best villain for a long time, I personally "liked" him even more than Vaas from Far Cry 3. But there are more great moments than only the ones with this above average evil villain.
The whole game is based on the theory "♥♥♥♥ this♥♥♥♥♥♥ there's nothing sicker than that possible". It's exaggerated, the humor is very black and the two higher difficulties are getting pretty hard.
First of all, I want to talk about Tiny Tina. She's a NPC, whom you get to know pretty early in the game. On one side she's childish and cute, but on the other side she's violent and a explosive expert. No matter what happens, she's always says the right lines, and except the scene with the "Butt Stallion" I haven't had a better laugh in th entire game.
You have to get used to the graphics in order to really like them, but once you're used to them, they increase the crazy atmosphere of the game even more.
The loot-system is very motivating. You want to get better guns (and we all know they got even bazillionder), shields or artefacts. There are different rarities (for example Legendary, Rare or scrap, and so on) and also some special effects on some items. This system makes it even more motivating to get some new guns.
The first playthrough can be finished in around 25 to 30 hours, but already at the second one you need way more time. For example, I needed nearly 60 hours.
The different classes are well balanced and the unplay is fluently and feels good. There are no unfair skills, so it all depends on your personal taste of characters.
Borderlands 2 is a awesome game with a giant load of long-term motivation. The dialogs, Handsome Jack, the crazy lines that enemies sometimes say when you shoot them and all the other scenes are perfectly perfect and will cause everyone to laugh. Furthermore, the gameplay is great.

This game is not finished.
Pros vs cons:
+ It's a game about fighting zombies and surviving in a huge world. How can it go wrong?
- It is not finished, thus being buggy, laggy and not a very enjoyable overall experience.
+ Huge, open world to explore, with several cities and vast wilderness (taken from ARMA II, but still).
- The world mostly consists of empty woodland and grassy fields, making most players gather in the cities.
+ It's ultra-realistic, as you need to eat, drink, keep warm and dry to stay alive.
- It's ultra-realistic, seeing as you break your legs (ofcourse your limbs can be broken, duh) if you free fall from higher than 1 m.
+ Graphics are good, not great, resulting in an enjoyable experience for most people, regardless of  gaming rig.
- View distance is INSANELY far by default, and cannot be changed in-game, resulting in very bad framedrops.
+ PvP is intense and dynamic, spanning from PvE-coop, gang wars, robbing lone wanderers and kidnapping people etc.
- Finding friends can be tideous, as there are no means of localizing yourself in the world, let alone a map.
+ Huge community with millions of players, lots of servers and 24/7 in-game activity.
- There seems to be hackers and cheaters on lots of servers
+ The game is being patched regularly.
- The patches rarely make significant changes that improves the experience of playing.
Overall, Dayz is a great idea that is poorly executed.

This is one of the best games i've played in a long time, I have always been a HUGE fan of Story Rich games (Mainly the Professor Layton games) which makes this game stand out quite quickly for me.
The characters we're all so unique, even the side charcters like Burgerpants and Temmie stood out so much. I respect the fact you made every singe side character different unlike some games who would make merchants and villagers all look the same.
The personalities were very broadened, each character had their own way of getting you attached. Toriel was sweet and cared deeply for you, making you feel bad about leaving the ruins. Sans is a jokester who seemed to be there for Comic relief (No Pun Intended) and i Love that you gave him
. I would say "This is the same for all the characters" But it's not, None of them our exactly the same. These characters felt real to me, real people i was interacting with, they were real friends.
The story is very strong and emotional in lots of different ways. At times i'd be laughing hysterically and other times i'd be crying joyfully or emotionally. What i like about the story is that it's not difficult to understand, i see lots of games who make the story so complicated and twisting i just can't keep up. In this game i understood everything, i figured out a a little before it actually happen. Don't get me wrong i'm not saying the story is simple i'm just saying it's not trying to branch out in too many directions. I won't post anything about what in the story i liked as i want people to be able to read this spoiler free.
To be Very honest i'm not the biggest fan this games way of characters remembering everything you do. I mean it wasn't bad at all, it was really interesting. I just wish i could do a True Reset incase i want to restar properly. Picture this scenario "You want to reset the game because you didn't do the Pacifist Route properly and you want to experience the proper text and actions of the characters, when you reset the characters remember you, your choices and who you may have killed" This is what happened to me. Again, don't get me wrong i didn't this feature i just thought it could have more of a free option to truly reset.
Despite that, the idea of Sparing, brilliant, something i don't see that often. Don't quote me on this but i hear a feature like that was in Metal Gear Solid(?). I'm glad i could finally be the Good Guy instead of the Murderous guy or even the other way round. A clever feature to go with this is the fact the Characters will actually react to your choices of murdering Monsters (Don't look if you haven't played this yet it's a HUGE spoiler e.g
).
This game is one of the best games recently, i feel like the characters are real. This game is so story driven i forget how retro the graphics are. If you are considering buying this game or you are looking for a Story Rich and Emotional game, please, Go with Undertale!
On the other hand if you are looking for something more choice based i would recommend a different game like:
Until Dawn
Minecraft:StoryMode (If you are into that)

The randomization of "gender" (i.e. weird-looking, alien-like female type humanoid) is one thing, but to force it on players in a permanent basis based on their steam ID is stupid.  Yes, female characters were needed.  Multiple races were needed.  Players should, however, be able to freely choose.  I know it's not very original, but being able to customize your avatar as you see fit is important in a game like this.  Whether you want the character to look like you or not is irrelevent.  The point is Facepunch is forcing its players (i.e. its backers, since it's still early access) to play a character not of their choosing and one they may not necessarily like.
I expect there to always be men who play female characters and women who play men, but if it's their choice, then I'm all for it.  But voice-chat will ruin any immersion.  I've heard the argument "so does a kid's voice coming out of a man's body."  Well, seems interesting considering this game is rated for adults only, and if not then why are no children character models in Rust for them to play?
That being said, it's a game.  It's supposed to be fun.  Remove enough of the choices that tend to make a game more attractive and pretty soon people will make the choice to not play anymore.
Had a lot of fun while it lasted.  Voting no out of principle.

Rust is a lot like a rollercoaster. One minute you're on an uphill climb, trying to find the blueprints and items you need to survive amongst the KOS (Kill on Sight) players. You may luckily stumble upon an simple barrel or box that drops an AK or Bolt with some ammo. At that very moment you hear a rustling in the bushes, A PLAYER. You dash to take cover, only to be shot down. You curse the player, telling them you will find them and-. They shoot you in the face, and call you a♥♥♥♥♥♥
This is rust, a game where you can build what you want almost anywhere in game. Players can harvest resources from nodes scattered all about the map. Random barrels and boxes will spawn around the towns that populate the map. You can easily find these by using
and find the server you play on. It helps to know where you are, and what is around you.
Early game can be frustrating if you are alone, that is unless there was a recent blueprint wipe. Blueprints(knowledge of craftable items) are wiped every 2 weeks typically, along with the maps. At first this turned me off a lot, all my hard work lost. But as I played one wipe cycle, another, two, four, 8... I reminisced about the bases I had built and what I had learned from getting raided. Each time I was raided I learned something, a new game mechanic or item that would help defend my precious loot.
I must say that defending against a raid is my favorite part of this game. It is the most NERVERACKING experience to hear footsteps outside your base, or shooting rockings or the beep beep of C4. Whats worse is when you hear them above you, in your own base. This game is about cunning and hand eye coordination, and resources. If you can outplay them, out shoot and outresource you will win every time. There will always be a way into a base with enough explosives, but you can try to negate a lot of raids by simple floor spikes.
Also, the servers. There are thousands, literally thousands of servers. I think anyone in the world could find one with a decent ping near them, and in my experience i've stuck with the 2x, 3x or 4x modded servers. Vanilla is fun to me, but I play solo a lot more than in a group. It's hard to get anything done with the vanilla loot table, and dying with a few thousnd wood is a tradgedy if you just started. I enjoy being able to teleport to my friends when they join, or have them teleport directly to the base I have been building instead of them wandering around for 20 minutes and wasting time. Another good feature, remove tool is just fantastic. I love to build but I mess up way too often to not have a remove tool, on some you can even pick up items like the walls and repair benches!
I have about 275 hours in this game right now, and it is my most played game on Steam. I've never played a game that has such finality to it. You make your own experience here, if you build a♥♥♥♥♥♥base, chances are it's going to get raided. Chances are your base will get raided regardless, but the point is that is a great part of the game. It sucks it you don't know how the game works, and can be very disheartening and frustrating. If you persevere you may find that this game has a lot to offer. I grew up playing SNES all the way up through PS4 now, and I never thought I'd see a game like this. I can't wait for the update bringing the XP system, I think I will enjoy that a lot more. Currently you are forced to lurk in the towns to get blueprint fragments to try and learn the items you find. Or if you are luck you might find the blueprint already made. Here's to hoping the XP system will be great!
Also, ♥♥♥♥ing bears. Watch out for the bears.  They will ♥♥♥♥ you up out of nowhere.
Pro tip: carry a bed on resource runs, when you feel nervous about the amount of♥♥♥♥♥♥you have ony you start paying attention to where you are and place a bag down. If you die you might get lucky enough to spawn near yourself and kill the player that got you or grab your loot and run!
10/10 Please keep working on this game!

The point is Facepunch is forcing its players (i.e. its backers, since it's still early access) to play a character not of their choosing and one they may not necessarily like.
I expect there to always be men who play female characters and women who play men, but if it's their choice, then I'm all for it.  But voice-chat will ruin any immersion.  I've heard the argument "so does a kid's voice coming out of a man's body."  Well, seems interesting considering this game is rated for adults only, and if not then why are no children character models in Rust for them to play?
That being said, it's a game.  It's supposed to be fun.  Remove enough of the choices that tend to make a game more attractive and pretty soon people will make the choice to not play anymore.

Since my original review, Rust has gone through yet another iteration, and most of my primary criticisms have either been addressed or are heading in the right direction.  Rust still needs some work on PVE (spoiled meat mechanics, more requirements on hydration), game mechanics (electricity? vehicles?) and customization for people who run servers.  Not everyone wants to play Rust 8 hours a day and PVE can be a huge grind, but Facepunch responds and iterates on player feedback.  PVP seems solid right now.  Base building and raiding seem "fun" and good enough for now.  Pathfinding and AI is being fixed, which should resolve many complaints and perhaps lead to other fun things.  I can say the game continues to strike a balance between beautiful and performant, fun and strategic, and even though it goes down directions that I think aren't fun, overall (3/4 years) it has been well worth the money and time spent playing.  I recommend this game because the developers do respond to the mountain of feedback they get from the community, and seem to care about the game being successful.
Forced monthly wipes are still a problem to me, but if you want a faster game that's more casual, two week and one month wipe cycles are good.  However, this limits the scope of this game's true potential.  All the other game mechanics have been seen in other games like Ark and 7DTD.  Unlike those games, Rust has better PVP and is at least on average, more performant and beautiful.

Alright, so its time I rectify this, if you read my old review it has been completely deleted, because as I have progressed farther in the game (still stuck on the last boss, or the easiest enemy in the game depending on how you look at it) and thought an amendment should be made.
Something you should know about me is that I don't like turn based strategy games, its not that I think that they are inherently bad, I finished KOTOR back to front twice loving the story but hating every second of the combat, in fact one of my favorite games of recent years was turn based (child of light). to me I don't like them because they strip me of control, I feel like I'm losing battles not based on my own skills but on lifeless statistics, and as Mark Twain once said, "there are three kinds of lies, lies, damn lies, and statistics".
However undertale gives you the ability to defend yourself (sort of, kind of, not really) so theoretically I should like this game, right? Well I did, for the first two of the three playthroughs you need to really get the full story, I never really did like the combat though. So there I go, killing a few things on my first neutral playthrough, and killing nothing on my pacifist run, but then I got to my genocide playthrough. As the name implies you need to literally kill everything you ever meet, oh and by the way that means you need to grind for several hours until all of the random encounters end. Which is about as interesting as watching paint dry, because at this point I'm so over leveled (because instead of sparing everything I'm killing everything) its not a challenge and therefore feels uninteresting. You need to do this for every major section in the game (which if I recall there are four of) and its not fun, its like gathering the animus fragments in assassins creed, it feels pointless and arbitrary because it is. Animus fragments serve to lengthen the already erroneous amount of time you spend to get 100%, while undertales grinding serves to artificially extend what would otherwise be a short and sweet final playthough.
Now the last few paragraphs (and the giant red thumbs down) might give you the impression that I hate undertale more then anything, which is not the case. It would be more accurate to say that undertale let me down, the first two playthroughs are fun, interesting, charming, funny, sad, and thought provoking. Providing me with some of the most interesting emotional conundrums I have ever experienced, If you didn't seriously consider not playing genocide after beating pacifist and THAT thing shows up and tells you the stuff, after you open the game again, then you probably don't have a soul. After all that, I'm reduced from having a great time, to being forced to memorize attack patterns and pounding on the computer desk in frustration.
In summery, I don't hate undertale, most of undertale is amazing and wonderful and you should play it, in fact I would say that about 88% of undertale is awesome, but that 12%... that genocide playthough. A playthough that at this point I'm only playing so I can beat the game and be part of the conversation, but that isn't why I play games. So go buy undertale, and judge it for yourself, heck I know that I'm one of the only people that thinks this.
Thanks for reading, keep on playn'

most negative reviews about borderlands 2 are short, to the point. but some of them played this game for a long time, got into almost all the DLC too, I loved this game, but looking back upon it, what was good, is now sour.
Here is a detailed reason why borderlands 2 is inferior to it's predescessor.
Memes are the most common complaint. Why hound the memes? Memes aren't inherently a bad thing, but they are best when they are homegrown, and are either in-universe-in-jokes among characters or spawned by the players of the games. The memes referenced in borderlands 2 are completely unrelated to the game, are years out-of-fashion by the time they are included, and are senseless throwaway references which are neither a creative shoutout nor are humoring.
A subject that you
not have heard as much in the steam reviews, is the painful, cringeworthy writing that tries to put doses of "reality" in between the cartoony, comical world that you're constantly blowing up. It's not even an ink stain, it's more like your dad dribbled his brown musty dinner gravy all over your comic book page because he wanted to teach you a rambling seinfeldian lesson that you've heard ten thousand times this year in every other facet of life. Scarlet's booty DLC goes completely full throttle with this, and the result is even more painful.
Player characters are awkwardly referred to as "vault hunter," as a replacement for any sort of name or pronoun. Borderlands the First worked around pronoun use by avoiding this kind of writing completely, and it flowed much more smoothly than the sequel. The game's lead antagonist- Handsome Jack had his most fondly remembered lines as improvised lines. Imagine what the character would've been if the default writing was kept in place?
story and gameplay segregation are going full force in this game too, bosses established as major threats become pathetically easy if you've managed to overlevel yourself, major characters die terrible cheap deaths in cutscenes, and the one mission that
game mechanics into the story is a throwaway near-end mission that tastelessly involves suicide.
I will speak nothing of homosexuality, whenever someone talks about that, it turns into a giant political slap-fight.
yes. there are less guns in borderlands 2.
there I said it.
seriously. play a drinking game- take a shot everytime you pick up a duplicate weapon, you will last shorter than you think.
I'm not the first to point this out either-
so anyways, why are there less guns overall?
you know how many gun brands were retooled to have their own quirks and gimmicks? this however, was a case of "one step forward, two steps back" in the department of gun quanity. Why?
and to make matters worse, many gun mods that were common in the first game (the masher revolver for example) became Rare-exclusives for borderlands 2.
finally, three gun brands were removed from the game, only one was replaced, and only a few new additions were made for guns overall.
Math always tells the truth.
TotalBiscuit did a glorious rant on this in regards to the pre-sequel:
I for one would like to extend this- borderlands 2 is an exercise in artificial longevity, whereas the pre-sequel refines artificial longevity.
borderlands the first had an amazing tidbit in its system for rares-
I have yet to see a game that actually implements something like this, what does the sequel do?
* lowers the drop rate by a factor of 10 to increase grind.
* locks certain rares to a specific boss, so you have to waste time walking from the start of the area to the boss itself.
* removes them completely from vending machines.
as bad as that is, what is worse, is the completely busted progression system. your rare gear that you got from the boss, underperforms compared to vendor trash that is two levels higher than it (this game doesn't want you to play favorites with your guns) unlike the first which level-uped the rare guns. character progression is FUBAR as well. Borderlands the first, the general caps for stats existed around the low-mid thousands range. Borderlands 2's progress stays fairly level by the time you reach the end of the main story, but for each successive playthrough, the progression skyrockets to numerical levels more common in something like the Disgaea series. why? to make it feel like there's some semblance of a challenge, even though the AI acts the same and simply kills you vastly faster.
to top all this madness off, the game's busted stat progression makes it's busted gun progression
as you level up!
the story and characters are often the highest praised part of this game- so much that it got a telltale games series. Even in the DLC, the characters are more remembered than anything else.
The grind of borderlands 2, however, makes you play through the story
before you've reached the level cap, its charm becomes meaningless and the game turns into a chore. You've seen it once? Do you like seeing the same jokes two more times?
? heaven forbid you want to play as another character, especially if you don't want to resort to save editing.
if you want to buy it for the story, that's fine, just try and buy it on sale if you do.

Let me start by saying this won't be a traditional game review. I'm not going to go into specifics about how the game looks, plays, and things of that caliber; alternatively, I'd like to take a moment to talk about something that many people seem to have a difficult time understanding: Happiness.
This is a concept that's easily comprehended by even the children in their youngest years of living, but later into things I've noticed that its true nature starts to get hazy. People start to question the very validity of the happiness that kids experience, and perhaps it is true that what some kids have isn't particularly real happiness, but if Undertale, Spirited Away, stories from across human history and even more than that has taught me, it's that children may understand happiness better than any of us. The young are filled with a desire to live and see what everything has to offer... an affirmative determination to learn more, laugh more, live more, and even love more. Maybe it is innocence that's the deciding factor, and maybe we do leave that behind at a certain age, but love, happiness, and peace ARE stronger than just simple innocence.
In my eighteen years of living, I've yet to gain any EXP or LOVE (which only people who've played to the near end of the game will get), but I've never had any real reason to even try to. And as much as I wish I could say we were all playing the same game... the truth is we aren't; we play by the same set of rules to be certain, but some variables change them and us in the process.
Some individuals lose the path to happiness. They do things that in their minds they see as logical decisions.
Killing people, killing ANYONE, including yourself, is never a logical answer, nor even a right answer; please take that to heart.
If you can't find your happiness... talk to someone. Talk to anyone willing to listen. I guarantee there's someone out there who will listen.
It's all so intensely daunting... but one thing I can tell you is all of this... all of this is a project. It's a continued piece of effort that we throw ourselves into daily or bi-daily. It's incredibly difficult to find happiness in a short amount of time; it's so difficult it can't be measured by clear way of passing; however, it isn't impossible.
To find it though, you just have to keep going.
I can't tell anything about this game that you can't already see from the trailer, the internet, or everything that's already been said about it, but I can say this: If you'd like a pleasant experience, one that may teach you a thing or two about the inherent nature of happiness and love, than I'd say that you should try it out. You might very well enjoy it.
Have faith in others.
Have confidence in yourself.
Stay determined.

It has also left me with questions. Many questions. I was mostly a pacifist, but there were a few deaths under my belt and I can't help but wonder how much they mattered. How different is the genocide run? What about something exactly in the middle? Is it possible to kill this particuar character, and how would this character react? How many different endings? What kind of secrets are in there? What kind of lore?
In short, I beat the game but I'm nowhere near done with it yet. I have forgiven two certain fonts for existing and I'm really tempted to buy the soundtrack, which is excellent. While the 8-bit 2D aspect of this game was a turn off for me at first it eventually became what gave this game its charm and what sets it apart from almost every other RPG I've played. Undertale seamlessly blends masterful storytelling, a beautiful soundtrack, and unique combat system into a game that’s still remarkably short, a truly impressive feat. Undertale is very much a repetitive game, encouraging multiple playthroughs but to say that this repetitive nature takes away from the overall experience would be doing it a disservice. Undertale is not only a good video game, it is a unique experience that is meant to be returned to time and time again. While it’s possible to say that this game is all hype and to simply pass it off as a cult classic, you would be missing one of the most unique experiences in all of gaming. Undertale is one of my favorite games of all time and one of the very best video games ever made. 10/10

I don't write reviews, mostly as I feel I can never get my point or feeling across properly that and I'm too lazy. However I felt the need to write one for Rust, which I must say is quite the accomplishment. If I could justify recomending it for getting me off my proverbial rear end I would. Sadly though this is not the case. I will start off by saying I know I don't have much in the way of shown hours logged, blame me for doing things like downloading patches to client based steam and non-steam games when I do play rust.
I bought rust back in 2013 I think might have been '14 little fuzzy on that detail. I enjoyed the game quite a bit, minus offline... I wouldn't call them raids more like vandalism. When it came time for the game to be split into legacy and whatever we call the current build I was happy for some of the changes coming. Frankly I was tired of staring at and running about the same map. I welcomed most of the changes that happened after that, one though most of all I despised. That was when I found our character appearence would be locked to our steam id's. I didn't complain at all about it as I figured later on we would get to create our characters eventually. Over time that hope was well frankly stomped on and finally buried with this latest update.
I know Garry runs this game like a little social expieriment seeing what happens when you tweak certain elements. I was okay with that for a while as long as it seemed like it was going to continue to be a game. After all I paid for a game, something to enjoy maybe have a bit of an escape from reality. If I'm going to be participating in an expierment I expect to be compensated for it, not to pay into it. No I'm not saying pay me jsut simply I'm not going to thro money at someone's research that I really have no interest it: especially when I'm one fo the "labrats".
I feel as though I can get into a game more if I make the character I want or if the character has a fairly fleshed out story if I am going to be playing a preditermined character. Rust however takes that away, I am who my steamID makes me. I don't get to choose who or what I am, I am simply thrown into random PC body #4,376,890. I can not connect with that character; I feel unmotived to play him, it just all around saps my enjoyment from the game when I can't play whom I want to.
I simply can not play Rust anymore. As an addtion, the responses to requests to add character creation, gender change or something along those lines by Garry had led me to a conclusion... He's a prat.
I do not support that Gender-Dictatorship!

Undertale is an amazing experience to enjoy... as long as your not spoiled to it. While it may have (in my opinion) very enjoyable gameplay, the big selling point and what everyone goes on about is the story and characters. The basic outline of the story is very basic, but the characters and world really make this plot interesting from a loving caretaker-esque goat to two very 'comical' brothers. Undertale has a strange feeling like the Mother series and will probably make you attached to tall the characters making multiple runthroughs a bad idea for your emotions.. The selling point of 'you don't need to kill everyone' only really effects the story in two majors ways with two routes feeling similiar and one being a complete tone shift, it still makes enough changes on each route make it feel (possibly) worth it (plus the twist near the end of a first runthrough is insane after oplaying so many RPGs). The soundtrack is incredible as well, mixing 16 bit tunes with 'real' instruments. Some may find the bullet hell combat to be unfair with cases like the (two of) the final bosses, all you really need is DETERMINATION... and skill.  Overall, Undertale is a above-average game when you've been spoilers (even then I loved playing it it) but if you haven't been, it's a once in a lifetime experience.

I really liked Undertale.  The theming is the strongest part of the game; it explores morality in a way I've never seen in another game.  In most games with moral systems, all you have to do is make key choices-- hit the A button to pick the "good" option and hit the B button to pick the "bad" option.  It doesn't matter what you do at any other time, or if it does it matters very little.
In Undertale, it goes farther than that.  Figuring out the actions you must take to spare a monster's life is more difficult than killing it, and makes the game more difficult as you don't gain XP.  If you decide not to kill anyone at all, the game acknowledges your decision and adjusts accordingly.  Likewise, if you put a lot of effort into massacring everyone, the game will acknowledge this decision as well.  So yeah, you have to constantly put effort into being "good" or "bad", and the changes are drastic if you go down either of those paths.
The other big thing the game has going for it is how charming it is.  The overall story is actually pretty thin, predictable, and feels kind of haphazardly put together at times.  However, the characters and the conversations you have with them are really well done.  Every single character is adorable, bursting with personality, and most importantly is sympathetic in one way or another.  You definitely end up caring about these characters as you play through the game.  The writing style is also very charming, it's funny most of the time and moving at other times.
I wasn't a huge fan of was the actual mechanics of the battles, where you have to dodge bullets.  I think I had trouble because I was playing with my controller.  On some parts it's nearly impossible to do what the game asks of you with a joystick-- basically any part where you have to continually switch back-and-forth between two directions.  Using the d-pad makes it a tiny bit easier, but certain sections I just found I could only do on the keyboard (and generally I'm better with the controller).  MOST of the game is playable, though.
Overall, it's a charming game with lovable characters and a deeper morality system than you would expect.  If you're looking for a game with a lot of heart, try this one.

There are but two games that have made me bawl like a baby, and both for much the same reason.  It's not for spoilerific reasons, so don't worry - simply, I felt bereft when I left these two games, a little hollower for the immediate lack of these people 9the characters) I've been with, in a sense, for all of those hours of gameplay.  I would not feel a sense of having been enriched by the experience until later, once my feelings of having left so fantastic an experience as them had faded ever so slightly.
Those two games are *Skies of Arcadia: Legends* and now there's always going to be an *Undertale*-shaped spot in my heart.  Filled with making me think differently of fighting, appealing to my natural tendacies as a pacifist that no other game has really catered to, at least in an RPG, feeling truly close to characters who are not simply "quirky" but feel more fully fleshed out than any I have ever encountered, and gameplay that is truly worth whatever price they charge for this.  I put a price tag on anything I want in this world, but few things to me seem to defy the idea that everything has a right price and several WRONG prices.  This is one of those rare exceptions - you simply must purchase this, certainly before someone spoils this game much for you.
Go into this game knowing little.  Expect to be sucked in and made to live in these characters' world, to laugh, to cry, to be amazed and to be a little disturbed.
In many ways, this game has the components of the best fairy tale, right down to a human child falling down into a magical world.  Ah, but this world is not all it appears to be, and it tells you that from the outset.    This is a story of so many unravellable threads that you don't quite know which to pull, but when you do, you find that rather than becoming disappointed at what you find, you gain a headier sense of admiration for the thing as a whole even with (mostly) everything laid bare.
I came because of Jimquisition, who said that you could date the hell out of a skeleton in this game.  And, I can assure you, yes, you sure can date the hell out of a skeleton.  Also a fish.

There are very few games that I could play for 50+ hours and enjoy EVERY MINUTE of it.
Undertale is one of those few games.
I never found a dull moment. Sure, some parts were a bit directionless, but there was always something to keep me going, whether it was the genuinely funny humorous moments, the twists and turns of the story, or the deep and interesting characters. Please, for the love of god, if you even plan on playing this game, do NOT spoil it for yourself. Don't look up a guide. Don't let others tell you how you should play it. This is one of the few games I played that weren't spoiled for me prior, and let me tell you that I'm so glad that never happened. The gameplay is simple, with a fun bullet hell style, but the impact it will make on the narrative and story is huge. Without spoiling anything, it has one of the most satisfying endings ever. It doesn't hide the story behind the most obscure secrets, and it has a "True Ending" as well, but you don't have to jump through tedious hoops with an online guide to get it. The game doesn't leave you in the dark. So, play Undertale, don't have it spoiled for you. Half of the entertainment comes from not knowing whats next, and being pleasantly surprised (or shocked) when whatever it is DOES happen.

If you are considering this game for purchase, DO IT and as long as you stay determined to play the game out, you will be greatly rewarded, I promise.

I don't write reviews, mostly as I feel I can never get my point or feeling across properly that and I'm too lazy. However I felt the need to write one for Rust, which I must say is quite the accomplishment. If I could justify recomending it for getting me off my proverbial rear end I would. Sadly though this is not the case. I will start off by saying I know I don't have much in the way of shown hours logged, blame me for doing things like downloading patches to client based steam and non-steam games when I do play rust.
I bought rust back in 2013 I think might have been '14 little fuzzy on that detail. I enjoyed the game quite a bit, minus offline... I wouldn't call them raids more like vandalism. When it came time for the game to be split into legacy and whatever we call the current build I was happy for some of the changes coming. Frankly I was tired of staring at and running about the same map. I welcomed most of the changes that happened after that, one though most of all I despised. That was when I found our character appearence would be locked to our steam id's. I didn't complain at all about it as I figured later on we would get to create our characters eventually. Over time that hope was well frankly stomped on and finally buried with this latest update.
I know Garry runs this game like a little social expieriment seeing what happens when you tweak certain elements. I was okay with that for a while as long as it seemed like it was going to continue to be a game. After all I paid for a game, something to enjoy maybe have a bit of an escape from reality. If I'm going to be participating in an expierment I expect to be compensated for it, not to pay into it. No I'm not saying pay me jsut simply I'm not going to thro money at someone's research that I really have no interest it: especially when I'm one fo the "labrats".
I feel as though I can get into a game more if I make the character I want or if the character has a fairly fleshed out story if I am going to be playing a preditermined character. Rust however takes that away, I am who my steamID makes me. I don't get to choose who or what I am, I am simply thrown into random PC body #4,376,890. I can not connect with that character; I feel unmotived to play him, it just all around saps my enjoyment from the game when I can't play whom I want to.
I simply can not play Rust anymore. As an addtion, the responses to requests to add character creation, gender change or something along those lines by Garry had led me to a conclusion... He's a prat.
I do not support that Gender-Dictatorship!

most negative reviews about borderlands 2 are short, to the point. but some of them played this game for a long time, got into almost all the DLC too, I loved this game, but looking back upon it, what was good, is now sour.
Here is a detailed reason why borderlands 2 is inferior to it's predescessor.
Memes are the most common complaint. Why hound the memes? Memes aren't inherently a bad thing, but they are best when they are homegrown, and are either in-universe-in-jokes among characters or spawned by the players of the games. The memes referenced in borderlands 2 are completely unrelated to the game, are years out-of-fashion by the time they are included, and are senseless throwaway references which are neither a creative shoutout nor are humoring.
A subject that you
not have heard as much in the steam reviews, is the painful, cringeworthy writing that tries to put doses of "reality" in between the cartoony, comical world that you're constantly blowing up. It's not even an ink stain, it's more like your dad dribbled his brown musty dinner gravy all over your comic book page because he wanted to teach you a rambling seinfeldian lesson that you've heard ten thousand times this year in every other facet of life. Scarlet's booty DLC goes completely full throttle with this, and the result is even more painful.
Player characters are awkwardly referred to as "vault hunter," as a replacement for any sort of name or pronoun. Borderlands the First worked around pronoun use by avoiding this kind of writing completely, and it flowed much more smoothly than the sequel. The game's lead antagonist- Handsome Jack had his most fondly remembered lines as improvised lines. Imagine what the character would've been if the default writing was kept in place?
story and gameplay segregation are going full force in this game too, bosses established as major threats become pathetically easy if you've managed to overlevel yourself, major characters die terrible cheap deaths in cutscenes, and the one mission that
game mechanics into the story is a throwaway near-end mission that tastelessly involves suicide.
I will speak nothing of homosexuality, whenever someone talks about that, it turns into a giant political slap-fight.
yes. there are less guns in borderlands 2.
there I said it.
seriously. play a drinking game- take a shot everytime you pick up a duplicate weapon, you will last shorter than you think.
I'm not the first to point this out either-
so anyways, why are there less guns overall?
you know how many gun brands were retooled to have their own quirks and gimmicks? this however, was a case of "one step forward, two steps back" in the department of gun quanity. Why?
and to make matters worse, many gun mods that were common in the first game (the masher revolver for example) became Rare-exclusives for borderlands 2.
finally, three gun brands were removed from the game, only one was replaced, and only a few new additions were made for guns overall.
Math always tells the truth.
TotalBiscuit did a glorious rant on this in regards to the pre-sequel:
I for one would like to extend this- borderlands 2 is an exercise in artificial longevity, whereas the pre-sequel refines artificial longevity.
borderlands the first had an amazing tidbit in its system for rares-
I have yet to see a game that actually implements something like this, what does the sequel do?
* lowers the drop rate by a factor of 10 to increase grind.
* locks certain rares to a specific boss, so you have to waste time walking from the start of the area to the boss itself.
* removes them completely from vending machines.
as bad as that is, what is worse, is the completely busted progression system. your rare gear that you got from the boss, underperforms compared to vendor trash that is two levels higher than it (this game doesn't want you to play favorites with your guns) unlike the first which level-uped the rare guns. character progression is FUBAR as well. Borderlands the first, the general caps for stats existed around the low-mid thousands range. Borderlands 2's progress stays fairly level by the time you reach the end of the main story, but for each successive playthrough, the progression skyrockets to numerical levels more common in something like the Disgaea series. why? to make it feel like there's some semblance of a challenge, even though the AI acts the same and simply kills you vastly faster.
to top all this madness off, the game's busted stat progression makes it's busted gun progression
as you level up!
the story and characters are often the highest praised part of this game- so much that it got a telltale games series. Even in the DLC, the characters are more remembered than anything else.
The grind of borderlands 2, however, makes you play through the story
before you've reached the level cap, its charm becomes meaningless and the game turns into a chore. You've seen it once? Do you like seeing the same jokes two more times?
? heaven forbid you want to play as another character, especially if you don't want to resort to save editing.
if you want to buy it for the story, that's fine, just try and buy it on sale if you do.
