Undertale is a really hard game to explain but I'll do my best...
You know, I came into this game practically by force. All I heard was reviews like "11/10" and friends begging me to play. I tried... I really tried to not blindly fall in since, to be honest, the game didn't seem much more than a passing fad by any quick look a Tumblr, but this game is so much more.  It's remarkable to see a game so comfortable about how it presents it's content and what it teaches, even by indie game standards. It helps the game be really immersive and balance it's vast set of emotions.
The game accomplishes so much in 6-12 hours it's staggering. It's confident in it's capibilities and never bites off more than it can chew. It just wants to be a game and do it's best at being a game. It balances a many unique elements and observations like some ridiculous juggling act, yet still remains humble for the moments where Toby Fox isn't being a massive troll. For time, here is the obligatory list of Undetale's accomplishments:

*It Parodies Normal RPG Behavior
*Has A Compeling, Foreshadowing Narrative
*Holds Entertaining, Deep Characters
*Has One Of The Best Soundtrakcs Of The Decade
*Is Really Freaking Funny
*Has Intresting Gameplay Mechanics
*Contains Memorable Locations & Set Pieces
*Has Unique Events For Every Stupid Little Thing You Do
Even then I haven't quite done it justice, the game is so obviously a labor of love by Toby Fox that it's almost impossible to explain it all to someone who hasn't experienced it. I know it's so easy to see the game as an over-glorified meme-generator. Though, under all of Undertale's fandom and fame, holds an astonishing game that I feel shows what video games can be as a medium. The game has legit given me new faith in the game's industry if a game of this caliber can be made by a team of 1-3 people.

I can't say anything that hasn't already been said about this game. I may be a young man of 20 years of age, but video gaming is my life and it has permanently gotten under my skin (Quite literally. Tattoos are addicting). That being said, this game will easily be one of my favorite games of all time. It has something for everyone.
Want to be reminded of the old retro games of the Rise of The Virtual Gaming Empires such as Nintendo, Atari, and others? Check.
Do you want to meet characters that emote, remember, and feel, just like, and possibly even exceeed the capacity of, actual humans? Check.
Do you want to be a heartless murderer and brutally slay anything that moves? Check.
Do you want to flirt, hug, pet, and fashionista-style pose your way through any and all hostile confrontations? Check.
Do you enjoy hearing childish, slightly immature humor that is constantly breaking the fourth wall in even the most subtle of ways? Check.
Do you want to laugh, freeze up in shock, feel your eyes well up with tears, and become aghast with horror, all in the span of a few hours? Check.
Do you like catchy music that you can't ever get out of your head? Double check.
I don't recommend this game. I don't think you SHOULD buy it. If you ever once referred to yourself as a fan of anything containing the words "video" and "gaming" in the same sentence (and preferably in close proximity to each other), you absolutely NEED this game. I think others have said it best when they say this game, funded off Kickstarter and largely produced by one legendary man (or one legendary dog, depending on who you ask), can easily contend with the big boys, such as the Witcher, Metal Gear Solid, Fallout, etc. for Game of the Year who have easily spent millions and, honestly, hardly hold a candle to a game of this caliber.
I think what speaks the loudest in regards to my opinion of this game is that. in addition to games, I absolutely love music. Who doesn't, right? I find myself whistling the soundtrack to myself at work, and often enough to the point that I'm sure it makes my coworkers want to strangle me. So I decide that, when I get home, I must have the soundtrack on my mobile device. I briefly consider ripping the songs off YouTube. But I can't bring myself to do it. Mr. Toby Fox has earned my admiration. It wouldn't be fair to him. I have the means, but I choose not to use them. I purchase his Soundtrack off Steam. Best $8 I've ever spent.

After pumping 100+ hours into this game, and not really liking the first iteration, I can easily say this is a vast improvement over the first title. Storyline is improved upon, characters are much more memorable, graphically (even with a cell-shaded style) it is greatly improved. Weapon variety is vast, both visually and in the effects they do.
One thing that is over looked a lot with this game is the fact that they have greatly improved it so that if you want to play by yourself, it's just as enjoyable as playing with others. Though you all share look, so you should probably be careful who you play with so you don't lose good guns you may need. However, if you're worried about that, just play by yourself.
As for characters, they all feel different, and have their own lines they say depending on what you do. It makes each feel slightly more diverse, but from a playing standpoint, their powers very in usefulness. The Siren is probably the best to play if you want to play on your own, where the Gunzerker is probably best left for group play.
Over all, this game is a wonderfully fun time if you are a fan of guns, loot, and basically being an all around "badass".
As a side note, of the DLC's, I had the most fun with the Dragon Keep DLC.

Okay. I'm going to say something truly, one percent honest about this game.
I love it completely. I completely recommend this game, espeically to those who enjoy a personal story and feel to their games, akin to Earthbound and such.
BUT.
I fully advise you, so there is not a SHADOW (Hah, Get it?) of a doubt once the game boots up and you fall into the underground. Know to do this.
Separate the fanbase, from the game.
Why do I ask this? Undertale is everywhere now. Shirts, bags, stickers, comic strips, (Insertinvoluntaryshiver) fan fiction. It's to the point where even the best of the tracks start to get annoying after hearing extended verion, after remix, after cover. There is LITTERALLY enough artwork of Undertale (Graphic or not...) to fit into a decent sized GALLERY. It's astonishing how a game made less then half a year ago, as grown into a massive population worldwide, similar to that of, (InsertGulp) Five Night's at Freddys. Talking about the Fanbases, not the actual games.
And those fanbases have a lot more in common then you would think.
Talking so much about a game they might not even played themselfs, just seen Game Grumps, or Markiplier do it. Harassing non-fans or skeptics into playing the game as well, spoiling major parts of a game based around YOUR reactions and feelings towards it, coveting MatPat as a thoeizing god, And let's not forget brashly lashing out at critics, trying to defend their beloved game...Even I have fallen victim to that.
Am I saying all Undertale or even Five Nights' fans are like this? Hell no!
Most of the ones you're gonna meet are (Hopfully) rather amicable and calm. But seeing how this is the internet, you're bound to find at least a few of...THOSE lunatics, browsing along. Just leave them alone, don't even repond to them. Common sense will usually kick in about three or four days after a post. Just know that, the fans aren't Undertale's fault.
A game can change your views upon a topic,Make you feel for fictonal characters, enlighten you on something, or even just keep you entertained. What it can't control, is what you'll do with all that inside your head after you turn it off. Whether you scream, rant, and rave about how your theory are correct and someone else's isn't, or just bringing it up in a friendly conversation with a fellow fan, the game cannot control your actions.
I understand if it's not your kind of game. I understand if you dislike the game. But please, don't lash out in frusration agianst the rabid fans on the game inself. In a vain hope for all the agruements to at least simmer down, I beg all of you, please.

I've played my fair share of Rust, I got the game before the remake that is available now and it's safe to say I've played enough to know what I'm talking about.
In it's core, Rust is a beautiful and solid game with a good dev team who care about it and try to make it better every week with each update. The game mechanics are good if a little unbalanced and "wonky" at times.
But this is where the real ugly comes in. Rust is as you know an early access game and it has been since it's release in almost 2 AND A HALF YEARS AGO! It has been 2 and a half years and the game is still stuck in ALPHA! Here you have a game that has been in an alpha stage of development while at the same time being accessible to the public for 2 and a half years, that is absolutely unacceptable.
This quickly ties in to my second problem with the game, the perfect unbalance of player progression. Rust is survival game in which you start with nothing and need to build your way up, so you'll be spending hours on end gathering resources to make your base and acquire weaponry. But the problem is that there are other players. And this makes for 2 thing:
1-Rust solo is absolutely unplayble as you will definitely run into groups more often than not and lose everything you have, resource gathering will take an obscene amount of time and there is no way you will manage to defend your base properly from, again, groups of players.
2-Rust in it's current state is simply a deathmatch with a survival and crafting gimick implimented.
I have tried several times to get back into Rust and enjoy myself but I just can't seem to be able to anymore.
I definitely don't recommend you buy Rust in it's current state or ever for what it's worth.

After pumping 100+ hours into this game, and not really liking the first iteration, I can easily say this is a vast improvement over the first title. Storyline is improved upon, characters are much more memorable, graphically (even with a cell-shaded style) it is greatly improved. Weapon variety is vast, both visually and in the effects they do.
One thing that is over looked a lot with this game is the fact that they have greatly improved it so that if you want to play by yourself, it's just as enjoyable as playing with others. Though you all share look, so you should probably be careful who you play with so you don't lose good guns you may need. However, if you're worried about that, just play by yourself.
As for characters, they all feel different, and have their own lines they say depending on what you do. It makes each feel slightly more diverse, but from a playing standpoint, their powers very in usefulness. The Siren is probably the best to play if you want to play on your own, where the Gunzerker is probably best left for group play.
Over all, this game is a wonderfully fun time if you are a fan of guns, loot, and basically being an all around "badass".
As a side note, of the DLC's, I had the most fun with the Dragon Keep DLC.

After 1111 hours, if I had to describe this game in two words, they would be "Broken," and "Disappointing."
It boils down to a terrible game engine with little to nothing done to improve it, and thats about it. I'm going to go into detail anyway, because I like to complain.
How many years has it been - about 3, yes? 3 years of development. Sure, the team started out small, and has gone through some changes over the years, but is this really all they have to show? Even when Bohemia took over, things didn't improve. Let me carefully go over all of the things I love and hate about this game, and why I never plan to play it again.
Major Cons:
- Sound.
It's broken.  While playing I am constantly bombarded  with repeating moans, split ammos, eating and drinking noises... oh god make it stop! Gates opening, clips being reloaded, and god knows what else. If anything, sound has gotten worse since the beginning, and now zombies make your ears bleed as they constantly spam random moan clips like they're part of a down-syndrome orgy, even if theres only one zombie. Good.
- Performance.
Yes, I am going to kick THAT dead horse, oh yes. I know it's basically a pile of mush and crumbled bones at this point, but god damn it, I expected some kind of improvement after this long, but if anything the game runs worse. Even on the lowest settings, where everything is basically a brown-green pixeled blur on the screen, the game runs like a man who is coma-stricken, severely asthmatic, and has no legs. The engine acts like an apathetic nurse, occasionally walking up to the man and flipping him over so he doesn't lay in his own feces for an hour.
-  Net-Code/Bullet Detection/What the @(!% is happening?
So I spend hours looting, feeling tense and unsure of my surroundings, adventuring and meeting people, until finally I catch someone from behind, blast them in the head (and see the blood), only to have them spin around and kill me. This happens all the time, and it's because even though I killed him, the server hasn't quite understood that he is dead yet, so despite his screen violently shaking and flashing red because he's technically dead, he will have no problem being temporarily undead and turning to return fire. Great.
- Movement
Holy mother of jesus. If anything exemplifies the fact that this engine sucks, and that it needs to be ripped out and completely redone... it's the movement. How many times do I have to press "V" before I vault over that fence? 2? 4? 6?? Well, sometimes it takes a few presses, and I die because of it. Kind of important to get over objects while being chased.
How about when your legs are broken? Heh, good luck fitting through doors, scrub. Oh, and if you do manage to sqeeze your obese♥♥♥♥♥through a doorframe, you'll have to do a kneel-stand-prone dance on any ledge above 1-inch that leads outside, and sometimes it doesn't even let you out. Hope you weren't being chased.
The half-second of input lag (was this intentional? If so, that is worse) whenever you try to start/stop moving makes you feel like your character is moving through thick mud (although feces would probably make more sense for this analogy). I cannot count the times where the delay between my release of a movement key and my character actually stopping has caused me to go flying off ledges, cliffs, and into the open. I'd call movement 'janky' or 'frustrastingly mind-numbingly bad' but I don't think there are words left to describe how awful it feels.
- Graphics/ability to see what the @($* is going on
This ties into performance, but I felt it needed it's only brief section because of how bad it is. Yes, on the lowest settings this game looks like garbage - we all know that. However, looking like garbage wouldn't be an issue if I could actually see enemies within 300 meters, but I can't. The settings are so♥♥♥♥♥♥that I can't see through windows, I can't see people, and I can hardly move around unless I'm in the middle of nowhere with no buildings around whatsoever. If you want to have a fight in the city, have fun - just make sure you have one of the NASA computers.♥♥♥♥♥♥
"Minor" Cons
- Broken Zombie AI (they are braindead, and still walk through walls)
- Weapons drop to ground even when you have bag space
- Bag space often glitches and requires relog
- After cutting down a tree a stick is put onto your back (what level of insanity is this?)
- Hands often glitch and can't be used to hold anything, requiring relog
- Bouncing off things at a great height and not dying (yet falling 4 feet can kill you)
- Horrible hit-detection with melee attacks
- Severe shaking when cold, but nothing to indicate level of cold - no way to effect temperature (other than fire and sort of heat packs?)
- "Default" button in settings is too easy to hit. Remove this from the god damn game. I spent hours getting things just right to accidentally hit this thing.
- Loot spawning is broken - buildings with dozens of coats while other buildings have nothing. Delete old loot, useless loot, and repopulate loot please. Nothing useful is up north anymore, at least nothing I can't just get south. This is silly.
- Drinking from well/pond. Let me drink until I want to cancel, or until I vomit. Don't make me spam "drink" over and over or wait five days to take one sip. I got♥♥♥♥♥♥to do, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.

Major Pros
- Adventure/tension
I like the adventure and tension... but only when the game isn't lagging, and when the server is responding... and when the admins won't just kick you for killing them. Huh, maybe adventure isn't so great.
- Meeting People
I like talking to people and wondering if they're going to stab me in the back or not, but nowadays I've given up on it. It's a risky thing to do, and after so many wasted hours, I don't want to waste 5 more just to be backstabbed by a 'friendly' guy. And that's why I never meet anyone anymore, or if I do it's at the end of their gun, pointing at my nose as it blasts hot lead through my brain until I am no more than a bloody puddle on the road.
Other Pros
- ???
So yeah, don't buy this. After 3 years the game has added a few articles of clothing, guns, and trucks - nothing more than a tiny strip of cloth acting as a "bandage" being applied to the long-since dead corpse that this game is. I became addicted to the adventure and tension early on, and I suckered myself into thinking the game would improve. It did not.
I am ashamed to have bought this now, and as I look back all I can do is shake my head in despair, wondering why things haven't changed. Well, the price changed. The price went up. Fancy that.
I wanted to make some great analogy about how Dayz is a skeleton and how terribly empty it is, but instead I'll just say the game is♥♥♥♥♥♥and always has been. I see no future in it, and neither should any of you.
Good day sirs.

There are very few games I can genuinely say I have felt a real connection toward its characters. In fact I can only say that's happened to me with only two or three characters. Characters like Chloe from Life is Strange, or Lee from TTG's The Walking Dead Season 1. However, I have to admit, never once have I ever felt that these characters have felt more like a genuine family member to me then any of the characters here in Undertale. Rather it's Toriel as my mother, or Asriel as my little brother, Sans as my cool uncle, or Papyrus as my UNcool uncle who's so uncool that he's actually super cool. I love these characters, I want them to succeed, I don't just feel bad for them, or sympathize with them, I feel happy when they are happy as well, and when they are sad, so am I. This became most apparent when I had fought Asriel at the end of the True Pasficet ending, as I SAVED him, and as began to scream and cry, begging for me to stop and let him win, I started to cry with him. After the fight, and it asked me if would forgive him, or not I did so without second thought. Then when the game asked me to comfort him, again I lost it, I wept several manly tears (okay maybe not very manly). Never before have I felt so attached to any characters in any work of fiction. I have never felt that I could relate, so closely then I have with this game. Toby Fox, if you actually read these (which is unlikely) Then I want to thank you personally, from the bottom of my heart, for making characters that I have come to love, so much.

If you are a highly competitive gamer, or very distastefull of 'immaturity' in your entertainment you probably wont get much out of Undertale.  I personally didnt have any problems with the gameplay or the humor, but even people who liked the game should be able to admit that the combat and puzzles alone arent enough to entertain.
Undertale has "8 bit" graphics and music. I cared about neither, but some people really dislike them.
If, however, you do not fit into the above categories, I recommend trying Undertale. Even where it fails, it fails attempting to do something interesting, which is more interesting than a lot of other games.  At 10 dollars, I dont think thats a huge risk.

(Probable spoilers below - it's hard not to with a game of this type. But I'll try not to)
So I've done 2 and a half playthroughs... my thoughts on each of them are below:
First playthrough (played like a normal RPG):
Up until the ending, I was pretty much "meh". Standard RPG fare, some good writing, some funny jokes and an unusual combat system. But, nothing special.
However, the ending is amazing.
Second playthrough (played using the unique "no fighting" combat system:
Not that much changed. It was harder, and some of the story changed, but it wasn't quite what I'd been led to believe. Still, it was good. I was more impressed with the attention to detail, than anything.
Third playthrough (played using a kill everything that moves, strategy):
This is the playthrough that, up until a certain point, was the most enjoyable. However, it gets to be, completely out of nowhere, probably the hardest game I've ever played. And there isn't a damn thing you can do about it. Reading forums, reviews and so on, it's caused a LOT of people to just give up on the game. And, sadly, I'm part of that group, because - and I'm not ashamed - I don't have the reactions required to complete it.
So, because of the game roadblocking you out of some of the content unless you have god-like reflexes, I can't recommend it... it really is a shame, because up until this point, it's been really good. But I can't tell people to buy a game that's just beyond difficult to complete.

Hello fellow steam users how are you doing today? I suppose you got to this review because you are deciding whether or not to buy undertale. The short answer is yes. It is a very good game if you like rpgs, or world exploration.
Gameplay: The fights can be described as a turnbased bullethell. If you are looking for a challanging bullethell like touhou then the combat is not for you, but if you are looking for a moderately challenging bullethell then the combat will apeal to you. I would rate the combat 7/10
Music: The music to this game is incredibly good. Even if you don't want to buy the game you should go listen to the soundtrack somewhere else, however the music matches the tone of each room incredibly well and really adds to the emotion of the events. So if you really want to get the full value out of the soundtrack you should play the game. I would rate the music 9.5/10
Story: The story is executed incredibly well. You truly feel the impact of the decisions you make in this world when playing. If you beat the game and decide to do another run the game changes based on your previous file. The changes may not be significant, but you definitely can feel it if you pay attention. I would rate the story 9/10
Characters: The characters in this game feel emotional. When you kill an enemy in battle, you feel the impact of killing them. The main characters in this game have personality and emotion that make it very easy to get invested into them. Even the generic NPC's add a lot to the game (especially the shopkeepers).  You can understand the wishes, and desires of every single enemy you fight, including the bosses you face. I would rate the characters 9.5/10
Overall this is a great game. It is emotionally griping at every corner, and that really imerses you into the world. My biggest complaint of this game is that it is pretty short. If you take your time and explore everything you should beat the game in around 10 hours. But at the same time the shortness of the game also adds to it for reasons I can't explain. This game is a wonderful adventure for any age and easily deserves a 9.5/10.

TL;DR:it's a great game, but it makes you do all the interesting stuff to get the good ending. so, after 2-3 playthroughs, you have gone through all the content the game offers.
Undertale is a mix of RPG and a bullet hell. the premise of the game is very simple: don't kill anyone. the game states it numerous times (although indirectly), and it's very clear when the consequences for your actions come to bite you back. the game is pretty short, I got 3 playthroughs in my 14 hours, and imo it's worth the 10€ price. tha being said, I don't see much replay value in the game. all the optional sidequests are mandatory to get the good ending, and they give you the best weapon in the game right before the final boss, no questions asked.
will you like the game? in the end, it boils down to preference. the RPG element is very, very insubstantial: you have two stats, attack and defense, and they are meaningless since you don't want to get hit and you don't want to attack anyone, except the final boss. so if you don't like bullet hell games, this game isn't for you. the characters are good, and they have some depth into them, but it might seem shallow if you are used to RPGs of bigger scales.

A must have game:
From first impressions, I wasn't so sure I would be interested in getting Undertale, some friends had told me about it and were trying to get me to buy it as they really enojyed it, I looked further in to it only to find myself buying the game, I barely touched it for the first couple of weeks when I owned it, but then came back to it. I became so absorbed into the game and ended up completing the Neutral and Pacifist run, however, I cannot bring myself to do a genocide run to comeplete the game, the reason for this is because I have grown to attached to the characters that I wasn't going to be able to see them die.
Undertale, while it's visual are simplistic. was great fun to play. The humour was definately relatable as well as the characters being genuinly enjoyable to "watch".
The soundtrack in this game is unbelievably amazing, I listen to most of the songs almost everyday and am still yet to find them even slightly tedious.
The combat in this game is simple yet almost unique to many other RPGs and has nice little elements to the attacks that the enemies dish out.
The greatest factor of all, you don't have to grind! The first 2 runs you do (If you play them in the right order) won't require any grinding at all otherwise you're playing it wrong, then when it comes to the fiendishly horrible task of completing a genocide run (Not because it's bad, but because it's sad) the game will simply give you enough exp to be at a good enough level to progress.
The story of it all is without a doubt the most important part of the game, it's what keeps it together, the foundation of it all, the simplicity is then ruled out by the complexity of the story and largely impactful secrets it holds. It may not seem like much, but this game has a lot more to offer than most AAA titles in 2015 and ones in 2016 as well.
I may have missed some stuff out but I can't spoil everything without people having a chance to have their own views on the game but I had to leave a review to credit the creator(s) just to make sure they know that this game was beyond a success. I would certainly recommend buying this game if you haven't already and give it a good try.

This game is amazing!, I have a few points to discuss.
Pros:
1. Game is very fun and requires time to gain and or regain skill, causing you to actually play the game a while before becoming a "Pro".
2. Pvp is mostly balanced, and if we complain about a problem, the devs will not ignore you, they will do what they can to fix the problem.
3. The Rust community produces more memes than ♥♥♥♥♥, IFunny, and Tumblr all combined. The communtiy is mostly amazing, nice, and not too shabby.
4. Forced wipes are a common theme in this game, where the devs force all servers to wipe their map, so if you start late, you can just mess around until the new wipe is scheduled.
Cons:
1. People with Assault Rifles, and many other weapons WILL kill you, no matter what you have, or what you are doing.
2.Raiding is sometimes unbalanced due to the building cabinet system.
3. Finding blueprints is too hard to do against people that have aroung 15-30 people in their team, causing you to be left with nothing, or being killed and losing you items. (This problem is either already fixed, or is going to be with the new XP system, I can't wait!)

This game is what most games have forgotten what games are made for: just to have fun and have a good time. It is not like "kill all the monster and get bonus levels" or "collect all the items and do all the side quests". It is really absolutely just to have a very good time. It is funny, it es emotional, it just entertains the player. But it is very deep and philosophic, too. As I played it, I did not have the thought "I have to play it, because I want more EXP or kill more enemies" I played it, beacuse I really wanted to know, what comes next, what the story is and just for fun. This game made me laugh more than all the other video games together I played before. It really gives you just a good feeling. And it's RPG-elements are SO MUCH better than those of big-budget-RPGs like Dragon Age. Really, in Undertale, you have the feeling that the NPCs actually live, and have their own thoughts and emotions, and that they are REAL and not just NPCs. This game made me survive a really hard time and helped me literally to start laughing again and love something and really get emotional. Thank you for this. This is more, than a game, this is really a piece of Art. Go and play it, really.
What I want to mention especially is, that all the characters are nice, what gives the game this wonderful atmosphere. No one says something bad about the other, and when you as the player get judged, than only by your actions.  It is the game, where I, personally, like every single NPC. And I think, the gerat NPCs are one of the reasons for it's absolutely wonderful atmosphere. Go and play it.
And the soundtrack is just wow. It is literally just wow. One of the best Soundtracks I've ever heard.

In Undertale, you fall down a hole and end up in a world of monsters. The story of Undertale may seem like a generic RPG plot, and it sort of is, but the core mechanic of being a nice person and not killing everything was a fresh take on the RPG genre for most people. And the whole idea that the game remembers everything is probably my favourite part of this game.
So, you may be wondering why I'm praising the game if I'm not recomending it. Well...
The biggest problem with Undertale is the community. Yes I know, every community has its weird side, but Undertale's is very large. There's also the fact that if you played it now, you would have every aspect of the game ruined for you. People would tell you what to do, who to spare. Just look at Markiplier's playthrough.
So if you were to play this game today, chances are, someone will spoil or has already spoiled a key part of what made Undertale great for me. You can get it if you want, but you won't experience it the way Toby Fox wanted you to.

Borderlands 2...impossible to be within 20ft of a gaming system or PC without hearing that name much like Call of Duty (CoD). Considering the hype this title got along with the raving reviews from critics, it'd be easy to assume Gearbox Software made a game that is Mario, Sonic, Micky Mouse, and Chuck Norris all rolled into one, epic, mind-blowing adventure of endless possibilities. What have the critics been saying? Things like "The grand loot-filled adventure you've been waiting for!" "...it's a no brainer." "...brilliant..." and then some odd ones that have nothing to do with the review of a game like "Claptrap made himself a mohawk! He's now my favorite robot!" "It runs well on PC." Now, these aren't just statements made about the game. They are the "quotation" of the whole review. Try it again like this: Why should I play Borderlands 2? "Because it runs well on pc and there's a robot with a mohawk in it."
Most of all, they say the game is funny beyond anything you've ever heard before. It's touted as BL2's main selling point and bragging right. I don't know where I can put that section, so let's start with it.
Humor 0/10
Like I said before, this game's humor is about as funny as your manager making jokes about cut-in-pay. Only very rarely did I find something funny. "Hey, he said♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ I LAFF ERRY TIM xD LOL!" is about 70% of the jokes. Ever been to a lunch table at middle school? Ever played 2 mintues of League of Legends? Then you've been playing Borderlands 2 before it was cool, baby! The rest of the humor is "Look, I'm torturing someone with fire and electricity! Isn't that funny?" What doesn't help is the NPC's have way, way, WAY, WAY too much dialogue that's pointless. I went 10 minutes into the game before I muted voices in the options menu and in my opinion, if I mute something in a game that quickly, the developers have failed to create something good. Further, the NPC's either try to be funny and aren't, or talk in circles, saying nothing. Try to run away from the chatty NPC? That's ok, they know your radio codes. Don't forget the flirtatious 50 yr old woman who names her gun "the vibrator" - no "M rated" video game humor is complete without that. Isn't that right,
Duke Nukem: Forever? (also made by Gearbox) The whole thing just SCREAMS "I was written by a horny 13 year old who knows better than my parents."
Plot 2/10
You're a mercenary in a world with no law go kill everything 'cuz I said so the end see ya' next sequel. Seriously? Who wrote this plot? Capcom? BL2's story is so bad, I'm tempted to make it my new standard of story-writing failure. Worse yet: BL2 is MARKETED as a role-playing game. When you "play a role", you have to have a large affect on the game's plot via either decision making, or your progress changes something. Neither happen. A radio chimes in and says "Good, now kill the next guy. I'll contact you with my next♥♥♥♥♥♥♥torture joke in 2 hrs. Until then, kill everything for the next 10 miles." Then the ending...my god, the ending...it lasts about 10 seconds and only implies "Thx for $ c u nex gam :D" The only interesting part of the game is quite shamelessly ripped off of World of Warcraft. I won't spoil it, but look up "Warcraft Dalaran" in Google. The final boss fight couldn't be more cliche and couldnt be more anti-climactic. They didn't even put up a decent effort in naming it. They lazily just plopped "The Warrior" on him. "Warrior" wasn't very significant, but THE Warrior? Now we're talkin'! Bad name? "The" has got yo' back! Admittedly, near the end, 2 of the characters have a very emotional discussion, and it gets the player into it, but that's it. Also, why are you introduced to Sir Hammerlock, then never see or hear from him again? Guess Gearbox found out he was a bad idea too little too late.
Grahpics 10/10
As much as I don't like this game, I have to grit my teeth and admit: the graphics are very, very good. Anyone that knows me knows that I roll my eyes at the sight of cell-shade. BL2 might have changed my mind by showing off what cell-shade can really do. It gives the game it's animated, cartoony appearance while still making the enviornments rather sightly. The guns (another of BL2's boasts) look great and character models look great save one exception. The new "soldier" class looks inconsistently handsome and realistic compared to his goofy, more animated teammates. The fighting zones are well varied and take you to a new, refreshing location often; which is a HUGE improvement from BL1 where everything was a brown-colored wash-out. A wide variety of enviornments and color pallettes keep things visually entertaining at all times. Aside from some nit-picking, I have no quarrel with this game's visuals.
Gameplay: 5/10
Everyone brags on BL2's humor and coop, but never praise its gameplay *hint hint*. You place the crosshair on your target, hold both triggers/mouse buttons, use special ability, rinse and repeat (maybe some hopping here and some back-peddling there). Honestly, it's not that "bad" its just meh; average. It's an average game with many questionable designs. In the end game, you wear the best shield in the game that gives you the most hp/hp regen, but you die in 2 hits anyway. That's like giving the player a bullet-proof vest but there's a bomb on it. What's the point in upgrading your shield at that level? Co-op? You'll forget you even have teammates until you die. There's no teamwork outside of "focus fire". Dying in single player during a boss resets the boss, but in co-op, you just respawn at the cost of some useless currency. Co-op bosses: no challenge. Single player bosses: too frustrating. There's a "second wind" mechanic where killing an enemy while "dying" brings you back, but enemies have too much health, and generally run away from you when you go down anyway. Sounds like the only way to win is...$$$. The DLC missions are also an abomination of game design not just in gameplay, but in bad marketing. C'mon, day 1 DLC with the best solo-play merc sold separatly? All in all, I did somewhat enjoy my time playing, but all these unecessary issues were an un-ignorable burden on an already uphill climb.
And what is this game's OBSESSION with the All-Seeing Eye? It's not just common, IT'S FREAKIN' ALL OVER THIS GAME! It got tiresome seeing that stupid eye everywhere as well as the satillite looking like a constant "eye". "Hey, this eye concept is neat. LET'S PUT IT ON E.V.E.R.Y.T.H.I.N.G."
No, serious. Count how many times you see an "eye" in this game. Gearbox is also OBSESSED with torture. You can safely rename this game "Mediocre Gear-Check Treadmill in Eyeball and Torture Lands 2".
Sound 5/10
Once again, not impressive. Some of the actors do a decent job, and one of them almost saved the whole bad story for me. An example of bad casting is the new soldier class. The same guy played the War-Mage Apprentice in "Orcs must Die!" performs for him. His voice is way too silly to fit the serious character he was chosen to play. The guns sound fine, explosions work, pew pew of lasers, not much to complain about there, but the music and most of the actors are just annoying. I muted the music and voices after a while. I couldn't stand it anymore. Some of the music is just unbearable and repetitive.
The Verdict
BL2 is an average game with a few thrills and some passable gameplay/co-op. It's far from the worst game ever, but it is NO. WHERE. NEAR. the hype it is getting. SP is too frustrating, co-op is casualized by removing any chance of failure, reducing boss fights to just "waiting for his health timer to tick", poor story, super lame humor, non-existant ending, and NPC's that are annoying as hell! If you find it for about $5, you can buy it, play it for a day or 2, then dump it. Not recommened, don't buy at full price, don't buy into the hype. Final score: 5/10. Average game.

I don't write many reviews, so I'll try to keep this brief.  Do you like games with a strong narrative?  Do you like games that make the player's choices feel impaxtful to the world around them?  Do you tend to project yourself onto your player character, even if they're expressionless, leading to you feeling personally responsible for many of their decisions?  This game is for you if you answered yes to those questions.
To say that Undertale is an amazing game is a bit of a misnomer.  As a game, Undertale is pretty basic, somewhat half♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and not all that innovative.  Bullet hell + rpg = combat system.  But as an experience, I haven't felt so impacted by a game in a very long time.
Also, if you've been convinced to play this game, do so alone.  Absolutely alone.  No guides, no friends.  After you're familiar with the game, sure.  The experience is very strong alone.  It's strong in groups too, but less so in my opinion.

1) Interesting enemy AI--besides being harder to shoot, some bandit designs subvert player expectations.  For instance, the Goliath flies into a berserker rage when you shoot it in the head, regaining its health and leveling up every time it kills another creature.
2) Guns feel better balanced overall, and the power curve is less easily skewed by certain key stats.
3) Character skill trees introduce several one-point skills, reducing the leveling down-time between interesting build changes.

2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

It's a pretty good experimental RPG.
Combat is simple, but each monster encounter is dynamic due to the neat, RNG-free battle mechanics. Enemies can be dispatched with a timing based attack system or dissauded from fighting via simple dialogue puzzles. Either way, you'll be given the opportunity to avoid their attacks with bullet hell-esque minigames unique to each enemy.
Puzzles are frequent, but nothing really threatens to roadblock the average player. If anything, it's a pacing mechanic to help off set the sometimes dialogue heavy nature of the characters. You can always destroy anyone who gets on your nerves, if your willing to face some consequences.
For the most part, the story is pretty cutesy and zany for those who roll with it, but the spoil-sports and NPC killers will quickly find the game taking on a
dark and cynical tone should they start causing too much havoc. More sentimental players will no doubt find themselves wrapped up in the coziness of peaceful playthroughs, but the game has its share of challenges either way.
Expect a rather personal experience, but not one that will last longer than five to eight hours.

The jump between Saints Row 2 and Saints Row: The Third is a sharp, almost jarring experience, but immensely rewarding.  The developers took to heart what made them different from the rest of the genre, and focused, expanded, and magnified those qualities a hundred fold to present the Saints Row we have today.
I feel that change is a perfect analogy for the difference between Borderlands and Borderlands 2.  Gearbox accepted the key things that made Borderlands stand out among the FPS genre (its multitude of guns, unique artstyle, unique brand of humor, etc), and expounded on those exponentially.  Borderlands 2 has more crazy guns, more off-the-cuff humor, more unbelievable characters, and more "fun-per-shot" than its predecesor.  Or, really, any other FPS RPG I've ever played!
Vastly improved over its predecessor are the unique traits of the guns.  You can have a variety of quirks to each weapon, such as burst fire while zoomed, multiple shots fired at a time, shotguns that fire explosive rounds, and even shotguns that hurl elemental globs of hurt, to ensure that every weapon has its own unique personality.  Much in the same vein, the abilities that each character has are much more destinct and satisfying to use, ensuring that every time you hit your ability button, you're in for a satisfying experience.
What I was surprised to find under my game of carefree explosions and chaos , however, was a surprisingly detailed and fleshed out story.  It kind of took me by surprise when I picked up an optional ECHO device and heard the origin story for the character's Siren, Maya.  Gearbox's story was lovingly crafted, I felt, and there is a significant amount of emotion within, with some elements that were entirely expected, and some that most certainly were not.  This made the experience all the more interesting and exciting, in my eyes, as I was more easily invested and driven to continue to see what would happen next.  And because of this, it made the final boss encounter immensely satisfying.
Of course, it doesn't stop after the final boss dies.  The replay value for Borderlands 2 ensures it has quite a bit of longeviety.  "True Vault Hunter mode" lets you play a New Game+, which ensures that the game is more difficult, but all the more rewarding with new guns and upgrades.  And, should you hit level 50 and decide you need more, the DLC packs will grant you "Ultimate True Vault Hunter Mode" and allow you to reach level 61 with MORE bad guys, MORE guns, and MORE loot to collect.
In summary, I wasn't expecting much from Borderlands 2, as its predecessor started to feel bland and repetitive towards the end of the campaign.  I was completely blown away by this gameplay experience, however, and I cannot wait to go through it again (and again!) and really truly explore every nook and cranny around Pandora to uncover what other secrets may lie within.
Game comes HIGHLY recommended.

While many probably don't realize it, this is in fact an action RPG at a mechanics level basing damage, loot, equipment, etc. off of your character's stats and level. This and the insane, yet darkly humorous story will draw you in. I highly recommend not passing this up as I initially did purely for the odd art style. You can edit the black lines out with some simple text file changes. There is also freeware that can give you a third-person view if you're like me and can't stand FPS (which in this game really seems odd given the huge focus on showing off unlockable skins).
Hilarious and wortwhile game with some of the best Co-op play to date. Completely deserving of the game of the year awards for taking non-standard shooter and adding a very engaging story. Within minutes of meeting Claptrap you'll be hooked.
My only complaint is the level gap in this game is insane and if you frequently play with other friends you will at some points find yourself completely under-leveled and unable to keep up. This is in sharp contrast to better thought out leveling such as in Blizzard RPGs. The online is also extremely taxing and should not even be attempted if you do not have a strong internet connection and powerful rig. With this I'd recommend purchasing the game on sale for 20 or less as I did.
The GoY pack is completely worth it and the DLC is (unlike most other games) better than the main game and I cannot recommend it enough. If the GoY is ever on sale I'd recommend grabbing it right away.
I have sunk plenty of time into just the main story, and am getting back into the DLC now. 9/10, one of the best games I've played in a while.

1) Interesting enemy AI--besides being harder to shoot, some bandit designs subvert player expectations.  For instance, the Goliath flies into a berserker rage when you shoot it in the head, regaining its health and leveling up every time it kills another creature.
2) Guns feel better balanced overall, and the power curve is less easily skewed by certain key stats.
3) Character skill trees introduce several one-point skills, reducing the leveling down-time between interesting build changes.

I got this game because I've seen it around for a while now and wanted something I could play with my friends that has better graphics than something like minecraft. I watched some youtube videos on it that showed the "leveling up" process, how basic gear leads to better and better stuff etc.
But there was no mention of how inaccessible mid to late game is to newcomers.
I spent 13 hours on this game and I have absolutely nothing to show for it. As soon as you get away from the starting area and move inland you're immediately shot by someone with full body armor and assault rifles (while I'm naked and have maybe crafted basic tools at this point)
There's simply no fun in this game. You run around, crouch, and hide in bushes while trying to gather supplies, completely paranoid that you might get killed by fully geared players who have nothing better to do.
I assume this is a major reason for the biweekly server wipes, since without this the players who are already fully advanced will simply shut down anyone who didnt start playing this game early on.
Aside from the massive amount of bugs (e.g. animals run in small circles until hunted, then escape clipping through stones and buildings, this game has been out for almost 3 years?), there's no worse feeling than finally starting to build your fort and being killed and looted before you have your 4 walls up. I think the problem is not just a toxic community, but also that the goal of Rust changes from a potentially great Minecrafty survival/crafting game to a mediocre, onesided FPS.
I've never written a review before, but with these 13 hours of utter frustration I can't recommend this game in its current state, and will not be playing it anymore.
Occasional FPS Drops and no Singleplayer option. However, you can join an empty server so that can be worked around.

I have been meaning to write this review for some time, however I honestly don't know where to start but here it goes...
When I first saw Dayz I recognised the potential it could have had, I invested my money in the development of this game and hoped that my money was being put to good use. Because lets face it, that's what we are, investors in early access games providing funds, testing and feedback.
I have sat n thought about what i really enjoyed about the game, trying not to display only the negatives. I will admit I am having a little trouble.
Dayz, at first, was fun and something a little different. It had a large map to explore, and it is huge. The survival aspect was good. I enjoyed having to try to survive in a harsh world where things are scarce, but not so scarce you die within 10 minutes from lack of food. There was plenty interaction with other players...which usually ended in death but one could hope you met a friendly player or group to make your day a little brighter.
This soon wore thin.
The community became worse and you can guarentee almost every player you come across will shoot you on sight.
The forums are not very welcoming either if you have an even slightly negative thing to say about Dayz.
The controls are terrible. You have to spam buttons just to hop over a fence or draw your weapon, which is not good in a situation which calls for quick reactions.
Yes, the map is big, but without vehicles, you are forced to run for hours to get anywhere and to find your friends if you have died. Usually, you die of starvation before you reach them as there seems to be a problem with loot spawning in specific areas and no where else.
Also there is no feeling of an apocalypse. More like the residents got bored n decided to up sticks n move somewhere else.
The zombies...oh my... at first they weren't too bad. I understand yes they are 'placeholders'. They ran through walls and doors, they managed to hit you from quite a distance, they weren't too bad to kill, you could run in circles or you could kill them with an axe to the head.
As time has gone by and they have tried to improve the zombies, they appear to have gotten worse. They spawn randomly and right next to where you are standing, they're almost impossible to kill. The damage they do is huge! they often kill you in a couple of hits and if they don't, they will ruin every single item on you regardless if its in a bag or protected in a box. The last time I played, they had removed the zombies from the map.
The general content of the game consists of guns. Guns, guns and more GUNS! It's slowly morphing into a military simulator. Yes, they have alot of content, but most of it's garbage. Right now, content is not what this game needs.
They have tried to add the ability to throw objects. Removed from the game at this time. Apparently they added wildlife and animals, I have seen 1 cow..1 cow in all my hours of running the map. Then they were removed and more guns added! Don't get me wrong, I love guns, but c'mon! really?! Apparently there is also persistance...NEXT..
The core mechanics of this game are terrible. This is what they really should be focusing on, not hoards of content and guns. Focus on the core architecture and mechanics of the game. Get this right and the rest will flow. You need a good solid foundation before you build a house.
Dayz is like building a mansion on quicksand.
There is no hope for this game. The updates are erratic and usually broken. This game has not progressed in a long long time.  I feel that the developers are playing everyone for a fool. Taking your hard earned money and snorting it up their noses because it's clear that Dayz has seen NONE of that cash.
How many millions of copies sold and money made, yet they still only have a team of 20 from Bratislava.
Don't waste your time or money.

So you know its a crafting survival game made by the vetrans at facepunch.
The general gist is you scavenge materials and blueprints which enable you to craft higher tier items and weapons.
In this game you will want to make friends to play with, as playing alone is a pretty hardcore life.
Your first 20 or so hours will be a steep learning curve, when to fight, when to run and where to build and especially where not to build.
Like all online games you will encounter hordes of asshats, but dont be put off. When playing with friends or teaming up with other randoms you will have a lot of fun.
Make sure you play on a wide range of servers with a good low ping, some servers can be toxic for a round until they are wiped. Some modded servers make the game a bit too hectic for new players and will frustrate you.
Things to know,
The game is updated almost every week.
Most servers wipe after 1 month, removing all buildings, items and things you have learned.
The game will change as updates happen so be prepared to switch your play style. e.g blueprints are going to be removed at some point in favour of an experience system, which will benefit players who can spend hours in the game. ( so kids with no jobs may well be running round with C4 before you can craft anything worth while)
Devs take the communities gripes into consideration and do make changes in a timely manner.
IMPORTANT
There are still rampant bugs that persist, EAC issues, start up crashes and hackers.
Some people who buy this may not be able to play due to these issues.
The game is in alpha and you ARE taking a risk when buying it, if this makes you feel uncomfortable then do not buy it.
This game does not support WINDOWS VISTA and most probibly will not in the future.
Make sure you are certain your machine will run this game above min spec's, it is in alpha and by the time its finnished there is a fair chance those min specs will become higher.

This is my honest opinion of the game, provided it changed dramatically through its course of development, from before its release, and up to this point.
I had been following Rocket's (Dean Hall - DayZ Lead) devblogs and reddit posts religiously since the Standalone's announcement, and the consistent delays and lack of transparency from the devs, which managed to lose the support of some of the community, seemed to only get me more excited for the game's release ('Just wait and see, they'll prove you wrong!' yada yada).
I started playing maybe a week into the launch, and I thought, 'eh.. it's buggy as ♥♥♥♥, runs terribly (averaging 20 FPS in cities, 50-60 FPS in the wilderness - On a decent computer running an SSD might I add) but I felt I could see solid groundwork, in the way they'd 'rebuilt' the engine, the loot system, inventory layout, and even the health system, as buggy as these and many other elements were, I saw (again, maybe a misguided sense of) potential, I was seriously hopeful about the development of this game. After a few weeks of course I got sick of it given the lagginess, both frame-rate wise and network wise, despite the apparent year of development before release that had gone into these two vital elements of the game (shoot me, I'm an optimist).
And so I went back to playing the mod: Epoch, Overpoch, etc. And that very reason is why the Standalone went down the toilet for me, it offered nothing new, maybe it projected some superficial differences and made up with its shortcomings in broken promises, but at the time it was, and to this day still is an inferior version of something we'd had for a good 2 years now, maybe I hadn't known it then, but it was the truth. I started out playing the mod, and it gave me some of the greatest memories in gaming I've ever had, memories I'll keep for a long time, because what the game had in it's early stages was, in which I can best describe is an enigmatic atmosphere, in having no idea what the hell to do, where to go and with nothing to guide or help you through a harsh and chaotic landscape. That sense of helplessness and fear of the unknown made for an incredibly immersive and addictive experience, (And that's where I can see why other survival games couldn't ever convey that same amount of loyalty and enthusiasm in a community) and I understand bringing this up isn't helping anyone, because I don't think there'd ever be a way of getting that feeling back, But I can still enjoy the mod without that feeling for sure (Though I can still get hints of it in certain moments - High pressure situations, finding rare loot, helicopters, firefights etc.), it's still a solid experience, a rugged one than what the Standalone promised, sure, but it worked, and where the Standalone sought to clean up its issues, recreating a platform for a more solid experience, I thought it'd be fantastic, but fundamentally, what the Standalone needed to survive in my eyes, was to do something different, to make the game fresh again, but most importantly, make something substantial and solid for the community to build upon.
Fast forward from launch about 1 1/2 years, since that time I'd come back to the game briefly every few months, and with the lack of any change in those core elements, I slowly lost hope in the game, but the downfall of this project didn't exactly dawn on me until fairly recently, when I realised how long it had been since this game had been released, and how little they'd done aside from add a few more items, a couple more towns and a truck.
I understand now that this game was just a money-grab essentially, and I think I'd known it for a long time, I remember when this was a humble passion project kept together by a small team, but it looks like the vision had been lost somewhere in the middle, whether that be Bohemia's takeover of the development, or the money, I chose not to believe any of it, I jumped on that hype-train and look where its brought us, to one of the biggest let downs in gaming, for me of course, some people wised up and jumped ship a long time ago, and ironically some people even love it, so what do I know.
EDIT
- 9 months on from my original review, I'd all but completely forgotten about this game.
I was spurred on by simple curiosity when a friend told me of an alleged 'lag fix' update, 'promising' (I use that word lightly whenever DayZ is the project in question) in a much needed Direct X 11 renderer port.
This would supposedly allow for dynamic weather events, enable stunning fidelity in the lighting and postprocessing effects, and most vitally, solve (or at least remedy) the infamous frame rate issues plaguing the game. These frame drops -primarily affecting large cities with complex assets- were always something I could never get past, and tainted the game for me, especially when the cities were the sorts of areas new players typically gravitated to; which surely wouldn't be giving them a great first impression if their first firefight appears to be taking place in a slideshow.
I've racked up about 50 more hours from playing with friends over the past couple months so I feel I'm right in making this point;
Too little, too late.
I sound somewhat egomaniacal in saying this, as I'm sure I don't even represent the majority of people who played this game, but over the course of this game's development, with the change in leadership, and with the disappointing amount of progress along the years, at least for me, the game hasn't changed at all.
A point could have been made at most a year into release that with the stream of minor content updates, while making no change to the core of the game (which was so desperately needed) were simply put in to keep the community at bay, while they slave away at the groundbreaking material.
It's coming up to 2 and a half years since the Standalone was released, yet still no groundbreaking material.
And I suppose, contrary to the message of this review, even after all this time, I'll keep an eye out for this next update over the coming weeks, just to see if I can get my money's worth.

The story in Undertale is hailed for a reason. I was sucked into it immediately with the (tu)Toriel arc in the Ruins and that emotional ride holds onto you the whole way through, no matter what route you're taking. The most notable gimick of Undertale being it's morality system, and the fact that anything you do, good or evil, will never be forgotten, even through your second and third playthroughs. All of the choices you make, you're forced to live with and that's rather unique in my eyes. Sorry to those of you who thought you had to kill goat mom, but there's always YouTube!
The controls in the game are very simple, you have simple 8-way movement and select/cancel, Undertale could technically be run with a NES controller (well, Mettaton might get a little difficult for you without Z.) I would complain that you only move at a fixed pace the entire time but all in all the game itself isn't very long for an RPG so it's not necessary in my eyes, I felt rather at easy with it. That also adds to the retro charm the game has to it as inspirations such as Earthbound and Yume Nikki were the same way. Keeping the controls simple left more focus on the gameplay itself, and I like that.
Speaking of the gameplay, the battle system is very creative, I don't think I've ever played an RPG that turned your defensive turn into a bullet hell gauntlet, that was one element that originally drew me into playing, and holy gasterblaster Batman, the game surely will push you if you're taking one particular route.
Typically if a game is selling it's soundtrack seperate that's a good indicator that it's rather good on it's own, (I did say TYPICALLY, I know there's quite a lot of junk out there trying to market it's music off as something you'd want to enjoy when in reality you would prefer to smash your skull against a wall for the same effect.) I haven't been able to make a trip to or from work recently without a play of Megalovania or Save The World to keep my spirits up, that says a lot about a person who's got over 200gigs of similar musics stockpiled up. Looking further, Undertale's OST has been given multiple awards and Top 10 placings, most recently in memory one from WatchMojo (for a personal favorite of mine.) The music in itself would be one reason you wouldn't want to spoil the game if the story doesn't interest you.
This new retro wave has served many indie developers well the past 10 or so years and I am ecstatic about it- that modern mechanics and experience can lend itself to the 8 and 16-bit aesthetic to give some really impressive results. Originally the fact that overworld sprites were colored and in-battle sprites were monochrome was a little puzzling to me but it gives a couple encounters a little room to expand it's impact. I can't decide whether or not I felt that was a good thing- eventually I stopped thinking about it when I became immersed in my first playthrough but it was one thing that nagged at me in the back of my head so it's worth noting.
Undertale has become one of my favorite games of all time and I will most definitely be coming back to play more of it in the future, there's so much mystique in and out of the game's story that the internet is salivating with creative user-generated artwork and fan theories proped up by one annoying little dog who managed to program the game by accident. To say it has colored my presence online and my search histories in font skeletons and determination is a bit of an understatement. I love the characters, I love the music, I love the story and I love how its sole programmer has been handling it all. This is one gaming experience you won't want to miss out on.
EDIT: Nominated this for the tearful award in the 2016 Steam Awards.

For brevity, this review will only compare Borderlands 2 with its predecessor because, quite frankly, if you haven't played Borderlands -- you need to or you simply won't enjoy this game (nearly as much).
WIth that in mind, the game has thirty hours of gameplay for the first play through with only completing the season pass DLC and about eighty-percent of the side quests, which is about on-par with the original title.  The difficulty is about the same, the loot is just as gloriously abundant, and the classes are still as enjoyable and customizable as before.  So there weren't any concessions when coming from the first game, which is always a nice surprise, and there were two major improvements:
First and foremost, Steam integration is now flawless.  In Borderlands you had to create a 2K account and add friends manually (there wasn't even an import option) and public play was tedious and didn't do anything to help your Steam Friends out.  However, in Borderlands 2, these problems all fade away.  You can invite people to your game via the steam overlay, you can add friends in the same fashion, and there are no third party accounts to remember.
Second:  The story line is more enjoyable than its predecessor.  This may be because of all the hat tips to the original game, picking up where the first title left off, or it may be better on its own;  I don't know.  The fact is you get to rescue, work with, and fight along side the characters you played in the original game.  Combine this with the areas you get to fight in being some of the old cities and locations, the game really hits the nostalgic button right on the nose.  The added "players" also make for a very impressive finale when you have eight (you, three friends, and four NPCs) fighting to reach Handsome Jack.
As always, this game's better with friends; so play it in CoOp!

Scone Recipe
Ingredients
225g/8oz self raising flour
pinch of salt
55g/2oz butter
25g/1oz caster sugar
150ml/5fl oz milk
1 free-range egg, beaten, to glaze (alternatively use a little milk)
Method
1. Heat the oven to 220C/425F/Gas 7. Lightly grease a baking sheet.
2. Mix together the flour and salt and rub in the butter.
3. Stir in the sugar and then the milk to get a soft dough.
4. Turn on to a floured work surface and knead very lightly. Pat out to a round 2cm/¾in thick. Use a 5cm/2in cutter to stamp out rounds and place on a baking sheet. Lightly knead together the rest of the dough and stamp out more scones to use it all up.
5. Brush the tops of the scones with the beaten egg. Bake for 12-15 minutes until well risen and golden.
6. Cool on a wire rack and serve with butter and good jam and maybe some clotted cream.

I really want to recommend this game, but seeing the state it's in now I can't. I could rant all day about it being in alpha since its release, or complain about hackers, but I won't because that would be redundant. What I WILL say though is that DayZ allowed itself to be just another one of the numerous "Early Access" survival games on the Steam Store: Reeling people in with cool content and trailers only to let them down with a lack of devotion to fixing the game and the community...
Holy♥♥♥♥♥♥the community is awful.
There is barely any concept of "Bandits" in this game, everyone will kill everyone. No where is safe, even in the remote parts of the map where nobody goes there's bound to be a sniper waiting to kill someone just for the sake of it. There is no efficient system in place to make killing a last resort instead of a sport. Sure your items get ♥♥♥♥ed up if you're sprayed with bullets but the psychopath with the gun pointed at you likely knows this, doesn't care, or he'll blow your brains out instead of going all Walking Dead and robbing you to save bullets.
In the relatively short time I've played this I met friendlies three times, and those were the best and worst moments of my time with this game. We traveled the land in search of supplies, sharing what we had so we wouldn't starve, defended each other with our lives, and ultimately got killed by another group of people who didn't care if we said we were unarmed or friendly, and unloaded bullets into us without remorse. After such tragedies I just went solitary: either avoid contact or kill if threatened. I only used small backpacks and satchelbags to keep a low profile, only wore clothing with non-revealing colors, and I would pass up loot opportunities  in towns if I got the slightest notion that someone else might be there. Sure I was surviving, sure that's a way to play the game, sure it was tense at times.
But it wasn't fun anymore. I was paranoid, always had my gun out, never went anywhere until I made SURE I was alone, nervous, scared, tense, stressed, I shot my gun in panic at what turned out to ambience noise. My experience was ruined by other players wanting to slaughter everything for fun and a Dev Team that turned a blind eye to what their game was becoming, what it IS. So in conclusion, if you buy this game you'll go through a varying process that starts with obliviousness and ends in either pointless bloodshed or unhealthy paranoid that's supposed to be gameplay...

So consider that up until this point I have been one of the hardest critics AGAINST this game...and unfair as it may be it was mostly because of the fandom.
But after having eventually biting the bullet and playing through a Neutral Run I have completely turned against my original opinion. This is absolutely every single bit as worth it as it can be, and for your $10 you shouldn't have a problem against anything it throws at you unless you are trying to find something to hate on.
Undertale completely makes its own game stand out on the absolute first battle you partake in....and when it comes to things that set it apart, it's actually taking the gameplay mechanic of 'your choices matter' to such an insane degree of truth that which TellTale Games only wish they could apply it to their own games. Literally everything you do in the game matters and will make a difference. Who you spared, who you killed, what equipment you're even wearing, what you say to certain characters will permanently be reflected in the file of the game you play and will actually even carry over onto the next game you play should you decide to restart and choose a different way to approach the story.
Then there's the amount of battling: there's a lot of fighting but the number of battles is only one thing: necessary. There's no actual grinding to be had in the game at all. You don't approach areas where enemies will get into random encounters. Instead there are physical points on the maps where you will face enemies and what happens afterwards is entirely up to you because there is only THAT enemy/set of enemies in that one spot you walked into under whatever conditions they may be.
On top of that, there's not a single period in the game where you're dealing with a long period of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t. There's no lull anywhere. You're constantly migrating from setpiece to setpiece, and whether or not it's filled with more story cutscenes is usually dependent on WHERE you are...but to say that Undertale contains the usual conventions of JRPGs (ones where you have to spend inane amounts of time in any given area to gain experience for a boss fight or spending time to get equipment for an encounter) would be an outright lie. You don't. You can go as slow or as fast through the game as you see fit.
For my absolute first time playing the game I clocked in under 300 minutes...roughly 297 if I remember correctly. But I still didn't see everything because each time I do the game a certain way there's new things to find....ON TOP of the aforementioned aspect of the game remembering all of your choices and that EVERY single choice you make actually matters.
If that all weren't enough, the music is as every bit filled with character and charisma that oozes everything I would personally want out of any video game. Every tune is humm-able, every tune fits the scene where you're at or its atmosphere...and most of all...every single tune is catchy as hell. Its splendid tonal changes from giving the feeling of a cold wintry cave to volcanic mountains, to a club named 'The Core' is the kind of funk I wanted from video games since I originally played Jet Set Radio and its subsequent sequel for the Xbox. The game does things where it jumps from 8-bit chiptune to SUDDENLY, (for example in the fight against Papyrus) plays the exact same tune you were just listening to but with a full accompaniment with actual instruments.♥♥♥♥♥♥like that just strokes my musical boner, and it doesn't help that every single boss tune perfectly describes the personality of the characters they play for and are as every bit full of life as they are different; much like the characters they're playing for in the first place.
To top it off, the final boss of just the Neutral pathway does something I never thought I would see: clever programming that breaks the 4th wall the likes I haven't seen since Earthbound for the SNES (much less a final boss that rivals Gigyas in terms of tonal change that they bring with them).

I'll be brief: It was amazing, but I can't tell you why. I can't tell you much, you'll just have to play the game yourself. The less you know, the better it will be for you. Trust me, I'm an internet stranger. I'll say one thing though: You will change everything.

I logged in. I spawned with nothing but a rock, a bow, and a few trusted arrows. My inventory was meager, but I did not let this diminish my ambition. As I looked over the horizon I saw a man. He was medium built and naked down to the boot. The only thing identifiable about this man was the look of hatred in his eyes when he turned towards me from over 200 meters away. Although we locked eyes for only a moment, we both had a silent understanding. We knew that only one of us could walk away alive.
The next thing I know I am sprinting towards this man with all the energy I could muster. The only thing on my mind was spilling this man's blood. As we approached eachother I pulled out my bow and nocked one of my few trusted arrows. I aimed the arrow high above his head and gently lessened the grip of the arrow until it jettisoned from my bow into his skull. In almost the blink of an instant my advisary was on the ground and screaming like a wounded deer.
I knew I had to put my prey out of its misery. As I gradually approached the injured man I recognized I had to dissociate this man as another person. I had to rationalize them as an animal in order to sever any doubts in my mind to finish the job. I then raised my rock high above my head and slammed it into his skull. A man no more. What was once a man is now an empty cadavar; a desolate shell.
As I gleefully looted my prey and took his items I heard a warcry from behind me. As I turn around I see a naked man about 100 meters away from me jumping in sheer jubilee. The last thing I see is his wooden spear flying through the air directly towards my head. I did not move. I stared blankly into my computer monitor, wondering what I had become.

Let's keep this short so you can get to play this game as fast as possible:
Undertale is a bullet hell game. If you don't like that, watch a playthrough on your prefered online video platform, because the story is still really intense and worth just to experience. If you happen to NOT be disgusted by bullet hell games or are up for new challenges (to which I sort myself in) you should give this game a shot. The worst thing that could happen is that you look up a wiki on the internet helping you on your way.
Because: I really like Undertale as a story, as a RPG and as a innovation. It deserves the 10/10 scores in my opinion even if I don't happen to be a reviewer that fixates his opinions in numbers and scores. Yes, the graphics are somewhat old school and not the most beautiful, but you'll grow to like it soon enough finding yourself in a beautiful world full of unexpected changes, turns, twists and jokes that even break into your comfort zone.
There are three ways to bring this story to an end based on your decisions and each of it's own is worth like 4-5 hours of playtime. There are even many many more secrets to the game that frighten me to uncover and yes, I just happen to say that about an RPG game where being frightened of the outcome out of your choices is something strange to say.
As I said, it's innovations are awesome, groundbreaking and truely what I would like to see more of. I personly happen to end the experience in the best possible state of outcome and continued to educate myself about the other ways this story could take on the internet. Why you might ask? Simple: I've just grown to like what I've accomplished and I really like to keep what I achieved in the best possible scenario. It touched my heart through simple pixels but with a strong bond and determination of myself and the characters that I encountered.
So yes, this game is one of the rare gems that you maybe won't find again in this decade of video game history and if it does happen again, then we can all agree on this game being the first of it's kind charming our hearts with loveable characters, quirkiness and determination, which only you have the control over.
